title: Niamh O'Brien, dancer and wife of Michael Flatley, dies at 52
content:
Niamh O'Brien, a former lead performer in Lord of the Dance and the wife of Riverdance star Michael Flatley, has died at the age of 52.

Announcing her death on social media on Monday, Flatley said his "heart is broken".

"My gorgeous bride of twenty years has gone to the Lord in Heaven."

O'Brien was a renowned Irish dancer who performed the lead role of Saoirse in the Lord of the Dance shows.

Flatley described her as "the most loving mother, wife and person and our lives will never be the same without her".

The couple had a son, Michael St James, who was born in 2007.

A representative for Flatley said that O'Brien died peacefully at the Beacon Hospital in Dublin after an illness, Irish national broadcaster RTÉ reports.

"The Flatley and O'Brien families are devastated by Niamh's sudden passing and have asked that their privacy be respected as they come to terms with this heartbreaking loss," said the representative.

"They express their sincere gratitude to the doctors, nurses and staff at Beacon Hospital who cared for Niamh over the past few weeks, and to everyone who has offered their kindness and support to the family."

title: Jeffrey Archer: bestselling novelist whose political career ended in scandal
content:
As many have observed, Jeffrey Archer, who has died aged 86, led a life as colourful as the plot in one of his novels.

He was, at one time or other, a senior Conservative politician, a best-selling author, a peer of the realm, and a convicted perjurer.

Possessed of huge drive, vast wealth and immense personal charm, Archer bounced back from disaster and, more than once, rebuilt a shattered life.

But for all his talents, he will be remembered as a man affected by a defective moral compass, whose public humiliation was entirely self-inflicted.

Jeffrey Howard Archer was born in north London on 15 April 1940.

Within two weeks, his parents moved to Weston-super-Mare in Somerset, where they bought a house from John Cleese's mother.

Archer's mother Lola was the first woman journalist on the weekly paper, the Weston Mercury.

In later life, Archer insisted that his father William, who was some 40 years older than his mother, was a decorated hero of the First World War.

In fact, he was a convicted fraudster who, according to a US newspaper, spent the war years conning people in New York.

In 1951, the young Archer went to Wellington School in Somerset.

Some people mistakenly assumed he had gone to the somewhat more prestigious Wellington College in Berkshire, and he did little to correct them.

Archer's academic career was undistinguished, and he left school with three O-levels. He did, however, embark on a fitness regime designed to improve his physique after his originally skinny frame led to taunts from fellow pupils.

After school, he drifted. There was a brief spell in the army and then a short course in physical education in America.

On his return, he spent five months as a probationary constable in the Metropolitan Police, before quitting to become a physical training instructor at a small prep school in Hampshire.

It was while holding a similar job at Dover College that his resume moved into the realms of fantasy.

He styled himself Jeffrey Archer, FIFPC, BSc, leading people to assume he had obtained a degree during his time in the United States.

In fact, as his unofficial biographer Michael Crick later discovered, Archer's alma mater in the States was, in fact, a bodybuilding club.

However, Dover College was so impressed, it backed Archer's bid to go to Oxford as a mature student to do a one-year Diploma of Education course.

At Oxford, he excelled in athletics, winning a Blue, although it was doubtful whether his course qualified him to be a bona fide member of the University.

More importantly, it brought him into contact with fellow students who would go on to hold senior positions in politics, finance and the media.

He also married Mary Weeden, a chemistry student whose beauty had attracted a long list of suitors. "It was love at first sight for me," the future novelist recalled, "but I don't think it was for her."

His public profile had been considerably raised when he managed to persuade The Beatles to come and support a £500,000 fundraising effort for Oxfam, a charity which Archer supported.

After serving as a Conservative councillor in London, he was put on the selection list for the safe Tory seat of Louth in Lincolnshire.

A reporter on the Times, John Clare, discovered that another charity for which Archer worked alleged he had misused expenses with claims for meals at posh London restaurants.

Clare buttonholed Archer and, according to his own account, the would-be candidate burst into tears and asked that the story be quashed.

It eventually appeared in the paper but with many of the salient details left out.

Concerns about Archer's suitability were ignored by the party members in Louth who adopted him. In a by-election in December 1969, he won the seat with a handsome majority.

He and Mary set themselves up in an expensive Kensington house and he became a member of Lloyds. He also began to build up his profile in parliament where he was seen as a liberal member of his party.

But, in 1974, he suffered a blow after being persuaded to invest in a Canadian company which claimed to have developed a process to cut carbon emissions. It turned out to be a scam.

Archer had taken out a second mortgage, as well as borrowing large sums from elsewhere, to raise money for the investment. Threatened with bankruptcy, he was forced to quit his parliamentary seat.

However, he managed to secure an agreement with his creditors and wrote his first novel, Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less in 1976.

Charting an American immigrant's rise from messenger boy to corporate tycoon, it was inspired, in part, by his own financial problems and did much to solve them.

Despite being rubbished by many critics, it sold well in the US and then in Britain, earning Archer a considerable sum in royalties.

Three years later, Kane and Abel, a ripping page-turner about the roller-coaster financial fortunes of two men who initially shared nothing but a date of birth, flew off the shelves.

A third novel, published in 1984, First Among Equals, about a cutthroat competition to become Prime Minister, cemented Archer's position as one of Britain's best-selling and highest earning authors.

It enabled him to purchase the Old Vicarage at Grantchester near Cambridge, formerly the home of war poet, Rupert Brooke, as well as a penthouse in London.

There, he entertained the great and the good with legendary parties, serving them with champagne and shepherd's pie.

First Among Equals, with its political theme, had more than hinted at Archer's desperation to get back into politics.

He got his chance in 1985, when Margaret Thatcher, impressed by his drive and personality, gave him an unpaid job as Deputy Chairman of the Conservative Party with responsibility for fundraising.

It lasted just a year.

In October 1986, the News of the World published a picture of Archer's friend, Michael Stackpole, paying £2,000 to a sex worker named Monica Coghlan.

The money was supposedly a bribe to persuade her to go abroad, to avoid the prying eyes of the press.

And while the News of the World did not allege Archer had slept with Coghlan, the Daily Star was less reticent.

Archer resigned his party post and sued the Star for libel. In court, he claimed the payment had been a goodwill gesture to a woman down on her luck.

Friends also gave him an alibi for the night the Star had claimed he was enjoying the company of Ms Coghlan.

It was the evidence of Mary Archer that swung the case.

Her appearance in court so captivated the judge, Mr Justice Caulfield, that in his summing up, he asked why a man with such a fragrant wife would sleep with prostitutes.

"Is he in need of cold, unloving, rubber-insulated sex," Caulfield asked, "in a seedy hotel round about quarter to one on a Tuesday morning after an evening at the Caprice?"

The jury duly found for Archer and he was awarded £500,000 in damages. The News of the World later settled out-of-court with him, admitting they too had libelled him.

He went back to writing his books which continued to sell. By this time, he was thought to be worth more than £50m.

In 1992, he was offered a peerage by Conservative Prime Minister John Major in recognition for his work with a charity set up to help Kurds who were being oppressed by Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein.

His wife, meanwhile, had joined the board of Anglia Television which, in 1994, was the subject of a takeover bid. The day after the move was discussed by the board, Archer bought 50,000 shares in the company on behalf of a friend.

When the news of the takeover broke, the shares climbed in value and Archer made a profit of nearly £78,000.

A subsequent investigation cleared him of insider dealing, but soured relations with the Conservatives who were mired in their own battle against allegations of sleaze.

Undeterred, Archer, with the support of new Conservative leader William Hague, was selected as the Conservative candidate for Mayor of London in 1999.

Once more, the threat of scandal forced his resignation when the News of the World printed an interview with Archer's former friend, Ted Francis.

Francis alleged that the politician had lied on oath in his 1987 libel action against the Daily Star and Archer resigned as Conservative candidate for Mayor the next day.

There would be no forgiveness.

"This is the end of politics for Jeffrey Archer," said William Hague. "I will not tolerate such behaviour in my party."

In 2000, Archer was charged with perjury and perverting the course of justice.

At the same time, his play, The Accused, opened in London.

It featured a murder in which the audience were the jury and decided the guilt, or otherwise of the protagonist at the end of each performance.

In May 2001, a month after Monica Coghlan's death in a road accident, Archer went on trial. This time, his wife's testimony failed to sway the court. He was convicted and sentenced to four years in prison.

Shortly after his conviction, police began investigating allegations of corruption.

These related to the Kurdish charity in which Archer had been involved. There had been complaints that much of the £57m he said he'd raised never reached the Kurds.

However, police concluded that Archer, in fact, had received very little of the donations himself.

First in HM Prison Belmarsh and then in HM Prison Wayland, Archer used his incarceration profitably - by writing a three-volume account of his time inside entitled My Prison Diary.

Two years later, he was released, having served half of his sentence. "I learned a lot from it," he said. "The British people are very forgiving."

He retained his seat in the House of Lords, as there was no mechanism to remove an errant peer. He remained a member of Britain's upper house until his formal retirement in 2024.

Writing well into his mid-80s, he continued to churn out at least one, if not two, novels a year.

In the last years of his life, there were several volumes of The Clifton Chronicles: detailing the turbulent life of former dockworker, Harry Clifton.

There were also seven novels about a fictional policeman, William Warwick, who rises from humble constable in the Metropolitan police to the very top of his profession.

In January 2026, the 85-year-old announced that his forthcoming novel, Adam and Eve, would be his last.

An epic tale inspired by Hitler's indecision about whether to invade Britain, Archer poured everything into it. "Everyone would like to run their last 100m at the Olympics and win the gold medal," he told BBC Breakfast in September 2026.

Few critics praised Archer's prose style, his sense of humour, or the emotional depth of his characters.

But none could match his talent for relentless, aspirational, rags-to-riches plots that, once started, could not be put down.

Lord Archer often appeared incapable of separating autobiographical fact from fantasy in his continuing drive for public recognition.

He died a wealthy man, albeit one whom very few trusted.

title: Blue Planet and Gandhi composer George Fenton dies aged 76
content:
Composer George Fenton, whose work included music for films such as Gandhi, Groundhog Day and The Fisher King, as well as TV shows like Planet Earth and Bergerac, has died at the age of 76.

The prolific musician received five Oscar nominations for his film scores, including those for Dangerous Liasions and Cry Freedom.

His work on the BBC TV show Blue Planet also earned awards from the Baftas, Emmy Awards and Ivor Novellos; and he also composed theme music for BBC News programmes such as Newsnight and Breakfast Time.

In a statement, Fenton's family said: "We are very sad to announce that George Fenton passed away unexpectedly today."

They continued: "He is survived by his loving wife Amanda, ex-wife Jane, children Gemma, Grace and Bridget, and grandchildren Lola, Audrey, Alfred, George, Frank and Beatrice, and a life of music."

The cause of death was not disclosed but, underlining the suddenness of his passing, Fenton had signed a new worldwide publishing deal just three weeks ago, external.

At the time, he said he was working on two new film scores and a musical.

Fenton was born George Howe in Bromley, Kent in 1949. According to a biography on his official website, external, his father was a mechanical engineer, and his mother had been a dancer before becoming a nurse during the war.

Both parents were musical - his father played drums and his mother played piano - but Fenton chose the electric guitar as his instrument at the age of seven.

That was "when music became more important than football," he later told The Express newspaper, external. "The Beatles had a huge influence on me."

He took his first lessons from a musician called Brian Rudd.

"He came into our lives as a chimney sweep, which he clearly wasn't," Fenton later recalled.

"My mother went mad at him because he filled the house with soot.

"As he left he said, 'I'm really sorry – but I tuned the boy's guitar for you.' She suggested that as compensation for the mess he could give me a lesson, which he did and then carried on doing."

Later, Fenton began to study the church organ, but rejected the offer of music college to pursue a stage career.

In 1968, he appeared in Alan Bennett's first West End play Forty Years On. Upon joining the actor's union Equity, he was forced to adopt his mother's maiden name, due to rules preventing two actors from sharing the same name.

During that production, he also understudied the musical director of the show, Carl Davis - who also became a prominent composer for film and television.

A year later, Fenton signed a record deal, and scored a top 10 hit in Sweden with a cover of The Beatles' Maxwell's Silver Hammer, external, but his career as a solo artist was short lived.

In the mid-1970s, he took a recurring role as the soldier Martin Gimbel in the ITV soap opera Emmerdale Farm.

But as time went on, he found that directors were always casting him in roles that required him to play an instrument, so he decided to make music his main focus.

Fenton got his first job as composer and musical director for a production of Twelfth Night at the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1974.

Eight years later, he was nominated for an Oscar for his score for Richard Attenborough's Gandhi, external, on which he worked with Indian composer and instrumentalist Ravi Shankar to develop themes reflecting the country's musical traditions.

It was only his fourth attempt at film music, and he was still almost entirely self-taught.

Throughout the 1980s, he wrote the soundtrack for a number of TV series, including the Bafta-winning The Jewel in the Crown, The Monocled Mutineer, and Alan Bennett's Talking Heads.

He also wrote many well-known theme tunes, including the BBC's One O'Clock News, Six O'Clock News, Nine O'Clock News, Newsnight, The Money Programme, and Radio 4's PM Programme.

For 1987's Cry Freedom - the story of South African campaigner Steve Biko, who was brutally killed by police - he worked with South African jazz musician Jonas Gwangwa, earning two Oscar nominations for best original score and song.

Almost by accident, the title track featured Fenton singing, external a list of anti-apartheid activists imprisoned or killed by the South African government.

He'd initially recorded the lyrics as a guide for Gwangwa - but the musician decided to keep some of them intact "as a gesture of brotherhood".

"Then it got nominated for an Oscar, so I then found myself singing it on live television to about a billion people, which was not what I intended at all," Fenton later told Radio 4's Desert Island Discs.

After composing the score for the BBC's Trials of Life in 1990, Fenton went on to create the music for what became known as David Attenborough's Earth Trilogy: The Blue Planet, external, Planet Earth and Frozen Planet.

Fenton's music perfectly complemented the stunning visuals of the ocean's depths and the polar ice caps, adding an emotional weight to the narrative, using the full might of the orchestra to evoke everything from wonder and awe to tension and suspense.

Following the success of the documentaries, Fenton created a show - The Blue Planet in Concert - which has been performed by leading orchestras in venues around the world.

Among his other well-known soundtracks were The Long Walk Home, You've Got Mail, Sweet Home Alabama, The Lady In The Van and Mrs Henderson Presents.

Fenton also scored more films for British director Ken Loach than any other composer.

Their 18 collaborations included Ladybird, Ladybird; I, Daniel Blake and The Wind That Shakes the Barley, which won the Palme d'Or at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival.

He also founded the Association of Professional Composers, which later merged with The Ivors Academy; and he is one of only a handful of musicians to receive the Academy's fellowship, alongside Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber, Sir Elton John, Kate Bush, Bruce Springsteen and George Michael.

In addition, Fenton was a visiting professor at the Royal College of Music and the University of Nottingham. He was made a CBE for services to music in 2023.

The composer often said that his musical career had been an accident, but nothing gave him greater joy than seeing his work come to life.

On his episode of Desert Island Discs, Fenton chose one of his own compositions - Reunion, from the soundtrack to the movie Accidental Hero - as it reminded him of watching pianist John Lowe play the melody in the studio.

"If I was sitting on a desert island and thinking about what a good time I'd had writing music, which I have, I want just one thing to remind me about the best part - which is the fact that you write something and then you're so surprised and thrilled at the way it's played," he told Sue Lawley.

"For a composer, that's the biggest kick you can get."

周一，美股三大指数收涨，纳斯达克指数创下历史新高，交易员忽视美国国债收益率上升并消化了新的经济数据。
道指涨90.93点，涨幅0.18%，报51267.89点；标普500指数涨51.23点，涨幅0.66%，报7773.95点；纳指涨286.44点，涨幅1.05%，报27477.31点，创收盘新高。
美股七姐妹多数收涨，英伟达涨2.12%，创历史新高，市值升至5.76万亿美元。特斯拉涨超2%，谷歌、Meta、微软涨超1%，亚马逊、苹果微跌。加密货币、油气、医药零售涨幅居前，诺瓦瓦克斯医药涨超20%，Moderna涨近7%，Coinbase、Circle涨超2%。美股Vaxcyte收涨30%，公司的肺炎球菌疫苗达到后期临床试验目标。SpaceX涨超7%。
Infrastructure Capital Advisors创始人兼CEO Jay Hatfield表示，科技股“有点像反向债券交易”。“就是买入科技股，卖出其他一切，所以它有点像不可阻挡的巨无霸。”
Hatfield补充说，自疫情以来，科技股一直是一种避险资产，理由是该板块与盈利相关的高增长以及对利率相对较低的敏感度。
“他们为债务支付多少利息真的不重要，而且对算力的需求如此强劲，所以（科技股）并不真正受利率影响，”Hatfield说。
随着科技股上涨，债券收益率也走高。美国基准10年期国债收益率最新上涨逾3个基点至5.311%，30年期国债收益率上涨逾3个基点至5.664%。由于交易员担心通胀将导致美联储在更长时间内维持更高利率，这两种收益率近几周均飙升至多年高位。
在交易员消化供应管理协会（ISM）关于服务业经济增长的最新报告之际，股票和债券均出现波动。ISM报告显示，9月服务业采购经理人指数为54.9%，大致符合预期。不过，该数字略低于前一个月的增长水平。
投资者现在将注意力转向美联储，其将发布9月会议纪要——可能揭示其上月加息25个基点的决定背后的考量。
国际油价5日下跌，截至当天收盘，纽约商品交易所11月交货的轻质原油期货价格下跌1.68美元，收于每桶89.43美元，跌幅为1.84%；12月交货的伦敦布伦特原油期货价格下跌1.93美元，收于每桶100.32美元，跌幅为1.89%。
第三季度财报季将于下周拉开帷幕，美国大型银行将发布业绩。数据显示，分析师平均预计标普500指数盈利将同比增长超过30%，主要得益于AI相关股票。
在债市近期动荡和中东战争持续的背景下，市场保持了显著的韧性。布伦特原油期货维持在每桶100美元上方，令投资者紧张不安。一些策略师认为回调理由充分，另一些则认为涨势仍有空间。
根据芝商所FedWatch工具，在周五就业数据显示美国9月就业增长放缓幅度超过预期后，交易员认为美联储10月会议加息的概率为24%，低于一周前的70%。

title: Author and former politician Jeffrey Archer dies aged 86
content:
Bestselling author and former politician Jeffrey Archer has died at the age of 86.

Archer sold more than 300 million books in his five-decade writing career, including the Clifton Chronicles and Kane and Abel, and often set the novels in his home town of Wellington, Somerset.

In a statement, Archer's publisher HarperCollins said the author died "suddenly and peacefully at home" on Monday between writing sessions.

The former Conservative MP was jailed for perjury in 2001 after being found guilty of lying and cheating in his 1987 libel case against the Daily Star.

Archer was born in north London in 1940 but soon moved to Weston-super-Mare in Somerset, where his family bought a house from John Cleese's mother.

In 1969, Archer was elected MP for the Lincolnshire constituency of Louth.

He served as an MP for five years before becoming Conservative Party deputy chairman.

He moved to the House of Lords in 1992 but was jailed for four years for perjury and perverting the course of justice in 2001.

He was found to have lied in libel action he had brought against the Daily Star newspaper, in which he was awarded £500,000 in damages.

The Star had alleged Archer had slept with a sex worker.

The peer was found by the court to have perverted the course of justice by asking a former friend to give him a false alibi and producing fake diary entries to back up his story.

He was also found to have perjured himself on oath during the libel trial.

He was released in 2003 and returned to the House of Lords until he retired in 2024.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described Archer's death as "devastating news".

"We will miss him very much," she told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday, adding that he had texted her earlier on Monday.

Badenoch said he was "very much loved by the Conservative family", adding: "I'm glad that I saw him recently."

Speaking about what she described as "other parts of his life", she said: "He did serve his time, he made amends, and he wanted to do a lot of good in the world."

Former Conservative prime minister Sir John Major said "we have lost a man who lived one of the most remarkable lives of our age", and that he will be "much missed – and long remembered".

Archer's last novel, Adam and Eve, was released on Tuesday.

Broadcaster Gyles Brandreth told BBC Breakfast that he was with Archer on Sunday. "I mean, literally 72 hours ago, doing a show in the West End of London celebrating this book, the publication, and he was in great form.

"He didn't really acknowledge that he'd changed much since being in prison, but I think he became a nicer person in some ways, a gentler, a milder person after the prison experience."

Former Conservative Party leader Iain Duncan Smith described Archer as "a remarkable man who did everything at full bore", adding: "There were simply no half measures with him."

Other former ministers also paid tribute. Sajid Javid said Archer had been a "dear friend", while Sir Jeremy Hunt said Archer had "showed enormous kindness with his advice about how to become a writer".

James Cleverly said the author and politician had been "a huge personality and fantastic storyteller", and that he had been very supportive when his wife Suzie was recovering from cancer.

Reform UK member and former Conservative minister Nadim Zahawi, wrote: "Jeffrey Archer was a dear friend and an extraordinary human being. His gift for storytelling was matched by his wit, warmth and boundless energy. Life was never dull in Jeffrey's company."

Michael Grade, who produced the TV adaptation of Archer's Kane and Abel, told BBC Breakfast he "was a consummate storyteller in real life as as well as on on the page".

"That was his greatest skill. But his greatest regret, I'm sure, was that he wasn't able to fulfil his political ambitions. I think he always secretly wanted to be - not necessarily so secretly - to be prime minister.

"But because of the mistakes he made in his life, it wasn't for me. But he loved politics more than anything," Lord Grade said.

Kate Elton, CEO of Archer's publisher HarperCollins, told BBC's Radio 4 Today programme: "He was curious about everybody and everything and he was just enormous fun."

Last week, Archer returned to his former school to promote his last book.

"It's wonderful to come back. What I got a real thrill about when I was walking towards the library is seeing the young boys and girls and thinking, 'that's the next generation'," Archer said at Wellington School.

Archer had been due to attend the Cheltenham Literature Festival on Saturday to discuss his final novel.

He and his wife Mary had celebrated their 60th wedding anniversary this year, HarperCollins said.

The couple have two sons and five grandchildren.

title: Former American Idol contestant sentenced to life in prison for murdering wife
content:
A US man who once appeared on the TV talent competition American Idol has been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for murdering his wife.

Caleb Flynn, 40, was found guilty last week after a short deliberation by the jury, which rejected his claim that an intruder broke into his Ohio home and shot his wife, Ashley Flynn, as she slept.

He was also found guilty of eight additional charges, including aggravated murder and tampering with evidence.

Letters from his two daughters were read in court during the sentencing hearing on Monday, pleading with him to finally admit his guilt and questioning why he killed their mother.

Flynn, a former music pastor, fatally shot his wife, a 37-year-old teacher, in February before staging their home in Tipp City to appear as if someone had broken in through the garage.

Flynn claims he was asleep when he heard gunshots and found his wife dead in bed after finding the garage door open. Their two children, ages 9 and 11, were also sleeping in the house at the time.

His wife's sister, Kayla Keyt, read a victim impact statement saying the murder had caused his daughters to question their Christian faith and had "shattered a family who trusted you".

One of his daughter's letters read: "Dear Daddy, I don't even know where to start. How could you do such a thing?"

She also said: "Mommy was the perfect person... And then you chose to kill the only mother I ever had."

The other daughter's letter began "Dear Caleb", rather than addressing him as her father, and asked him to "tell everyone what you did it and receive your outcome".

"You made me feel like an idiot thinking I could trust you," his daughter said. She added that she continues to have faith in God, and that she will never visit her father in prison.

Flynn sobbed loudly as the letters from his children were read.

The sentencing hearing also included Flynn reading a statement expressing love for his family, apologising for unspecified "decisions" that he made, and again claiming that he did not kill his wife.

"I made vows to Ashley on our wedding day. I failed those vows," he said.

Judge Jeannine Pratt called Flynn an "extreme" risk to the public as she imposed her sentence.

The murder verdict last week followed eight days of testimony, during which several incriminating text messages Flynn sent to his former mistress, Alleigha Botner, were read out and AI-generated songs were played that prosecutors said he made for her.

Evidence presented during trial included police body camera footage and activity on Flynn's iPhone and Apple Watch from around the time of the murder when he claimed to have been sleeping.

The prosecution also called dozens of witnesses, including Botner, whom he met while she was an intern at his church.

Botner read aloud in court some of their 100,000 text messages, including one where Flynn wrote: "I was up until 4am last night crying, literally thinking of ways to kill her and not go to jail."

In another message, he wrote: "I just want her dead and gone."

Flynn did not testify during the trial, and his defence team called no witnesses.

His lawyer, Patrick Mulligan, has said he plans to file a notice of appeal, telling reporters last week: "There's a lack of evidence on prior calculation and design."

Mulligan argued that evidence of infidelity was not evidence of murder and questioned why Flynn was being accused of tampering with evidence because his gun could not be found.

This gun, which had been kept in the console of his truck, has been missing since investigators arrived at the scene and found the truck's centre console open.

Prosecutor Paul Watkins read a statement from Ashley Flynn's family in court after the verdict in September, saying: "Ashley loved Jesus with her whole heart."

"She loved people," the statement continued. "Most of all, she loved being a Mum."

Flynn briefly appeared on American Idol in 2013, saying that he loved his wife "more than anything".

title: 沙特主导的联军称在也门荷台达省实施军事行动
content:
当地时间10月5日，沙特主导的多国联军发言人图尔基·马利基表示，联军海军部队当天在也门荷台达省实施军事行动，打击了胡塞武装相关军事目标。
马利基称，行动摧毁了武器库、装有爆炸物的船只储存设施以及海军水雷等目标，并挫败了一项针对红海南部水道发动袭击的计划。

title: 铜产业要跳出结构性困局
content:
来源：经济日报
近期，铜价连续刷新历史高点。伦敦金属交易所3个月期铜价格盘中一度突破14800美元/吨，创历史新高；国内 沪铜 主力合约也站上11万元/吨关口。随后价格虽迅速回撤，但整体仍运行在高位区间。
市场行情持续火热之下，铜产业链利润分配却严重失衡：手握资源的上游矿企尽享量价齐升红利，盈利大幅增长；中游冶炼加工环节却持续承压，铜精矿现货加工费跌入负值区间，企业倒贴成本组织生产。同一行业、同一行情下的两极分化，本质是低端加工模式的结构性困局。
铜是支撑新能源迭代、算力基建落地、高端装备升级的重要金属，是先进制造业不可或缺的基础材料。经过多年发展，我国已建成全球规模最大的铜冶炼与加工产业体系，产能产量稳居世界首位，产业体量优势十分突出。但规模庞大不等于产业强大，体量优势并未完全转化为竞争优势。
产业链盈亏分化，表面是短期供需错配导致的周期现象，根源是行业长期固化的粗放发展路径。当前全球铜矿供给进入刚性收缩周期，海外核心矿山品位持续衰减、生产扰动频发，新建矿山开发周期漫长，新增产能难以匹配全球新兴产业带来的增量需求。而我国铜精矿对外依存度高达80%，冶炼产能持续扩张，存量产能规模庞大，形成典型的“矿少炉多”产业格局。多数企业长期停留在初级加工环节，依靠固定加工费维持营收，陷入“产能越大、内卷越重、利润越薄”的恶性循环。这种重规模扩张、轻价值提升，重初级加工、轻技术创新的发展模式，在行业平稳周期尚可维系，在资源持续紧平衡、全球产业高端竞争加剧的当下，已然难以为继。
产业转型提质，首先要纠偏产能扩张惯性、夯实资源保障根基。一方面严守产业准入红线，严控新增冶炼产能，有序清理低效、违规产能，优化存量产能结构，坚决遏制低端产能无序扩张。另一方面构建多元韧性的资源保障体系，加大国内深部找矿和低品位铜矿高效开发力度，稳步拓展海外权益矿多元化布局。同时激活再生铜“城市矿山”价值，完善废旧铜回收、提纯与高端利用体系，形成原生冶炼与再生利用互补共生的供给格局。
技术创新是破解低端困局、拉升产业价值的重要抓手。近年来，国内产学研协同攻关实现多项技术突破，为产业高端化转型提供有力支撑。中色科技股份有限公司研发的高端耐热细晶铜板带填补国内空白，实现批量出口；中色正锐（山东）铜业有限公司攻克超薄铜箔精密制造核心技术，打破海外长期垄断，实现高端电子铜箔国产化；铜陵有色集团公司成功量产6N级高纯铜，7N级超高纯铜技术稳步迭代，持续补齐高端铜基材料短板。这些实践充分证明，唯有深耕高端材料赛道，才能摆脱低价“内卷”，拓展产业增量空间。
深挖产业链价值潜力，需要全面提升资源综合利用水平。依托成熟冶炼工艺与技术积累，全面盘活冶炼伴生资源，深挖产业链隐性价值。伴随AI算力、高端电子产业快速崛起，昔日的冶炼边角料、附属产品，已成为支撑高端制造的核心新材料，价值实现翻番。从单一冶炼加工到全元素高效利用，是铜产业重构盈利体系的关键路径。
当前全球铜产业竞争早已告别单一产能比拼，转向技术、材料、价值链的全方位较量。我国铜产业必须主动破除低端加工路径依赖，以资源强基、技术赋能、价值重塑推动产业提质升级，加快实现从“体量领先”向“质量领跑”的跨越，为新能源、高端制造等战略性新兴产业高质量发展筑牢坚实的材料支撑。

title: 也门胡塞武装称对沙特境内多个目标实施三轮军事行动
content:
也门胡塞武装10月5日夜间发表声明称，为回应沙特过去24小时对也门发动的军事行动，胡塞武装当天实施三轮军事行动，使用大量弹道导弹、巡航导弹和无人机，分别袭击沙特利雅得哈立德国王国际机场、拉比格阿美炼油厂，以及艾卜哈机场、海米斯穆谢特基地、阿西尔省阿基法军营和纳季兰、吉赞省的多个敏感目标。
声明称，过去24小时，沙特对也门首都萨那以及焦夫、塔伊兹、荷台达、萨达和马里卜等多省发动60次空袭和导弹袭击，造成包括妇女和儿童在内的平民伤亡。自军事升级开始以来，沙特对也门胡塞武装发动的空袭和导弹袭击总数已达到1576次。
胡塞武装称，第一轮行动针对利雅得哈立德国王机场，袭击“精准、直接”，导致机场航空运输活动受到影响。第二轮行动针对拉比格的阿美炼油厂，声明称，袭击同样“精准、直接”，并导致目标地点起火。第三轮行动则针对艾卜哈机场、海米斯穆谢特基地和阿基法军营，以及纳季兰、吉赞省其他敏感目标。声明称，相关袭击均“精准命中”。
胡塞武装同时警告所有使用沙特领空的国际航空公司不要继续运营航班，称沙特领空已经成为其军事行动的“战场”，但麦加和麦地那的圣地上空除外。
声明还称，胡塞武装拥有应对当前军事升级所需的能力和资源，并表示已经为“这一天”做好准备。
沙特外交部谴责胡塞武装持续袭击沙特平民及民用设施
当地时间10月5日，沙特阿拉伯外交部发表声明，强烈谴责胡塞武装持续针对沙特境内平民以及民用和经济设施发动袭击。声明同时表示，沙特重申对也门总统领导委员会、也门政府和也门人民提供全面的政治和军事支持。
（总台记者 张雨辰 张亚宁）

title: AI狂热掀起造富浪潮 科技巨头跻身史上最高光年份
content:
如果感觉2026年是全球科技亿万富豪的丰收之年，那么数据也证实了这一点。
彭博亿万富豪指数显示，截至9月30日，全球500大富豪中约100位科技富豪的财富合计增加8450亿美元，创历年前九个月最高纪录。
推动这一增长的力量与全球市场的主要 驱动力 如出一辙：人工智能热潮和科技股飙升，尤其是在美国。科技亿万富豪目前的财富总额达到4.6万亿美元，占该指数全部财富的36%，尽管他们只占上榜人数的约五分之一。
这种分化十分明显。同期，在科技行业以外积累财富的亿万富豪合计损失620亿美元，而美国富豪贡献了该指数净财富增幅的94%。自9月10日以来，全球十大富豪全部来自美国，这是彭博2012年开始追踪亿万富豪以来首次出现这种情况。
财富增长也高度集中在最顶端。全球首富埃隆·马斯克今年截至9月底财富增加3100亿美元，约占该指数总增幅的40%。SpaceX与他的人工智能公司xAI合并并于6月上市后，马斯克曾短暂成为全球首位万亿美元富豪。
全球十大富豪中有九人的财富来自美国科技公司。戴尔科技创始人Michael Dell的财富增长81%，达到2540亿美元，得益于公司数据中心销售业务迅速扩张。随着Meta Platforms推出新的Muse个人AI助手，其股价9月上涨27%，创近四年来最佳月度表现，马克·扎克伯格今年财富增加230亿美元。

title: Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
content:
President Donald Trump has said the US moved its bombers out of RAF Fairford because of "some threats" to the base.

The Pentagon confirmed on Sunday it had removed its bombers - thought to be about a dozen B-1s - from the base back to their home stations in America.

Speaking to reporters as he departed for Nebraska on Monday, Trump said the US had known of a "threat", which led them to move the bombers.

US media reports suggested that the decision was made due to intelligence suggesting that Iran was plotting a drone attack. The BBC has not confirmed this and Trump has refused to be drawn on the question.

The exact nature of the threat that prompted the aircraft's removal from RAF Fairford remains unclear, but sources in Washington speculated to the BBC it might have revolved around sabotage attempts or attempts to strike the sensitive, expensive aircraft in the event of resumed hostilities with Iran.

One source close to the White House pointed to Ukraine's Operation Spiderweb as an example of what an enemy force could do, even at a distance.

Operation Spiderweb was an operation in June last year in which Ukraine smuggled drones into Russia. These were carried on lorries to locations near airbases by drivers who were unaware of their cargo, then launched and set upon their targets.

The source added: "Whatever they thought it was, it was taken extremely seriously."

Earlier on Monday, a No 10 spokesperson had insisted RAF Fairford was safe and pointed to Trump's comments last week, where he praised the UK's "police, defence and security services" in relation to the base.

Trump's comments appear to confirm reports by US media that a new threat led to the bombers being removed after a major incident on 27 September when police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.

While speaking to a group of reporters outside the White House, Trump was asked if a "specific threat" had led the US to pull its bombers from the airbase.

Trump replied: "Yeah I think we can say that. They didn't fly out by accident.

"There were some threats. And rather than tempting the enemy, we'll capture the enemy and beat the enemy. But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit. Not very far."

He added Washington "actually knows the people that made the threat", but he did not confirm who - though later said "they would be linked to Iran" when asked.

The BBC has contacted the White House and the Ministry of Defence for comment.

Trump's comments, and those of Vance before him, stand in stark contrast to those of Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

While both Trump and Vance pointed to an unspecified threat, Rubio was much more guarded in his language, noting that it was "not unusual" for military units and assets to rotate and be moved around the world.

RAF Fairford - in the Cotswolds in Gloucestershire - has been at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter-terror police.

Five men were initially arrested on suspicion of terror offences and subsequently released on bail. A sixth man, a UK-Iranian national, was also later arrested and released on bail.

Following the release of the first five men, Trump criticised the decision and US officials suggested Iran could have been involved in the incident.

Whitehall sources have not disputed that the decision from Washington to remove the bombers was in response to the incident at the airbase in Gloucestershire.

Speaking earlier on Monday, Rubio said he would not directly tie last week's incident to the decision to pull bombers from RAF Fairford.

He added: "It's not unusual to see movement of assets to different parts of the world based on exercises, redeployments, people changing out and new people coming in, new planes coming in and old planes going out."

Rubio said the US still had full confidence in the security of all its bases and that British authorities had been very co-operative since the incident.

Vance later said the bombers had been moved out of an "abundance of caution", adding Washington felt Iran was doing what it had "done for 49 years... which is engage in acts of terrorism against the US and against a lot of other people".

Days after the incident at RAF Fairford, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident but he did not provide further details, while Rubio said it had "clearly involve[d] the hands of a foreign actor" without going into further details.

Tehran has strongly denied any involvement.

In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

RAF Fairford, near the village of Whelford, has been used as a forward operating location by the US air force for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

The redeployment from RAF Fairford will reduce America's capacity to "quickly surge sorties against Iran, reducing the threat level somewhat", Christoph Bergs, research analyst at defence think tank the Royal United Services Institute told the Reuters news agency.

However, the use of the base had already been limited given London's stipulation that it should only be used for defensive strikes, he added.

The planes could potentially be sent to either Diego Garcia or bases in the Gulf to reduce the need for air-to-air refuelling but that would depend on capacity availability, negotiations with allies and security, Bergs added.

title: US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia
content:
President Donald Trump says the US is looking "very strongly" at the case of a Russian lab technician who died at a plague research centre in Siberia.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was watching closely amid concerns the incident could lead to the spread of pneumonic plague, but there was no cause for alarm.

Announcing the cause of death as "pneumonia of undetermined etiology", Irkutsk's governor said "no micro-organisms" linked to the woman's work had been found "in her biological samples".

Unconfirmed reports suggested the woman fell ill either after breaking a test tube containing the pathogen or following a field trip to a region where plague occurs naturally among wild rodents.

Asked what Washington was going to do about the risk of plague spreading from Russia, Trump said he had not spoken to the Kremlin about it.

"I hate to see them having it," he said, but added: "We'll help. Everybody who has that kind of a problem, we'll always help."

No other cases of staff from the plague institute seeking medical attention since the lab technician's death had been reported, Irkutsk governor Igor Kobzev said, quoting Russia's consumer and health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor.

The watchdog said a biological safety team had inspected the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk and found no emergency situation there.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged people not to "listen to various rumours" but "rely on Rospotrebnadzor's official statements" instead.

Russian media reported last week that nearly 200 people known to have had contact with the dead woman were under medical observation as a precaution.

Asked by a reporter for an "update on the suspected plague case in Russia", Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: "It seems that there was a worker at the lab that was infected and there's concern that that, you know, could have spread, at least internally - you've seen them do quarantine of this and that nature.

"If something like that gets out, it can quickly spread. So we're watching and monitoring it closely. I don't think it's cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and the cause to just keep an eye on it and we're doing that."

The woman who died, whose first name was given by Russian media as Daria and who was in her late twenties, had recently visited the Buryatia region on the border with Mongolia.

The plague bacterium or Yersinia pestis, external, which killed up to half the population of Europe in the 14th Century when it was known as the Black Death, is found among rodents such as marmots in the area.

It was in response to an outbreak in the 1920s that the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, external was founded just over 100 years ago.

Dr Simon Clarke, an associate professor in cellular microbiology at the University of Reading, told BBC Radio 4's PM programme that the pneumonic version of Yersinia pestis was nearly always fatal if left untreated, but could be overcome with antibiotics.

"Pneumonic plague can transmit from person to person and that is why there is the concern around this," he said.

He added: "But of course people's thought with any outbreak of infectious disease at all runs to... lockdowns and Covid and that is just not what's going to happen here."

"People think, 'Oh the plague, that's gone, that went hundreds of years ago,' but it hasn't," Clarke said.

"It's still around and in certain parts of the world, it's a threat to human health and that's why they need to study it."

Asked if the pathogen might have been studied for potential use as a bio-weapon, the scientist agreed it was possible.

"Because this is Russia people's thoughts are running to that, but I think my earlier explanation is probably more likely," Clarke said.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pneumonic plague has a very short incubation period - sometimes just 24 hours - and can be fatal, if not diagnosed and treated early.

People can be infected through:

infected flea bites

contact with bodily fluids or contaminated materials

the inhalation of respiratory particles.

Symptoms include shortness of breath and coughing, often with blood-tainted phlegm.

title: 土耳其一客机发现爆炸物威胁纸条 143人安全撤离
content:
总台记者 获悉，当地时间10月5日晚，一架从土耳其首都安卡拉飞往尚勒乌尔法的客机上发现一张声称机上有爆炸物的纸条。
尚勒乌尔法省省长哈桑·舍尔达克表示，涉事客机为AJet航空4180航班，于当天19时从安卡拉起飞，20时05分降落在尚勒乌尔法GAP机场。机上共有136名乘客和7名机组人员，目前没有人员出现健康问题。
舍尔达克表示，相关纸条是在飞机洗手间内发现的。安全部门对飞机进行了搜查，随后还将检查机上行李。有关部门还将对乘客进行笔迹分析，以调查纸条来源。
据悉，受此影响，尚勒乌尔法机场一度发布航行通告并暂时关闭。（总台记者 陈慧慧）

title: 视频丨年轻人爱上房车旅行！国庆假期房车消费迎来新变化
content:
今年国庆假期，公路出行占比预计超90%，自驾游成为出行主力，房车消费发生转变，从短期租赁体验，走向直接购置自用。政策加码+配套完善，房车从小众爱好走向更多人消费。
国庆假期第五天，全国交通出行陆续迎来返程客流。5日全社会跨区域人员流动量超3亿人次，公路出行预计占到90%以上，自驾游是绝对主力。长假催生大量跨城深度游需求，带着“家”奔赴远方的房车，收获越来越多消费者青睐。
房车租赁爆单
玩房车的年轻人越来越多
以往租客以银发群体为主，今年90后、95后年轻家庭正快速增长 。出游需求从周边短途露营，转向跨省长线自驾。假期房车门店一车难求，平均租赁时长拉长至7天。
国庆前夕，杭州一家房车租赁门店迎来提车高峰，陈女士一家正准备开启西北长线房车之旅。此前他们只租房车做周边短途游，充足的长假，让一家人计划奔赴更远目的地。
陈女士表示，近几年出游优先选择房车，出行自由度更高，不用卡点赶酒店退房，吃住全部在车上，私密性强，老人小孩出行也更加从容。
门店负责人介绍，过去房车租赁的核心人群是55至65岁、偏爱长途旅居的银发群体， 今年租客群体明显年轻化，90后、95后家庭数量快速增长 。
门店负责人谈到，长线异地还车订单大幅上涨，游客出行从周边露营转向全国长线旅行，平均租车时长达到7天。门店常备约100台车辆，在这个国庆假期已经全部租满。
不满足只租，有人干脆直接买！
房车消费逻辑转变，不少游客结束租赁体验后选择购车。购车需求分化：大空间拓展款、小型宿营车各有市场。房车销量持续走高，新能源车型成为增长新亮点。
租赁市场热度攀升的同时， 直接购买房车的消费者持续增多 。在江苏常州房车门店，选购房车的年轻人明显增多，房车度假模式，正在被年轻群体接纳。
在房车门店，有消费者现场提车，售价63.8万元的房车带有双拓展舱，车内空间宽敞。可满足车主多样化出行需求。
门店销售经理介绍，今年门店房车销量相比去年提升近30%，新能源车型销量占整体产品的25%。
据中国汽车工业协会房车分会数据显示，2025年，我国自行式房车总销量首次突破2万辆大关。今年上半年，我国自行式房车累计注册量已超过1.2万辆，同比增长32.6%，新能源房车渗透率攀升至18.4%。业内人士预计，在假期出行热和政策利好的双重带动下，2026年全年房车销量有望再创新高。
房车营地一票难求
房车产业链加速发展
十部门出台房车消费支持政策，覆盖供给、通行、营地建设。房车营地配套持续完善，加水充电等基础服务更加便利。 国庆营地预订火爆，自有房车用户占比持续提升。
今年九月，文化和旅游部等十部门联合发布了《关于促进房车消费的若干措施》，从提升房车供给质量、保障房车通行和停靠、加强房车营地建设 等方面提出九条政策举措，带动整条房车产业链加速发展。
杭州西溪湿地公园旁的房车营地迎来大批国庆游客，房车临湖停放，推门即见湖景绿意。不少游客慕名而来，大家直观感受到营地数量增加，加水、充电配套更加齐全，让出行体验更加舒适便捷。
营地负责人介绍，营地占地60余亩，拥有25个专业房车泊位。国庆10月1-2日预订车辆共15台；10月3日之后订单量在80%，后续计划将泊位数量扩容一倍。
配套持续落地 报废年限调整
产业发展空间进一步打开
截至2025年底，全国各类房车营地数量已经超过3100个。多地加快基础设施布局，高速服务区陆续增设房车补给区与专用泊位，房车营地等配套服务正在快速落地。
房车生产企业负责人介绍，新政调整房车报废年限，租赁房车由原来15年强制报废延长至25年，显著降低企业运营成本，释放产能空间。

title: 欧元汇率创17个月新低 法国债市危机引发“传染”担忧
content:
欧元汇率持续走弱，成为又一个值得警惕的信号，市场越来越担心法国债务状况可能威胁整个欧元区的稳定，令政策制定者面临更大压力。
周一欧盘交易时段，欧元兑美元汇率一度跌破1.12美元，触及1.1161美元，创下17个月以来新低；与此同时，欧元兑英镑、瑞郎和日元也大幅走弱。
分析师表示，法国正处于当前欧洲金融市场担忧的核心，该国政府正寻求推动一项不受欢迎的2027年预算方案，以降低财政赤字并控制创纪录高位的债务规模。但在议会严重分裂的情况下，这一目标难度很大。且随着各政治阵营为明年的总统大选展开布局，法国国内政治不确定性进一步升高。
不愿冒险的投资者正在抛售法国国债，同时买入被视为更安全的德国国债。目前，投资者持有法国国债而非德国国债所要求的额外收益率溢价，已升至2010年至2012年欧元区债务危机以来最高水平。外汇市场因此开始担心，这种压力可能进一步向其他欧元区国家蔓延。
欧洲面临的风险不容小觑：这个本就经济增长乏力的区域正受到政治不确定性的冲击。德国总理默茨领导的政党上月在一场地方选举中遭遇战后以来最严重的失利。周一，西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯宣布提前举行大选；意大利也将在明年举行选举。
“本周初，欧洲成为市场关注的焦点，财政和政治担忧正在冲击整个欧元区。”XTB研究主管Kathleen Brooks表示，“法国是当前担忧的核心，但西班牙也将迎来提前大选，这进一步加剧了投资者的担忧。”
与此同时，能源价格飙升已经推 高通 胀，而债券收益率上升又进一步增加家庭和企业的借贷成本。如果欧元继续走弱，欧洲央行可能陷入两难：一方面需要遏制通胀，另一方面又要稳定债券市场。
上周，法国与德国10年期国债收益率之差扩大至2012年以来最高水平；与此同时，意大利与德国国债收益率之差一度接近130个基点，创下新冠疫情危机以来最大的单周升幅。
分析师警告称，法国债券市场的压力可能蔓延至欧元区其他国家，引发市场对2010年代欧元区主权债务危机重演的担忧。
进一步下跌风险
“债券抛售正在引发更大范围的波动，任何被市场认为存在脆弱性的资产都会受到冲击，这也导致欧元遭到抛售，而且这种抛售势头正在不断加剧，”法国 兴业银行 首席外汇策略师Kit Juckes表示。
Juckes补充说：“此前支撑欧元兑美元维持在关键水平上方的那些因素……我认为已经消失了。”他所指的是市场此前认为能源冲击只是暂时性的，以及美国方面希望推动美元走弱的预期。
尽管欧元目前仍明显高于2022年俄乌冲突爆发、欧洲陷入能源危机时创下的20年低点，但债券市场的剧烈波动正在给欧元疲软增添新的因素。
美国银行 外汇策略师估计，法国与德国国债收益率利差每扩大10个基点，欧元兑美元就可能下跌约0.4%。
高盛 分析师在一份报告中表示：“在大多数时候，利差对汇率的影响接近于零，但在市场出现严重压力时，这种影响可能显著上升。”
他们表示：“除非利差成为唯一重要的因素，否则利差通常并不会真正影响汇率。”他们还指出，当风险事件导致德国国债收益率下跌、而欧元区其他国家的国债收益率上升时，利差对欧元的影响会进一步增强。
美国商品 期货 交易委员会（CFTC）的持仓数据显示，交易员目前押注欧元进一步下跌，这一看法也反映在外汇期权市场中。
分析师表示，欧元兑美元可能测试1.10美元关口。Juckes还指出，欧元兑日元和瑞郎等货币同样面临较大下行风险。9月份，欧元兑日元已经下跌近4%。
随着欧元汇率下跌与债券市场承压同时出现，市场开始讨论政策制定者应如何稳定金融市场，尤其是在2027年法国大选可能进一步加剧市场压力的情况下。
Eurizon SLJ 资产管理 公司首席执行官兼联合首席投资官Stephen Jen表示：“如果欧洲的财政传染风险无法得到遏制，我认为欧元兑美元仍可能进一步走低，尽管从估值来看，欧元目前已经略显低估。”
（文章来源：财联社）

title: England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender
content:
Harry Kane will write another chapter in his illustrious England history by equalling Peter Shilton's record tally of 125 caps if he plays a part in the Uefa Nations League meeting with the Czech Republic at Wembley.

England's captain is already his country's record scorer with 89 goals in 124 appearances in a full international career he started by opening his account 79 seconds into his debut.

Since that 4-0 win against Lithuania at Wembley in March 2015, he has been England's mainstay. He is still irreplaceable at 33 and their top scorer in major tournaments with 21 goals in 36 appearances across six of those showpieces, ahead of Gary Lineker's 10 goals in 18 appearances.

He is in the process of building a monument to his goalscoring brilliance at elite level as he stands 36 goals ahead of England's second highest scorer Wayne Rooney, who boasts a record of 53 goals in 120 games.

Kane is unquestionably England men's most important and influential player of the modern era. The only blemish on his magnificent career is the failure – not his alone it must be stressed – to add to the one men's World Cup won in 1966.

Irrespective of that space for silverware on his CV, how highly does Kane rank in the pantheon of greats who have represented the England men's team? Could he even be the greatest? He has made himself a serious contender.

Moore? Charlton? Rooney? - where does Kane rank?

This argument will instantly cut away from Kane to Bobby Moore, the elegant, unflappable defender who remains the only England captain to lift the World Cup, leading his team to triumph at Wembley in July 1966 as West Germany were beaten 4-2.

Moore was only 25 at the time, and had enjoyed success at club level with West Ham United, winning the FA Cup and European Cup Winners' Cup before the World Cup. He won 108 caps between May 1962 and November 1973.

And then, of course, the conversation must turn to Sir Bobby Charlton, who survived the Munich Air Disaster with Manchester United in 1958 to become arguably England's most famous footballer of his era.

Charlton was a global beacon of dignity and world-class ability, winning the World Cup then, two years later, captaining Manchester United when they became the first English team to win the European Cup, scoring twice as Benfica were beaten 4-1 at Wembley.

He remains third on England's list of scorers, with 49 goals in 106 games.

Sir Geoff Hurst will always claim a special place with his hat-trick in the World Cup final win, while many others will have their supporters from recent times, including the likes of Wayne Rooney and David Beckham.

Former England midfielder Danny Murphy, said: "Bobby Moore will always be in people's conversation. Sir Bobby Charlton also, because of what they did and the memories they created.

"As you move forward, for me as a kid Gazza [Paul Gascoigne] burst on the scene and became a hero, especially as a creative midfield player myself.

"I think Rooney was arguably the most all-round footballer we have ever had, the most talented I've seen – but no-one can argue with Harry Kane's quality, numbers and longevity. It is the record of an England great."

He added: "There is one thing there is no debate about. Harry Kane is England's greatest goalscorer.

"No-one can take that away from him. The numbers over such a period of longevity are incredible. This, in itself, deserves all the accolades in the world. To stay at that level and not have anybody displace him is testimony to his ability and professionalism.

"He's a born goalscorer. He's a super professional. He's technically brilliant. He's been an absolute credit to himself and his family in the way he's conducted himself and the longevity he's had in his career.

"Is he England's greatest player? This is all about opinions and eras, but his record and longevity alone informs you that he is an England great. He is in that elite group."

'We are guilty of underestimating what is in front of us'

Kane's status as an England great is beyond question. Where he stands in that list of greats will be shaped by eras and opinions, according to former internationals Paul Robinson and Murphy.

Robinson told BBC Sport that the scale of Kane's greatness might only be fully appreciated in years to come.

He said: "Harry Kane is an England great. There is no argument. He will always be part of that conversation now.

"I think we are guilty in the modern era of underestimating what we've got in front of us. We are quite happy to look through rose-tinted spectacles at what we had in the past.

"We will talk about Bobby Moore and Sir Bobby Charlton, but football now is a completely different game. The life of a footballer is completely different and it's almost like they are playing a different game.

"What Bobby Moore and Sir Bobby Charlton achieved, nobody in an England shirt has done since. You respect what they did in the era, and the status and legacy that comes with winning the World Cup and everything else they did, but we must also say it is a different game now."

Kane's double in Saturday's 7-0 win in Croatia took his tally to 11 goals in 12 games for England in this calendar year. He has also scored in six consecutive England away games, with only Sir Tom Finney having a longer run, seven between September 1946 and May 1948.

Last season alone, Ballon d'Or contender Kane scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for England and his club Bayern Munich.

He has scored five hat-tricks in an England career which includes 110 starts, with a 66% win rate.

"The biggest compliment you can pay Harry Kane is to ask yourself how long we've been pondering the question 'what will England do if Harry Kane gets injured?'," Robinson added.

"There is no-one close to his class in that position. It is taken as read the captain is playing and without the captain, we would be in trouble.

"I think we'll appreciate him even more in another 10,15, 20 years when you look back and see what he has achieved. People will point to the lack of silverware with England, but he can't play everywhere can he?

"We look back with nostalgia and fondness, saying we've had this great and that great – and England have – but make no mistake Kane is right in that debate and will be for years to come."

'The big moments haven't yet happened for him'

Kane's lack of a major international trophy will undoubtedly be the argument used to counter suggestions he is England's greatest.

He has come close, only to lose two World Cup semi-finals and two European Championship finals.

The next Euros in the United Kingdom and Ireland in 2028 could be his last chance to change that unwanted record.

Murphy, said: "The only thing really missing from him is the icing on the cake, namely getting over the line in a major tournament, which is looking less likely for him as the years go by.

"I suppose that will always be one criticism of him, as well as many England players and generations. Nobody has managed to get them over the line since 1966, and the responsibility usually does fall on the strikers or the captain.

"He didn't score in the World Cup semi-final against Croatia in 2018 or in the Euros final against Italy at Wembley. He missed a penalty against France in the World Cup quarter-final in 2022, then obviously he didn't score in the Euro 2024 final against Spain or the World Cup semi-final against Argentina.

"People will look at that and say in the big moments, it didn't happen for him.

"I don't adhere to that observation at all because it's not just him and he did so much to get England in those positions. Anyone can miss a penalty. The reality is the team itself, the tactics, all those things factor into why England haven't got over the line."

As Kane stands on the brink of equalling the England caps record, he still has time – and the enduring quality - to state his case as an all-time great even more forcefully in the future.

title: 美国将轰炸机全部撤离险遭恐怖袭击的英国基地
content:
美国从成为疑似未遂恐怖袭击目标的英国皇家空军基地撤走了所有轰炸机。
美国官员称，在与伊朗有关的新威胁浮现后，美军以异常迅速和紧急的方式完成了此次转移。
美国副总统JD·万斯周一启程前往阿拉斯加州进行助选前对媒体表示，重新部署是“出于高度谨慎，是为了保护我们的人”。
万斯表示，美国政府“有一定把握”伊朗正企图“对美国以及其他许多人实施恐怖主义行为。所以，我们极其谨慎。”
但国务卿马尔科·卢比奥对此有着不同的解释。他对媒体表示，这是常规调动，而它之所以引起关注只是因为几天前发生了未遂袭击。
他说：“根据演习、重新部署、人员调离、新人加入、新飞机加入、旧飞机撤离等情况在世界各地进行轮换和调动并不罕见。所以机组人员一直在变化。”
“我们对所有基地的安全都有信心，因为从理论上来说我们所有的基地随时都可能受到威胁，这就是为什么我们在基地周围搞了这么多的安全措施，” 他还说。
美国国防部一位官员表示，部署在费尔福德皇家空军基地的所有美军轰炸机都已返回本土。美军战机在2月开始的对伊朗军事行动中使用了该基地。

title: What prompted the US bombers to leave RAF Fairford?
content:
The unexpected mass withdrawal of America's heavy bombers happened so suddenly on Sunday that it has got everyone wondering what prompted it.

An "abundance of caution," says US Vice-President JD Vance, adding that Washington felt Iran was doing what it has "done for 49 years... which is engage in acts of terrorism against the US and against a lot of other people".

An abundance of panic is how others have seen it.

For the last seven months, America's B-1 Lancer bombers and other aircraft have been operating out of Fairford to strike the Iranian missile launch sites.

In July, Iran threatened any country that provided the US with such a facility would be considered a "legitimate target".

Then on 27 September, a major incident was declared when five British men were arrested and later bailed after being seen acting suspiciously with their three white vans in the dead of night close to the airbase perimeter.

At the weekend, a UK-Iranian dual national was arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. He was also released on bail.

Twelve valuable and strategically important B-1 bombers have now departed en masse and seemingly in such a rush that, reportedly, the air-to-air refuelling aircraft needed to get them back across the Atlantic to their home bases in the continental US were still being fuelled up while the B-1 Lancer crews were being ordered to scramble to take off.

So something was considered urgent and dangerous enough to prompt this.

Speaking after his vice-president's remarks, President Donald Trump himself said the US had removed its bombers because of "some threats" to the base.

"Rather than tempting the enemy", he added, the US had moved the planes "around a little bit".

There was almost certainly a fresh piece of intelligence, whether true or not.

British officials would not reveal what it was, but they did say "there is an ongoing high tempo of threat from Iran to the UK, and it is logical that US airbases would be pretty high on any targeting list".

Iran has denied any connection with events at RAF Fairford. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also played down any suggested link between this rushed evacuation and the arrests made on 27 September.

The context here is that while the UK is not at war with Iran, the US is - and that is a distinction Tehran has publicly challenged. As far as the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps is concerned, Britain is already a participant in America's war with Iran.

There is also a cost factor involved here.

The B-1 Lancer bombers which have now left each cost about $330 million.

The Americans have already suffered heavy financial losses from Iranian strikes on US bases in the Middle East.

In late March the Iranians hit Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, destroying an E-3 Sentry Awacs early warning plane.

That aircraft alone cost over half a billion dollars.

General Sir Richard Barrons, who served in one of the highest ranks in the British Armed Forces, said: "We now live in a world where a £1,000 drone could wreck one of those aircraft.

"So, I don't know what the threat was but the most prudent thing to do would be to remove them to Texas given that they were not doing very much at the minute."

But how does the US ordering the bombers to leave RAF Fairford reflect on Washington's confidence in the ability of the UK to keep the base secure?

Britain remains an incredibly close ally of the US and there are still hundreds of American servicemen and women stationed at RAF Fairford, as well as at other bases at Mildenhall and Lakenheath.

Work will likely be ongoing in secret now to review security at the base on both sides of the perimeter fence.

But it is hard not to conclude that, despite efforts to play down the drama, this is an embarrassing episode for the UK.

Rubio said the US has "confidence in the security of all our bases" and said the administrations was working "very closely" with UK authorities, who "couldn't be more co-operative".

UK counter-terrorism police are still investigating what happened at RAF Fairford and are keeping an open mind as to what exactly was behind events there.

I have been told a large amount of data, CCTV and other information is still being trawled through while the men remain on bail.

Meanwhile, now that the bombers have left British soil, the US insists it can still deploy them from its domestic bases anywhere in the world.

That could be seen as putting a brave face on something which, for Iran, sees a major US strike force effectively driven back to its home base in the continental United States.

title: Meta和微软设法减少员工对Claude的使用
content:
Meta和 微软 正努力减少员工对Claude的使用。
微软此前预计内部使用Claude AI的支出为10亿美元，在要求员工减少使用Claude以节省成本、并投入更多时间使用微软自研AI工具后，已将这一支出预期下调逾三分之一。

title: 以色列消息人士：迪拜航空副驾驶作案动机是“为加沙复仇”
content:
当地时间10月5日， 总台记者 获悉，迪拜航空公司客机驾驶舱冲突事件的阿曼籍副驾驶哈马姆·哈马米在受审时供述，其 作案动机是“为加沙复仇” 。
以色列消息人士表示，哈马米在阿联酋接受多国联合审讯时承认，他选择执飞该赴以航班并企图坠毁客机是蓄谋已久的报复行为。
另据以色列情报和特勤局（摩萨德）官员4日向以内阁成员透露，哈马米近年来曾对多个对以敌对国家进行短暂访问。目前，以情报机构正在核实其行程，以调查其背后是否存在特定组织或人员的招募。据悉，联合调查人员已获取哈马米的手机并正在梳理其内容，但以官方现阶段对其是否属于单独行动尚未作出定论。
此外，阿联酋调查人员在应以方请求对同机组其他成员进行问话后，目前已排除其他机组人员的涉案嫌疑。
不过相关内容未得到以色列及阿联酋官方证实。（总台记者 赵兵）

title: “麦加防务联盟”决定启动集体防御机制
content:
视频丨战火升级 也门政府宣布夺回战略要地 沙土巴紧急启动集体防御
当地时间10月5日，沙特阿拉伯、巴基斯坦和土耳其在利雅得举行“麦加防务联盟”战略政治与防务委员会紧急会议，并发表联合声明，宣布启动集体防御机制。
声明宣布，委员会决定立即推动落实集体防御承诺，并采取必要措施，向商定的军事力量和相关能力提供保障，确保其能够按照已经批准的安排以及各成员国国内法律，在沙特境内迅速部署。声明称，此举旨在提升战备水平、军事一体化程度以及三方共同应对和遏制威胁的能力。
声明说，三方此次会议主要讨论沙特面临的安全形势和威胁。作为“麦加防务联盟”机制建设的一部分，委员会决定任命巴基斯坦退役中将努曼·马哈茂德担任联盟首任秘书长，任期三年。
三方还在声明中强烈谴责针对麦加和麦地那的袭击企图，以及持续针对沙特平民、经济设施的袭击，并重申坚决反对任何针对沙特安全和领土完整的袭击或威胁。（总台记者 张亚宁 刘畅）

title: Katie Price's ex urged girl not to tell, court told
content:
Katie Price's ex-husband told a 13-year-old girl he is accused of raping "not tell anyone". adding he might "get in trouble for this", a court heard.

Kieran Hayler, 39, is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault of the teenager in West Sussex in 2016, all of which he denies.

Earlier, jurors were told that on the first alleged occasion, Hayler told the 13-year-old he really liked her and began speaking to her about having sex.

He told her it was a "special thing" and they should do it, before he raped her, the court heard.

The court was played the complainant's police interview in which she said Hayler told her how special and "important" the first time was.

She said: "He started crying and saying, 'Maybe I shouldn't take it away from you, it's so important'."

The complainant said she did not have a "conversation" with Hayler afterwards, and recalled thinking "I was probably a bit young".

Hayler allegedly raped the girl again on two further occasions.

The second occasion, she said, was two or three weeks later.

On this occasion she said she remembered waking up to Hayler being there, and after, he acted like "like nothing had happened".

On the third alleged occasion, the court heard Hayler told her she should not tell anyone, and then sexually assaulted her.

She said he told her: "You can't talk about it, you can't tell anyone, I might get in trouble for this."

It is alleged he grabbed her hand and put it down his trousers.

Speaking after this alleged incident, the complainant told police: "I think by that point I knew it wasn't quite right, he kept telling me to 'shh', I had to be secretive and not tell anyone."

She told police: "I tried to forget it for so many years."

In 2021, the complainant contacted the NSPCC charity which referred her to the police, prompting the investigation.

Hayler was first interviewed by police in January 2022 and denied any of the allegations took place and that anything sexual occurred.

He was married to media personality Price at the time of the alleged incidents, before the couple's relationship broke down in 2018 and they divorced in 2021.

Hayler suggested his ex-wife had "launched a campaign" against him when their marriage ended, and the allegations form part of this, the court heard.

The alleged victim is not part of Hayler or Price's extended families.

Price is expected to be a witness in the trial which is expected to last about a week.

The trial continues.

title: Prisoner took his own life after terror order had 'substantial impact' on mental state, inquest finds
content:
A prisoner took his own life after strict terrorism control measures imposed by the government had a "substantial impact" on his mental state, an inquest jury has concluded.

Akhtar Uddin, 35, a builder from east London, died in HMP Wandsworth on Christmas Day 2021 after being jailed the previous year for breaching Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPIM).

The jury at Inner West London Coroner's Court also found the prison service had failed to provide the support that Uddin needed.

Jurors concluded that Uddin died due to an action he took but said that it was "not possible to determine whether he intended the outcome to be his death".

Prior to being jailed in February 2020 for breaching the TPIM order, Uddin had served a sentence for racially or religiously aggravated harassment.

TPIMs allow the authorities to control people whom the government believes are involved in terrorism, but who are not facing criminal charges. The home secretary acts on advice from MI5 when imposing TPIMs.

Subjects of TPIMs face measures such as wearing an electronic tag, curfews, relocation to a different part of the country, bans on internet use, controls on finances, and limits on who they can meet and where they can go.

Breaches can result in a terrorism conviction and prison sentence. TPIMs can currently last up to five years, up from a maximum of two years when Uddin was under one.

Uddin breached the measures 12 times by withdrawing more money than he was permitted. The inquest heard he largely spent it on drugs. He had over 20 previous criminal convictions - none of which were for terrorism offences.

The inquest, which was the first ever to consider the impact of TPIMs, heard that Uddin believed the order was originally imposed because he had made reckless statements while under the influence of drugs, but that he insisted he was not a terrorist.

It is understood he was alleged to have made verbal threats and associated with people regarded by MI5 as being involved in terrorist activity.

Coroner Bernard Richmond KC said Uddin was "loved and loving" but was "not someone without his troubles" and these revolved around his drug use.

The coroner said he will be issuing a report to the government out of concern about a risk to other people under the terrorism control measures.

When the TPIM was first imposed on Uddin in January 2020, he was forcibly relocated to the West Midlands after being arrested at the prison gates in front of his sister who had come to meet him on release.

The full reasons for a person being on a TPIM are typically kept secret, even from the person subject to the TPIM, because they are based on MI5 intelligence.

The inquest heard that Uddin feared the TPIM would be re-imposed when he left prison early in 2022, and that he would again breach it due to drugs.

Today the inquest jury concluded the following:

"We are satisfied that the imposition of the original TPIM and its unusually restrictive nature had a substantial impact on the mental state of Akhtar Uddin."

"We are satisfied that the fear of a likely reimposition of such a restrictive TPIM, and its possibly never-ending nature, had a significant impact on the mental state of Akhtar in prison."

"We are satisfied, as a result of the consistent evidence that prison services were unaware of TPIM restrictions and their likely impact on Akhtar, there was a failure to provide support most suitably targeted to Akhtar's specific needs and situations."

A governor at HMP Wandsworth accepted in evidence that lack of knowledge of TPIMs by prison staff had resulted in "unintentionally cruel" treatment of Uddin.

Giving evidence, Uddin's sister said that, in the weeks before his death, he had described "counter terrorism officers" questioning him in prison and saying he would never get off the TPIM.

A statement from Uddin's family, issued by their solicitors Birnberg Peirce, said they welcomed the inquest's findings.

"Although nothing can bring back their loving son, brother and uncle, they hope that this will make a real difference to those who are currently at the mercy of this inhumane regime."

His former solicitor, Amer Ahmad, had told Uddin in autumn 2021 there were "highly limited prospects" that he would succeed in having the TPIM legally overturned, the inquest heard.

Dr Richard Latham, an NHS consultant forensic psychiatrist, appeared as an expert witness for the coroner and concluded that Uddin had an undiagnosed "personality disorder", associated "psychological problems and vulnerabilities", and this resulted in impulsiveness, grievance and paranoia.

He said Uddin probably assumed the worst about the TPIM in future, and that this prospect would have created "distress and a sense of hopelessness".

Dr Latham added TPIMs are intended to create a "degree of isolation," but that plays on psychological vulnerability and can create "emotional isolation".

Questioned by Jesse Nicholls, representing the bereaved family, Dr Latham said Uddin "felt a sense of injustice" about being branded a terrorist.

The inquest heard there was little or no awareness by staff in HMP Wandsworth of TPIMs. The coroner said "very few people, if any" knew about Uddin's TPIM, the revocation, or potential re-imposition.

In the absence of jurors, the coroner said there was much assessment by the state of Uddin's potential risk to others, but he had seen "nothing" showing any assessment of risks to him. He said there is a "paucity of support for people subject to TPIMs" and there is a potential risk to other people subjected to them.

For this reason, he added, he would be writing a preventing future deaths report.

There has been a trend towards TPIM subjects having mental health issues.

The independent reviewer of terrorism legislation, Jonathan Hall KC, has noted in previous reports that the "Home Office recognises poor mental health as a dominant feature amongst recent TPIM subjects" and that "poor mental health and neurodivergence (autism)" as being in evidence amongst them.

A government spokesperson said TPIMs were "a last resort to manage the risk posed by terrorists who cannot be prosecuted or deported" and are "carefully considered and strictly focused" on stopping a person's "involvement in terrorist activity".

The government was dealing with a prison crisis it "inherited", the spokesperson added, and was improving training to help staff "manage risks of self-harm and suicide".

title: 俄外交部：将对日本新的反俄措施采取对等反制
content:
俄罗斯外交部发言人扎哈罗娃5日在俄外交部网站发表评论说，俄方将对东京的不友好举措采取对等反制，首先针对那些对日本具有重要利益的领域。

title: King's funding for Andrew not to be used for legal action against police
content:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been told that the allowance given to him by King Charles should not be used to fund his legal action against Thames Valley Police and the Central Criminal Court.

The King uses his own private money to support his brother and to accommodate him on his estate in Sandringham.

But a royal source said that this funding should not be used for a legal challenge being launched by Mountbatten-Windsor against the search warrants issued ahead of his arrest in February.

The former Prince Andrew was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office in the wake of information that emerged from the Epstein files in the United States.

Mountbatten-Windsor has consistently denied any wrongdoing linked to his association with Epstein.

The former Prince Andrew is not a working royal - so Buckingham Palace no longer speaks on his behalf and is not involved in his legal battle.

But a royal source said the King's financial support for his brother should not be directed towards paying for the judicial review that Mountbatten-Windsor is seeking.

It's not been disclosed how much the King gives to Mountbatten-Windsor, but the funding for his brother was part of the arrangement when the former Prince Andrew was moved from his previous home at Royal Lodge in Windsor.

This allowance for Mountbatten-Windsor is not from the Sovereign Grant, which is the £138m in public funding for the monarchy.

It is drawn from the King's private money, which includes his income from the Duchy of Lancaster, private estates and his own investments and inheritances.

At the time of Mountbatten-Windsor's arrest, the King said the "law must take its course", and the Palace is now distancing itself from the former Duke of York's legal pushback.

Mountbatten-Windsor's lawyers are understood to be challenging Thames Valley Police and the Central Criminal Court over the lawfulness of warrants used for searches of Sandringham and Royal Lodge - in what has been Andrew's first public response since his arrest earlier this year.

Thames Valley Police has confirmed it is "engaged in legal proceedings in relation to warrants previously obtained from the Central Criminal Court".

It added: "As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further."

Mountbatten-Windsor, who lost his titles as a prince and Duke of York over his connections to the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, wants a judicial review to consider the legality of the search warrants.

A court hearing on Thursday afternoon will be part of Mountbatten-Windsor's bid to quash the warrants.

The warrants had been issued by a judge at the Central Criminal Court on 18 February - the day before Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested in Sandringham.

"Even if Andrew succeeds in having the search warrants quashed, that would not necessarily be the victory it might first appear," said Nick Vamos, a criminal lawyer at Peters & Peters and former head of special crime at the Crown Prosecution Service.

Vamos said disputes over warrants were not uncommon - but if the police lost on a technical error, they could still sometimes keep what they had obtained in a search.

"The police can apply back to the Crown Court to retain the material if they have grounds to immediately seize it again," said Vamos.

It would need to be a more fundamental issue with the granting of the warrants for the police to be required to return the material from a search, he said.

Mountbatten-Windsor's arrest, carried out on his 66th birthday, followed a series of revelations from the Epstein files, published by the US Department of Justice.

They included emails appearing to show official documents being shared by Mountbatten-Windsor with Epstein and others, at a time when he was the UK's trade envoy.

Mountbatten-Windsor had already been stripped of his titles by King Charles, after emails had shown Mountbatten-Windsor had continued his links with Epstein, beyond when he had publicly said connections had been severed.

After Mountbatten-Windsor's arrest he was taken to Aylsham police station. A photograph captured his departure later that day, looking exhausted, after he was released under investigation.

title: 这三张图表，有望重新点燃投资者对股市的信心

摩根大通 策略师米斯拉夫・马泰伊卡在研报中写道：“站在大盘整体角度，我们维持观点：一旦油价与利率的波动平息、9 月季节性低迷阶段过去，股市将重启上涨。10 月即将迎来大概率表现亮眼的第三季度财报，会进一步助推行情。科技股权重很高，如果科技板块走势转强，对大盘的带动作用会十分明显。”
以下是 Truist 投行的三张市场图表，传递出乐观信号。
图表一：估值完成回调重置 从估值角度看，当前股市并不算贵。 Truist 数据显示，标普 500 指数远期市盈率为 19 倍；自 6 月 2 日以来指数点位基本横盘。
图表二：盈利成为股价的核心驱动力 今年美国企业财报整体表现强劲。要说亮眼案例， 耐克 （NKE）就是代表。

title: 某艺人涉“台独”！零跑汽车紧急声明
content:
来源：车联新生态
10月4日晚，零跑汽车发布声明。零跑汽车表示，零跑汽车始终坚持一个中国原则，台湾是中国领土不可分割的一部分，坚决反对任何形式的“台独”分裂活动及一切伤害民族感情的言行。蔡康永仅为我司过往合作内容的参与艺人，并非零跑代言人。目前，我司已下线与其相关的全部内容，并保留追究相关方法律责任的权利。
事件导火索发生在 10月4日。 台湾主持人 蔡康永被现场直播镜头拍到，现身沈伯洋的台北市长竞选总部成立大会。他坐在会场前排，手持现场应援棒挥手。沈伯洋不是普通的参选政客，早在 2024年10月就被国台办列入“台独”顽固分子清单，2025年重庆警方已对其立案侦查，长期鼓吹分裂言论，操弄对抗议题。消息一经曝光，迅速引爆全网舆论。
面对 “站台台独” 质疑，蔡康永经纪人对外解释，到场只是计划采访两位台北市长候选人，前来了解候选人理念，并非站台支持 ， 但这套说辞难以平息大众不满。在顽固 “台独”分子的造势大会现场落座前排、挥舞应援道具，这样的行为在民族情感面前，很难简单用“采访调研”来解释。 据《汽车行业关注》 发现，蔡康永 已经 清空 了 自己微博全部内容，账号关注归零， 也侧面印证了相关性。
据了解，蔡康永于 1962年3月出生于中国台湾省台北市，祖籍浙江省宁波市，台湾东海大学外文系本科，美国加州大学洛杉矶分校电影电视研究所编导制作学硕士，中国台湾男主持人、作家、设计师、演员、编剧、导演。零跑汽车于9月8日发布官宣主持人蔡康永担任品牌挚友，联动《时尚芭莎》为全新车型D99打造宣传内容。
事件证明，无论代言人、品牌挚友还是短期嘉宾，只要公众人物参与品牌宣传，就会和品牌声誉深度绑定。立场问题不存在 “轻度合作就免责”的缓冲空间 ，任何触碰民族底线的行为，无论合作深浅， 都零容 忍、无例外。
目前，公司已下线与其相关的全部内容，并保留追究相关方法律责任的权利。《时尚芭莎》也删除九月刊蔡康永封面人物故事宣传微博。目前， 蔡康永的微博内容也设置半年可见，也取消了所有关注。

title: British Museum boss 'sorry' for Bayeux Tapestry visitor issues
content:
The head of the British Museum has apologised for the experience some visitors have had at its blockbuster Bayeux Tapestry exhibition.

The London institution has announced changes to how visitors see the historic work over concerns of overcrowding.

"Anyone that doesn't have a good experience, we're really sorry about that and we want to put it right," Nicholas Cullinan told the BBC's culture and media editor Katie Razzall.

The new plans include longer opening hours, an audio guide, additional seating and clearer signage.

Some people reported waits of up to two hours. Last week, hundreds of ticket holders were reportedly turned away due to backlogs when the museum closed early for a private event.

"You don't want anyone that comes to see it to have a bad experience, so our focus is very much on getting it right and learning lessons," Cullinan said.

"Obviously we want everyone that comes to have a fantastic experience. To put it into context, we're three weeks into the exhibition run. Next week, we'll hit our 100,000th visitor, which is a pretty extraordinary statistic. The vast number of visitors report having a very good experience."

Asked if the museum team had asked the embroidery's home museum in Bayeux for advice on queue management and timings, Cullinan said they had.

He also denied the museum had let too many people book tickets and said that the issues arose because visitors want to spend more time with the work than expected.

The problem "isn't just the interest, it's that people want to spend more time than anticipated. And that's a good thing. We want people to come and enjoy it, but it means we have to adjust accordingly and that's what we're doing," Cullinan said.

Some visitors have been spending longer than their allocated 40-minute slot viewing the tapestry, meaning others have to move through more quickly, he said.

While the museum is reimbursing those who have been turned away, when asked if they might also compensate people for travel costs, Cullinan said it was "a possibility", but added that "obviously this is an incredibly expensive exhibition to mount."

The exhibition has also faced some criticism over accessibility, but Cullinan said they had done "everything they could", given the stipulation that the tapestry had to be laid flat, making it more difficult for wheelchair users to see.

Demand for the exhibition has been high since tickets first went on sale in July, with a record 100,000 sold on the first day.

Members of the public who were not successful in the first ticket release will have two further chances to view the masterpiece when additional tickets go on sale in October and January.

Adult tickets cost £33 during peak times and £27 at off-peak hours, compared to the €12 (£10) fee to see the tapestry in its home in Bayeux, Normandy. Children under 16 can visit the London exhibition for free.

The 70m-long Bayeux Tapestry depicts 58 scenes outlining the extraordinary events surrounding the Norman conquest of England, the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and the end of Anglo-Saxon rule in Britain.

Despite its name, the work is an embroidery rather than a tapestry and contains approximately 626 human figures and 200 horses.

The Bayeux Tapestry is on loan from the French government, having been transported from its home in Normandy - where it has been exhibited since 1983. It will be on display until July 2027.

The loan marks the first time the tapestry has returned to the UK since it was created more than 900 years ago.

title: 花旗建议加码巴西风险资产 此前博索纳罗在首轮投票中表现强于预期

title: 沙特阿美CEO警告：全球石油供应“安全垫”已低得令人担忧
content:
来源：财联社
财联社10月6日讯（编辑 牛占林） 随着霍尔木兹海峡原油运输量回升，波斯湾产油国纷纷争夺市场份额。沙特阿美将11月运往欧洲的原油售价上调，但面向亚洲买家的原油售价折价幅度扩大至六年来最大。
据沙特阿美公布的价格表显示，沙特阿美将11月面向亚洲买家的阿拉伯轻质原油官方售价设定为较迪拜/阿曼基准价每桶低5美元，而10月的折价幅度为每桶2美元。
此次降价表明，作为全球最大石油出口商，沙特阿美可能正试图扩大对亚洲市场的原油销售，其他波斯湾产油国也在采取类似行动。与此同时，沙特阿美将11月面向欧洲客户的所有原油品级价格均上调每桶3美元，而对美国客户的原油价格则维持10月水平不变。
目前，沙特阿美正在利用阿曼湾附近的船对船转运方式，以降低伊朗袭击运油船只的风险。所谓船对船转运，是指先由较小型油轮在波斯湾装载原油，穿过霍尔木兹海峡后，再在阿曼附近海域将原油转装至等待接货的超大型原油运输船上。
与此同时，就在沙特阿美大幅降价、试图争夺市场份额之际，沙特国有石油公司负责人警告称，用于缓冲供应冲击的全球石油库存已经“低得令人担忧”。他表示，如果霍尔木兹海峡无法重新开放，石油市场面临的风险可能进一步加剧。
沙特阿美首席执行官阿明·纳赛尔周一在伦敦举行的能源情报论坛上发表上述言论。就在几天前，全球主要经济体政府宣布计划释放最多1亿桶应急石油和柴油库存，以缓解不断上涨的燃料成本。
纳赛尔当天表示：“在霍尔木兹海峡完全重新开放、市场信心恢复之前，现实情况是，油价两端的压力都将进一步加剧。”
他指出，尽管原油供应紧张的情况已经十分严重，但成品油价格的涨幅更加剧烈。
纳赛尔表示，全球原油消费仍在增长，未来至少两年，各国都将需要更多石油供应，以重建此前被消耗的库存。这意味着全球石油需求可能至少额外增加200万桶/日；如果各国政府决定进一步提高战略库存水平，新增需求甚至可能更高。
他补充说，美伊战争爆发时，全球石油库存约为100亿桶，如今已经降至不足60亿桶。其中，受各种技术限制，实际上能够动用的库存仅占约10%。
这一说法与摩根大通分析师Natasha Kaneva今年5月的警告相呼应。
纳赛尔表示，释放剩余全球库存中的一部分，可以为各国经济争取一些时间，但无法解决供需之间的失衡。
他指出，海湾产油国正在努力提高石油产量和出口量，目前已经成功将原油运输量提升至接近战前水平。
沙特、阿联酋和科威特等海湾国家一直在使用自有油轮，通过霍尔木兹海峡运输原油。自2月底美国和以色列袭击伊朗、引发地区战争以来，霍尔木兹海峡一直处于至少部分受阻的状态。
尽管原油运输量有所回升，但对石油市场的缓解作用十分有限。市场仍在计入波斯湾和红海地区供应面临的安全风险，国际基准布伦特原油过去一个月一直徘徊在每桶100美元左右。
与此同时，更多油轮虽然开始通过霍尔木兹海峡，但船只也不得不承担遭遇袭击风险上升的代价，而沙特过去一个月还多次成为袭击目标。
不过，纳赛尔表示，沙特阿美目前所有上游产能均保持完好。这使公司能够继续履行与欧洲和亚洲客户签订的供应合同。
他声称，沙特阿美一直在利用不同出口路线、调整不同原油品级之间的供应分配，并调动自有油轮，以确保向客户供货。
纳赛尔表示，沙特阿美正在寻找替代性原油出口路线，以避免过度依赖任何单一运输方式将原油运往全球买家，但他没有透露具体方案。此外，他还表示，公司正在研究将储油设施容量扩大至目前两倍甚至三倍的计划。
（财联社 牛占林）
