"I don't need to say I think it's gone," Russell said, "but, of course, it's exceptionally unlikely and that's just the reality.

"I knew if I wanted to come back, I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I had luck not on my side.

"So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if it was on the other side it would have been an 18-point gain. So it's a real shame, but that's just how it is."

It's not the first time an engine problem has robbed Russell of big points this year.

"You've almost got to laugh," he said. "I'm beyond disappointment. It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame. Of course, but just keep on fighting."

But Antonelli has had his reliability issues, too, and to about the same level.

The reality, as Russell has acknowledged many times, is that Antonelli has been the better performer on balance this year - as he was again in Malaysia after his off weekend in Baku - and he will deserve the title when it comes.

title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
content:
US murderer Christa Pike remains critically ill in hospital and her prognosis is still unclear following her failed execution, her lawyer has said on Sunday.

Speaking to CNN on Sunday morning, Pike's lawyer Stephen Ferrell said doctors were still trying to clear two doses of pentobarbital from her body.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

She survived two execution attempts on Wednesday, and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee.

Ferrell said: "She's still in the hospital, on a ventilator, critically ill, we really don't know the prognosis yet, and may not know for several days."

He didn't believe she had regained consciousness at any point, adding that he has been receiving updates through her medical power of attorney rather than consulting directly with doctors.

He has not been in to see her. "She is guarded. I'm not sure who may have seen her," he said.

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. But Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year - and the head of prisons in the state said he would resign on Saturday.

"If she recovers - she may not fully recover - and there may be issues about her competence. I mean, we just don't know any of this," Ferrell said. "We have had no discussions about this. The Tennessee attorney general's office so far has not given us any indications of what their intentions will be."

He called on the governor to commute her death sentence to a life sentence "at the very least". "She has endured a torturous attempt at executing her," he said. "She's spent over 30 years in prison, most of that in solitary confinement."

"We don't know right now - and we may never know - what sort of torture she endured during [her failed execution]."

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.

She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

Slemmer's mother May Martinez travelled to Nashville for the execution, which moved ahead despite last-minute legal challenges.

Martinez, who supported Pike's death sentence, told local news outlet WJXX that she "broke down in tears" after finding out it was not successful.

"I think that the state owes me a big apology," she said.

The state's Department of Correction has defended the use of lethal injections, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Pike's lawyers previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

title: Indian police accused of sexual harassment against journalists at protest
content:
Three female journalists have accused police officers in India of sexual harassment during street protests in the capital Delhi.

The claims were made on Saturday after the force detained scores of young people calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner.

In a post on social media, Delhi Police said its New Delhi District had received the complaint, and it had been transferred to its crime branch for a "fair and impartial" inquiry.

Thousands of protesters gathered in Delhi and Mumbai cities for a third day on Sunday demanding that Gyanesh Kumar step down over large-scale changes to voter rolls.

The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.

Videos online show people being physically dragged away from the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi.

The accusations by the women journalists include inappropriate touching by some police.

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said women fear for their safety and the home ministry must "answer for this".

"Police dragged me by my hair," Aahna Singh, an activist and student at Jawaharlal Nehru University told Reuters news agency during the protests.

She said the police were resorting to "brutality".

The Press Club of India has demanded immediate action on the complaints against police officers, saying it was "shocked and dismayed" by the treatment of journalists.

"Behaviour of this kind cannot be normalised in a democracy. Journalists must be allowed to work freely, without fear, and document those who gather to raise various issues," it said in a statement.

The protesters say the voter-roll revision will benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries.

It says the last revision was done nearly a quarter of a century ago and the voters' list needs to be updated to account for those who have died, left the country or are registered in more than one place as they've moved to a new address.

But the exercise has been mired in controversy from the start with the opposition parties accusing Kumar of manipulating voters' list to favour the BJP during elections. Both the BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the accusations.

The protesters have included supporters of the influential Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that began as an online satirical movement.

The pressure group recorded its first major victory in July when it forced the then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign after weeks of protests calling for education reforms.

The CJP called for the latest protest after a report in The Indian Express, external said that Kumar's two fellow election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had formally objected at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders they said had been issued without their knowledge.

The differences were reported to be mostly over the controversial revision of the country's electoral rolls known as the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, which began last year.

The Election Commission has defended its way of working and said in a statement that "differing views" were part of the "decision-making process" and that all the decisions were taken unanimously.

But the revelations sparked a furore, with opposition leaders demanding Kumar's resignation.

title: 环球一周展望：美欧央行纪要料凸显通胀忧虑 惟加息紧迫性已降温
content:
在美国9月份就业数据疲软、法国金融市场压力急剧上升之后，美联储和欧洲央行决策者在本月会议上连续第二个月加息的紧迫性已经下降。
未来几天，两家央行都将公布上月政策会议的纪要。当时，它们都因担忧通胀压力不断上升而提高了基准利率。
在美国，稳健的经济增长一直在支撑就业市场，使美联储可以把注意力集中在通胀上。美联储9月份会议纪要将于周三公布，内容可能显示，许多决策者当时非常担忧核心价格走势，并预计年底前至少还会再加息一次。
不过，周五公布的最新数据显示就业增长低于预期，工资增速也较为疲弱，这进一步表明，劳动力市场并未加剧现有的通胀压力。当周早些时候，美联储青睐的价格指标经过修正后显示，今年通胀低于此前认为的程度。
经济研究的观点
“10月份加息的门槛如今已经很高。即使会议纪要提醒市场，美联储官员9月份的立场有多么鹰派，此后公布的数据也增强了保持耐心的理由。服务通胀持续顽固，可能会让12月份加息的选项继续存在，但美联储在再次收紧政策之前，可能需要看到更明确的证据表明价格压力已经重新抬头。”
—Anna Wong， Andrew Sacher和Eliza Winger．
此外，两名资深的利率决策者——美联储副主席菲利普·杰斐逊和纽约联储行长约翰·威廉姆斯——相隔两天分别发出明确信号，显示他们认为美联储没有迫切需要再次采取行动。投资者也因此降低了对加息的预期。
美联储官员将于10月27日至28日开会，距离竞争激烈的中期选举仅有数日，这可能使会议结果笼罩上党派政治色彩。
周四，欧洲央行将公布9月9日至10日会议纪要，投资者将寻找有关下一次加息时点的线索。
在欧元区，最新数据显示，9月份通货膨胀加剧且超过预期，主要原因是战争推高了能源成本。尽管价格压力仍然偏高，投资者认为欧洲央行10月份加息的可能性很低。
债券市场压力已经蔓延至全球，其中法国受到的冲击尤其严重。该国议会严重分裂加剧了市场对预算和赤字问题的担忧。
此外，加拿大的失业和贸易数据将显示该国与美国关税战的影响。约十几个国家的央行将宣布利率，预计印度、肯尼亚和秘鲁将加息。
亚洲
一大关注焦点将是印度央行周三的利率决定。经济学家预计，印度央行将把回购利率提高至5.5%，加入日本、澳大利亚和美国收紧政策的行列。
澳大利亚西 太平洋 银行周一将公布消费者信心数据，预计将显示，在最近的加息后，消费者信心进一步下降。
日本周二将公布8月份工资数据，市场将重点关注实际工资是否连续第八个月上涨。
泰国和菲律宾未来一周将公布消费者价格数据，预计三地9月份通胀都出现加速。
未来一周期间，一系列国家和地区将公布外汇储备数据，其中韩国最值得关注，以观察其高额的贸易顺差带来的资金是否体现在相关数据中。印度和泰国也将公布相关数据。
欧洲
法国的财政问题可能继续成为焦点，这也将使市场把注意力投向被视为潜在“救火队员”的欧洲央行。
按预定日程将公开露面的利率决策者包括欧洲央行首席经济学家Philip Lane、奥地利央行行长Martin Kocher以及比利时的Pierre Wunsch。欧洲央行9月份会议纪要将于周四公布，也将受到密切关注。
围绕欧洲央行新任官员人选的角力正在加剧。国际清算银行负责人Pablo Hernandez de Cos以及荷兰央行前行长Klaas Knot将于周一出席同一场活动。两人都是接替欧洲央行行长克里斯蒂娜·拉加德的竞争人选。
据知情人士透露，德国总理弗里德里希·默茨计划与两名候选人会面，与Knot的会面在未来几天。
欧元区财长周四在卢森堡开会时，可能开始讨论欧洲央行执行理事会成员Isabel Schnabel的继任者人选。由于法国债券市场动荡，这次会议也将受到密切关注。
欧元区数据方面的重点包括多项制造业数据。从周二开始，德国将连续公布工厂订单、工业生产和出口数据。法国、西班牙和意大利也将陆续公布工业生产数据。
当周晚些时候，欧盟贸易专员Maros Sefcovic访问北京时，欧洲工业面临的挑战也将成为关注焦点。
央行官员的讲话可能成为英国方面的一大看点，该国也正面临自身的债券市场挑战。共有五名官员将公开露面，其中包括周四出席活动的英国央行行长安德鲁·贝利。

title: 软银集团孙正义罕见地就AI安全风险表达担忧 呼吁各国携手应对威胁
content:
软银集团领导人孙正义是人工智能最坚定的信奉者之一，但即便是他也表示，随着机器正迅速获得更多能力，他对安全风险感到担忧。
孙正义周日在京都举行的“科技与社会”论坛期间的一场活动上表示，人工智能的能力呈指数级增长，这就要求各国必须建立互信，才能共同驾驭这项技术。他当时与白宫科技政策顾问Michael Kratsios一同发言。
孙正义说：“我们已经没有让人类彼此争斗的奢侈选项了，” 各国需要携手合作来控制强大人工智能模型所带来的更大威胁。他表示，如果超级智能落入错误的人手中，可能会变得“超级危险”。
对于孙正义而言，发出上述警告实属罕见，也反映出最近几个月人工智能模型发生令人不安的安全事故后外界担忧不断加剧。这位69岁的日本亿万富豪已将软银近650亿美元的资金投入ChatGPT开发商OpenAI，多年来也一直在宣扬人工智能带来投资回报和帮助人类的能力。
Kratsios当时到访京都是为了宣布一项由美国牵头的涵盖17国的合作计划，旨在更好地利用人工智能来加快科学研究。包括日本、韩国、英国、德国、新加坡和阿联酋在内的多国代表与Kratsios一同登台见证了这一时刻。

title: 沙特支持的也门部队发动全面攻势 试图夺回胡塞武装控制区
content:
在伊朗支持的胡塞武装与沙特阿拉伯之间的冲突升级数周后，也门获国际承认的政府发起全面军事行动，试图夺回胡塞武装控制的所有地区。
也门总统领导委员会主席Rashad Al-Alimi周日在一次公开讲话中表示，也门军队所有军种均接到命令开始行动，将战斗到“直至将国家从恐怖主义的胡塞武装分子的手中解放出来”。
自9月初以来，由沙特领导、包括也门部队在内的联合部队一直在与胡塞武装进行地面和空中战斗。当时，胡塞武装发动新一轮攻势，占领了也门西海岸的战略要地。
此举加强了胡塞武装对曼德海峡的控制。这条狭窄水道位于红海与亚丁湾之间，是一个咽喉要道，沙特阿拉伯一直利用这里出口石油，从而绕开霍尔木兹海峡。
胡塞武装基本上没有参与2月底爆发的美以对伊朗战争，但在7月份宣布封锁沙特船只，以回应其所称的对也门的“围困”。此后，胡塞武装多次袭击沙特，包括以该国石油设施为目标，给这个全球最大的原油出口国带来更多挑战。
周五报道称，沙特阿拉伯一直在筹划针对胡塞武装的攻势，行动将由也门地面部队主导，并得到沙特空中力量支持。
Al-Alimi周日表示：“从这一刻起，所有的国家军事、安全和民事机构都进入动员和高度戒备状态，直至任务完成并取得胜利。”

title: Green Party members back 'Zionism is racism' motion
content:
Green Party members have adopted a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism, in a move that has divided senior figures at the top of the party.

The party's joint deputy leaders have been at odds over the subject, with Mothin Ali backing the move, and Rachel Millward describing the wording as "problematic".

Activists endorsed the policy motion, which was put forward by a group of members at the party's conference in Brighton, by 1022 votes to 813.

Discussion about the vote has dominated the conference, and exposed divisions between the party's newly enlarged membership base under leader Zack Polanski and its MPs elected at the last election.

The motion adopted by Green members defines Zionism as an ideology in support of "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".

"The real, material, manifestation of Zionism has been the historic and ongoing dehumanisation, displacement, dispossession, disenfranchisement and destruction of Palestinians," it says.

It has attracted criticism from some Jewish groups, including the Board of Deputies and the Jewish Leadership Council.

In a letter to the party sent ahead of the vote, the organisations said Zionism was an anti-racist movement, adding that "modern Zionism was formed in part as a response to antisemitism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it."

It also raised concerns about the safety of Jewish members in the Green Party, as well as the implications for Jewish institutions in areas represented by the Greens.

Debate about the motion, as well as the conflict in Gaza, has featured heavily during the conference, which is taking place after a surge in its membership in the wake of Polanski's election as leader in September last year.

Speaking after the vote, Lubna Speitan, the Green member behind the motion, argued its backers wanted to voice opposition to "racist systems of oppression".

"We stand united against all forms of racism and discrimination - no exemptions," she added.

Polanski himself did not vote in the debate, having left the conference early to campaign in Holborn and St Pancras, where he is standing to be the MP. A full list of candidates in the contest can be found here.

Asked about the motion on Friday, Polanski said: "If your Zionism is the displacement of the Palestinian people then that is clearly racist, and I say that as a Jewish leader of a British political party."

However, he said he wanted to see the reference to a single Palestinian state changed, arguing: "I don't believe we as a Green Party of England and Wales, or even the British government, should be deciding what the future settlement looks like."

He had also said he wanted to see the motion amended to specify that it should not be used to discipline Jewish members attending synagogues that consider themselves Zionist.

However, both amendments favoured by Polanski were rejected by Green members.

A Green spokeswoman insisted the party would protect Jewish members - and they would not be persecuted for attending synagogues which defined themselves as Zionist.

Speaking after the motion had been approved, chair of Jewish Greens Vivien Lichtenstein told the BBC she could consider her future in the party.

Polanski has not specified whether he supports the motion passed by members, but added his name to a joint statement from the party's five MPs and deputy leaders issued after the vote.

The statement pledged to ensure the Green Party was "an anti-racist party in every way" and added that there was "no conflict between supporting the rights of Palestinians and the rights of Jewish people".

Over the course of the three-day conference, key figures in the party have expressed differing positions about the Zionism motion.

Four of the party's five MPs - Ellie Chowns, Adrian Ramsay and Carla Denyer, Sian Berry - had publicly opposed it, with Denyer arguing it could risk "alienating a significant proportion of Jewish people".

Chowns, as well as former Green Party leader Caroline Lucas, both spoke against the motion during the debate.

Addressing members, Lucas said: "I urge you not to support the over-simplification at the heart of this motion - a refusal to accept complexities which is leading to so many Jewish members feeling scared and unwelcome in our party."

Deputy leader Mothin Ali, who had expressed support for the motion before the vote, said it was calling for "a state that's democratic, that guarantees the rights of every single person living on that land".

He added that he was "absolutely not" calling all Jewish people who define themselves as Zionists racist.

Following the vote, Israel's Foreign Ministry said the motion went beyond "the boundaries of legitimate political debate" and was "a stain on the history of the United Kingdom".

Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

The Conservatives criticised the motion, saying it demonstrated the Green Party was "toxic to its core".

Labour chair Bridget Phillipson said the vote "crosses a line" and called on Polanski to "make clear that this will not be their position moving forwards".

"It is shameful to vote against a two-state solution for Israel and Palestine and to condemn the vast majority of British Jews and Jews around the world as racist for supporting Israel's right to exist," she added.

Liberal Democrat MP Luke Taylor said the motion did not address "the rising threats" of Islamophobia and antisemitism in the UK.

He added: "This is a divisive motion that pours fuel on the fire of tensions in the UK, and will leave many British Jews feeling less safe."

title: 苹果新任CEO特努斯上任即亲掌设计，10月密集推新品对冲服务业务放缓
content:
苹果 新任首席执行官John Ternus上任头几周将设计列为优先事项。此外，除了触摸屏和转向OLED技术外，苹果改版后的MacBook Pro还有另一项重大变化。最后，该公司即将发布新的智能家居中枢、HomePod mini和搭载Siri AI的Apple TV。
苹果首席执行官John Ternus将大量时间用于监督公司的硬件和软件设计工作。在早期讨论由John Ternus接替Tim Cook出任苹果首席执行官时，这位较年轻的高管曾质疑自己是否能胜任这一挑战。“我不像你，”Ternus对Cook说。“你做了那么多了不起的事。”Cook以他一贯不动声色的语气回答：“我知道你不像我。”他的意思是，Ternus需要做他自己。Ternus在向员工讲述这段经历时，将其描述为一个转折点。Ternus说，Cook的话“确实引起了我的共鸣，并让我铭记在心”，即他在担任首席执行官期间，把时间花在能为苹果“创造最大价值”的地方。“而我需要把时间花在能为苹果创造最大价值的地方。”他说，这一理念让Ternus得以以不同方式对待这一角色。“我们在时间分配上会有差异，但使命和目标是相同的。”
在担任首席执行官期间，Cook将大部分时间花在运营、销售、财务战略和苹果供应链上。他还经常处理公共政策、隐私问题，以及公司与白宫和世界各国政府的关系。Ternus则是从硬件工程师一路晋升，他正在设定明显不同的优先事项。他基本上将公司的财务运营交给首席财务官Kevan Parekh，将供应链交给首席运营官Sabih Khan。相反，Ternus花大量时间与首席硬件官Johny Srouji和硬件工程负责人Tom Marieb在一起，深入参与产品工程。但我获悉，他还将大量精力投入到另一个长期缺乏单一最高负责人的领域：设计。
自Jony Ive于2019年离职以来，苹果一直缺乏一位统一负责工业设计——即硬件的外观和质感——以及人机界面设计——即塑造公司软件的设计——的设计主管。在随后的几年里，工业设计和人机界面设计各有负责人，而不是由一位高管统一管理这两个团队。他们最终向时任首席运营官Jeff Williams汇报。Williams是一位没有设计背景的制造专家，他之所以被选中负责该部门，很大程度上是因为他与Cook关系密切。当Williams去年退休时，这一安排发生了变化。尽管Cook在新闻稿中宣布，Williams离职后设计团队将直接向他汇报——表面上的确如此——但实际上他们开始向Ternus汇报。作为最终过渡到首席执行官的一部分，Cook将设计职责交给了他。在4月至9月的首席执行官过渡期间，苹果的设计负责人实际上是Ternus在Cook卸任前唯一的直接下属。
作为苹果硬件工程负责人，Ternus已经在一定程度上参与了设计工作室的工作，因为这两个职能需要密切协调。然而，自担任首席执行官以来，他已深入参与工业设计和人机界面团队。几位熟悉该部门的人士称，他每周都会多次亲临工作室，有时一天会去好几次。当然，Steve Jobs在与Ive合作期间也以类似方式直接参与设计。但Ternus的参与标志着与Cook时代的重大转变。设计师们称，Cook通常每月最多去工作室一次，每次约一小时。
Ternus的首要任务之一是恢复设计工作室在公司内部的地位。该团队曾有大量员工流失，去了Ive的公司LoveFrom，以及OpenAI的硬件团队和其他公司。这导致其在苹果内部的影响力和可信度下降。人员流失迫使公司提拔初级设计师，并从外部大量招聘以补充团队。苹果长期负责软件设计的Alan Dye跳槽去了Meta Platforms Inc．。Ive的工业设计主管继任者Evans Hankey也离开了，最终加入了OpenAI。Hankey后来由Molly Anderson接替，Anderson在更广泛的设计界知名度较低，在2024年成为工业设计副总裁之前，从未在苹果管理过如此规模的团队。到那时，该团队许多最资深的成员已经离开，缩小了苹果内部候选人的范围，使Anderson成为唯一现实的内部人选。
鉴于设计在苹果产品开发以及为未来设备构思创意中的核心作用，公司内部和接近公司许多人士认为，苹果应该从外部招聘一位首席设计官来统管整个组织。但我获悉，目前并没有进行这样的搜寻。相反，苹果在iPhone Duo发布期间做出了重大努力，将Anderson和Dye的继任者Steve Lemay塑造为其设计负责人。Ternus与Anderson以及新手机合影，而Anderson和Lemay在一段联合视频中帮助介绍了该设备。该公司还在继续重建其工业设计团队，上周聘用了比利时家具设计师Julien Renault。但这一切都没有消除由一位领导者统一管理工业设计和软件设计的需要，就像苹果在Ive时代那样。随着Ternus将设计列为重大优先事项并在该部门发挥如此积极的作用，他似乎已经选定了苹果新的设计领导者和最终决策者：他自己。放弃从设计界外部招聘是否是正确选择，仍有待观察。Ternus出身工程领域，而非传统设计背景，但首席执行官的密切参与至少确保设计再次在苹果高管层中拥有有意义的一席之地——并在公司最重要的产品决策中拥有强有力的发言权。
苹果的触摸屏和OLED MacBook Pro还有一项新变化。今年苹果还有更多我们已经知道的产品即将推出。iPhone Duo于10月23日发货，而带显示屏的新智能家居中枢、更新的Apple TV机顶盒和新款HomePod mini——均旨在展示Siri AI——距离发布不到两周。但还有两款产品将紧随其后：一次重大的MacBook Pro改版，首次将OLED和触摸屏技术引入Mac；以及首款OLED iPad mini。新款iPad mini预计在10月底至11月间的某个时候发布，是一次重大但直接的升级：更好的屏幕、更快的芯片，以及横向放置的FaceTime摄像头，使其与苹果其他iPad保持一致。更高端的MacBook Pro则是更大的看点。转向触摸屏意义重大，采用OLED——即有机发光二极管——同样如此，OLED可提供更锐利的对比度。macOS Golden Gate也有支持触摸输入和灵动岛的变化。但我获悉，还有另一项重大差异：新款MacBook Pro更轻——明显更轻。苹果重新设计了机器内部结构，将部件小型化并重新排列组件，使电脑更便于携带。目前的16英寸MacBook Pro重达4.8磅，而15英寸MacBook Air为3.3磅，因此任何有意义的减重都会立即被察觉。我预计这些目前正在用macOS 27.2测试的机器将在下个月前上市。
苹果新的智能家居中枢将与 亚马逊 的Echo Show竞争。苹果计划于10月13日举行活动，发布其期待已久的带屏幕智能家居中枢、新款HomePod mini和更新的Apple TV。这三款设备都将以Siri AI为核心。首席执行官John Ternus正寻求加快产品开发、削减成本、抵消服务业务放缓的影响，力求让这家iPhone制造商更快、更精简。

title: US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
content:
A US Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan, local officials say.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the crime as a "brutal and heinous" robbery and murder. She said she had urged the US to "enforce stricter discipline" of its personnel.

Japan's public broadcaster NHK identified the victim as Yagi Anna, 39, and the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who is stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma.

"We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine," the Marine Corps said on social media, extending condolences to the victim's family.

Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said the woman's body was discovered early Saturday morning in a hotel in Naha City, the capital of the Okinawa prefecture.

"Such an incident is utterly inexcusable and fills me with strong indignation," Koizumi wrote on social media, adding that "incidents and accidents involving U.S. military personnel cause significant anxiety to the local community and must never occur".

The US Embassy in Tokyo said that it was fully cooperating with the Japanese government and local police. Japan's foreign ministry said it summoned US ambassador George Glass to discuss the incident on Sunday.

Okinawa is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops.

Okinawa Governor Genta Koja says the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline.

"The fact that this kind of event has happened again leaves us no choice but to conclude that the US military's efforts in maintaining discipline, educating personnel, and other such measures are completely ineffective," he said.

title: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
content:
The head of Yemen's internationally recognised government has announced it will wage an all out war in an effort to take all territory held by the Houthis.

It follows an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in recent days.

The Iran-backed group said it had struck sites belonging to Saudi national oil company Aramco, in response to what it described as 50 Saudi-led coalition strikes in 12 hours. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment.

The Yemeni government's fierce statement was expected after the Houthis' offensive last month, which saw them seize control of the country's coastline, including the vital shipping lane of the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

On Sunday, Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address: "Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory."

Yemen's capital, Sanaa, which has been held by the Houthis for more than a decade, has come under sustained attack as government forces try to weaken the group's military capabilities.

Attacks on the Houthis have also spread across Yemen, including to the Saada region, the group's northern heartland.

But security sources say the Iran-backed Houthis have continued to make gains.

The frontline in Yemen remains focused around the key city of Taiz, which is still controlled by the internationally recognised government.

On Sunday, the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking Taiz with Aden, the interim capital of the Yemeni government, AFP news agency reports.

Citing three Yemeni military sources, AFP also reports that the Houthis now control the area and supply route, effectively encircling Taiz.

"They've achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven't fully taken control of it," Farea Al-Muslimi, a research fellow at the Chatham House think tank, told AFP.

Al-Alimi was unlikely to have made the fierce announcement without the green light from Saudi Arabia, which remains the key backer of his government.

Saudi Arabia has been under constant attack as the Houthis try to target the country's economic lifeblood - oil.

On Sunday, Yemen's Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had launched a ballistic missile and drone attack on Aramco sites in the capital, Riyadh, and the oil-rich Khurais area in the kingdom's east.

"Both operations successfully achieved their objectives," the spokesman said in a statement. "The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites."

It is not the first time the group has said it has hit Saudi oil sites. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment on Sunday's claimed attack, but has previously dismissed some claims as misleading, mocking the Houthis for "chasing imaginary victories".

But it has once again shown the price Saudi Arabia - and, as a consequence, the global economy - could pay if it launched a new all-out war against the Houthis.

In retaliation, Saudi Arabia has also been striking Houthi targets, according to the Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV channel. It said at least two people had been wounded in strikes on Sunday.

On Saturday, Yemen's government also said its forces had hit Houthi targets across the country, including in Sanaa, Saada and the group's positions near Taiz in the south-west.

Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis.

A war erupted in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital city from the Saudi-backed government, before going on to take control of swathes of the country's north.

Riyadh intervened in the war the following year, leading an international coalition.

After several years of relative calm, the war reignited in July amid the widening conflict in the Middle East.

Last month, a lightning offensive enabled the Houthis to seize the country's entire Red Sea coast, stopping Saudi Arabia from using it as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.

The strategy benefited the Houthis' main sponsor, Iran. But it has also forced Saudi Arabia back into direct military confrontation with the Houthis.

title: OPEC+主要成员国同意11月维持产量目标不变
content:
OPEC+主要成员国同意下个月维持产量配额不变，与此同时中东冲突继续导致该联盟相当大一部分石油生产陷入停滞。
OPEC在一份声明中表示，由沙特阿拉伯和俄罗斯牵头的七个成员国组成的小组于周日举行了月度视频会议，将在11月维持产量目标不变。这与其目前的产量政策路线图相符。
根据周日的声明，这个七国小组将于11月1日再次举行线上会议，届时可能敲定12月份的计划。

title: 余承东回应误发“余总转发文案”：没想到工作备注比正文还抢镜
content:
新浪科技讯 10月4日晚间消息，10月3日，华为常务董事、产品投资评审委员会主任、终端BG董事长余承东在微博转发鸿蒙智行宣传内容，文案中却出现“余总转发文案”字样，疑似将工作人员发送的提醒一并发出。
随后，有网友发现，余承东微博删除相关文案后重新发布。“余承东微博代运营”等话题登上热搜。
对此，10月4日下午，余承东在微博评论区回应称：“没想到，工作备注比正文还抢镜，已改，谢谢大家提醒！祝大家假期愉快，出行平安！”

title: Family of teenager killed in crash to sue acquitted driver
content:
The family of a teenager killed in a car crash near Stirling two years ago are launching a civil case against the driver who was cleared of causing death by careless driving.

Kyle Marshall, 19, and Jayden McConnell, 17, died when a car driven by Charles Gray spun out of control and into the path of a lorry on the A91 near Bannockburn Interchange in March 2024.

Gray, who had passed his test a month earlier, was acquitted of causing the deaths of his two friends after a five-day trial at Stirling Sheriff Court last November.

According to the Scottish Sun,, external the Marshall family are now suing Gray for a six-figure sum, alleging negligence.

A spokesman for Digby Brown, the law firm representing the Marshall family, confirmed: "A civil action has now been raised in the Court of Session on behalf of the loved ones of Kyle to help them secure answers, support and recognition.

"It would be inappropriate to comment further at this time however we will continue to support the Marshall family during this time."

The trial heard that Gray, who was 17 at the time of the crash, had lost control of the Vauxhall Corsa on a wet Sunday afternoon, on a stretch of road known as "greasy corner" because it had a reputation for becoming slippery.

Soon after leaving a roundabout, the car spun onto the opposite side of the carriageway and was hit by a heavy tipper lorry coming in the other direction.

Kyle Marshall and Jayden McConnell, in the rear of the vehicle, were killed while Gray's then girlfriend, Lauryn Moir, who was in the front passenger seat, survived without serious injury.

Gray himself was initially not breathing but an ambulance crew, who were passing the crash scene by chance, opened his airway, saving his life.

He was very badly injured with a ruptured spleen, spine damage and a brain injury.

Often choking back tears during his evidence, he said he could remember nothing of the crash itself and only learned what had happened to his friends when he woke up from an induced coma four weeks later.

The trial heard that analysis of an insurance company "black box" showed that Gray had been a "perfect driver" in the weeks before the collision.

The court was also told that police had not tested how slippery the road was or carried out a number of checks that might have established if there was a fault with the vehicle.

title: Wales' Elfyn Evans wins his first World Rally Championship
content:
Elfyn Evans became Britain's first world rally champion for 25 years after rival Oliver Solberg crashed in a highly dramatic finish to the season in Italy.

Sweden's Solberg was on course to snatch the lead on the final stage of the last round of the World Rally Championship, and thereby deny Evans the title.

But Solberg lost control of his car with less than 100 metres to go of the Rally Italia Sardegna, which meant the glory went to Welshman Evans, a five-time runner-up in the championship.

"It hasn't sunk in," said a shocked Evans.

"I was sure it was over. I feel for Oliver - he had an incredible weekend. I don't know what to say."

The 37-year-old and co-driver Scott Martin had led for much of the 2026 season and took a 21-point advantage into the final round in Sardinia.

But that gap had shrunk to a solitary point by the time the drivers lined up for the last of 17 stages, bringing back painful memories of previous narrow misses for Evans.

Solberg, 25, needed only to beat his Toyota team-mate in the final stage to claim enough bonuses to be champion, but he crashed two corners from the finish.

Evans becomes only the third British man to win the WRC title after Colin McRae in 1995 and Richard Burns in 2001.

Solberg, whose father Petter won the WRC title in 2003, won the rally by almost a minute ahead of nine-time world champion Sebastien Ogier.

He and English co-driver Elliott Edmondson were also on course to win the final stage and collect a maximum 35 points for the weekend to take the title by two points.

However, his crash meant he finished five points behind Evans in the overall standings.

A third Toyota driver, Sami Pajari, finished a further one point behind in third - having seen his own title challenge evaporate on the final weekend.

An inconsolable Solberg remained in his car for some time at the end of the stage before being encouraged to take to the podium by Gazoo Racing team principal Jari-Matti Latvala and team-mate Ogier.

"Two corners, two corners," said an emotional Solberg.

"First congratulations to Elfyn, he has been very consistent all season. That I even had a shot after my rollercoaster of a season is incredible.

"I tried everything. I knew I was pushing but didn't know if it was enough. I pushed even more and I couldn't save the car. I tried my very best."

Evans, from Dolgellau in north Wales, had previously missed out on the title on the final day three times and in two of those seasons he had taken a lead into the concluding rally before losing out to Ogier in 2020 and 2025.

"I don't really know what my reaction is. It's surreal with how it happened. It's a relief," he said.

"It wouldn't by my proudest way of winning it, but it's job done."

For Toyota sporting director Kaj Lindstrom there were mixed feelings.

"That was the hardest thing. The ending was quite something, I didn't expect it," said the Finn.

"It was a good fight and we all saw that Oliver was all or nothing. It held all the way to the end.

"Oliver still has time but Elfyn finally got his title so we're really happy for him."

The WRC season was reduced to 13 rounds when the Saudi Arabia event, originally planned for next month, was cancelled because of the ongoing unrest in the Middle East.

Rally Italia Sardegna marked the end of Jon Armstrong's rookie season at the top level of WRC, and he produced his best result when finishing seventh.

"It's been good to have a clean weekend with a strong result," said the M-Sport Ford driver.

"It's not been an easy year and this was a rally to show we can put it together. A big thanks to everyone who has been supporting us, it's been a great year and it's been a privilege to drive this car."

Armstrong's team-mate and fellow Irishman Josh McErlean did not fare as well despite running as high as sixth on Saturday before retiring after a collision with a tree.

He also had to stop twice on Sunday before finishing well off the pace but claimed ninth spot in the championship.

title: British Museum announces changes to ease Bayeux Tapestry queues
content:
The British Museum has announced changes to how visitors see the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition after concerns over long queues and overcrowding.

The measures include plans for longer opening hours, as well as an audio guide, additional seating and clearer signage.

A museum spokesperson said the public response to the 11th Century embroidery had been "extraordinary", but acknowledged that some visitors had waited longer than they would have wanted.

Some people reported waits of up to two hours, while hundreds of ticket holders were reportedly turned away due to backlogs when the museum closed early last week due to a private event.

Some ticket holders took to social media to complain about the disruption.

One disappointed visitor said the trip had been a "big event" they had looked forward to, while another wrote she had been waiting since she was seven to see the Bayeux Tapestry, and bought tickets only to be turned away after queuing.

The museum later apologised to those who had been unable to enter and said they would be issued refunds and priority booking slots for a rearranged time.

From Monday, visitors will be offered an audio guide with more information about the embroidery, while additional signage and seating will be provided for those queuing to reach the main exhibition.

The museum said it planned to introduce longer opening hours to prevent queues building during the day and allow people with later bookings more time to view the exhibition.

Details of the extended hours have not yet been disclosed.

Demand for the exhibition has been high since tickets first went on sale in July, with a record 100,000 sold on the first day.

Members of the public who were not successful in the first ticket release will have two further chances to view the masterpiece when further tickets go on sale in October and January.

Adult tickets cost £33 during peak times and £27 at off-peak hours, compared with its usual €12 (£10) fee to see the tapestry in its home in Bayeux, Normandy. Children under 16 can visit the London exhibition for free.

The exhibition opened on 10 September but has experienced a series of problems with queues and congestion, with some visitors spending longer than their allocated 40-minute slot viewing the tapestry.

Visitors were later stopped from taking photographs and a recorded message was introduced encouraging people to continue moving through the one-way exhibition.

The 70m-long Bayeux Tapestry depicts 58 scenes outlining the extraordinary events surrounding the Norman conquest of England, the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and the end of Anglo-Saxon rule in Britain.

Despite its name, the work is an embroidery rather than a tapestry and contains approximately 626 human figures and 200 horses.

The Bayeux Tapestry is on loan from the French government, having been transported from its home in Normandy - where it has been exhibited since 1983. It will be on display until July 2027.

The loan marks the first time the tapestry has returned to the UK since it was created more than 900 years ago.

title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
content:
Rebel forces in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region have said they have temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital, Mekelle, as fighting with the national army moves towards the city.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which has been running the region, said its decision to relocate was made because of concerns about risks to civilians.

Two residents in Mekelle told the BBC that pro-government forces now control the city and TPLF forces have abandoned it. One resident also said mobile phone services appear to have resumed in parts of the city.

Fighting has erupted in recent weeks between the TPLF and federal government forces alongside allied fighters in parts of Ethiopia's northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

The development marks a major shift in the conflict and raises concerns among observers that the fighting could further destabilise the Horn of Africa, potentially drawing in neighbouring countries.

The US Department of State called for "restraint" and "dialogue" on all sides ahead of a diplomatic meeting about the conflict in Egypt on Sunday with leaders from some of Ethiopia's neighbours.

Tigray residents have been trying to recover from a devastating two-year civil war that ended in 2022 when the African Union (AU) brokered a peace deal, known as the Pretoria Agreement, between the two sides.

However, in the last six months there has been a worsening of relations, with both sides accusing each other of violating the agreement.

Last month, the TPLF joined six other armed movements, including the Fano militia from Amhara, to form an alliance whose stated objective is to remove Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government from power.

The civil war was one of the most deadly conflicts this century - the AU's mediator estimated some 600,000 people died as the fighting drove the region to the precipice of famine.

On Friday, neighbours Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic relations with each other after Addis Ababa accused Asmara of supporting a new rebel alliance - an allegation that it denied.

Ethiopia has also accused Egypt of supporting the rebels, leading to the expulsion of an Egyptian diplomat, which Cairo responded to by ordering an Ethiopian embassy official to leave within the same period.

The United Nations has warned that the deteriorating security situation in northern Ethiopia is severely disrupting humanitarian work and has called on all sides to guarantee safe and unhindered access to people in need.

title: I'm a classic old school Conservative, says Kemi Badenoch
content:
Kemi Badenoch has declared herself a "classic old school Conservative" as she begins her party's annual conference with a string of policy pledges and a 100 page statement on her guiding principles., external

"I believe in common sense, people working hard and being rewarded for that effort," she told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg.

She added that welfare should be a "safety net, not a lifestyle".

The Tory leader is trying to ensure her party stands out in a crowded political field. The Conservatives are trailing Labour and Reform UK in the opinion polls and have yet to recover from their historic defeat at the 2024 general election.

Badenoch, whose personal poll ratings are higher than that of her party, has characterised Reform leader Nigel Farage as a "grumpy grandpa" and she told Laura Kuenssberg that Labour leader Andy Burnham is "the cheesy uncle who does all the dad jokes".

She described herself as a "no-nonsense mum".

Asked if her plan for benefit cuts and a massive increase in prison places was a return to the "nasty party" of the past, she said: "It's the common sense party. That's what we're doing.

"And, quite frankly, if we were doing so well the old way, then why did we have such a terrible issue in 2024?"

In her essay The Right Way - a deliberate echo of an essay written by Margaret Thatcher in 1976, external entitled The Right Approach - Badenoch says the last Conservative government failed because it did not know what it stood for.

Despite the party's rhetoric during its 14 years in power, she said: "We did little to reverse the structural changes Labour had made which took the country in the wrong direction.

"The result was that the state grew by stealth."

The essay says the "next Conservative government will have one central principle: business, not government, creates growth".

The Tories would achieve growth through tax cuts, cutting red tape and reducing the size of the civil service back to pre-pandemic levels, the essay says.

And it adds: "What is really missing from politics and government today is people prepared to say no.

"Political parties now need to recruit those who have the stomach to say no to good causes when the resources simply are not there to do everything."

As their conference gets under way in Birmingham the Conservatives have pledged to end a childcare "cliff edge", which currently means parents earning more than £100,000 do not qualify for the entitlement.

The party has also promised to deliver 50,000 new prison places by slashing the overseas aid budget to £1bn a year in a bid to end the early release of offenders.

Over the 14 years the Conservatives were in power, around 500 net prison places were created, which takes into account 14,142 added in existing and new jails, set against 13,660 lost mainly to dilapidation and closures.

Speaking in the main conference hall, Badenoch sought to make the case that the party had moved on from 2024 and outlined her expectation that the next few days in Birmingham would be a chance for members to discuss their ideas.

She said: "We're going to be having debates, we're going to have arguments, they are going to be fun.

"We're going to challenge each other and afterwards we're still going to be a united party."

During a question and answer session, Badenoch focused on different topics covered in her essay – including citizenship and how communities need to operate on trust.

She said the UK is "not a dormitory, it is not a hotel" before speaking how "British culture means something".

To applause in the well-attended hall, Badenoch said: "I don't want lots of little ghettos of separatist communities where they are recreating the place they come from - that will ruin the United Kingdom."

Responding, Labour Party chair Bridget Phillipson said the Tory Party "is stuck in the past and remains completely out of touch with what people across Britain want to see".

"Last week Andy Burnham set out a plan to bring back hope to Britain. Kemi Badenoch wants to drag our country back to a politics that let so many people down over the past 40 years."

title: Medieval leprosy hospital uncovered in Lincoln
content:
The walls of what is thought to be one of medieval England's earliest and largest leprosy hospitals have been uncovered in Lincoln by Time Team archaeologists.

A three-day dig started on Friday on the South Common at the site of the Hospital of the Holy Innocents, which housed up to 20 people with leprosy around the late 11th to early 12th Centuries.

Time Team's Prof Carenza Lewis said they had found traces of square features where it is thought people were housed, which "haven't been excavated before, anywhere".

The dig marks the beginning of a three-year project backed by the National Lottery Heritage Fund.

The remains of the building were found last year during a Local Landscapes and Hidden Histories project.

More than 100 volunteers were involved in excavating test pits which uncovered what were thought to be the medieval boundary walls of the hospital.

Time Team carried out a geophysical survey of the area, like an X-ray of the ground, and volunteers have dug a 30m-long (98ft) trench to join up the two test pits where traces of the walls were found.

Lewis said a wall runs all the way down the trench and either side of it, according to the survey.

"We know from historical documents that there were up to 20 lepers housed here, and we know that they had little sorts of curtilages… which implies they're separate little buildings, little houses with a little yard, perhaps," she explained.

"What we've got all along this wall here are traces of little square features, about 5m (16ft) across, that are big enough to be a little building or a yard area, and we've got lots of them."

City of Lincoln Council said it believed the hospital remained in use for about five centuries.

The Hidden Histories Unearthed project, supported by £248,139 from the National Lottery Heritage Fund and led by Anglia Ruskin University, aims to uncover more about the people who lived and died at the hospital.

"You'd need to have resources to get in here," Lewis said.

"If you had enough money and could buy your way into a leper hospital, it's a bit like getting a place in a private care home or something like that."

The council said local residents would have opportunities to get involved in further archaeological excavations and activities as the project continues.

title: Daughter of MP murdered five years ago tells BBC politicians still at risk
content:
The daughter of murdered MP Sir David Amess says politicians are still at risk and questioned if anything has changed five years after her father's death.

Katie Amess told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg what happened to her father "wasn't an isolated incident, we are seeing increased threats towards members of parliament".

Sir David was the Conservative MP for Southend West when he was stabbed multiple times while holding a constituency surgery in Leigh-on-Sea, Essex, in October 2021.

The government commissioned a review into his death in August, to identify lessons to be learned and recommend steps to minimise the risk of future tragedies.

The review is being led by former Conservative justice secretary Sir Robert Buckland, with the aim of reporting within six months.

The safety of politicians has been a prominent issue in recent years since the death of former Conservative MP Ann Widdecombe in July this year, Sir David's murder in 2021 and Labour MP Jo Cox's murder in 2016.

The five years since her father was killed have been "absolutely devastating and heartbreaking", his daughter told Kuenssberg, adding: "It's a very, very real situation that we're living with."

She has previously called for a public inquiry into the safety of politicians so people can have "the full facts to hand, full openness, honesty, and transparency".

The nearing anniversary of Sir David's murder comes after the man accused of murdering Widdecombe was also charged with preparing acts of terror, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Amess, who knew Widdecombe as a family friend and called her Aunt Ann, said: "It's absolutely so tragic and heartbreaking that now she isn't here either."

She added: "My dad was murdered five years ago so if so much has changed why are we still seeing other members of parliament or former members of parliament being targeted like this."

Widdecombe was not a sitting member of parliament when she died, but was a member of the Conservative Party and the member for Maidstone and the Weald from 1987 to 2010. She became a member of Reform UK in 2019.

Separately, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch confirmed to the BBC the man who pleaded guilty to sending her threatening messages also sent them to her family.

Kieran Kyle, 43, pleaded guilty to two counts of sending communication of an indecent or offensive nature to Badenoch and her family when he appeared in court in September. He will be sentenced on October 29.

"I just think that whether it's Nigel Farage, or even Keir Starmer who had his home fire bombed, that there is a threat to politicians that is increasing and we just need to crack down on this," she told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg.

Asked how Badenoch coped with threats to her safety, she replied: "it's really tough, but you just have to get on with it".

Reform UK's deputy leader Richard Tice, who told the BBC he also experienced threats to his safety, told the programme "this was far from where any of us want to be".

"We have to find the middle ground where we're accessible but we're protected and in the overall scheme of things if that requires a bit of extra taxpayers' money, I think hopefully voters would say 'yes'."

Amess said her father "loved meeting people", saying "he was one of the easier members of parliament to take a meeting with because that's what he lived for - to meet people, shake their hands, smile, help them with their problems. My dad wouldn't have wanted constituency surgeries to stop."

She added that he would have wanted to be alerted to someone being reported as a potential threat.

His killer, Ali Harbi Ali had been referred to the government's counter-terror programme Prevent in October 2014 but his case was closed in 2016.

A review published in February 2025 found Ali's Prevent case was closed too early after "problematic" assessments.

title: Purchase of field aims to expand 'green lung'
content:
Conservationists have said they are planning to buy a field to extend a "green lung" in one of Jersey's most built-up parishes.

The National Trust for Jersey said it had secured the rights to acquire the land near Maupertuis Farm in St Clement and hoped to complete the purchase shortly.

A green lung is an area of fields, parkland or vegetation within an otherwise urban area, providing space for wildlife and helping to reduce pollution.

The trust previously raised £50,000 in 37 days to buy a nearby field on Samares Lane in 2021.

The trust said the latest acquisition would help preserve the agricultural heritage of Maupertuis Farm and the surrounding area.

Chief executive Alan Le Maistre said green spaces were becoming "ever more precious" and protecting them was particularly important in densely developed parts of the island.

"It is a privilege to have the opportunity to extend this green lung for both the wildlife and people of the area," he said.

The National Trust for Jersey, which celebrated its 90th anniversary in August, manages about 1,800 vergées of land across the island.

It invited people who want to support the latest acquisition to contact the charity directly.

title: Verstappen wins in Malaysia after long delays as Russell retires
content:
Max Verstappen took his and Red Bull's first win of the year with a dominant drive in a dramatic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia that started amid chaotic and unprecedented scenes.

Verstappen led home the Mercedes of Kimi Antonelli, who took a giant leap towards his first world title when team-mate George Russell retired from third place with a power unit failure with five laps to go.

Antonelli now leads Russell by 84 points with either six or seven races remaining.

Lewis Hamilton drove an extraordinary race after dropping towards the back with an incorrect tyre choice for a wet start to fight back to pass Red Bull's Isack Hadjar for third place with three laps to go.

All that came after a delay of an hour and a half caused initially by heavy rain and then by a series of bizarre technical problems that left several cars crawling as they completed formation laps on the wet track behind the safety car.

After that problem, it took some time for governing body the FIA to decide the order in which the cars should take the start.

The key stories of a madcap afternoon were:

Verstappen's dominant win in a revived Red Bull

The effective death knell for Russell's already faint title hopes

A stunning recovery by Hamilton

A series of questions over race organisation, particularly over the start

Once the race got under way, with the cars in their original order, Verstappen and Hamilton on the front row immediately lost ground and the Mercedes of Antonelli and Russell swept past them into first and second places.

Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers took the start on intermediate tyres on the still-wet track after a torrential tropical downpour had delayed the start.

Hamilton chose soft-compound slicks and immediately regretted the decision as it became apparent that the track was still far too wet for that option. He and others who chose slicks soon dropped to the back of the field, and lost nearly a minute to the leaders in the early laps.

Meanwhile, Verstappen repassed Russell for second place on lap six, and was on Antonelli's tail when a safety car was deployed to allow marshals to recover the Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas, who had spun off at Turn 13 on lap nine.

The leaders took the opportunity of the safety car to pit for slick tyres, and when the race resumed four laps later, Verstappen immediately passed Antonelli at Turn Four, the Italian also losing out to Russell on the exit of the corner.

From that moment on, Verstappen was in total control and he edged away into a race of his own.

Behind him, Antonelli had pace on Russell and passed him on lap 21 at Turn Four, the move seemingly settling the top three positions.

A late safety car caused by Alex Albon's stricken Williams led to everyone switching to fresh tyres for a four-lap dash to the flag, but again Verstappen was supreme and remained unchallenged.

Even then, there was drama, as Russell pulled off just before Turn One with five laps to go before the safety car had even ended.

In the immediate aftermath, Lando Norris was apparently distracted by Russell's car and had to take to the gravel at Turn One to avoid running into the back of team-mate Oscar Piastri, dropping from eighth to 11th.

He recovered to ninth by the end, immediately behind Fernando Alonso, who scored points for Aston Martin for only the third time this year after their strongest performance of the year.

Strong recovery by Hamilton

Hamilton and the others who chose to use dry tyres at the start immediately lived to regret their decision, as they were passed by all the cars on intermediates.

Within a few laps, Hamilton was nearly a minute behind the leaders and down in 17th place, his race apparently over.

But he stayed out during the safety car, sticking with the soft tyres he had chosen for the start, and when the race restarted he began to pick off the cars in front of him, driving an excellent race to get back into contention for serious points.

Hamilton passed car after car until by lap 24 he was on the tail of Isack Hadjar's fourth-placed Red Bull.

They pitted together on lap 31, Hadjar sticking to soft tyres, and Hamilton having no choice but to move to mediums.

Hamilton trailed the Frenchman for lap after lap, right on his tail, but was never quite able to get close enough to pass, despite a number of attempts, before the late safety car.

That gave Hamilton the chance to switch to the preferred soft tyres, and a lap after the restart he passed Hadjar into Turn One to take the final podium position.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc also passed Hadjar in the closing laps, with Oscar Piastri taking sixth after a dispiriting weekend for McLaren, ahead of Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Alonso.

Norris and the second Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10.

What happened before the start?

After the tropical downpour, the race was initially started with formation laps behind the safety car. But immediately the problems started.

Verstappen and Hamilton were the first of a number of cars that were afflicted by a software issue that left them unable to do more than crawl along.

Governing body the FIA said this was caused by a combination of the weather, low speed, the mandated wet-weather energy management settings and the circuit layout.

A software update removing the constraint on energy limits was issued by governing body the FIA during the subsequent start delay to enable teams to resolve the issue.

Most teams who were afflicted managed eventually to get their cars going, but the field order was jumbled, and that led to a debate as to the positions in which the cars should take the restart.

The rules did not cover the situation, which was unprecedented. And although they outline positional penalties for any driver who is not able to regain his position by a certain place on the track having lost it on a formation lap, this was ignored in restarting the race in its original order.

title: Porridge makers from opposite sides of globe triumph in world championship
content:
Two national porridge-making champions from almost opposite sides of the planet have triumphed in the annual world championships held in the Scottish Highlands.

Gina Saarberg, 28, took the coveted Golden Spurtle using the same recipe that saw her crowned Dutch champion in July, using organic pinhead oats, salt and water that she brought with her from the Netherlands.

Australian champion Rob Reid took the speciality award - where competitors can combine oatmeal with any ingredients - with his porridge cannoli, an oaty spin on a tube-shaped dessert that originated in Sicily.

Thirty competitors from 14 countries took part in the contest, held each year at Carrbridge, just north of Aviemore.

Gina, from Zuthphen, started eating a kind of porridge using rolled oats in her student days because it was a cheap meal.

But she had never tasted the traditional variety until she learned about the Dutch porridge-making contest and decided to enter as a "bit of a joke".

"When I first tasted it, it was a world of difference - I've been missing out all these years," she told BBC Scotland News.

The contest rules only allow three ingredients - oats, water and salt.

She only started adding salt to her porridge ahead of the competition, but quickly realised it "really brings out the nuances and different aromas".

She believes her secret weapon may have been the water which she brought with her from her home city.

"It's very soft, and I think the mineral content may have something to do with it. I'm not sure - but it worked last time and this time as well, so maybe it's the water".

In the Speciality Porridge category, Rob, from Sydney, came up with his recipe just a few weeks before competing in the Australian national porridge championships - the Pearly Spurtle - after realising how seriously everyone was taking it.

Tapping into his family heritage - his father is Scottish and his mother is Sicilian - he decided to make a porridge cannoli.

"I then had to engineer it," the 36-year-old told BBC Scotland News.

The cream uses the traditional mix of ricotta, mascarpone and sugar but he blended in porridge, sieved it and added some ground toasted oats.

It provides the filling for shells, made like brandy snaps but using Sicilian Marsala wine instead.

"After I came up with the idea, I spent a whole day in the kitchen with one of my daughters at home making multiple different types of shells and different creams, trying to work out how to put the porridge in the cream," he said.

Having won the Pearly Spurtle, he then spent the next six weeks improving the recipe in preparation for the ultimate challenge in Scotland.

Rob used to own a café, but he now installs blinds and curtains for a living and uses his free time to channel his culinary creativity.

"Not working in a kitchen for something like this meant I was able to be really creative with it because it wasn't my job and I was able to play with it a bit more," he said.

The annual contest was started in 1994 in Carrbridge by a local hotel owner as a way of promoting the health benefits of porridge as well raising the profile of the area.

Porridge Chieftain Alan Rankin said: "The World Porridge Making Championship is a wonderfully quirky tradition that thrives on good humour and friendly competition, offering a wonderful escape from the daily grind.

"Each year, our local community opens its doors and we hope everyone who joined us leaves with fond memories of their visit."

title: Sinn Féin will co-operate with PSNI investigation over Drumcree protest, says McDonald
content:
Sinn Féin will co-operate with the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) over any potential investigation into the protest on the Garvaghy Road, the party president has said.

Protesters have remained on the Garvaghy Road since Sunday 27 September as the fallout over the proposed Portadown District Orange Lodge march continues, and rallies on both sides of the dispute were held on Saturday.

Mary Lou McDonald has said that "there's no question with us co-operating with any process that will unfold".

Speaking on Sunday, Portadown District Master Nigel Dawson said police confirmed to them that Saturday's gathering on the Garvaghy Road was "unnotified" and police were "taking evidence".

McDonald and Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill are among those who have attended the protest, which police have described as unnotified and "therefore illegal".

The Portadown District has maintained a presence at Drumcree Church after talks to end the parading dispute ended without agreement on Thursday.

Orangemen attempted to march again on Sunday morning.

Elsewhere, large crowds were on the Garvaghy Road on Sunday evening, with Irish language rap group Kneecap in attendance.

It's understood the trio went to a local school before holding a private meeting with local residents at a community centre.

They group then made their way up to the junction with Drumcree Road where residents and their supporters have been maintaining a presence for over a week.

However, it's understood the group will not be performing during their visit.

On the Garvaghy Road protest, the PSNI said that anyone "found to have broken the law will face criminal justice consequences".

However, speaking on the BBC's Sunday Politics programme, McDonald said: "There are moments in politically life where you have to take a stand, and this is one of those moments."

When asked about the legality of the protest she said: "Others will determine whether or not that is in fact the case."

The Parades Commission's decided that the parade - which is opposed by residents of the Garvaghy Road - could go ahead on Sunday 27 September with restrictions.

A fresh legal bid by the residents to prevent the march was due to be heard on Friday - but has now been postponed until Monday.

Speaking of how many times the Portadown District have attempted to proceed with their march in the past week, Dawson told BBC News NI on Sunday: "I haven't been keeping a running check on it, but I think it's 15 times we have attempted to implement the determination issued by the Parades Commission and re-enforced by a High Court judge."

He said that "on each and every occasion the message from the PSNI headquarters is they are unable to offer us safe passage down the road".

"So we continue to be here waiting for the Chief Constable to apply the law to a lawful determination," Dawson said.

"Obviously I'm not involved in policing matters and we respect the police but I suspect that time is running out, that he can't continue to say that he is unable to his job."

Dawson said Portadown remains a "very determined district".

"Some of us have been here for the last 28 years each and every Sunday, and we are happy to allow the law to take its course but the law needs to be implemented and it needs to be respected by everybody across the communities."

The actions of McDonald, O'Neill and others have received condemnation including from members of the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).

In a post on social media, deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly said the "behaviour of Michelle O'Neill and her party has been disgraceful" and a "complete abdication of leadership".

McDonald said that this "comes down to right and wrong", and that as people who care passionately about the future, her and O'Neill know that for "that to happen we have to stand four square with the community of the Garvaghy Road".

She said there was a "broad crowd politically and otherwise" at the rally on Saturday, adding that it was "resolute but good humoured with a real eye for the future".

"I cannot fathom anybody suggesting that 28 years on when progress has been made in such significant ways, not least in Portadown and in the wider Garvaghy community, why it is that anybody would seek to reopen that wound."

Meanwhile, in response to DUP leader Gavin Robinson's comments that Sinn Féin is attempting to goad unionists into collapsing Stormont, McDonald said it is "anything but", adding that it is about the ability of communities to live work, and build futures together.

Speaking to BBC News NI at Drumcree on Saturday, DUP MP Carla Lockhart said there could be "repercussions for a very long time if mob rule wins over the rule of law".

"No, we need the police service to step up and do their job. I do think if the real residents step forward we can and should discuss further options and resolutions, because we do want to see this resolved," Lockhart said.

McDonald said that "the real voices of the Garvaghy Road" have called for support and people to come stand for them and "my god have they had a response, not just in Ireland but right across the world".

McDonald said her party has pressed Northern Ireland Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant and Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin.

She said that "we have found ourselves landed in this situation by an utterly reckless determination by the Parades Commission".

McDonald added that Martin and her both agree that the Parade's Commission determination as "incomprehensible and wrong".

Speaking at a Fianna Fáil dinner on Saturday, Martin said that "absolutely nobody benefits from the reopening of the dispute over the parade on the Garvaghy Road".

In a social media post on Sunday, Sir Chris said he is "pleased that events have passed this weekend in Portadown without major incident".

"I continue to speak with people of goodwill on all sides and believe a mutually agreeable solution is still possible if people can show leadership based on openness, compromise and magnanimity."

McDonald said the resolution is that Sir Chris needs to "call this, make it clear that he puts a stop to this march and thereby creates the space for a mediation".

Elsewhere on Sunday, a number of people carried a cross from Craigwell Avenue to St Mark's Church in Portadown under the 'Carry the Cross Initiative'.

Organisers intended to depart from Drumcree Parish Church, but the Parades Commission determined it was necessary to alter the assembly and departure point of the parade, external "so that it avoids the areas where tensions are currently heightened".

Organisers said the initiative had been "strictly curtailed" following the determination, which also limited the gathering to fewer than 10 people.

The organisers are appealing for "healing, unity and genuine reconciliation across Portadown, pointing to the unifying message of the cross of Christ to break decades of division".

What is the Drumcree dispute?

Drumcree was one of Northern Ireland's most serious parading disputes, when stand-offs over attempts by the Orange Order to march along the Garvaghy Road were accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.

When the Orange Order was prevented by police from walking down the route in July 1995, there was a tense stand-off. It was the same for the next three years.

In 1998, the newly-established Parades Commission ruled that the Orange Order should not march down the road - a decision that was upheld for the past 28 years.

The row re-emerged last month after a court case in which a ruling by the Parades Commission was overturned, and a fresh application to parade was lodged.

Last Friday, the commission decided that the march could go ahead with restrictions in place.

However, that decision was challenged in several Belfast courts on Saturday, before finally being given the go-ahead just hours before it was due to take place.

title: Scottish Tory leader Findlay says SNP's indy 'obsession' is dangerously irresponsible
content:
Scottish Conservative leader Russell Findlay has described the SNP's "obsession" with independence as "dangerously irresponsible".

First Minister John Swinney has said he wants to hold a second Scottish independence referendum by 2031, despite successive prime ministers refusing to countenance another poll.

Findlay told the Conservative Party's UK conference that while the United Kingdom continues to face "grave threats" from China, Russia and Iran, a divided UK would be "a gift to our enemies".

And he called on Swinney to respect the result of the 2014 referendum where a majority of Scots voted no to independence.

Findlay told delegates: "We face Russian hostility in our waters and Iranian plots on our streets. These totalitarian regimes want a divided United Kingdom.

"And we have SNP politicians who share that aim. They want to shut down Faslane. They oppose Britain's armed forces. They would make us less safe.

"In today's volatile world, relentless SNP chatter about independence is no longer just a dangerous distraction. It is now dangerously irresponsible."

The Scottish Tory leader also used his speech to attack what he described as the SNP's "broken" benefits system.

He said the Scottish government's approach was trapping people in a life of misery on "Benefits Street" and also giving the green light to "chancers and crooks".

"My party values the safety net of social security, despite the tiresome anti-Tory tropes peddled by our rivals," Findlay said.

"But Scotland's benefits system under the SNP is broken. Around one pound of every seven spent by them goes on benefits.

"By 2031, Scotland's benefits bill will be more than £9bn. That's more than we spend on schools, universities, colleges, police, courts and prisons combined.

"Social security should be there for times of need, it shouldn't be a lifestyle choice."

Benefit fraud bill

Findlay said the Scottish Tories would launch a Benefit Fraud Bill to help recover overpayments.

"We will demand taxpayers' get their money back, instead of just asking nicely.

"Overpayments could be taken directly from bank accounts, as happens elsewhere in the UK.

"Driving licences could be confiscated if refunds are not forthcoming. Our law would double the maximum sentence for benefit fraud to 10 years.

"Benefits should be for those suffering genuine hardship.

"That would deliver true fairness, dignity and respect."

The Scottish Tory leader went on to criticise John Swinney for "cosying up to Sinn Fein" at a recent summit in Cardiff.

Findlay said: "Since Mr Swinney was a teenager, all he's cared about is breaking up the United Kingdom.

"Sorry Mr Swinney, and your new friends in Sinn Fein, but we won't let that happen.

"Let's not forget that Sinn Fein has never denounced the IRA slaughter of innocent men, women and children.

"Yet Mr Swinney works with them to destroy the United Kingdom. A disgrace."

title: “要让肇事者付出代价！”东航就“空姐下跪事件”报案，六成网友支持“应加大惩戒辱骂者”
content:
文 | 《BUG》栏目 徐苑蕾
近日，“东方航空空姐下跪事件”相关话题多次登上热搜。东方航空发布最新通报，涉事旅客涉嫌扰乱民用航空器内秩序，已正式向公安机关报案，并暂停为涉事旅客提供承运服务。
根据网传视频显示，在涉事航班上，一名乘务员双膝跪在客舱通道餐车旁，身旁旅客情绪激动。有目击者谈及事件经过：“乘务员推着小车给乘客分发饮料，不小心碰到这位乘客手肘，乘务员给他道歉了，他就开始不饶人，大吼大叫，说要么你给我踹一脚，乘务员委屈得掉眼泪，最后跪着跟他道歉。”
对于东方航空的处理，不少网友评论予以肯定，并表示“干得漂亮，要让违法行为付出应有的代价”，“按闹分配（指遇到纠纷不靠规则，而是靠闹腾、施压来解决问题的不良现象）的日子一去不复返了。”
今日，一则关于“机闹”的网络投票显示，超过六成网友将“加大对辱骂、威胁机组人员行为的惩戒力度”视为减少此类事件最有效的办法。紧随其后的是“加强民航旅客普法，明确客舱行为红线”与“强化安全员现场干预能力，及时制止冲突升级”，投票占比均约两成。
“尊严不能无限让步”
9月28日晚，东方航空MU6741合肥至大连航班飞行途中，发生一起客舱服务纠纷事件。根据网传视频，一名乘务员双膝跪在客舱通道餐车旁，身旁旅客情绪激动。
有目击者在社交平台发文谈及事件经过：“乘务员推着小车给乘客分发饮料，不小心碰到这位乘客的手肘，其实也没啥问题。乘务员给他道歉了，他就开始不饶人，说你道歉迟了，对着乘务员大吼大叫。无论怎样，这位乘客就是不满意，说要么你给我踹一脚。乘务员委屈得掉眼泪，最后跪着跟他道歉，跪着求他给她一脚，求心理平衡。”
9月30日，东方航空官方发布首份情况通报：经核实，航班乘务员在推餐车提供饮料服务过程中，全程提示旅客注意，因一名旅客处于睡眠状态，不慎造成餐车与其手肘发生触碰。乘务员当即反复致歉，查看旅客状况。该旅客情绪激动，连续使用粗俗过激言语，并出现威胁脚踢乘务员、要求当事乘务员落地后陪同就医等言行，该乘务员受到惊吓。
随着舆论持续发酵，10月3日，东方航空再次发布通报，释放更为明确的态度。通报称，在前期复盘基础上，公司已基本完成证据固定、事实核查与法律评估，认为旅客欧某某涉嫌扰乱民用航空器内秩序，严重侵害员工人格尊严和履职权益，公司已正式向公安机关报案，并依据旅客承运管理制度暂停为欧某某提供承运服务。
对于东方航空的处理，不少网友评论予以肯定，并表示“干得漂亮。”有网友表示，“我支持东航，这种情况要站在自己员工一方，做坚强的后盾，不要和稀泥，不要息事宁人，要让肇事者付出代价，这显然是平时颐指气使习惯了，以为到哪都是大爷。”
“按闹分配的日子一去不复返了。”还有网友称：“东航这次选择报警+暂停承运该名乘客，是一次很有标志性的纠偏，服务要做好，但尊严不能无限让步，消费纠纷 【下载黑猫投诉客户端】 可以协商，但羞辱和威胁不能免责。”
北京中银（广州）律师事务所韩斌律师向《BUG》栏目表示，依据《治安管理处罚法》第二十六条，涉事旅客可能面临警告或五百元以下罚款；若被认定为“情节较重”，则可能面临五日以上十日以下拘留，并可处1000元以下罚款。
韩斌分析称，涉事乘客还可能涉及“公然侮辱他人”的情节，这在处罚时也可能被纳入考量。言辞过于激动、行为持续时间长、严重扰乱公共秩序和安全等行为，则可能被公安机关认定为“情节较重”，从而触发拘留处罚。
上海申宜禾律师事务所合伙人王龙国表示，涉事旅客还可能面临民航惩戒，被列入民航“黑名单”。根据《民用航空法》第二百五十二条的规定，实施妨害民用航空运输安全和秩序的行为，情节严重的，国务院民用航空主管部门可以在一定期限内限制其乘坐民用航空器。
内部人士解释“空姐为何下跪”
东方航空通报还显示，公司已对当事乘务员“予以关爱慰问、心理疏导和法律援助”。王龙国表示，从民事侵权角度，乘务员本人可以单独起诉涉事旅客侵犯人格权，并可以主张精神损害赔偿。
王龙国称，“涉事旅客在航班上对乘务员连续使用粗俗、过激言语，并进行威胁，属于对乘务员人格尊严的严重侵害，乘务员作为直接受害人，有权依据《民法典》的规定，请求涉事旅客承担停止侵害、消除影响、赔礼道歉等民事责任。乘务员因辱骂、威胁、下跪等行为受到严重惊吓，若产生了精神损害，也可依法主张精神损害赔偿金。”
谈及乘务员为何宁愿以下跪的方式极力平息机舱矛盾，一位航空公司内部人士透露称，航司普遍有硬性规定，乘务员不能与旅客起争执，再委屈也要当场化解。而一旦形成有效投诉，乘务员绩效、评优、晋升都会受到影响，连排班也会被调整。
“比如这次事件，源头是餐车碰到乘客，确实存在磕碰在先，哪怕对方明显借题发挥，只要旅客坚持投诉，公司判定起来就非常麻烦，乘务员天然处于被动地位。”该人士称。
2024年，民航局曾发布《关于进一步加强和改进新时期客舱安全管理工作的意见》，要求各运输航空公司“秉承实事求是、客观公正的态度，妥善甄别和处理”各类客舱服务投诉，并以“谁主张，谁举证”为原则完善被投诉人员申诉机制，降低无效或恶意投诉给机组成员正常履职带来的负面影响。
然而，制度层面的改进倡议与航司实际执行之间或仍存在落差。当下国内民航业复苏进程仍显缓慢，叠加燃油价格波动、市场竞争加剧、人工与运维成本上涨等多重因素，头部航司普遍面临亏损困境，经营压力持续攀升。在此背景下，航司对服务品质和旅客满意度的追求变得更加刚性。
东方航空乘务员下跪事件的舆论发酵，也让公众再次聚焦民航“机闹”乱象。实际上，在“机闹”治理层面，近年来法治手段正在持续加码：自2023年7月起，民航公安机关开展整治“机闹”专项行动。数据显示，截至2024年4月，全国民航公安机关共打击处理“机闹”事件669起，采取刑事强制措施6人次，行政拘留311人次，每百万旅客中扰序行为人占比较专项行动前下降13.2%。到2025年，全国民航公安依法处置机上案事件1081起，同比下降6.5%，每万班次发案率同比下降17%。

title: Glastonbury 2027 tickets sell out in 42 minutes
content:
Tickets for Glastonbury Festival 2027 sold out in 42 minutes, organisers have said.

Thousands of people joined the online queue at 09:00 BST in the hope of securing tickets to the festival at Worthy Farm in Somerset, which returns from 23 to 27 June after a fallow year.

Organisers confirmed last month that tickets for the weekend were at their highest price ever - £408, including a £5 booking fee per ticket - an increase of £29.50 from the last event in 2025.

Headliners have yet to be announced but organiser Emily Eavis previously said the team was "very excited" and things were "coming together really well".

Glastonbury posted on Instagram shortly after 09:40 to announce that tickets had sold out, and notified those who were in the queue.

"Thank you to everyone who bought one and we're sorry to those of you who missed out on a morning where demand greatly exceeded supply," the post said.

"There will be a resale of any cancelled or returned tickets in Spring 2027."

The first round of tickets, which were for coach packages, went up for sale on Thursday and sold out in less than half an hour.

Despite the increase in cost, Zoe Scott, who has been to the festival twice, said "the price is totally worth it".

"You're getting to see thousands of acts, there's over 100 stages," she said.

"It's such a vibe at Glastonbury- everyone's so happy and free-spirited. You're just on a constant high from friends, music and the sun is usually shining".

A couple who first met at Glastonbury will also be heading to Worthy Farm next year to celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary.

Nick and Helen Nugget from Amersham met through mutual friends at the festival in 2007 and will be returning next year with the same group.

Nick told BBC Your Voice that they were "absolutely delighted" to be going back.

The couple last went to the festival in 2011- although they were successful in securing tickets in 2019, they were unable to attend due to the adoption of their daughter.

'Fairer than ever'

Dave in London was in several groups all trying to get tickets through their laptops and phones on Sunday morning, and was successful.

He said: "Actually it seems like it's fairer this year than it's ever been.

"All the hacks that people used to use don't seem to have the same impact, and about a quarter of the people on the groups we are on managed to get tickets."

Sarah in Dorset was surprised she also managed to get hold of some.

She said: "A mobile phone on 5G in Shaftesbury seemed to be the optimal way to get tickets. We didn't even know Shaftesbury had 5G until this morning."

Among those who were not successful were Mat Chapman and his daughter Amy.

Mat told the BBC that he used to watch the festival on TV with Amy when she was little, promising to take her when she was five years old as "she always wanted to have her own flag that you could see on the telly".

Mat had hoped that after 20 years of trying, he would be able to beat the queue this year, on Amy's 26th birthday. Unfortunately he only ever moved from "two bar hell to three bar purgatory".

"There's always next year. We'll fly the flag there one day."

This year's Glastonbury tickets have breached the £400 mark for the first time.

Tickets have increased over the years, from £185 in 2010 to £408 for the upcoming 2027 line-up.

Most price rises have come since the pandemic, with tickets climbing from £318 in 2019 to a peak of £408 in 2027.

But unlike recent years, much of the 2010s saw relatively steady price hikes.

Any tickets from today's sale that are not paid for in full by the early April 2027 deadline will be put back into an official resale pool, festival organisers said.

The exact date for this is yet to be announced, but in previous years it has been in late April.
