title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
content:
Cornell University's president says the school "must do better" after a woman alleged she was drugged and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house.

In an eight-minute video statement released on Saturday night, Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations raised by the woman, identified as Jane Doe, as "deeply disturbing".

The alleged incident has raised questions around the culture on campus of drug and alcohol use, and the way investigations were conducted in the case, Kotlikoff said.

Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the university when she says seven men from its Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine on 19 October 2024.

She said she had reported the incident two weeks after it happened to Cornell University police, which investigated, but no charges were laid.

Last month, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university, in which she alleged Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved.

Kotlikoff said Cornell was "committed to investigating" the way the case was handled, and said the school administration and community "must do better".

"We must foster a culture in which sexual assault is inexcusable and ensure our community is empowered and understands informed consent," he said.

He added that university leaders need to create an environment where victims of sexual assault "feel safe coming forward and are treated with compassion and dignity".

Kotlikoff said it is a "defining moment" in the university's history.

"We must lead the way, we owe it to Jane Doe and to survivors of assault to get this right. And we must keep each other safe," he said.

On the university's campus this week, the BBC saw growing frustration about the situation.

At a public hearing for students to speak about the alleged gang rape, many told the BBC they were ashamed of what happened and said the university had failed Jane Doe.

"Our administration needs to change and it needs to change drastically and it needs to change fast," one student told the BBC. "Something like this never should have happened, this is a disgrace."

As part of "broader work" that needs to happen, Kotlikoff said in his video statement that there should be a "serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life".

"Being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility for our own actions, for how we treat others, or for speaking up when someone may be at risk," he said.

The university president also said that at the "appropriate time", the school would speak about how Cornell will "use this moment, this conversation, this anger, to help lead the broader effort to combat sexual assault not only on our campus, but beyond it".

New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said she was "deeply disturbed" by how the investigation was handled, and has appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to lead a review of the case.

Kotlikoff said he supported the decision to appoint James to lead a criminal investigation, and welcomed an independent review by a law firm of how Cornell has handled the matter.

Jane Doe said in her lawsuit that she was intoxicated during the alleged incident and could not provide consent.

title: Why Canada is wargaming a (long shot) US invasion
content:
Prime Minister Mark Carney admitted last week that he has prepared for a once-unthinkable scenario - a US invasion.

Noting the risk was low and the likelihood highly improbable, he told the New York Times he had a responsibility to consider all possibilities as the US-Canada relationship is redefined under the Donald Trump presidency.

"That's just risk management," Carney said.

Trump's global tariffs and his often-repeated desire to make Canada the 51st state has led Canada to war game an attack by the Americans.

In 2025, the US president said it was "highly unlikely" that the US would ever use force against Canada. Instead he said, he would continue to exert economic pressures to obtain political aims.

"President Trump has done more than anyone to protect the great people of Canada," the White House told the BBC in a statement this week.

Military experts who spoke to the BBC also think an invasion is a long shot, pointing to the multiple ways the two countries work together on defence.

But the issue is clearly weighing on Canadians' minds.

In January, after the US captured Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela, a Leger poll suggested that over 30% of Canadians believed that a US invasion was likely.

Why it is unlikely to happen

A war between Canada and the US would be complicated and almost difficult to imagine, said Lt-Gen Christopher Coates, a former military officer of 34 years with the Royal Canadian Air Force who held various senior positions.

"I was involved in military operations for my whole career, and we never considered the possibility that there would be a military attack coming from US territory," he told the BBC.

Coates, who had served on Nato missions, noted that Canada and the US collaborate on many aspects of military defence.

They are both members of the north Atlantic defence alliance, which mandates members to defend a fellow member-nation should they be attacked.

The two countries also conduct joint Arctic defence missions under the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD), and frequently share intelligence.

Because of this, Coates said he believes an attack by the US on Canada would not begin with an armed assault, but rather with more discreet means like cyberwarfare.

Not always the best of friends

After World War II, Canada and the US became natural allies for the latter part of the 20th Century, and have become heavily integrated economically, militarily and culturally.

But it wasn't always this way. In fact, a core tenet of Canada's identity is its resistance of US expansionism in the 18th and 19th Centuries, said Tim Foran, a researcher with the Canadian War Museum.

"Fear of the United States is foundational to the political project that is Canada," he said.

Canada was formed as a collection of British North American colonies who remained loyal to the British Crown when the colonies in the modern-day US rebelled.

Before the formation of Canada, the US had attempted to invade British North American colonies, taking control of Montreal in 1775 and nearly conquering Quebec City.

In the war of 1812, the Americans invaded what was known then as Upper Canada, Lower Canada and the maritime colonies repeatedly, resulting in a stalemate. During that war, British troops famously burned down the White House in retaliation.

Foran said that at the time, the colonies that later became Canada relied on Great Britain and its Royal Navy for its defence, as well as indigenous peoples who served as generals in major battles.

Canada again contemplated war with the US post-World War I in response to its growing power and influence.

It drafted a plan that was informed by secret trips to border cities made by Canadian army generals, who would pose as tourists and snap photos of bridges and highways for intelligence.

They also spoke to local residents to better understand their enemy.

A war was an unlikely scenario then, said Andrew Burtch, a researcher with the Canadian War Museum with expertise on Canada in the 20th Century, but the Canadians still wanted to be prepared.

"That's part of what militaries do," he said. "They envisage all sorts of different scenarios."

What a US invasion could look like

Even if a US invasion is extremely unlikely, Matthew Schmidt, an associate professor of national security at the University of New Haven in Connecticut, said the fact that Canadians were preparing was a sign of just how drastically the global order has shifted.

He added Canadian leaders do have hard questions to ask about how closely they want to continue working with the American military - a partnership that gives them valuable information should they want to harm Canada in any way.

"It's really doing harm to relationships with the United States, and there's a certain amount of legitimate fear," he said.

Americans might not take Trump's comments about making Canada the 51st state seriously, he said, but Canadians clearly do - and are prepared to defend themselves if needed.

So what would it be like if it happened?

The first phase of a war could be quite short.

According to the model used by the Canadian military, as reported on by the Globe and Mail newspaper earlier this year, a US attack would see Canada's strategic positions overwhelmed within a week

Its military would quickly be outnumbered, forcing Canadian forces to resort to guerilla-type warfare to try to suppress their enemy.

Allied nations like France and Britain would be called on to provide support and defence for Canada, the newspaper reported in January, citing senior government officials.

The theoretical model is believed to be the first time in a century that Canada planned for an American assault.

The modelling is on the lighter end of military combat planning, Coates said.

He said that Canada, unlike its Nato allies, was lagging behind when it came to having a response plan in place in the event of any ground invasion, and that it was now playing catch-up in this era of unpredictable geopolitics.

Part of that, he said, was made evident by a recent call by Canada's defence chief to drastically increase the size of its military, including the addition of as many as 300,000 lightly trained citizen soldiers.

An invasion of Canada might not be straightforward from the US point of view either.

Even with its outsized military, the US would have a difficult time getting buy-in for a fight with Canada, said Schmidt.

"I think you would have a large number of American officers who would resign if given the order to invade Canada," he said.

"They would see it as an illegal and immoral order."

Schmidt said Canadian soldiers and American soldiers routinely train together, and share a mutual respect.

But in the unlikely scenario that relations would deteriorate to the point of combat, Schmidt said the US would likely focus on acquiring valuable Canadian resources like oil and minerals, and political decapitation.

"You would see a a kind of operation that would mirror perhaps what you saw in Venezuela," he said, referring to US military action earlier this year to capture former Venezuelan President Maduro.

Although he acknowledged the US has greater military capacity, he said that "pound for pound" Canadian soldiers would be able to put up a fight.

title: The murder of a journalist 25 years on - why has no one been caught?
content:
The brother of a journalist, who was shot dead as he walked home with his wife, says if he did not continue to fight for answers around the murder "the guilt would kill me".

Earlier this week marked the 25th anniversary of the 2001 murder of investigative reporter Martin O'Hagan.

The 51-year-old died in Lurgan, County Armagh, and was shot when walking home from a pub - a killing that was claimed by the Red Hand Defenders, a cover name used by both the Loyalist Volunteer Force and Ulster Defence Association.

But while his murder received widespread condemnation, and numerous charges that were subsequently withdrawn, no one has ever been convicted.

Those close to Martin have said pledges from police and government officials to find those responsible have gone unfulfilled, and they remain frustrated that his death has not received the same recognition as other high profile killings.

Martin was the first person to be murdered for being a journalist in Northern Ireland since the outbreak of the Troubles in 1969.

As a reporter for the Sunday World newspaper, he had built a reputation for stories which exposed paramilitaries and drug dealers operating in Northern Ireland.

He had infuriated County Armagh paramilitary bosses, particularly murdered LVF leader Billy Wright who he labelled 'King Rat', by exposing crime and drugs rackets.

His brother Fintan told BBC News NI there was "talk that he was digging into collusion, digging into the finances of the LVF but there was never any proof".

"At the time I believed they did it because Martin made a mistake moving up there on the outskirts of Mourneview, a loyalist estate.

"Martin said at the time: 'the war is over'. It's all very well wishful thinking but at the end of the day it was a foolish thing to do. He made it easy for them and that's a very hard thing to live with," Fintan said.

"Within a short period of time the police were assuring us they were going to catch them" and "we, like fools, believed them".

Fintan now says he believes the people who murdered Martin were British agents.

In 2022, security sources told a BBC Spotlight investigation that police were given names of people said to have been involved in the killing within 48 hours but did not act on the information.

Fintan said, given the extensive surveillance of the Mid Ulster LVF, to believe that the intelligence service did not know Martin's murder was being planned is "just unbelievable".

He said the family have flagged a number of details about the case with the Police Ombudsman's office and if they are not included in the upcoming report then it's "not worth the paper it's written on".

He said while he is "hopeful", the family have had so many disappointments they do not get their hopes built up and deal with it in a "business-like fashion".

"It will come out, whether or not it confirms everything that I have experienced and seen and read – I doubt it."

In a statement, the Ombudsman's office said that since her appointment as new Police Ombudsman in June, Jacqui Durkin has been in contact with the O'Hagan family and "assured them that the completion of the public statement is one of her early priorities".

"She is actively reviewing the draft public statement and will provide the family with a publication timeline in due course."

A UK government spokesperson said Martin's murder was a "horrific attack on freedom of speech" and urged anyone with information to contact police.

"The safety of journalists is paramount," they added. "The UK government remains steadfastly committed to ensuring journalists are able to carry out their work free from threat, intimidation, or violence."

Martin had a history of involvement in the Official IRA (the group from which the Provisional IRA would emerge) and spent five years in Long Kesh prison in the early 1970s for moving weapons.

Fintan said he turned his back on violence when he got out of prison, got his degree and became a journalist.

"I think the fact that Martin had been in jail and in the Official IRA, which is no secret, I think that affected things," said Fintan.

"The first journalist [to be murdered in Northern Ireland], the flag bearers of free speech and the right to know is journalism, and it didn't really catch fire the way it should have, and I think it was his background of being a working-class republican," Fintan said.

"If you can't protect your journalists there's no such thing as news or free speech."

'Journalists continue to be threatened'

Richard Sullivan worked alongside Martin at the Sunday World and said the then Secretary of State John Reid stood in their offices and pledged that they would catch his killers and "no stone would be left un-turned in pursuing them".

"He also said that he would ensure that journalists would be able to work in Northern Ireland free from threat.

"Yet journalists continue to be threatened, even right up to this current day. And obviously, 25 years, a quarter of a century after Marty was killed, there's no sign of a prosecution," Sullivan said.

Martin's case has been contrasted with the murder of journalist Veronica Guerin in Dublin five years previously.

She had written several exposés of organised crime in Dublin and had been subjected to threats and beatings.

Within a week of her murder, the Irish government enacted the Proceeds of Crime Act 1996 and the Criminal Assets Bureau Act 1996, so that assets purchased with money obtained through crime could be seized by the government, leading to the formation of the Criminal Assets Bureau (CAB).

Brian Meehan was convicted for his role in the murder of Guerin.

'Contrast couldn't be greater'

"Dublin was in the grips of an organised crime war. And Veronica did an awful lot of reporting and covering of that. She was a victim of a contract killing," Sullivan said.

"And in a very similar way, that's what happened to Marty. But in Veronica's case, the government and security force reaction down there was like night and day to what happened up here.

"If a journalist was gunned down and shot on the streets as he walked home after a drink with his wife in London or Manchester or Liverpool, you would never hear the end of it, they would move heaven and earth to have the law changed to get these people caught.

"But in Marty's case, the investigation just fizzled out and stopped, even though they say the case is still open.

"Nothing has happened, and there's no sign of anything happening in the near future. The contrast couldn't be greater," Sullivan said.

Fintan will continue to fight for answers for what happened to his older brother.

"What I'm doing is not just for Martin, it's for me because if I wasn't doing anything the guilt would kill me for not doing something for my brother, and this is really the only thing I can do."

However, he said the more time passes the less likely that will happen.

"If you have an inquiry that's not being done properly or running into obstacles and the longer it goes on the less people care; the only people who care are family, close friends and colleagues.

"If the state's involved, which I'm convinced they are with what I've seen, why would they move heaven and earth to find the culprits?"

In a statement, the PSNI said they "continue to appeal anyone who has information about those responsible for this heinous act to do the right thing and tell us what they know".

"As this matter is currently subject to an ongoing Police Ombudsman investigation, it would be inappropriate to comment further."

A Government spokesperson said: "Martin O'Hagan's brutal murder was a horrific attack on freedom of speech and the vital role that the media plays in a democratic society. Our deepest sympathies go to the O'Hagan family at this time.

"The safety of journalists is paramount. The UK Government remains steadfastly committed to ensuring journalists are able to carry out their work free from threat, intimidation, or violence.

"We would urge anyone with information regarding the circumstances of Mr O'Hagan's death to contact the police."

title: US father and son arrested after 'gas station heroin' deaths
content:
A father and son who worked at a Mississippi smoke shop have been arrested and charged in connection with the death of at least one university student who died from a suspected overdose of kratom, sometimes called "gas station heroin" in the US.

The pair worked at a shop that allegedly sold derivatives of the substance to University of Mississippi students.

US prosecutors charged Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, for possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances in connection with the death investigation of two Ole Miss students last month.

Although their deaths have not officially been attributed to kratom, officials afterward issued warnings about consuming kratom.

The criminal complaint alleges that on 21 September, an Ole Miss student was found dead in his dorm room. The apparent cause of death "appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose", the US Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Mississippi said in a press release.

Law enforcement found packages - with some tablets missing - of suspected kratom derivatives.

About an hour later, a second student was found dead from a suspected overdose in another location, also with packages of suspected kratom derivatives.

Officials connected the packages with the local vape, tobacco and beer store, the US Attorney's statement said.

Law enforcement executed search warrants and seized suspected kratom derivative controlled substances from the store. The Mosleh's, father and son, were later arrested.

The two students' deaths have sparked alarm and warnings from officials about the plant-based drug referred to as "gas station heroin".

Kratom - a herb with opioid-like effects - has grown in popularity in the US over the last decade, and is typically purchased over the counter and consumed in pill or liquid form.

For years, anti-kratom advocates have pushed for bans, and in some countries, like the UK, it is illegal. But Kratom is not regulated by the US Food and Drug Administration and is legal in some states, including Mississippi.

The Mississippi prosecutors said that kratom derivatives, such as MGPI, MGM-15 and MGM-16, are now schedule I controlled substances in the US and can be significantly more potent than natural kratom leaf products and morphine.

title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference
content:
Kemi Badenoch has said a Conservative government would scrap the "cliff edge" that means parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than £100,000 a year.

Speaking to the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, the Conservative Party leader said: "What we want to see is that people who work harder don't get punished for doing so."

The earnings limit means only families where no parent earns more than this threshold are eligible for government-funded or tax-free childcare.

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham.

Badenoch, who arrived in the city on Saturday, has vowed the party was new and different from the one that lost the 2024 general election.

The Conservatives - who have been polling behind Labour and Reform UK over the past year - are expected to use the four-day event to lay out more of its policy agenda ahead of the next general election.

Ahead of the conference, the Conservatives produced a 100-page essay setting out their principles, external including a "central" belief that business, rather than governments, create growth.

It argues that governments should create the conditions for growth, particularly through the tax system.

In her interview with the BBC, Badenoch pitched herself as a "classic old-school Conservative" adding: "I believe in common sense - people working hard and being rewarded for that effort."

She insisted the Tories would keep the state pension triple lock, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to change if Labour wins the next election.

She said the policy, under which state pensions rise each year by the highest of inflation, average wages, or 2.5%, was "the right policy for pensioners".

She added: "What we don't want to see is people going after the elderly, chasing after vulnerable and disabled people, and then the extremely large cohort of people who can work, who are not working, are left alone."

The Conservatives have long called on the government to cut the growing welfare budget including by implementing tighter restrictions on claimants.

'Wrong choices'

The party said its childcare announcement would be a "first step" in broader efforts to address issues in the tax system which damage incentives to work or invest.

This will be a theme of shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith's conference speech on Monday.

Since September 2025, working parents in England have been entitled to 30 hours of free childcare, external for children aged between nine months and four years old.

However, to qualify both parents must earn less than £100,000 a year, although all three and four-year-olds are eligible for 15 hours of free childcare, regardless of parental income.

The same £100,000 eligibility threshold also applies to the government's tax-free childcare scheme, external, and has remained unchanged since it was originally set under the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government.

For every £8 paid into an online childcare account, the government adds £2, up to £2,000 per child per year, which parents can then use to pay for childcare.

The Tories said that if they return to power, they would remove the £100,000 threshold entirely for tax-free childcare and free childcare hours.

The threshold has been criticised by economists, who point out it can leave parents worse off overall even after a pay rise of tens of thousands of pounds.

In her interview with Kuenssberg, Badenoch added: "What we want to see is more people in work and not taking the wrong decisions or the wrong choices, and it doesn't matter whether they're earning £10,000 or £100,000 - what matters is that people are out there working".

Asked if this could result in someone who earns £1 million a year get free childcare under a Conservative government, the Tory leader responded: "It doesn't matter what you earn - we don't want you to be punished for working hard. What we're trying to do is grow our economy."

The Tories argue the threshold may mean some people may delay having children until their incomes change, or decide not to start a family at all, describing scrapping it as "both pro-family and pro-growth".

By providing an increased incentive to work, the Tories said the move would also boost economic growth.

They added that it would tackle the "unfairness" that the threshold is calculated on an individual earner's income rather then for the whole household.

The party said the policy would be funded by cutting the number of public servants working in "executive non-departmental public bodies" - organisations which have a role in the processes of national government but operate at arm's length from ministers, such as Arts Council England and the Environment Agency.

It said this would save £1.6bn by 2029-30, covering the estimated £700 million cost of removing the childcare "cliff edge".

title: Are AI models the next big danger for body image?
content:
AI models are popping up more and more across social media and advertising, but how might this affect body image?

Mia Perumal, who has recovered from an eating disorder, said she's worried the technology could make unrealistic beauty standards even harder for young people to escape.

The 19-year-old Cardiff University student said she believes if she'd had access to AI during her eating disorder, it would have had a "terrible impact".

AI-generated videos and photos are getting harder to spot too, she said.

This story contains material about eating disorders and self-harm.

When Mia Perumal was 12 she says she was fed harmful content via social media algorithms.

Now she fears the rise of AI models is magnifying the damage on other young people.

Mia has noticed an increase in very thin AI beautiful people on social media in the past year, the comments often being from 12-year-old girls saying: "Dream body, drop your workout routine I want to look like this."

She said she finds it "really sad" because looking like AI models is completely unobtainable, she believes the only option to prevent harm is for AI to be controlled.

Mia said: "It's all very well saying 'oh, it's AI, it's not real,' But eating disorders don't really listen to rationality."

She said she wants young people to "be cautious, question everything".

In the early 2000s Kelly Watts, like most teenagers, was worried about the way she looked and said she was constantly comparing herself to people around her and models in magazines, she said.

Now 41, she is worried her 11-year-old son will compare his body to fake photographs of "perfect people".

As a freelancer in marketing, AI in business images are something Kelly is seeing everywhere, but often without tags meaning it is hard to determine whether it is real or fake.

"At first, I didn't realise they were AI, but the more you see it, the more you can't unsee it. Now, I see it on quite a regular basis," said Kelly.

Her son Oscar loves playing rugby and is becoming more aware that "some friends are taller", she said.

While he has not raised concerns about his body, she fears he could look up to AI characters online.

The 11-year-old watches YouTube and does not yet have social media. But this does not keep him away from AI, which she fears has infiltrated YouTube's content.

Watching footballers who have six-packs is already a body-image influence, she said, let alone being then shown AI generated people who are unrealistic.

"Especially with children, it's going to be 'can they ever get to that point?

"It's putting a lot of pressure on them, which they don't need," she said. "No one and nothing is perfect. I don't want him growing up thinking he has to be perfect."

"I'm his mum, and the last person he's going to listen to over a big influencer," she said, even if that influencer is AI.

Kelly said AI-literacy is important, and being able to spot real vs fake is essential.

"At what point do we need to be aware that it potentially can be damaging to us and our children, and AI should definitely be labelled more?

"Why do we want to compare ourselves to a robot instead of a human?"

"As human beings, we have this tendency to compare ourselves to others," said Phillippa Diedrichs, professor of psychology at the Centre for Appearance Research, UWE Bristol.

She said: "If we're comparing ourselves to a very narrow beauty standard, which typically tends to be the case, the beauty ideals that we have are very narrowly defined, and that inevitably means that many of us are not going to meet those beauty ideals.

"This is particularly the case with social media and digitally constructed images because they don't even exist in biological reality.

"We compare ourselves and when we fall short, this can lead us to doubt ourselves and feel negatively about our own appearance."

She said if AI was used to create more diversity and inclusion, then "when we compare ourselves, we feel alike and similar, which can either have a neutral or positive impact on our wellbeing".

Diedrichs said unless the designers prompt AI to show realistic or diverse features, "it's going to give you an image that defaults to the average" data set of the "narrow" traditional beauty standards.

"So for example, people of colour, gender, queer people, people with kind of interesting and distinguishing facial features, it means that they're going to be left out," she said.

"You can try and overcompensate that with the way you prompt and create these images. But if you don't do that, you're going to get very generic images, which tend to reinforce a lot of the biases that we have in society."

She said it could create even more unrealistic beauty standards, "if it's not done carefully or with some thought because it will default to the average of whatever it's learnt from.

How can you spot AI models?

Diedrichs said there are "tell-tale" signs like "the texture of the skin or the eyes" and how "coily hair" looks.

She added that the absence of blemishes or pores can be a good way of identifying AI, however it is constantly getting better.

Diedrichs said teenagers can be influenced but they are also often "critical and aware, and have more knowledge about technology than older people".

"The thing is, though, we can be aware that these things are happening, but it doesn't necessarily stop us from wanting to look like those images," she said.

She said she recommended asking if the images or advertising is "serving you, does that make you feel good about yourself? Does it make you feel inspired, lit up?"

"If it's making you feel lacking, that's a really important signal to pay attention to, and suggests that maybe this isn't for me to be looking at."

Diedrichs said AI models in advertising could enable small brands to have a large number of diverse models, or global brands to advertise in multiple markets.

"There could be these benefits for diversity," she said.

However, she noted the "knock on effect to creative industries and people working in this space. I would never like to see AI completely replace" the artistry and creativity of humans.

"As a consumer, you have a lot of power as well. You can express your views on this in the comment section," she said. "Brands will see."

Zoe Lee and Hannah Marriott, researchers at Cardiff Business School said AI-generation fashion models and digital twins, virtual replicas of real models are becoming more common.

Brands such as Balmain, Levi's and H&M have experimented with the technology, they said.

But Lee and Marriott's research has found that consumers often reacted negatively to AI-generated models once they realised they were not real.

In focus groups, participants told them they would "rather have a real person and way less people representing us, but they be real", arguing AI models could never reflect lived experience.

Marriott said they also found people would "emotionally detach themselves" from images once they discovered they had been generated by AI.

H&M said it worked with real models in 2025 to make "digital representations/twins of the models" who "themselves retained full control and ownership of their digital twin".

However this "exploration was paused during spring 2025" to consider the next steps.

Balmain, Levi's, TikTok, Meta and Google were contacted for comment.

title: 贝森特批评AI风险警告是危言耸听
content:
美国财长斯科特·贝森特批评人工智能领域一些知名人士就这项技术带来的人类存亡风险发出警告，称这些言论是在危言耸听，没有助益，并呼吁该行业进行自我监管并拿出解决方案。
贝森特在Axios周六发布的采访文章中表示：“我认为，我们必须为各种情况做好准备，但另一方面，人工智能领域一些人只会危言耸听，却拿不出解决方案，这并不是领导力。”
Anthropic PBC首席执行官Dario Amodei、OpenAI负责人萨姆·奥尔特曼以及xAI的埃隆·马斯克9月份呼吁放慢最先进模型的开发速度，理由是这些模型给人类带来的风险日益上升。微软联合创始人比尔·盖茨也警告称，AI技术的强大程度足以造成“10亿人死亡”，并呼吁政府加以监管。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普几乎立即反驳了这些呼吁，把有关人工智能对人类构成风险的警告称为“骗局”，并坚持认为，美国必须继续推进人工智能发展，以保持领先地位。
“实验室里的人必须承担起责任，我同意这一点，”贝森特说，“我认为，这些实验室也已经开始接受这种想法。”
不出台新监管
本周，特朗普在与多名行业高管举行的一次会议上否定了出台新的联邦监管规定的想法。与会者包括埃隆·马斯克、微软首席执行官Satya Nadella、Meta Platforms Inc．的扎克伯格、Palantir Technologies Inc．首席执行官Alex Karp以及OpenAI总裁Greg Brockman。
特朗普当时对记者表示：“有一种看法认为，应该有强大的自我监管，同时我们自动的也有司法部、联邦调查局等方面的监管，但自我监管非常重要。” 在与硅谷企业领导人达成的不具约束力的协议中，他支持由外部机构来评估人工智能系统的安全性。
当被问及人工智能行业高管要求监管的呼吁时，贝森特对Axios说：“那么，他们就应该放慢速度。”
“我们希望实现安全的加速发展，”他说，“实验室里的人必须承担起责任，我同意这一点。”

title: 工资涨不过物价 美国人想尽各种办法维持消费
content:
过去五个月里，美国物价上涨速度一直快于工资增速，这种现象本该促使消费者削减开支。但实际上，他们仍在继续消费。
8月份美国消费增速达到一年多来最快水平，本周公布的政府数据显示，汽车、服装和餐饮等类别的支出均有所增加。
为了维持消费，美国各个收入阶层的家庭正在想尽办法：动用住房净值，去食品银行领取免费食物，或者使用ChatGPT降低食品杂货开支。
里士满联邦储备银行行长汤姆·巴尔金也观察到了这种现象。他从企业财报中看到这一趋势，在与辖区内的企业和居民交谈时也有类似感受。该辖区从马里兰州一直延伸到南卡罗来纳州。
“日子开始有点紧了，物价在涨，工资却跟不上，但大家还是想维持原来的生活方式，”巴尔金在接受采访时表示，“消费者的足智多谋真是让我佩服。”
在亚特兰大北部郊区，61岁的Elizabeth Gentile和丈夫并不一定非得减少开支，但他们一直都过着量入为出的生活。如今，全美汽油平均价格超过每加仑4美元，这对夫妻在当地Kroger加油站采用了一个小窍门，一些人把这种方法称为“双车加油”。
他们会把家里的两辆车分别停在Kroger加油泵两侧，一辆车加完后把油枪递给另一人给第二辆车继续加，这样整个过程仍算一笔交易，从而可以享受每加仑最高1美元的优惠。
Gentile说：“如果我们加油时有别的车开过来，我们总会礼貌地解释我们在做什么。我们会笑着说，我们是在共享每加仑减1美元的加油积分。到目前为止，大家都能理解。”
到目前为止，美国的通胀已经连续六年处于巴尔金等美联储官员乃至许多普通美国人都认为过高的水平。
自2020年初以来，美国食品杂货价格已上涨32%，一磅碎牛肉的平均价格目前达到创纪录的7.16美元。疫情后的繁荣、关税以及如今的伊朗战争接连引发价格冲击，令家庭承受了沉重压力。工资如今也已经跟不上物价涨幅，美国劳工统计局数据显示，自3月份以来，工资增速一直落后于物价涨幅。
这种情况令消费者感到沮丧，消费者信心仍徘徊在今年早些时候创下的历史低点附近。不过，彭博经济研究和彭博行业研究最近对企业季度财报的分析发现，尽管存在这些压力，消费者状况还是有所改善。
包括 沃尔玛 在内的大型零售商称，一些消费者正在转向更便宜的商品、寻找折扣，并购买价格低于品牌商品的自有品牌产品。但Darden Restaurants Inc．的首席执行官上月也表示，他们旗下包括Olive Garden在内的休闲餐饮连锁店还是有很多回头客。
足智多谋
为了有钱花销，里士满联储的巴尔金所说的足智多谋可谓体现得五花八门。其中一种方式是“先买后付”服务。这类服务迅速走红，尤其受到年轻人的欢迎。根据里士满联储银行的研究，自2021年以来，该服务的年增速高达约20%。
来自亚特兰大Duluth郊区的教师Kenny Marbry则利用起了人工智能工具。他会把超市购物小票上传到ChatGPT，让它判断Kroger和山姆会员店哪一家更便宜，或者拍下商店整排货架的照片，让AI帮他评估哪种商品最划算。
38岁的Marbry估计，在聊天机器人助手以及自己因为比价养成的消费纪律的帮助下，他每个月能省下约100美元。
Marbry说：“现在我看到一个价格后很可能会问自己，‘我真的需要买吗？能不能去别的地方买得更便宜？或者我能不能自己做？’这些细小的决定累积起来影响很大，尤其是你要养活一家五口、想尽办法让每一美元都更经用的时候。”
对另一些人来说，去食品银行领吃的成了常态，这样能省下钱来应付其他开销。
美国规模最大的食品银行——Houston Food Bank的负责人Brian Greene表示：“住房援助和租金援助很难申请。食品援助要容易得多。”
碰撞维修专业人士协会执行董事Aaron Schulenburg表示，许多汽车车身维修店目前在议论，手头拮据的消费者宁愿忍受汽车上的小凹痕和擦碰，也不愿进行维修。他说，这至少部分上是因为保险成本大幅上升，如今2000美元的免赔额已经不再罕见。
Schulenburg说：“他们现在面临着财务上的取舍。在以前人们经济压力没那么大的时候，决定去把车修好要容易得多。”
面对平均已达到5万美元的惊人新车价格，为降低月供，美国人正越来越多地选择期限更长的汽车贷款。汽车服务公司Cox Automotive的数据显示，在8月份，31.3%的汽车贷款期限超过六年，创下历史新高，较一年前上升5.8个百分点。
“这提醒我们，人们考虑的始终是每月还款额，”Cox的执行分析师Erin Keating表示，“这相当惊人。他们会想，‘怎么做才能把月供降到让我能负担得起的水平？’”
投资和住房净值
较富裕的消费者则在动用疫情后大幅升值的资产。 摩根大通 研究所的一份报告显示，自2019年以来，从投资账户净取款的人所占比例已增加一倍。研究人员发现，尽管其中以较年 长和 更富裕的人群为首，但各年龄段和收入群体的取款都在增加，这表明“越来越多的年轻人也在利用投资财富进行消费”。
过去几年房价大幅上涨的房主则在以住房资产为抵押借款，以支付大额支出。根据美联储数据，第二季度以房屋净值作为抵押的贷款较上年同期增长9.4%，升至2017年以来最高水平。
Jefferies股票分析师表示，从历史上看，相当大一部分住房净值贷款被用于住房项目。如今30年期抵押贷款利率已超过7%，那些此前锁定很低利率的房主很可能会继续在房屋上投入大量资金。
与此同时，低收入家庭不得不举债度日。德克萨斯州 “不让孩子挨饿”组织委托进行的一项最新调查发现，在美国人口第二大州德克萨斯州，有39%的家长为了支付食品杂货开支而负债。
今年贷款需求之旺盛令Copper Basin Federal Credit Union总裁兼首席执行官Jessica Grostic感到意外。这家信用合作社服务于田纳西州和佐治亚州蓝岭山区的四个县。5月份和6月份，该信用合作社贷款业务创下纪录，而通常较为清淡的9月份，截至25日时表现已超过预期。
Grostic表示，越来越多的人开始使用一种贷款项目，该项目会根据客户的直接存款记录自动提供最高2000美元的贷款。
Grostic说：“人们有时急需现金来付账单，这很可怕。有时候一切都会突然崩塌。我只是不知道什么时候会发生。”

title: Astronomers get permission for mini-observatory
content:
A group of amateur astronomers have been given permission to set up a mini-observatory at a village hall.

Members of the Shropshire Astronomical Society (SAS) now plan to transfer over the out of use dome and telescope once used by the Irish Rangers at the Tern Hill army base near Market Drayton.

They have been based at Rodington Village Hall, near Shrewsbury, for 25 years but think the telescope will raise interest in astronomy.

In granting permission, Telford and Wrekin planners said the curved gloss white fibreglass dome used to house the telescope would be "somewhat unusual" but would add "some visual interest to the site.

In the group's application, the society's Stephen Szwajkun wrote: "It will be a first public astronomical observatory in the area and provide inspiration for the diverse residents of Telford and Wrekin as well as the wider area."

Society chairman Philip Osman said a permanent observatory would encourage participation and also give the group the opportunity to organise community outreach activities.

"The dome will be the only publicly accessible observatory in the county and we hope that this new facility will allow us to broaden our outreach activities and successfully engage with a new generation," he said.

Osman also said an agreement had been reached to purchase the mini observatory in May.

The domed structure is set to be a little less than 2.7m (8ft 9inches) tall and council officials were satisfied that the proposal would not result in unacceptable noise, disturbance or any other disruption for nearby residents.

They added that it was "not considered likely to result in a significant increase in traffic or parking demand".

Planners agreed that it would provide a useful additional community and educational facility.

This news was gathered by the Local Democracy Reporting Service which covers councils and other public service organisations.

title: Sinfield completes final ultramarathon challenge
content:
Sir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024.

Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final.

The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020.

Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us."

Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 UK Super League clubs along the way.

The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity.

Along the way he was surprised by royals, including The Prince and Princess of Wales and the Princess Royal, as well as famous names from the sporting world such as former England football manager Sir Gareth Southgate and Leeds boxer Josh Warrington.

Each day was split into 7km, hour-long blocks with an additional extra mile for members of the MND community to join.

Funds raised by the challenge will go towards the work of the MND Association, Leeds Hospitals Charity, My Name5 Doddie Foundation, Darby Rimmer Foundation, MND Scotland and the Irish MND Association.

Sinfield, 45, who played his entire professional career with Leeds Rhinos, is one of the most successful players in Super League history.

He and Burrow met at the Leeds Rhinos academy aged 14 and 12. They went on to win seven titles together with Leeds Rhinos.

Burrow's wife, Lindsey Burrow, told BBC Radio 4's PM that her late husband "would have been incredibly proud" of his friend.

"It's bittersweet that Rob's not here today to see Kevin finish his final challenge but Rob will be with us in spirit and it's just testimony to Kevin that he's so humbled to do this not just for Rob but for the whole MND community," Lindsey said.

"It's just incredible. I am in complete awe of the efforts of Kevin and his team over the last seven days, and not just over the last seven days but over the last seven years," she added.

Sinfield's son, Jack Sinfield, lined up in the Wakefield side seeking to clinch their first top-flight title since 1968.

title: I'm a wildlife cameraman but 'special' rare sightings can still take me by surprise
content:
A wildlife cinematographer and shark guide has spoken about the unexpected surprise and joy of seeing a humpback whale in the Celtic Deep just off the Welsh coast.

Dan Abbot, known as Sharkman Dan on his social media, shared a recording of the exciting moment just off the Pembrokeshire coast.

He has seen the large marine mammals before, on planned trips where humpback whale sightings are not as unusual, but this experience was "a complete surprise".

Lloyd Nelmes from Sea Trust said the sighting was "unusual for someone who works in the field... who probably has their eyes on the water every day", adding, "for a normal person, it's insanely rare".

Abbot guides blue shark snorkelling trips off of Pembrokeshire and was on a scheduled snorkelling trip in the Celtic Sea on 25 September when he discovered the rare find.

The group had just left the snorkelling site after seeing multiple sharks and were 25-30 miles offshore.

Abbot recalled seeing lots of feeding going on among bluefin tuna, dolphins and gannets which he said was not unusual in the waters there at this time of year.

When a guest on board "saw a whale blow in the distance", Abbot inititally suspected it was a minke or fin whale, the two most common whales in Welsh waters.

"I said if it's a big blow, then it's probably a fin whale," he said.

"So we then watched it blowing, quite far out, and slowly moved towards the area where there was lots of feeding going on because sometimes you can see whales lunge feeding."

"As we got a bit closer and parked the boat a bit to let things develop around us, I noticed that when it came up for a blow, it actually had white pectoral fin, which fin whales don't have," Abbot said.

"And then the other thing they don't do is they don't lift their tails out of the water, which humpbacks do. You could see barnacles around the front of the head, which fin whales don't have.

"I actually went quiet for a moment. At that point, it was pretty clear it was a humpback whale."

He continued: "I don't really get that excited, which sounds strange. I'm usually one of the quietest ones on the boat, but I think it was just because it was such a surprise to see that species.

"I'm a wildlife cameraman but when something happens like that unexpectedly and catches you off guard, there's something about it that kind of makes it even more special."

Guests on the boat were already in high spirits after the four-hour snorkelling trip, but Abbot said 'then to see a humpback whale was just an incredible way to finish the day".

Lloyd Nelmes, an aquarium manger and marine project officer with Sea Trust Wales, spotted a humpback whale in Pembrokeshire in 2024.

Nelmes said: "The whale jumped out right in front of us. It was incredible, and it's still probably my top wildlife moment of my life."

He explained that humpback whale sightings were rare but not unheard of in Welsh waters, with sightings happening once every two or three years.

Nelmes said the way to spot a humpback whale was by the overall shape, white pectoral fins, and knobbly skin also known as barnacles, as well as the whales' behaviour.

"We've seen humpbacks here on the rare occasion... but it seems to be becoming more common, which is awesome," he said.

"It's quite likely just an indication of how much food is about at the moment."

He said he had been on an "incredible" trip out to the Celtic Deep the day before Abbot's discovery and had seen six fin whales, tuna balling up and 1,000-plus dolphins, adding it was not too surprising that a humpack was "out there also making the most of the food".

title: OpenAI安全部门员工辞职 呼吁采取核电级别的防护措施
content:
OpenAI一名专注于人工智能安全的员工已从公司离职，并警告称，顶尖人工智能公司在降低风险方面做得还不够。
此前负责OpenAI安全团队透明度工作的David Robinson在为《 大西洋 月刊》撰写的一篇文章中称，这家ChatGPT开发商“一直通过反复试错发展壮大”。但是，这种方式不可避免会有失败的时候，随着AI技术的能力不断提升，这些失败造成的风险也在加大，他还以OpenAI未能阻止其人工智能在测试过程中失控作为例证。
Robinson在文章中写道：“我以前的同事都很聪明、工作努力，也努力做出正确的选择。但随着公司从一个产品发布冲向下一个产品发布，它并没有达到我认为所需要的谨慎程度。”他补充称，真正需要的是“第一次就做到更接近完美”。
最近几周，多家顶尖人工智能公司的员工都对该技术可能带来的灾难性风险发出警告。一些人甚至表示，AI有朝一日可能会消灭人类。
在这一背景下，Anthropic PBC首席执行官Dario Amodei呼吁放慢开发最前沿模型的速度，并表示其公司将引入第三方评估人员，协助审查以保证安全。业内其他人士，包括OpenAI的萨姆·奥尔特曼，也公开支持Amodei的计划。
Robinson在文章中表示，人工智能公司应该更像核电站那样运营，“设置多层冗余机制，并进行谨慎且耗时的规划，以免偶发且不可避免的人为错误打开通往灾难的大门。”
他说，目前“人工智能公司不知道该怎么做，但其他人知道。”
OpenAI一名发言人表示，该公司正在作出调整，以加强研究和测试环境的安全性，训练AI模型以负责任的方式完成任务，扩大与第三方评估人员的合作，并改进实时监控以发现模型令人担忧的行为。
这名发言人周六通过电子邮件表示，公司正在确保其模型的能力不会增强到超出OpenAI能够安全管理的程度。

title: 报道：特朗普指示动用纳税人资金投放颂扬其总统任期的广告
content:
据知情人士透露，美国总统特朗普亲自指示预算局局长动用纳税人资金投放电视广告，宣传他本人及其执政成果，由此敲定一份价值 2000 万美元的合同，资金取自国土安全部。
广告已在有线电视与各大广播电视网播出，覆盖福克斯新闻、CNN、MS Now；福克斯的橄榄球赛事，以及 CBS、ABC、NBC 的全国新闻节目，其中包括特朗普常看的《会见新闻界》。
知情人士称，特朗普迫切希望看到这些褒扬广告上线，并要求管理与预算办公室主任拉塞尔・沃思从政府内部筹措资金。预算办公室法律顾问马克・保莱塔与白宫法律顾问威尔・沙夫均表示，使用国土安全部资金此举合法。特朗普与白宫幕僚长苏西・怀尔斯，都就广告事宜与国土安全部长马克韦恩・马伦进行过沟通。
联邦档案显示，隶属于国土安全部的美国海关与边境保护局于 9 月 20 日，将这份合同授予马里兰州营销公司 LMD。
本文基于对 12 名知情人士的采访，他们要求匿名，讲述总统推动广告投放的相关安排。
这批由税款买单的广告，遭到民主党乃至部分共和党人的批评，认为此举可能违反联邦法律，禁止使用纳税人钱款用于 “宣传或鼓吹”。与此同时，特朗普还在动用其超级政治行动委员会 MAGA Inc． 的资金 —— 该机构在秋季伊始手握 4 亿美元，特朗普自 2024 年胜选后便持续为其筹款。
目前尚不清楚为何选择动用税款，而非超级政治行动委员会的资金投放广告。
白宫称这些广告属于公共服务公告，合规，因为广告中没有 “号召投票给某位候选人” 的内容。部分助手还强调，特朗普当前并未参选，试图以此反驳 “广告挪用公款违法” 的指责。
周三被记者追问时，特朗普表示：“如果有人说这件事不对，我愿意自掏腰包偿还这笔钱。”
他补充道：“但这些广告是为国家而做。你要明白，我不是在推举候选人。我不是宣传我自己，因为我没有参选。我是在宣传这个国家。”
据媒体追踪机构 AdImpact 与知情人士透露，目前至少已经播出 4 支广告，花费约 550 万美元，后续开支预计继续增加。其中一支广告配上 JMSN（本名克里斯蒂安・贝里沙伊）的歌曲《Love Me》，画面展示特朗普。另一支广告与特朗普 2024 年竞选视频几乎完全一致，谴责总统眼中的敌对 “恶人”。使用原本竞选素材，让批评者不认同白宫 “仅为公共服务公告” 的说法。
第三支广告主题涉及伊朗战事，出镜人员包含特朗普与国防部长皮特・赫格塞思。
常规公共服务公告一般会标注出资机构。而这批广告全部使用特殊标语：“由美国政府出资”。
8 月 7 日的会议
8 月 7 日，特朗普在椭圆形办公室会见几名共和党策略师、首席政治顾问詹姆斯・布莱尔以及怀尔斯。常年为他整理正面报道的助理娜塔莉・哈普也在场。
当时共和党候选人已经焦虑数月，等待特朗普最终批准动用超级政治行动委员会资金资助中期选举候选人。但这场会议上，特朗普更想看关于自己的视频素材。
他吩咐哈普，向众人展示他喜欢的影像素材。哈普在平板上调出白宫数字团队制作的一系列视频：特朗普站在庞大人群前、特朗普身旁的海军一号、头顶飞过战机的特朗普。其中一段视频是 UFC 总裁达纳・怀特在 2024 共和党全国代表大会上称特朗普是 “我见过最坚韧、最顽强的人”，此后特朗普反复开心地提起这句话。
特朗普明确表示，他计划亲自到场为中期选举候选人助选，但同时，助手制作的广告必须把宣传他本人的总统任期放在核心位置。
当月晚些时候曾有报道，MAGA Inc 原本计划大规模投放以特朗普为中心的中期选举广告。但后续，一家和特朗普有关联的非营利机构投放了包含达纳・怀特那段评价的广告，花费不到 6 万美元，主要在 9 月 2 日、3 日于华盛顿地区播放，确保特朗普能够看到。
几周之后，一批颂扬特朗普的广告开始在全美播出 —— 这次资金来自纳税人，由海关与边境保护局拨付。其中就包括《Love Me》版本广告。
在这批公费广告播出期间，MAGA 只直接资助了一场特定竞选，为得州参议院竞选投入超 2000 万美元。另外两家隶属于 MAGA Inc 的新机构 ——No Going Back PAC 以及 Safety and Affordability PAC 近期成立，已经在全美各地竞选广告上投入并预留超过 1.63 亿美元。但这些广告里特朗普出镜很少。
白宫新闻办公室发来一份未署名声明回应本文：“这些公共服务公告旨在提醒美国人热爱自己的国家，明白是什么让这个国家值得守护 —— 在本土、边境与海外。”
白宫称投放这类广告存在先例。白宫通讯主任 9 月 27 日在 X 平台发文：“别让假新闻肆意抹黑我们正在电视播出的重磅公共服务公告。”
白宫邮件称：“总统公共服务公告并非新鲜事物”，将这批广告类比往届政府宣传医保政策的宣传片，或是伍德罗・威尔逊总统一战时期的宣传项目。
美国政府问责局此前就发现过多起违反反宣传规定的案例，包含两任总统执政时期。但那些案例均为政策宣传，而非聚焦总统本人的广告。
资金拨付
9 月 19 日，管理与预算办公室将 2000 万海关与边境保护局资金划转至名为 “宏伟法案纪念活动” 预算科目，这笔广告资金得以启用。
次日，海关与边境保护局和总部位于马里兰州哥伦比亚市的营销公司 LMD 签署 2000 万美元合同。知情人士称，实际广告时段采购由另一家公司 LMO 完成，该人士无权对外公开发声。
管理与预算办公室发言人拒绝对本报道置评。国土安全部发言人仅表示：“国土安全部遵守所有适用的采购规则，并向所有决策者同步信息。所有采购决定均依法作出。”LMD 与 LMO 公司发言人没有回应置评请求。
广告最初小范围投放，很快在有线电视与广播电视网高频滚动播出。AdImpact 数据显示，广告大量出现在晨间节目如《早安美国》《CBS 晨间》，也登陆《吉米夜现场》《极速前进》等娱乐节目；其中一支广告在福克斯周末橄榄球赛事反复播放。
这不是特朗普政府首笔耗资巨大、充满争议的电视宣传项目。2025 年时任国土安全部长克里斯蒂・诺姆出镜参与耗资超 2 亿美元的政府广告宣传活动。广告播出后招致特朗普不满，也成为诺姆被解职的理由之一。
这批宣传广告上线之际，特朗普的民意支持率走低。《纽约时报》民调显示，其支持率大约 37%，数月维持低位。共和党人愈发担心民主党拿下参众两院控制权，同时在各州议会选举大获全胜。
特朗普依旧持续为华盛顿各项建设项目、白宫相关项目以及他未来总统图书馆大规模筹款。上个月他承诺，中期选举可能投入 4 亿至 5 亿美元，但强调超级政治行动委员会的资金由他掌控。
特朗普称：“这是我掌控的钱。”

title: 台积电探讨与马斯克 Terafab 项目开展合作
content:
半导体巨头台积电正考虑与埃隆・马斯克的 Terafab 项目开展合作，在美国建立先进的端到端半导体制造产能。据通讯刊物 Culpium 的独家报道，该消息后续得到马斯克在 X 平台证实，两家企业正在洽谈组建合资企业，以此扩大美国本土半导体制造规模。
该方案的设想是由台积电负责发展晶圆制造能力，Terafab 则提供资金支持、股权投资、采购协议以及保障新晶圆厂产能运转所需的其他配套条件。部分企业管理层认为英特尔或许无法兑现承诺，因此 Terafab 需要双渠道获取技术能力。
此前报道显示，英特尔已经和 Terafab 达成合作。在位于奥斯汀的马斯克 Terafab AI 芯片综合体项目中，特斯拉将成为英特尔 14A 工艺节点的首个主要客户。但这笔交易的细节尚不明确，包括 Terafab 是否能够获得 14A 节点的工艺开发工具包（PDK）授权。
台积电与英特尔理论上可以共存于 Terafab 项目当中，但需要注意：台积电或许不会把自家最尖端半导体技术带到美国，其最先进制程仍将保留在总部，Terafab 只会作为次级项目。英特尔和台积电或许会在技术需求上形成互补，但这一点目前尚未确定。
Terafab 的目标是把整套芯片制造流程整合在同一厂区内。该工厂计划在单一基地集成逻辑芯片制造、存储芯片、封装、测试以及掩膜版生产多个环节。行业惯例中，上述工序一般分散在多家不同专业工厂、不同企业完成，因此这种模式十分罕见。
仅仅投入资金并不能保证项目成功。从零打造一座具备竞争力的晶圆厂需要数年落地周期，设备需要向阿斯麦、泛林半导体、科磊、东京电子等厂商采购；这些设备商往往会提前数年接收订单，之后才会向台积电、三星、英特尔交付设备。因此，搭建设备、原材料与零部件供应链也需要数年时间。 报道称 Terafab 已经向上述设备厂商下订制造设备，预计数年后才能产出首批硅片。

title: 苹果将加强Mac隐私控制 警告AI智能体带来的风险上升
content:
苹果公司表示，计划为Mac用户推出新的隐私控制措施，并警告称，向包括AI智能体在内的第三方软件授予广泛的数据访问权限所带来的风险正在上升。
这家iPhone制造商周五在一份声明中表示，将推出更多控制措施，以确保希望向某款应用授予“完全磁盘访问权限”——也就是允许其完全访问系统文件、邮件、信息和浏览历史——的用户只能通过“非常明确的用户操作”来完成授权。
苹果表示：“我们致力于确保用户在授予此类访问权限之前，能够清楚了解这些风险，从而就自己的数据和隐私作出知情决定。”
能够在无人监督的情况下代表用户执行操作的AI智能体正迅速走红。OpenAI本周早些时候表示，超过3500万人正在使用其智能体工具ChatGPT Work和Codex，高于7月份的1000万人。与此同时，Meta Platforms Inc．的Muse上月推出后登上应用商店下载排行榜榜首。这些智能体往往需要用户授予其访问个人文件和应用的广泛权限才能正常工作。
苹果在声明中没有点名具体程序或开发商，但表示，随着“AI智能体的能力和自主性不断增强”，“与这种级别访问权限相关的风险将大幅上升”。

title: 贝森特称国债收益率上升符合全球趋势 不必感到惊恐
content:
尽管通胀担忧已推动一些基准收益率升至20多年来最高水平，但美国财长斯科特·贝森特表示，近期美国国债收益率上升符合全球趋势，不必对此感到惊恐。
贝森特在周六发表的采访文章中表示：“如果我们看到的是某种美国特有的上涨，我会感到担忧。我们并没有看到人们卖出美国国债、转而购买德国国债或日本国债。”
他说：“我无法控制债券市场。我能做的是让人们慢下来，认真思考。”
贝森特还称赞美国为救助阿根廷而采取的金融干预措施，并表示未来仍有可能实施类似救助。
他说：“我认为，阿根廷局势的稳定推动拉丁美洲发生了翻天覆地的变化，这可能是跨世代的，甚至可能是历史上第一次，从来没有这么多拉丁美洲国家与美国结盟。所以，我们有没有可能再这么做？当然可能。”
特朗普政府去年买入阿根廷比索，并向特朗普的盟友、阿根廷总统哈维尔·米莱领导的政府提供了200亿美元的货币互换额度，此举帮助阿根廷捍卫了本币汇率，并避免了一场全面的经济危机。
美国还曾帮助日本支撑日元汇率，包括两国实施自1998年以来首次协调买入日元的干预行动。
尽管周五疲软的美国就业数据带来一定缓解，但美国国债已经历了持续数月的抛售潮，本周一度推动基准10年期美国国债收益率升至2002年以来最高水平。
旷日持久的伊朗战争推高燃料价格，加之市场对美国财政状况的担忧以及人工智能支出激增，共同推高了借贷成本。
生活成本一直是选民关注的一个关键问题。创纪录的柴油价格以及目前高于7%的抵押贷款利率都给选民造成沉重压力，也给特朗普和共和党带来更大的在11月份中期选举中失利、从而令民主党取得国会两院控制权的风险。
贝森特认为，伊朗战争产生的连锁影响掩盖了美国经济的内在强劲表现，并指出消费者支出“强劲”，工资中位数增速与整体通胀率大致相当。
贝森特还淡化了对人工智能推动泡沫的担忧。他认为，微软、Alphabet旗下谷歌以及Meta Platforms Inc．等主要企业正在投入大量资本，并为Anthropic和OpenAI等公司带来显著的营收增长。
关于已进入第八个月的伊朗战争，贝森特说：“我们终将度过这场伊朗冲突，我认为石油供应会变得更加充足。能源冲击将会消退。”

title: Debris found from plane that went missing off US coast
content:
US authorities have found debris from a medical transport aircraft that went missing with six people on board.

The Federal Aviation Administration told the BBC it had lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane just after 01:00 local time (05:00 GMT) on Saturday, while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston, Massachusetts.

The search for survivors continues off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, the US Coast Guard said.

Authorities have notified the next of kin of those on the flight, four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals.

"Search crews located a debris field confirmed to be from the aircraft off the coast of Nantucket," the US Coast Guard said in an update on Saturday night. It added that ships, helicopters and planes were involved in searches that would through continue the night.

The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International at 01:30 EDT (05:30 GMT).

According to the tail number released by the Coast Guard, the plane belonged to Latitude Air Ambulances, a company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.

Among those on board were two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

The crew flew to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, who are not Canadian, Togeretz said.

FlightAware's tracker shows the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

Radio transmissions shows trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net.

"You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?," the air traffic controller asked. "Are you declaring an emergency, or no?"

The pilot's response was inaudible.

"You're coming in a little weak so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not," the air traffic controller said, according to the Globe.

The air traffic controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

An area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews just after 01:00 EDT to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue".

The dispatcher later said "the aircraft has lost radio and radar".

The Coast Guard said it would provide an update on Sunday morning local time.

title: Noel Gallagher guitar sells for £12,000 at auction
content:
A guitar which originally belonged to Noel Gallagher has been sold for £12,000 at auction.

The limited edition Epiphone instrument in Manchester City blue was one of a number of items put up for sale by the son of Huw Richards, a former front-of-house sound engineer with the band.

Another of the items in his collection, a Kangol rain jacket produced for the band's touring personnel, sold for £2,000.

But a set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m were pulled from the auction last week, after the band filed an injunction.

That collection of recordings, known as The Desk Tapes, includes recordings of 63 live shows, soundchecks and more than 100 hours of rehearsals from the band's rise and rise in the 1990s.

Littleton Auctions in Worcestershire, which handled the auction, said it had agreed to postpone the sale until the legal dispute had been resolved.

The Epiphone guitar was made in 1997 and the auctioneer said it is believed to be one of five identical guitars gifted to Noel Gallagher by the manufacturer.

It was later given to Richards, Littleton Auctions said.

A collection of 11 framed platinum discs, from the Oasis album What's the Story Morning Glory which also belonged to Richards sold for £2,000.

They had been presented to him by Creation Records to recognise United Kingdom sales of more than 3.3 million copies.

Other items in the Richards collection to sell at the auction included tour itineraries, promotional material and a Be Here Now wrist watch.

A number of other sellers also had memorabilia up for sale at the auction, including a rare original concert ticket for The Rain, the Manchester band which later became Oasis.

That sold for £2,400 and an early Oasis demo tape sold for £3,600.

A collection of early Oasis photos sold for £5,400 and a pair of leather shoes which once belonged to Noel Gallagher sold for £1,200.

But a baby grand piano which featured in the artwork for the Supersonic single, which was valued at between £100,000 and £150,000 failed to sell.

title: OpenAI安全部门员工辞职 呼吁对AI采取核电级别的防护措施
content:
OpenAI一名专注于人工智能安全的员工已从公司离职，并警告称，顶尖人工智能公司在降低风险方面做得还不够。
此前负责OpenAI安全团队透明度工作的大卫·罗宾森（David Robinson）在为《大西洋月刊》撰写的一篇文章中称，这家ChatGPT开发商“一直通过反复试错发展壮大”。但是，这种方式不可避免会有失败的时候，随着AI技术的能力不断提升，这些失败造成的风险也在加大，他还以OpenAI未能阻止其人工智能在测试过程中失控作为例证。
罗宾森在文章中写道：“我以前的同事都很聪明、工作努力，也努力做出正确的选择。但随着公司从一个产品发布冲向下一个产品发布，它并没有达到我认为所需要的谨慎程度。”他补充称，真正需要的是“第一次就做到更接近完美”。
最近几周，多家顶尖人工智能公司的员工都对该技术可能带来的灾难性风险发出警告。一些人甚至表示，AI有朝一日可能会消灭人类。
在这一背景下，Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪呼吁放慢开发最前沿模型的速度，并表示其公司将引入第三方评估人员，协助审查以保证安全。业内其他人士，包括OpenAI的萨姆·奥特曼，也公开支持Amodei的计划。
罗宾森在文章中表示，人工智能公司应该更像核电站那样运营，“设置多层冗余机制，并进行谨慎且耗时的规划，以免偶发且不可避免的人为错误打开通往灾难的大门。”
他说，目前“人工智能公司不知道该怎么做，但其他人知道。”

title: 韩国一储蓄银行遭黑客攻击，约4万客户数据泄露
content:
韩国耶加兰储蓄银行（Yegaram Savings Bank）表示，9月30日，一名身份不明的黑客入侵了存放客户数据的服务器，导致约4万名客户的个人信息泄露。
泄露的信息包括客户姓名、出生日期和联系方式；银行仍在确定受影响的确切人数。
该行怀疑黑客利用了其使用的外部软件解决方案中的远程漏洞。

title: 美国据悉将向维斯特拉公司提供42亿美元贷款，以提升核电产能
content:
知情人士周六表示，美国将向维斯特拉公司（Vistra）提供约42亿美元贷款，以提升其核电发电量。
该消息人士称，美国能源部长赖特将于周一在位于俄亥俄州伊利湖畔的维斯特拉核电站宣布这一消息。
这笔贷款将用于提高发电量，即对维斯特拉旗下四座核电站中的至少三座进行“功率提升”，此举无需获得美国核管理委员会的新许可。
美国能源部和维斯特拉公司尚未立即回应置评请求。

title: Police name two men who died in workplace incident near rural road
content:
Two men who died after a workplace incident at a road in County Down on Friday have been named by police.

Joseph Hobbs, 23, from Comber and Mark Glover, 38, from Ballygowan received medical treatment but were pronounced dead at the scene.

The incident happened on the Ballygowan Road in Crossnacreevy at about 10:45 BST on Friday.

Police said their sympathies remained "with all those affected by this tragic incident".

The police said they will continue to work with Northern Ireland's Health and Safety Executive (HSENI) as enquiries continue.

On Friday, Democratic Unionist Party MP Gavin Robinson said on social media that his thoughts were with the men's families and loved ones "at this devastating time".

Alliance Party MLA Peter McReynolds said it was "an absolutely heartbreaking incident" and his thoughts were with the families and emergency service personnel.

title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
content:
Alison Hammond has said she is home and "feeling so much better" after she went to hospital for a heart check-up after leaving ITV's This Morning midway through Friday's show.

The presenter, 51, left the programme during its live broadcast, appearing to clutch her chest as she was helped off set by co-host Dermot O'Leary. He later told viewers she was "feeling a little unwell".

Soon after Hammond said she had "a little bit of a palpitation" and was undergoing tests.

In a video on Instagram on Saturday, she said she was "all OK, all-clear, which would mean I had a massive panic attack on live TV. I mean, the shame of it."

"It felt very real to me. I'm really new to panic attacks, so I need to learn more about it," she added.

The Birmingham-born presenter, who also co-hosts The Great British Bake Off, thanked NHS staff and her colleagues at This Morning, including O'Leary.

"It's really warmed my heart actually. I didn't necessarily want to be on the news or anything like that but this is a new world to me," she said.

"I'm going to take stock, take some rest and I'll see you soon."

Friday's edition of the ITV show began at 10:00 BST with Hammond and her regular co-host O'Leary at the helm, before she left at 11:30 during a segment about pets.

O'Leary, 53, addressed her absence when the show returned from a break, saying: "Welcome back to This Morning, Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she's just had to duck out. Hopefully she'll be back."

He later updated viewers that she would, in fact, not be returning, "so I'll be here for the rest of the show".

Hammond rose to fame as contestant on Channel 4 reality show Big Brother before appearing on I'm A Celebrity and Strictly Come Dancing.

She became a co-host in This Morning in 2021, and was part of the team that won a National Television Award for best daytime programme the following year.

She joined Bake Off in 2023 and took over from the late Paul O'Grady on For the Love of Dogs in 2024.

title: Police searching for mum of baby girl found on shoreline tell her not to be afraid to call
content:
Police searching for the mother of a newborn baby girl whose body was found on a north Wales shoreline have set up a special phone line, urging her to contact them.

A member of the public found the body on the Menai Strait shoreline near Siliwen Road in Bangor, Gwynedd, on Sunday shortly before 17:00 BST.

In an update on Thursday, North Wales Police said a post-mortem examination revealed the newborn was a girl, adding that she may have been in the water for up to a few weeks.

Supt Llinos Davies from North Wales Police said a specialist would take a call from the woman directly and could support her confidentially and told the woman not to be afraid to speak to the police.

"We understand that you may be scared to come forward, but we urge you to contact us," Davies said.

"I want to reassure you that your welfare and safety continues to be our priority and utmost concern and that you receive any medical attention and support you may need.

"Whatever has happened, you do not have to face this on your own," she added.

The director of midwifery and women's services for Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board Fiona Giraud last week also appealed directly to the mother to come forward.

Davies said a trained specialist whose role was "simply to listen, understand, and help" would speak to her.

"This is not a conversation you need to be afraid of. You will be treated with compassion, dignity and respect.

"If making that call feels too difficult, please consider telling somebody you trust. A friend, family member, neighbour, healthcare professional, or anyone who can help you reach out."

The phone number is to strictly only be used by the mother to seek specialist help, North Wales Police said.

"We are concerned the baby's mother may not be in a position to reach out for support, so we are appealing directly to her, the father and those who may have knowledge, such as friends, family, neighbours or colleagues, to contact us," Davies said.

She added that all names provided would be treated "with the utmost discretion" and urges people not to speculate on the circumstances surrounding the baby's death.

Officers are appealing to anyone who routinely walked in the Siliwen Road and Ashley Fields areas of Bangor between 30 August and 27 September to come forward.

They are also asking for any photos or videos taken in and around the Menai Straits shoreline in Siliwen within the same time frame to be uploaded to the force's major incident public portal.

title: Republic of Ireland news conference ends abruptly amid accusations
content:
For more than 11 minutes of Saturday's pre-match news conference, Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson fielded questions centred on Sunday's Nations League Group B3 'home' game against Israel in Serbia.

The Icelander revealed that Dara O'Shea - captain in place of the injured Nathan Collins - was not with the squad, as his wife was due to give birth. He may arrive back in Backa Topola prior to Sunday's 19:45 BST kick-off.

Hallgrimsson also gave his thoughts on the strain of this four-game international window and reflected on Thursday's 2-2 draw against Austria.

As the first section of the media conference, which is allowed to be broadcast live, was ending, the mood soured.

One reporter tried to quiz Hallgrimsson on his thoughts about the incident on Wednesday when a co-pilot attacked a pilot on a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.

The Republic of Ireland manager was also asked by another journalist about alleged racism by Irish players during last Sunday's 3-0 win over Israel in Hungary and refused to give up the microphone.

Promptly, the news conference was brought to a close by Football Association of Ireland (FAI) head of communications Kieran Crowley after calling those allegations "completely untrue".

The allegations of racism by an Irish player comes after it was confirmed the FAI is investigating reports of racist abuse directed towards Republic of Ireland striker Adam Idah by Israel fans in Debrecen.

Minutes before the news conference was brought to an abrupt halt, Hallgrimsson insisted he would not be drawn on either matter and would not "get involved in that as others will process that".

"It is a game with a lot of emotions attached," Hallgrimsson said.

"I haven't read anything and it's not something I want to get involved with. It goes to a process, both in our department and with Uefa.

"Something was reported by both teams so I just hope we can focus on football and football will be the winner after this.

"I have not gone into details looking at this as I have enough to think about."

The Republic of Ireland boss revealed the team have taken to a group prayer before leaving the dressing room before recent games "just to cool our heads before we go on to the pitch" and said that has been led by midfielder Conor Coventry whom he joked is now known within the squad as "Brother Coventry".

It has been a challenging international window for the Republic of Ireland with the Israel double-header dominating discourse in Irish football.

Since the teams were drawn together in February, a 'Stop The Game' campaign was launched by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine to boycott the fixtures in protest of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war.

'Togetherness is stronger than individuals' - Hallgrimsson

Before last week's 'home' game for Israel in Hungary, goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the fixtures, saying "it would be wrong to participate" while a vote by players to play the games passed by a "significant majority", according to FAI chief executive David Courell.

There were protests during the game against Austria in Dublin on Thursday, with tennis balls thrown on to the pitch and a protester briefly interrupting the game when he ran on to the turf, waving a Palestine flag.

Hallgrimmson said under the circumstances, it will be a "a big win for this group and the association if we go through undamaged".

"The most pleasing thing for me is to see the togetherness and how they stand up for each other. Whatever they have done, they have done it with respect to the situation, to each other and after this, this bond of brothers will be stronger than ever. All the obstacles this group will face in the future will be lesser than it is.

"When we look back, this camp will be a moment we grew the most and stepped up as leaders, supported each other and stuck together. The power of togetherness is stronger than individuals."

title: Teenager taken to hospital after Glasgow shopping centre gang attack
content:
A teenager who was attacked by a gang of youths inside a Glasgow shopping centre has been treated in hospital for his injuries.

Video posted on social media shows the young man, who was using a crutch and wearing a medical boot, being knocked to the ground, then repeatedly punched and kicked inside the St Enoch Centre on Friday afternoon.

A second person was also pushed to the ground but security staff intervened.

Police Scotland said the 19-year-old was taken to hospital and officers were reviewing CCTV footage to identify his assailants.

The attackers had run off by the time officers arrived and the injured man, who was bleeding from a head wound, was initially helped by shoppers and security staff.

The St Enoch Centre is located inside the Glasgow city centre dispersal zone which was established in March as part of a crackdown on crime and anti-social behaviour.

Officers are able to ask groups of two or more to leave the designated area if their behaviour is "impacting on the safety and well-being" of others, and they can be banned from returning for 24 hours.

The attack came just a few days after it was confirmed that the dispersal zone powers would be extended into December.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "An investigation is under way after police received a report of a disturbance involving a number of males in the St Enoch Centre, Glasgow.

"A 19-year-old male was taken to hospital. Officers have been reviewing CCTV images and enquiries are ongoing to locate and identify those involved. Police are following a positive line of inquiry."

title: Greens would offer two-year jobs to unemployed under-24s
content:
Young people would be offered a guaranteed two-year job within four months of leaving education or training, under a new proposal unveiled by the Green Party.

Announcing the policy at the party's conference in Brighton, co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said there were a million "bored, desperate and lost" young people who were out of work, training or education.

Under the proposed scheme, youngsters would be offered posts in the private sector, with the government paying half their salary.

The Greens have not specified a budget for the policy, but have argued it would reduce spending on welfare and boost tax receipts from employment.

The party says it would initially target the plan in areas with the fewest jobs openings for young people, citing Rotherham, Ceredigion, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Broxtowe and South Staffordshire, with an ambition to roll it out nationwide.

Employers would be exempt from paying National Insurance contributions, but would have to provide in-job training, the party says.

The party is seeking to pitch the plan as more ambitious than the government's own scheme, which subsidises six-month job placements for benefit claimants who have been looking for work for 18 months.

Ali also criticised ministers for previously suggesting youngsters refusing a role under that scheme could lose access to benefits, telling activists: "Threatening young people with cuts to Universal Credit if they don't accept short-term work placements - that's not a youth strategy."

He added: "Working class kids should be able to dream. But more than dream, they should have a genuine chance of making those dreams a reality.

The number of 16-24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training has been rising since the Covid pandemic, with figures reaching almost one million.

A long-awaited report into the problem by former Labour minister Alan Milburn is expected to be published this autumn.

In her own speech to the conference, Ali's fellow co-deputy leader Rachel Millward said the Greens would immediately bring both Thames Water and South East Water back into public ownership.

She argued this could be done without paying compensation to shareholders, pointing to water supply problems and a lack of new reservoirs.

Andy Burnham has promised to bring water under greater public control, but has stopped short of announcing plans to nationalise any water companies.

Millward told the conference the prime minister was "making a mistake" and his "10-year plan of gentle threats and vague notions of control is not enough".

"We need public ownership now, and we have all the tools we need to make it happen," she said.

South East Water said it was "focused on delivering on our commitments by investing £1.9 billion into local infrastructure and resilience over the next five years.

"We support working closely with the communities we serve and are accountable to, so that we can provide the best possible service for customers".

Thames Water has been approached for a response.

title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected
content:
A project which aims to restore ancient woodlands in Sussex has hit a significant "milestone" with over 5,500 trees now recorded.

Since March 2024, volunteers with the Lost Woods project have been recording ancient, veteran and notable trees across a 121-sq-miles (314-sq-km) area from Lewes to Storrington.

According to the latest figures, they have now recorded 5,570 trees, a number which Lost Woods outreach adviser, Bob Epsom, said is more than "we expected" and signifies a "milestone" for the project.

"When we look at the map of it, we can see the new clusters of trees being added...that's where the volunteers have been active," he said.

The Lost Woods is a partnership with four charities: Woodland Trust, Action in Rural Sussex, Sussex Wildlife Trust and Small Woods Association.

The work, funded by the National Lottery Heritage Fund, is part of a wider Lost Woods restoration programme which Epsom said comprises "19 individual projects".

About 20 volunteers are each given a square kilometre area to cover, and once recorded and verified, trees are added to the Ancient Tree Inventory which has been mapping the oldest and most important trees in the UK for 20 years.

The volunteers are working to find and record every ancient and veteran tree in the project area by next year, and Epsom, who leads the team, said they still "have a reasonable amount to cover".

Of the 5,570 trees recorded, there were 348 ancient trees, those that are in the third and final stage of their lives, and 2,467 notable trees, mature trees which are large in comparison with other trees around them.

The biggest proportion of trees, 2,743, are veteran, survivors which have developed some of the features found on ancient trees.

The remainder fall into a different category of tree.

According to Epsom, these trees are "very important for the landscape, (and) very important for biodiversity" because of their fungi.

Epsom said the mapping process was "only the first step", and that ultimately, there was a wider goal.

He said: "We need to make sure that trees are recognised, cared for and protected so that they can continue to support wildlife and communities for generations to come."
