title: Suppliers pile pressure on government over energy bills
content:
The government should take immediate action to help those struggling with energy bills this winter, the suppliers' trade body has said.

Energy UK said domestic gas prices, which rose on Thursday, and forecasts of steep rises in January meant inaction would lead to a longer-term, more costly and deeper crisis.

Figures revealed by the BBC earlier this week showed forecasters predicting a 16% rise in domestic energy prices in the new year for 20 million households on variable tariffs affected by regulator Ofgem's price cap.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the government was considering any measure that took the pressure off.

Households in England, Scotland and Wales on variable energy tariffs set by Ofgem's price cap, which puts a maximum price on each unit of gas and electricity, were hit with a 4% price increase at the start of October.

That is the equivalent of about £60 per year - or £5 per month - taking an annual bill to £1,723 for the typical household using both electricity and gas and paying by direct debit if this level was sustained for a year.

But forecasts show a far greater increase is possible for bills in January. Consultancy Cornwall Insight said its latest forecast suggested the same typical annual bill would rise to £1,999.

Energy UK said it accepted the government had already provided some support. VAT on electricity bills was cut on Thursday, and some levies were cancelled or shifted into taxation earlier this year.

But the trade body said these savings had been wiped out by high wholesale prices, paid by suppliers, that were the result in part of international events - namely conflict in the Middle East and the disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

It said bills were soaring as they had in 2022 when they were driven up by the impact of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

"We cannot afford to wait for the same scale of crisis before acting again. We must heed the lessons from that time," said Dhara Vyas, chief executive of Energy UK.

She said that the urgent intervention needed was highlighted by growing levels of customer debt, the cost of which now added an average of £67 a year to everyone's bills.

On Thursday, the boss of supplier EDF Energy, Simone Rossi, warned that the UK was "walking into a second energy crisis" and Vyas said that action was needed before bills jumped again.

"Last-minute emergency interventions run the risk of being badly targeted and costing us all more," she said.

Energy UK is calling for government measures including:

targeted support over and above the £150 Warm Home Discount, given to people on benefits, which would eventually lead to the introduction of a discounted social tariff

a debt relief scheme for the most severely affected households as part of a strategy that will also help prevent debt build-up among new tenants and homeowners

removing more levies from electricity bills and shifting them to taxation, as part of a wider move to electrification

Adam Scorer, chief executive of charity National Energy, which campaigns against fuel poverty, told BBC Breakfast he agreed with what Energy UK's analysis.

"[The increase in debt is] not more people getting into debt, that's more poor people getting into more serious levels of debt."

He added: "Until you do something about that, there's no way forward, there's no breathing space, there's no future for households who can't see their way beyond debt."

At the Labour Party conference last week, Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the BBC that he would not call Rossi's crisis warning an overstatement, adding that the cost of home energy, as well as petrol and diesel, was "very difficult indeed".

"We're looking at any measure that can give people breathing space, that can take the pressure off," he said.

How will you be affected by the price cap rise? Do you have a story to share?

title: EV drivers love their cars, but some passengers feel sick - this could be why
content:
Lola Baird has just asked her boyfriend to pull over. Forty minutes into a journey and she's feeling "overwhelmed" by nausea - and can't stop herself throwing up on the ground next to his car.

Lola, 24, from north London, had never experienced motion sickness until her boyfriend bought an electric vehicle (EV) two years ago. Ever since, she's been feeling "very nauseous" when he takes her on long car journeys.

It's become so severe she's even asked him to change his car.

Lola isn't alone. Other people told BBC News that they or their children notice feeling more car sick when sitting as a passenger in an electric vehicle. But at the same time, many EV drivers say it's not been a concern.

So what could explain these reports of motion sickness?

Dr Irene Di Giulio, senior lecturer in anatomy and biomechanics at King's College London whose research includes motion sickness, says research so far suggests some people experience more severe motion sickness in electric vehicles than in non-electric vehicles.

It's something Dr Nicholas Hac, a neurologist at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago who specialises in dizziness and vertigo, has also heard from some of his patients. "They just notice that they're much more likely or prone to be motion sick" in electric vehicles, he says.

"I've heard about it many, many, many times," he adds, saying about two patients a month specifically reference feeling motion sick in electric vehicles.

But research into any possible link is still in its early stages, and some academics say there isn't sufficient evidence to say anything definitive.

Dr Bill Yates, who has researched motion sickness at the University of Pittsburgh, says the body of research is "pretty sketchy at this point".

"There's some anecdotal information, but not a lot of really serious, extensive studies done yet," he says.

'Wonderful to drive... but my daughter gets unwell'

When Mark Quigg was looking at options for a new car last year, an electric vehicle seemed like the best choice because of the lower running costs.

Mark, 45, from Lincolnshire, says his shiny new electric vehicle has been "wonderful" to drive - but he quickly noticed that his nine-year-old daughter's motion sickness got much worse in it.

She only used to get motion sick on their 600-mile drives to France during the school holidays, but now he says even the 30-minute trip to the nearest city makes his daughter feel unwell.

On one recent journey, he says his daughter even threw up, which had never happened before.

Motion sickness doesn't affect all EV passengers - many owners got in touch with BBC News to say they and their relatives don't get sick in electric vehicles. Others said they felt less sick in EVs compared with traditional combustion engine cars.

Vicky Edmonds, the CEO of EVA England, an association for electric vehicle drivers, says motion sickness isn't a concern among her members. "This has never come up as an issue," she says.

But Chinese electric vehicle maker XPeng, which has showrooms across the UK, has previously publicly addressed the issue, external, telling people who've noticed a link between electric vehicles and travel sickness that "it's a fair question, and it's not your imagination". It's caused by "side effects of how electric cars are engineered," it adds.

What could cause it?

Motion sickness is caused by "a mismatch in sensory cues," Hac says. Our bodies rely on three main sensory inputs to show that we're moving, which come from what we see, what our inner ear's balance system perceives, and what fibres in our body sense, he says. When one of these is in conflict with the others - like if you're looking at your phone so you don't see visual signs of movement out of the window - that can cause motion sickness.

Research suggests several reasons why it may be more severe in electric vehicles.

Humans have adapted to associate sound with movement in vehicles, experts explain. Because electric vehicles don't have the auditory cues and vibrations from the engine that we're used to, which indicate when the car is accelerating, this could trigger motion sickness, Di Giulio says.

EV motors deliver maximum power straight away without needing to reach particular revs or shift through gears - which for passengers can come across as sharp or abrupt.

Another reason is regenerative braking, the process whereby when drivers release the accelerator, the motor starts acting as a generator. This creates resistance that slows the car down and also produces electricity that can be stored in the battery. The accelerator needs to be released gently, or it can lead to harsh deceleration.

The capability of EVs to accelerate and decelerate so sharply can feel very uncomfortable to those used to conventional cars.

"It forces the person to perhaps feel like they're rocking back and forth for that brief moment when the speed of the car suddenly changes," says Hac.

This is something Carolyn Le, 24, from California, has noticed. She gets "horrendous" motion sickness when her friend drives her in his electric vehicle in busy cities, she says. The regenerative braking means it "constantly feels like the car is stopping all the time".

Electric vehicles can also accelerate and decelerate much more quickly than conventional combustion cars, which Di Giulio says can cause motion sickness.

Edmonds, of EVA England, says developments in electric vehicle design have made them better at moderating the acceleration so they don't gain speed as rapidly.

She adds that the association thinks motion sickness in an electric vehicle is caused by "other factors" like the motorist's driving style rather than the vehicle itself.

Some features of electric cars may feel unfamiliar to drivers at first, adds Mike Hawes, head of the Society of Motor Manufacturers.

He says EVs can offer a different driving experience. "However, drivers typically adjust quickly to these characteristics, and many models also allow regenerative braking to be tailored to individual preferences."

Some people are also just more prone to motion sickness, and genetics have the biggest influence on this, according to Hac, and experts say women and children are more susceptible.

Motion sickness typically peaks between the ages of eight and 10, after which it decreases through more exposure, says Prof John Golding, who has researched the subject at the University of Westminster, the Royal Navy and the RAF.

Hold your head still and open the window

As their popularity increases, avoiding electric vehicles can be a challenge - the number of new zero-emission cars registered in the UK rose by 40.5% in April to June 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, latest Department for Transport figures show. , external

At the end of June 2026, 5.8% of all licensed cars on UK roads were zero-emission vehicles, the data shows. The sale of new purely petrol or diesel cars is set to be banned from 2030.

Lucinda Harrison, 24, from London says she often books taxis that turn out to be electric vehicles, and has to endure the trip feeling nauseous, sweaty and clammy.

The thought of travelling in an EV fills her with dread, she says. Even just a five-minute lift from a colleague to a Tube station recently was enough to make her feel "horrific".

Academics say there are several steps passengers can take to reduce feelings of motion sickness.

Look out of the front window and don't look at your phone or read a book

Sit in the front passenger seat rather than in the back, if possible. If you do have to sit in the back, opt for the middle seat so you can still see out the front window

Keep your head still by holding it against the headrest

Recline your seat

Regulate your breathing

Open the window to let in fresh air

Take travel sickness tablets if needed, though these can cause drowsiness

Before a long journey, make sure you're hydrated, have slept well and have eaten non-greasy food

Experts also say we can become desensitised to motion sickness through prolonged exposure. The more journeys you take in electric vehicles, the less likely you are to become motion sick as your body adjusts, Golding says.

There are also things carmakers can do to alleviate motion sickness in electric vehicles, says Prof Cyriel Diels, professor of mobility design at the Royal College of Art. These include having software that smooths out rapid acceleration, adding sound systems and subtle seat vibrations to signal to passengers that the car is moving, and offering adaptive regenerative braking that reduces sudden deceleration.

In some EVs, regenerative braking can also often be turned off.

Matt Adams from BEAMA, which represents UK manufacturers of electric vehicle charge points, says he's confident that "if future research identifies the reason for car sickness that vehicle manufacturers can respond and improve accordingly".

But for Lola, she just wants her boyfriend to trade in his car. She says that day can't come soon enough.

Are you an EV driver or have been a passenger in an EV? Have you experienced nausea due to motion sickness? Tell us your story.

title: 美股要“通宵”了！12月起迈入23小时交易时代
content:
来源：华尔街见闻
12月6日起，纳斯达克（Nasdaq）、纽交所Arca等四大核心交易所将正式增设夜盘时段，华尔街全面迈入每天23小时的“通宵交易”时代。
这一历史性扩容旨在应对加密货币及预测市场“全天候交易”的跨界竞争，并加速捕获海外投资者的增量需求。美国证券交易委员会（SEC）数据显示，尽管当前夜盘仅占美股总成交量的1%左右，但其同比增速已高达358%，展现出极强的爆发力。
机构资金观望：流动性与价差成核心隐忧
交易时段的延长在全球市场引发分歧。支持者寄望于打破时区壁垒，但手握重金的机构投资者却对潜在风险保持高度警惕。
Crisil Coalition Greenwich高级分析师David Easthope指出，机构的核心痛点在于延长时段后的“市场质量”——即流动性与买卖价差，而非单纯的运营或人员排班问题。该机构去年下半年（2025年下半年）针对买方交易员的调查显示，由于常规时段外参与者稀缺，强行入场可能面临流动性枯竭及价差扩大的双重打击，甚至影响交易员的身心健康。不过Easthope补充称，随着监管层实质性推进改革，买方对这一趋势的“不可避免性”已有心理准备。
Themis Trading股票交易联席主管Joseph Saluzzi直言对新规缺乏兴趣。他指出，当前交易所盘前与盘后交易量之和仅占总量的10%，机构资金绝不会贸然进入一个低流动性、宽价差且极易波动的市场。
Liquidnet市场结构主管Jeff O’Connor则认为，机构目前处于“观望模式”。若12月的扩容能实质性改善夜间价格发现机制并降低交易成本，机构资金终将入场捕捉夜盘Alpha（超额收益）。
海外与散户主导：交易标的高度集中
海外资金与散户成为当前夜盘的绝对主导力量。SEC数据显示，今年二季度，海外投资者贡献了夜盘总成交量的37%。
参与者结构的失衡直接导致交易标的高度集中。今年8月，仅15只股票就包揽了夜盘50%的成交量，其中频繁出现注册地在中国内地和中国香港的“不足一美元”低价股。作为对比，在流动性充裕的常规时段，需要256只股票才能达到同等成交比例。
目前提供夜盘撮合服务的另类交易系统（ATS）Blue Ocean Technologies首席执行官Brian Hyndman表示，12月新规落地后，现有的活跃玩家将无缝衔接。但他同时坦言，买方机构和投行的持续缺席，意味着市场仍缺失最关键的一块拼图。
清算基建就位：每日仅留一小时“空窗期”
尽管资金端存在分歧，华尔街的底层基础设施已为“通宵”做好了准备。
负责美股清算的美国证券存托与清算公司（DTCC）已于今年6月切换至“24x5”模式，运行时间从纽约时间周日晚8点持续至周五晚8点。同时，负责分发报价及交易数据的证券信息处理器（SIPs）也已获批延长运行时间。
根据最新时间表，12月扩容后，纳斯达克和纽交所在现有的常规时段（美东时间9：30-16：00）、盘前（4：00起）及盘后（16：00-20：00）基础上，将新增晚9点至次日凌晨4点的夜盘。
至此，美股全天将仅在晚8点至9点保留一个小时的休市时间，用于系统维护与交易处理。
风险提示及免责条款
市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

title: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises?
content:
Months before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.

You'll also probably know the set list, the stage design, and - if you've really been paying attention - where to stand to get the best view.

When it comes to films and TV series, spoilers tend to be guarded against with warnings.

But for many major gigs, there's no escaping a stream of fan videos from the shows if you're online, whether you like it or not.

Last week, US pop star Olivia Rodrigo kicked off her Unraveled tour, and surprises from the show, which scores of fans have paid a lot of money to see, have already been dissected online.

Tours by Harry Styles, Charli XCX and Ariana Grande have also been filmed from every angle and shared over the past few months.

While some fans lap up the opportunity to see what's coming, others are taking extreme measures to preserve the element of surprise.

Aurélia Collins is one of them, spending weeks trying to trick her algorithm into not serving her content about her favourite artists and tapping "not interested" when videos come up, even though she says "it hurts my soul".

It can mean her social media feed is a bit bland, but she tells BBC Newsbeat "it's worth it for the surprise".

The 20-year-old criminology student is a huge One Direction fan and says she just about managed to avoid spoilers for Styles' Together, Together tour over summer.

But when one slipped through the net about Niall Horan before she was able to see his show in London on Saturday - her first time seeing him live after being a fan for 16 years - she was "gutted".

"When I was younger, we couldn't afford to go to events like this and hear live music and because it's such a moment, I really want to take it in," she says.

"I want the full experience, and that includes the element of surprise that people that go to the opening night of the tour can get."

Not all fans think spoilers are a bad thing, though. In fact, Georgia McAdam claims she loves them.

"I'm the type of person that loves to be prepared," the 22-year-old says.

"I love to know what the stage is looking like, what the set list consists of and where to stand."

McAdam's a huge Olivia Rodrigo fan and sees online spoilers more as "teasers". She feels no amount of online videos can ever really take away from the excitement of the real thing.

"Sometimes you get different surprise songs to what's online or you never know what an artist might do," she adds.

'You have to not look at TikTok'

Some artists have reacted by switching up their sets in small ways each night to make sure fans coming to later dates still see something unexpected.

Taylor Swift had bespoke outfits and surprise songs during her mammoth Eras tour, Sabrina Carpenter performed unique positions during her song Juno and switched up her Nonsense outro, and Jay-Z has been changing up his set list on his current run.

But the Guardian's deputy music editor Laura Snapes says it's not just fans who can benefit from these twists.

"One way that they can make sure they're staying in the press is by having something different happen in their show every night," Snapes says. "Obviously, it'll be all over TikTok."

Figures shared by TikTok with Newsbeat show posts using #CharliXCX have increased by more than 40% since the singer launched her Music, Fashion, Film tour last month.

If you want to avoid spoilers, there's only one thing you can do, according to Snapes: "You have to not look at TikTok.

"If you want to be surprised, you have to protect yourself from absorbing any of that culture."

Phoebe Bridgers is taking things one step further to make sure fans are surprised at her shows - she's banning phones altogether.

Those attending are required to lock their phones and any recording devices in a special pouch when they enter the venue to see the US singer. Anyone found breaking the rules will be escorted out.

McAdam wouldn't support a ban on phones, saying recording at gigs is "part of the experience" for a lot of fans.

But Collins says she's "not totally against it".

What she'd prefer is to see more spoiler warnings on videos so fans have the option to be surprised if they want.

But even if you know the set list, the staging and the outfits, "you're still probably going to get to see moments of humanity and stuff that's unplanned," Snapes adds.

"I went to the Edinburgh Eras show where Taylor Swift was really snotty and she had to blow her nose. That's not part of the script.

"You're always going to be surprised."

title: India throws month-long birthday bash for Narendra Modi
content:
Michael Stott and Jyotsna Singh in Vadnagar and Andres Schipani in New Delhi

Published October 3 2026

Bearing water from the river Ganges, 500 motorcyclists are crossing India this month and heading to Vadnagar — where Prime Minister Narendra Modi was born 76 years ago.

Another 500 are riding in the opposite direction to Varanasi, the Hindu holy city which is Modi’s constituency, planting trees and cleaning streets in honour of his quarter of a century in public office, which will be celebrated October 7. He has led India for 12 years, after 13 years as chief minister in his home state of Gujarat.

Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party is using the twin celebrations for its revered leader to try to revive its fortunes after a summer of youth protests. Candle-lighting and prayer sessions across the country marked Modi’s birthday on September 17.

“Prime Minister Modi and his dedication to public service for 25 years are the inspiration for young people like me all over India,” said Deepesh Yadav, 32, a member of the BJP youth wing from Gujarat, as he passed through New Delhi after joining the motorbike rally.

“What he did in the past 12 years is automatically inspiring . . . now we must do something for Mr Modi.”

But the BJP cadres’ enthusiasm for their leader has less of an echo on the streets, where many of India’s 370mn youths are expressing anger over a broadening range of issues, including a lack of well-paid jobs and long-running sexual violence.

“Young people are not interested in the activities of mainstream politics, whether it’s birthday celebrations or whatever journeys the BJP organises,” said Eeshna Gupta, a 25-year-old opposition student leader in Delhi. “They are instead focused on their issues: we need jobs, social security, good education, and safety for women.”

Modi and his party’s youth-centric campaigns were “creating even more distance”, she added.

Now serving a third consecutive term as prime minister, Modi dominates India ’s political landscape like no other leader this century. As well as the national government, the BJP and its allies run 22 of India’s 31 states and territories with elected governments.

But mass protests over the summer by the upstart Cockroach Janta Party have cast a shadow over the celebrations in his name.

The CJP, which began as an online satirical movement but quickly morphed into a nationwide force, forced the exit in July of Modi’s education minister and close ally, Dharmendra Pradhan, over problems in the national exam system.

It launched more protests on Friday in Mumbai, where thousands gathered over allegations that the nominally independent election commission has improperly excluded tens of millions of voters from electoral rolls.

“Obviously, the government is under pressure,” said Pratap Bhanu Mehta, an Indian political scientist and former vice-chancellor of Ashoka University. “A lot of the accumulated problems of Indian society and the Indian economy are beginning to express themselves through protests.”

Modi biographer Nilanjan Mukhopadhyay said that while there was no denying the prime minister’s political achievements over a quarter of a century, the CJP protests had punctured his aura of invulnerability and “for the first time he was mocked at a mass level”.

“In the last two-months-plus, Mr Modi has not been able to reinvent himself,” Mukhopadhyay said.

Faced with this challenge to its leader and biggest electoral asset, the BJP is rallying its extensive grassroots operation to paint the premier as a dedicated and effective leader deserving of many more years in power.

Ram Madhav, a BJP national vice-president and former national secretary, emphasised the party’s commitment to seva , selfless devotion to others, and hailed Modi as an exemplar. “He is a very motivated type of leader,” Madhav told the FT. “He is not just doing his political duty. He thinks it’s a spiritual commitment to the welfare of the people.”

The mainly pro-government press has published birthday cover wraps with advertisements extolling Modi’s virtues. The celebrations even extended abroad, with the world’s tallest building, Dubai’s Burj Khalifa, illuminated in the colours of the Indian flag and a “Happy Birthday” message projected on to it above a photograph of Modi.

Madhav dismissed criticism that the party was too focused on its leader. “It’s not as if we’re creating a personality cult,” he said. “We are presenting [Modi] as an example of how a seva-minded politician should act.”

Modi’s birthplace in rural Gujarat has been a focus of the celebrations.

Passengers arriving at Vadnagar railway station snap selfies in front of the modest teal-coloured metal hut on the main platform, from which Modi says he helped his father serve tea as a boy chai-wallah . Outside, a giant kettle in a flower bed reinforces the message of his humble origins.

Still even in Vadnagar, where roads have been improved, a giant new archaeology museum built and public buildings associated with Modi’s life renovated, some residents are sceptical about the achievements of the town’s most famous son.

“There are better roads since Modi became PM and the town is a lot cleaner. Yes, the town has changed a lot but our lives haven’t,” said dairy farmer Vishnu Popat. “We are happy for Mr Modi and the celebrations but there are no jobs or business here. What about our children? How will they survive?”

Modi remains a formidable political operator, physically fit on a strict vegetarian diet with daily yoga exercises and no alcohol. After the youth protests, the prime minister summoned the 65-strong BJP national leadership for a meeting lasting more than four hours where he asked each to speak in turn and listened intently, participants said. Ministers have been ordered to hone their Instagram skills to project better to a youth audience.

Bhanu Mehta noted that with three years until India’s next general election, Modi and the BJP had “a lot of headroom to recover in the face of widespread social discontent and protest”.

But he said that despite Modi’s energy, the prime minister faced a fundamental contradiction in his efforts to address youth protests.

“He’s by instinct a centraliser. The power is centred in his persona. And these are governance challenges that you cannot solve by extreme centralisation,” he said.

title: Chill out: Japan’s top vending machine maker now cools data centres
content:
Harry Dempsey in Tokyo

Published October 3 2026

Japan’s biggest vending machine maker has reworked its refrigeration technology to offer power-hungry AI data centres an energy-efficient way to cool their servers.

Fuji Electric, which makes 80 per cent of Japan’s vending machines, has created a cooling system for data centres that it claims can cut energy consumption by 85 per cent, using a technology originally designed to chill sodas, teas and coffees.

The push is the latest by a Japanese industrial group to reinvent itself as a key supplier of components used in AI infrastructure, joining the likes of Panasonic, Mitsubishi Electric and Sumitomo Electric.

Cooling servers accounts for 30 to 40 per cent of data centres’ energy consumption, presenting a big opportunity for Japanese companies specialising in air conditioning and refrigeration.

Fuji Electric’s technology was born out of efforts to make vending machines more energy efficient after they became a symbol of waste following the Fukushima nuclear meltdown in 2011.

Shintaro Ishihara, Tokyo’s governor at the time, had gone as far as demanding a complete shutdown of vending machines to save energy as Japan faced a power crunch in the disaster’s aftermath.

That call prompted Fuji Electric and Toyota supplier Denso to develop a new cooling system. In 2015, a team of researchers created an ejector using a CO₂ refrigerant that did away with the need for a compressor and saved energy by 20 per cent, according to the company.

“Simply extending conventional technology wouldn’t have been enough,” said Hideto Shirai, who is leading efforts at Fuji Electric to sell the technology to data centres.

Most cooling systems deploy a compressor, which uses a large amount of electricity to turn a refrigerant into a hot, high-pressure gas. Fuji Electric’s ejector uses waste heat to drive refrigerant through a precisely shaped nozzle and raise its pressure through the movement of fluid.

However, the technology was never adopted inside vending machines because it was too costly to install when the machines only cost a few thousand dollars.

“We knew the technology was effective,” said Shirai. “But it was difficult to make it blossom inside vending machines. So the idea began: what if we applied it to a different industrial field?”

The Tokyo-based electrical equipment supplier is aiming to sell more than ¥10bn ($61mn) worth of ejector systems to data centres by 2030. It already sells ¥100bn a year in data centre-related components such as switchgears.

The company’s role as an AI “picks and shovels” supplier, as well as improving margins in its energy components business, has helped Fuji Electric’s shares rise almost 47 per cent in the past year. The company is valued at $13.9bn.

Alex Cordovil, research director at Dell’Oro, a research group specialising in data centre infrastructure, called the technology “promising” but said it was still “genuinely emerging”.

The data centre cooling market is shifting from traditional systems that use water and glycol or hydrofluoroolefin refrigerants towards direct liquid cooling, which circulates a liquid coolant directly to heat-generating components such as CPUs and GPUs.

Fuji Electric’s system could be used in direct liquid-based cooling systems. The ejector technology performs better in regions with high temperatures, creating a potential opening in parts of Japan, where summer heat can often exceed 35 degrees, and south-east Asia.

But Cordovil said a rival technology that uses waste heat — absorption chillers made by Japan’s Kawasaki, Ebara and Yazaki — had an edge over Fuji’s system for data centre adoption.

Ryo Harada, analyst at Goldman Sachs, expressed doubts about whether Fuji Electric would be able to access the large US data centre market.

“The technology may be compelling, but commercialisation is equally important,” he said. “Hyperscalers have largely locked in their next-generation data centre architectures for the next two to three years, so it is likely to take at least that long for new entrants to gain meaningful traction.”

title: G7打响“油价降温战”!一亿桶石油储备释放叠加特朗普放弃禁运，全球通胀迎来关键减压阀
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，在七国集团及其合作伙伴同意释放部分应急燃料储备、以遏制价格飙升之后，他不会宣布单方面禁止美国柴油出口。
G7紧急大规模释储与维持贸易畅通共同缓解柴油短缺，有望降低运输、农业和制造业的成本压力，释储缓解即时供应紧张，放弃禁运降低市场割裂风险，两项措施共同改善燃油供给预期。虽然西方国家能源供应救急已经全面启动，推动能源通胀短暂降温，但能源通胀能否持续迈向下行仍是重大未知数。投资者们关注点正从原油桶数转向成品油交付、大型炼厂利用率和能源航运效率，政策成效将由真实供给兑现决定。
法国总统马克龙所推动的G7（七国集团）协调释储，已经从讨论方案升级为行动承诺；特朗普随后则明确表示，美国不会实施柴油出口禁令。这套关于石油供给的政策组合可谓同时针对两项重大能源通胀压力——通过释放库存缓解即时石油供应紧张，通过维持跨境贸易避免欧美柴油市场价格进一步割裂。G7及伙伴计划在四个月内协调释放最多1亿桶储备，并在最初20天集中投放大量柴油，同时协调炼厂检修、在条件允许时提高开工率。
不过对于投资者们而言，需要准确区分的是——最新动态是原油和成品油储备安排，并非新增原油产能；官方也尚未明确最终产品分配比例。
“欧洲有大量柴油，他们将为全球供应作出重大能源贡献——我们也一样，”特朗普当地时间周五在白宫对记者们表示。“因此，我们不会实施出口禁令。”
这个由欧洲、北美和亚洲主要经济体组成的集团，在特朗普政府展开强力施压之后，于周五同意释放最多1亿桶应急原油和柴油资源储备。
“我确实向他们提出了这一要求，我们将获得大量石油，”特朗普补充表示。“他们做得非常好。”
特朗普作出上述表态之际，柴油等一众成品油交易价格正经历创纪录的价格飙升。柴油为现代经济中的大量活动提供核心能源动力，包括驱动农业机械、支持美国广泛运输业，以及为农村社区提供供暖和电力。
柴油可谓是运输和商业活动的命脉，其关键作用意味着，价格上涨已经传导至整个经济，推高了多种消费品的成本，而11月美国中期选举即将到来。
总统的这一决定，意味着他从此前考虑限制柴油出口的立场上后退，也拒绝了农村和中西部地区一些选情告急的共和党人的诉求。这些人士曾要求实施能源出口限制，以降低在选举前令选民承受沉重压力的燃料价格。
特朗普周五坚称，柴油出口禁令从未被当作一个认真考虑的选项。“我们从来就没打算这么做，”他对记者表示。“我想我们没有。”不过在上个月，这位美国总统曾表示，他已鼓励顾问支持这一措施。
特朗普目前的做法，也是在两大核心支持群体之间寻求微妙平衡：一方是美国腹地的农业社区，其中一些共和党现任议员正面临艰难选战；另一方是受益于总统支持传统化石燃料政策的石油利益集团，比如埃克森美孚和雪佛龙这两大全球最大规模传统能源巨头。
最近几周，包括艾奥瓦州参议员查克·格拉斯利，以及正面临激烈连任选战的阿拉斯加州参议员丹·沙利文在内，多名知名共和党人曾推动限制出口。
然而，石油行业领袖和能源专家们再度发出警告，限制柴油对外销售，最多只能带来短期价格缓解；随后，随着国内库存膨胀促使美国石油生产商和炼油商削减产量，成本将迅速再度上升。
包括能源部长克里斯·赖特和内政部长道格·伯古姆在内的部分政府官员，也曾在内部表达类似担忧。
在中期选举前，燃料和其他消费品成本是选民最主要的不满之一。柴油价格的涨势尤其突出，因为俄罗斯和中东地区的战争导致部分炼油设施停运，并扰乱了能源运输。
根据美国汽车协会的数据，截至周五，美国柴油平均零售价格为每加仑6.37美元。
周五宣布、由国际能源署协调的石油储备释放行动，预计只能带来短期缓解。法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙周五表示，相关供应将在未来四个月内陆续投放，初期的能源投放重点是柴油。
欧洲高度依赖美国柴油出口，此次释储被视为避免美国禁止燃料对外销售的一项举措。G7国家现已重申承诺，在成员国之间“不对能源及能源产品实施出口限制”。
在美国，石油企业高管一直恳请特朗普政府官员考虑其他方案，并警告表示，即便短期出口限制也会引发国内减产效应，损害美国在欧洲和拉丁美洲的盟友。
根据一项特朗普政府正在认真考虑的方案，特朗普政府将取消对红色或染色柴油销售的限制。这类柴油通常供越野用途使用，并长期享有免税待遇。该方案将允许零售商们出售免征每加仑24美分联邦消费税的染色柴油，供卡车及其他公路车辆使用。
整体而言，特朗普政府正认真考虑放宽染色柴油的销售和用途限制。这类通常呈红色的柴油主要用于非公路作业，并享有免税待遇。若方案实施，零售商将获准向卡车及其他公路车辆销售这类柴油，同时保留其免征每加仑24美分联邦消费税的待遇。
一亿桶启动“柴油降温战”，禁运威胁退场，油价盘中急跌后出现反弹
G7及伙伴计划在四个月内协调释放最多1亿桶储备，并在最初20天集中投放大量柴油，同时协调炼厂检修、在条件允许时提高开工率。
在此消息推动之下，周五油价确实出现了大幅回调，但这一描述仅仅适用于盘中交易时段，最终结算表现显示油价经历盘中暴跌后又强劲反弹。G7国家协同释储消息推动布伦特一度跌破每桶100美元，随后明显收复跌幅；最终布伦特几乎收平，WTI原油则保留了较明显的跌幅。以2月28日战争爆发前最后一个交易日——2月27日——为基准，能源价格仍显著高于战前水平。
10月2日结算价显示，国际原油基准——布伦特原油价格收于102.25美元/桶，最终收跌0.06%，从盘中一度跌破100美元后出现反弹；WTI原油价格收于91.11美元/桶，当日跌1.90%；布伦特与WTI原油期货较美伊战争爆发之前最后一个交易日分别大涨41%以及36%。
供应端，沙特正在加速恢复绕开霍尔木兹海峡的能源交付能力。据媒体援引知情人士透露的消息报道，沙特东西向输油管道输送量接近每日600万桶，约占700万桶设计运能的大约86%；扣除西海岸炼厂需求后，可供出口约450万桶。这里恢复所强调的是运输能力，可供出口流量不等同于已经装船的出口量。延布港北上欧洲可经苏伊士运河，南下亚洲则通常需要经过曼德海峡，因此绕开霍尔木兹并不意味着整条运输路线都已摆脱安全约束。
中东局势仍呈现“能源运输恢复、军事风险持续”的并行状态：霍尔木兹的部分能源运输增加，但仍存在关闭船舶识别信号通行的情况；美国继续部署第三艘航母及增援兵力，伊朗在通过卡塔尔保持间接接触的同时，准备在遭到新一轮大规模打击时扩大反击。
在霍尔木兹海峡能源航运持续面临军事打击与封锁之际，曼德海峡方向，有媒体最新披露沙特正筹划支持也门部队对胡塞武装发动攻势，以改善红海航道安全，行动尚未实施。与此同时，媒体援引知情人士透露的消息报道称，在当地时间周五晚些时候，一艘大型原油运输油轮在阿曼以东约4海里遭不明投射物击中，船员安全。
释储打开能源成本减压阀，但是长期限国债市场仍在重估通胀与财政压力
G7协调释储与美国放弃柴油出口禁令，为缓解全球能源成本提供了双重支持：补充短期供应，并维持跨境贸易畅通。柴油广泛用于货运、农业机械和工业活动，其价格变化会通过运输与生产成本影响企业利润和居民消费价格。国际能源署指出，中东原油出口已经明显恢复，但成品油供应仍受到严重限制，俄罗斯炼厂遭袭进一步加剧了柴油紧张。因此，优先投放柴油、协调炼厂检修和提高可用产能利用率，更有针对性地回应了当前的供应瓶颈。
这轮协调政策的积极作用，是为炼厂和运输体系恢复争取时间。最多1亿桶储备将在四个月内释放，其中大量柴油安排在最初20天投放。不过市场交易员们可能更加关注的是中东地区乃至全球范围的实际能源交付速度、产品构成以及后续供应能否接续，而不是仅凭宣布的总量判断价格降幅。
能源供应改善有助于缓解通胀压力，但全球金融市场长期国债收益率同时受到政策利率预期、债券供给和期限溢价影响。周五美国非农公布后，十年期美债收益率一度降至约5.157%，随后在纽约尾盘回升至5.281%，当日反而上涨约4.7个基点；英国长债温和修复。这些最新迹象都在说明各国债市仍在依据自身通胀、财政和货币政策条件进行定价。
从投资角度来看，柴油供应改善首先有利于运输、农业和制造企业控制成本；对于半导体及AI算力主题的热门AI基础设施企业，积极影响还可能通过通胀预期缓和、融资条件改善和风险偏好回升进一步积极传导。能源成本下降为估值修复创造了有利条件，而实际的修复力度仍取决于10年及以上的长期无风险收益率走势、债券市场信用利差以及那些与AI算力相关占据指数高权重的核心企业盈利预期的共同变化轨迹。

title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'
content:
"I witness men hitting women all the time," says Kgomotso Mathekga, 30. "Especially when they are both drunk."

"I once had an argument with my girlfriend," he admits, "and I grabbed and slapped her."

Mathekga is speaking frankly during a gathering of men aimed at helping reduce the high levels of violence against women in South Africa.

The meeting is held in a narrow street in a Johannesburg informal settlement known as Organic Market. It is a maze of corrugated metal shacks and unpaved roads, close to Alexandra township.

"Now I feel pain," Mathekga continues. "We broke up and I no longer see my child. I feel like I've contributed to the problems in South Africa, instead of being the gentleman that I know I am."

At a nearby tavern, a group of men have pulled their chairs into a circle in the dust.

At the centre stands Itumeleng Stephen Tamaga, known locally as Bra Steve.

He raises his fist.

"We are men!" he shouts.

The group clap and cheers. Some sip bottled beer.

"Listen guys," Bra Steve says. "We must stand together to fight against gender-based violence and femicide."

Bra Steve is the local organiser of Father A Nation, a non-profit that works with men and boys to promote positive masculinity and help end violence against women.

The group's meeting comes as South Africa grapples with renewed anger over renewed cases of femicide and violence against women.

The discovery of the bodies of 12 women over three months, in the city of Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg has reignited questions about the scale of what many people see as being a crisis of violence against women.

South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa has acknowledged that his government has not done enough and announced measures he hopes can make women feel safer.

The country has one of the highest murder rates in the world, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.

In that period, according to the South African Human Rights Commission, 569 women were killed, an average of six a day, and 1,052 others survived attempted murder.

A report in 2022 by the Human Sciences Research Council found that more than 35% of South African women experienced physical or sexual violence, many from their own intimate partners.

For Bra Steve, part of the solution to the crisis is helping men to understand the issue and take responsibility for their actions.

"We are a lost generation," he says. "We must restore dignity to the men around here."

Amongst the group of men outside the tavern is Zizipho Mtwesi, the project co-ordinator of Father A Nation.

Reflecting on recent weeks, he says more should be done.

The latest measures announced by Ramaphosa, including better street lighting and a review of unsolved cases, are too little, he says, and too late.

"When I think about all of these recent murders in Johannesburg, I get angry. Why do we have to wait for this to happen for us to act?"

He looks around and gestures at the meeting. "We are trying to reach men before things like these murders happen again."

Craig Wilkinson is the founder of the group. "We get men to talk, to process their feelings," he explains.

"And as they do, this healing takes place. And the second phase is teaching and training positive masculinity.

"We ultimately hope that this will eliminate the scourge of gender-based violence."

He stands up, moving into the centre of the group, calling out to the men.

"You as a man are a powerful force for good," he tells them. "You choose what kind of man you want to be. Women need to be safe."

Father A Nation operates across South Africa, teaching healthy masculinity and running training programmes across dozens of schools and colleges.

Mystery surrounds the spate of murders which has sparked South Africa's latest moment of soul-searching about the safety of its women.

Police have not ruled out potential links between some of the Ekurhuleni deaths but have not said they are investigating a serial killer. Suspects in some of the cases have appeared in court.

But the spate of deaths has sparked new concerns and in Organic Market some women are more fearful than ever.

Outside a nearby shack Linkie listens with interest as she cleans clothes in a large metal bucket.

"We are not safe when we are outside our place," she says.

"We are afraid when we see a car behind us when we walk. We feel afraid. We feel scared. What if this guy's going to kidnap me or do something to me?"

It is a feeling shared by many women here. In the local hair salon, sporting a mane of thick pink braids, is Providence Maseko.

She comes to the door to speak to Bra Steve.

"Safety here is very bad," she says, "Maybe you are the serial killer. How do I know who to trust?"

Bra Steve laughs. "We must talk about these things," he urges. "Come to our meetings and we can learn to trust each other."

Maseko tells me that she now takes an e-hailing taxi everywhere in the hope that it is safer.

Back at the tavern, the men's meeting is wrapping up.

"As we try to stop gender-based violence," says Zizipho, "each and every man needs to know that they need to play a part in this.

"And if they wouldn't allow these things to happen to their own daughters or own mothers, they mustn't allow it to be done to someone else's daughter, which is their wives or their girlfriends."

Mathekga is impressed with what he has heard.

"I would love them to keep on practising what we have learned, because we no longer have role models," he says. "Our fathers and our uncles, they are there in prison. We must now become role models and help make this country better."

title: Cornell frat house rape accuser 'under siege' online, says lawyer
content:
The lawyer for the woman who alleges she was raped at a Cornell University fraternity house says she is "not doing well" as she finds herself "under siege" from online sleuths seeking to identity her.

Thomas Giuffra said the woman known in legal documents as Jane Doe was "incapable of consent" because she was "completely, grossly intoxicated" when she turned up at the home where she says the assault took place.

The woman alleges she was assaulted by seven men at the campus in Ithaca, New York, in 2024.

No charges were initially filed in the case. It has reopened since she filed a civil lawsuit that thrust the claims into the national spotlight, reigniting the possibility of criminal charges.

In an interview on Friday with CNN, Giuffra said: "She's under siege on social media where people are trying to identify her."

He said that postings have "incorrectly" identified other women as Doe.

In an interview with CBS, the BBC's US partner, Giuffra argued that his client, aged 20 at the time, was unable to provide consent because she was intoxicated when she arrived at the fraternity house.

Giuffra said she had been pressured into taking the drug ketamine before she was allegedly raped.

His comments came as New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed the state's top prosecutor, Attorney General Letitia James, to take over the investigation.

At a news conference on Friday, Hochul said she had "lost faith" in the county prosecutor's ability to oversee the case.

"This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable, and then at every turn she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her," Hochul said.

She also vowed to close a "loophole" of state law that makes it difficult to press rape charges if an alleged victim voluntarily consumes alcohol or drugs.

During an interview with investigators, Doe told campus police investigators: "I was a sex doll for all intents and purposes, which is sad but, unfortunately, something I'm not used to, or something that I haven't experienced before."

She also said that she "felt like bait" as the attackers were "like lions around me", according to records from the school's disciplinary investigation, obtained by US media.

Social media feeds are filled with women trying to shield the Cornell accuser's identity by posting videos of themselves under the title "I am Jane Doe".

As well as seeking to complicate internet searches for her name, the messages of solidarity included clips of women detailing their own experiences of sexual assault.

Efforts to rally round Jane Doe gathered pace after a political commentator vowed to unmask her, arguing it was unfair for her to remain anonymous while the men are publicly named despite not being charged with a crime.

Online sleuths have also tried to locate the addresses of the so-called Cornell Seven, leading to at least one case of mistaken identity.

An active-duty US Marine Corps sergeant who had the same name as one of the men was incorrectly served the woman's lawsuit, leading to a torrent of abuse and threats, according to the Free Press, external.

title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
content:
For the first time in more than 30 years, a hurricane has not formed in the Atlantic throughout September - normally the most active month for hurricane activity.

With just two months left of the defined hurricane season, there is an increasing possibility that no hurricanes will develop at all.

This would make the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season the only one in the satellite era without a hurricane.

The biggest reason for this is El Niño, which traditionally stifles activity in the Atlantic but brings a very active season in the eastern North Pacific.

The Atlantic hurricane season was predicted to be quieter than normal as a result of this.

With a very strong El Niño forecast, the US National Hurricane Center in May predicted a total of eight to 14 named storms. Of those, three to six were predicted to become hurricanes, with one to three becoming major hurricanes.

September is typically the most active month for tropical storm and hurricane activity.

But, this year marks the latest date on record since the start of the satellite era (1960s onward) where no hurricane has formed in the North Atlantic.

There were, however, four named tropical storms that formed in September: Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo and Hanna.

All but Edouard stayed out in the open waters of the Atlantic.

The National Hurricane Center suggests there is no sign of any tropical storm activity or hurricane over the next week at least.

Forecasters at Colorado State University, who also monitor activity, suggest the strong El Niño is likely to disrupt wind patterns across the Atlantic and "likely result in below-normal activity" over the next two-weeks.

As the typical peak of the season has passed and is now on a downward trend until 30 November, a season without a single hurricane is looking increasingly possible.

In the historical Atlantic hurricane database, there has not been a year without a hurricane recorded since 1914. However, this was pre-satellite monitoring so it is impossible to say with certainty that none formed.

How does El Niño affect tropical development?

While El Niño is the natural warming of the tropical Pacific, it can disrupt weather patterns around the globe.

As wind patterns shift during an El Niño, upper winds over the Atlantic increase and this leads to more wind shear, where wind changes rapidly with height.

Strong winds blowing at different speeds and directions at higher altitudes rip apart thunderstorms, preventing them from growing into tropical storms or hurricanes.

Meanwhile, the Pacific typically becomes more active during El Niño because the sea surface temperatures here are much higher, combined with more favourable wind patterns.

The warmer waters give storms more energy to grow into tropical storms and hurricanes.

This year, temperature records have already been broken in a key region of the central-eastern Pacific, with daily sea surface temperatures now exceeding the previous record set during the very strong El Niño of 2015.

There have so far been 17 named storms in the basin including nine hurricanes, seven of which were major.

In terms of the amount of energy these storms have produced - known as the Accumulated Cyclone Energy - this season is around two and half times more active than normal at this point.

El Niño is predicted to continue to strengthen with forecasts suggesting it will reach its peak in November or December.

title: Traitors claim their first victim as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin
content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.

As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.

Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment.

"It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day.

"But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."

The episode drew in a peak audience of 8.6 million viewers, just short of the debut episode with an average of 8.9 million viewers.

The morning following Rajan's banishment, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."

Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.

The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.

The 69-year-old spent much of Friday's episode trying to repair the damage from his earlier exchange in the bar, where he blurted out that he was a traitor to Joe Lycett, Rob Beckett and several others.

Obviously a man who made such an excellent Spice Girls manager in the 1997 masterpiece Spice World: The Movie is hard for anyone to picture as a traitor, so many other players assumed Grant was attempting some elaborate double bluff.

Catch up with all the latest news from this year's show

Jama is off to a much stronger start. "I am quite shocked at my ability to just lie to everyone," the Love Island host said in the castle's diary room. "I'm an all-or-nothing kind of honey."

As the players gathered for breakfast, other theories began to surface. Mathematician Hannah Fry said she had spotted Leigh-Anne Pinnock putting on make-up late in the evening, perhaps heading to the turret.

"I think it's James," declared Jerry Hall, suddenly giving viewers hope that the new cast will be better traitor hunters than last year's. Until she clarified that she was talking about James Blunt, not Acaster.

As the players prepared to head out for the mission, conversations turned to far more important matters. "Do you have more teeth than a normal person?" Grant asked Beckett.

The players made their way to the mission, which had the usual slightly convoluted rules that took Winkleman quite a while to explain.

In a nutshell, the celebrities were to be buried alive in pairs, with only one duo left above ground.

Ross Kemp was pre-selected by the traitors to be protected from burial along with his grave partner Romesh Ranganathan, who did a delightful dance when he found out he wouldn't be going underground.

Kemp and Ranganathan then had the opportunity to dig up some gold graves which would add to the prize pot, or alternatively dig up and free their fellow players.

They opted for the latter, which resulted in some other players struggling, external to get the soil off their faces. In the end, all the celebrities were released, with the exception of Fry and Hall.

The pair were freed early after Hall shouted the emergency word "Haggis!" – effectively a Scottish version of "I'm a celebrity get me out of here!" - because she was visibly uncomfortable being buried alive.

It might have led to an early release, but it ultimately guaranteed that either she or Fry will be murdered next, unless the traitors recruit again.

"Just you and me up for murder," Fry told Hall afterwards. "You'd better not be a traitor or I'm really screwed!"

In a flashback shown to viewers, Acaster explained the decision to protect Kemp from burial, telling his fellow traitors: "I think if we give it to Ross, he'll overthink it, and behave in a way that would draw suspicion."

Very clever. "You're a wonderful traitor," observed Grant. (Certainly better than him.)

Finally, it was time for the first banishment of the series, with Grant still in damage control mode.

"I have a slight pinprick of advantage," he told himself in the castle's diary room. "Nobody would possibly believe that anybody would be so stupid as to come forward and say 'I am a traitor'. I'm hoping that I do get away with it."

His fellow traitors clearly wanted to be supportive, but things were getting dicey.

Acaster described him as a "loose cannon", while Jama said: "I want to save him, even though he's dug himself the biggest hole imaginable."
