The latest banished and murdered celebs have their say in Uncloaked

Back in the castle, Ranganathan pointed out: "If somebody else had behaved like Richard, we wouldn't even be having a debate about this, you would just go 'you've got to vote for him'."

But others had a slightly different take. "Richard feels a little too easy," reflected actress Myha'la, "and then anybody pushing him feels suspicious to me."

Comedian Joanne McNally agreed some players were "using him as a fall guy and a decoy," although she did admit later that he's "made such a shambles of it now".

As discussions got going, it took a surprisingly long time for Grant's name to come up, as the other players debated other suspects such as Julie Hesmondhalgh.

The actress aroused suspicion because she was the first celebrity this year to receive a shield. The group seemed to have overlooked she only got that - in the opening minutes of the first show - after the other contestants voted her the most trustworthy.

But as discussion turned to Grant, Hesmondhalgh put forward one of the most convincing cases of the night.

"You came into the bar, and said you were a traitor," she told him. "It was a bold move. It was chaotic and we love you for your chaos.

"I think we are at risk of being the most idiotic group of faithfuls in the world, if we go for someone else tonight based on nothing at all, when somebody has come into the room and said 'I am a traitor'. There's no reason to say it unless you are."

Miranda Hart agreed that "the joy when he took off his blindfold" when Winkleman first selected the traitors made Grant look suspicious.

Viewers will have to wait until the next episode to see how the round table goes, as the episode finished before voting had even started.

(It's worth saying that, as cliffhangers go, this was far less irritating than ending an episode in the middle of voting, as producers often do.)

"You've given us all a problem," Ranganathan told Grant as the episode drew to a close and the players prepared to vote. "By doing that, it was a big mistake by you, I feel like you forced our hand."

Admittedly, it's not looking good - the round table is shaping up to be a landslide vote against Grant. But we still wouldn't bet against him.

"I do not go down without a fight," he concluded. "I couldn't have survived showbusiness for four decades without a fight."

Celebrity Traitors continues on Thursday at 20:00 BST on BBC One and iPlayer.

title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting
content:
The operator of a popular amusement ride at the Munich Oktoberfest has been handing out free cycling shorts to women, after thousands of voyeuristic videos emerged on social media.

Some videos showing women on the Teufelsrad, or Devil's Wheel, have been viewed millions of times. One is said to have made thousands of euros for a woman who posted it online.

The Teufelsrad is one of the oldest attractions at the Oktoberfest, the annual beer festival which comes to an end this weekend after 16 days. Its circular platform rotates faster and faster until its riders fall off, and the motion and speed often make skirts fly up.

Filming under skirts is illegal in Germany, and carries a two-year sentence in jail.

However, critics believe the law does not go far enough, and the videos of women on the Teufelsrad in their traditional dirndl dresses often show their underwear. Sometimes, the images have been digitally altered to show them naked, according to local broadcaster BR.

One woman made €9,000 (£7,650) from a single clip, according to BR, whose investigations found that a group of professional YouTubers from Ukraine and several people from Bavaria were behind the videos.

At least 32,000 videos of women on the Teufelsrad have been in circulation, according to Munich-based daily Süddeutsche Zeitung. Some have apparently been viewed millions of times.

The operator of the Teufelsrad, Elisabeth Polaczy, told the BBC that, for the past three years, she has been handing out free cycling shorts to women and girls wearing dresses, to protect them from people filming in the crowd.

This Oktoberfest she has handed out more than 100 pairs, she says: "I want to do everything I can to make people feel secure."

Polaczy, who is now 80, said donating cycling shorts wasn't cheap, but it was worth it for her own peace of mind.

The Teufelsrad tent is hung with signs and police posters in German and English warning against filming under people's skirts, but Polaczy says it is impossible to control everyone filming with smart phones.

Some waitresses at this year's beer festival say they have also started wearing cycling shorts under their dirndls.

A spokesman for the Bavarian police told the BBC that since 2025, it has run a poster campaign at the Oktoberfest, warning against upskirting.

This year, police arrested a 45-year-old Swiss man for using his phone to film under a German woman's dirndl. Last year there were 10 arrests for upskirting and seven in 2024.

However, Josephine Ballon, who heads German non-profit organisation Hate Aid, which aims to support victims of digital violence, told the BBC that the current law against upskirting does not provide enough protection.

Although she says there are plans for a new law, current legislation "applies only when you film under the skirt", and not when a skirt simply flies up and gets photographed.

The new camera glasses are also a threat, she believes.

Ballon wants anyone who has uploaded intimate pictures of women on the internet to be punished, along with the platforms that put them up.

Meanwhile, the city of Munich has sought to tighten up on influencers and content creators who earn money from their social media postings and who want to film at the Oktoberfest.

Munich has banned broadcasting live streams from the festival and requires anyone who wants to film there to hold a permit, which is issued by the city for a fee.

Hundreds of licences have been issued this year to influencers, who make money from product placement or sponsoring.

title: US road rage killer's sentence quashed because AI video of victim was shown in court
content:
An Arizona road rage killer will be resentenced after an appeals court ruled that an AI-generated video message from his dead victim was improperly aired in court.

Gabriel Paul Horcasitas was found guilty by a jury of shooting and killing Christopher Pelkey, 37, during a confrontation at a red light in 2021. He was sentenced to 10 years behind bars.

But his legal team appealed, arguing that the trial judge should not have allowed an AI video, created by Pelkey's family, to be shown in court ahead of last year's sentencing.

The Arizona Court of Appeals agreed, ruling that Horcasitas, 55, must be resentenced because the AI clip "crossed that line".

"Rather than document an event or recording a particular moment, the AI video presents a depiction of the victim and his thoughts created from the imaginings of the victim's sister," the court of appeals wrote on Wednesday.

Horcasitas' lawyer, Kristen Reller, who filed the appeal, declined to comment.

Jessica Gattuso, an attorney for victims in the case, did not respond to a request for comment.

Pelkey's sister, Stacey Wales, told the BBC last year the family had used voice recordings, videos and pictures to recreate him for the AI video.

"To Gabriel Horcasitas, the man who shot me, it is a shame we encountered each other that day in those circumstances," said the AI version of Pelkey in court in 2025. "In another life, we probably could have been friends."

"I believe in forgiveness, and a God who forgives. I always have and I still do," the AI version of Pelkey - wearing a grey baseball cap - continued.

At the time of the sentencing, the judge who oversaw the case, Todd Lang, seemed to appreciate the use of AI.

"I loved that AI, thank you for that. As angry as you are, as justifiably angry as the family is, I heard the forgiveness," Judge Lang said. "I feel that that was genuine."

title: 苹果确认iPhone 18 Pro Max存在AT&T网络故障 受影响用户需换机
content:
苹果 公司表示，近期升级至iPhone 18 Pro Max的 美国电话电报 公司（AT&T）客户中，有“少数”用户遇到故障导致手机失去蜂窝网络服务，从而需要更换设备。
这款售价1，299美元的手机于两周前开售，是苹果除即将推出的折叠屏手机iPhone Duo之外最高端的机型。AT&T网络故障导致部分iPhone 18 Pro Max用户无法拨打电话、获取数据或收发短信。目前尚不清楚受影响用户的具体人数。除非连接Wi-Fi，否则受影响设备基本无法正常使用。
苹果发言人在提供给媒体的声明中表示：“我们已发现影响AT&T网络上少数iPhone 18 Pro Max用户的问题，该问题可能导致设备失去服务并无法拨打电话。”

title: 沃什淡化利率前瞻性指引 美联储两位高官讲话仍牵动市场 10月加息预期大幅降温
content:
尽管美联储主席沃什已明确表示，不希望通过前瞻性指引向市场释放明确的利率路径信号，美联储两位高级官员本周的讲话仍然显著影响了投资者预期。美联储副主席杰斐逊和纽约联储主席威廉姆斯先后表示，美联储有时间进一步评估经济形势，无需急于再次加息，促使市场大幅下调对10月加息的押注。
根据联邦基金期货定价，在威廉姆斯周二发表讲话之前，交易员预计美联储在10月27日至28日会议上加息的概率约为70%。而到了周四杰斐逊结束讲话时，这一概率已降至约25%。其间公布的通胀数据弱于预期，也进一步削弱了市场对近期加息的预期。
不过，美联储官员并未排除进一步收紧货币政策的可能性。通胀仍然高于政策目标，而定于10月14日公布的美国消费者价格指数（CPI）数据，可能成为决定后续政策方向的重要依据。
两位美联储高官接连表态 市场迅速下调10月加息押注
美联储在9月16日的议息会议上以全票通过加息25个基点，这是该央行自2023年以来首次提高政策利率。当时，美国经济整体增长出现加速迹象，而通胀持续居高不下，促使决策者重新采取紧缩措施。
在随后公布的经济预测中，美联储官员释放出今年可能再加息一次的信号。这一政策背景推动市场迅速押注10月继续加息，美债收益率也大幅攀升，进一步推高了美国经济的借贷成本。
不过，威廉姆斯和杰斐逊本周相隔仅两天发表的讲话，改变了市场对加息时点的判断。两人均强调，美联储可以等待更多经济数据出炉，再决定是否需要进一步提高利率。由于纽约联储主席不仅在联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）拥有永久投票权，而且按照惯例担任该委员会副主席，因此威廉姆斯的政策表态一直受到市场高度关注。
传统上，美联储主席、副主席和纽约联储主席被视为货币政策决策层的核心三人组合。在部分前任主席任内，投资者通常认为，副主席或纽约联储主席的公开讲话可能反映这一核心决策层的共同立场。不过，目前没有证据表明杰斐逊与威廉姆斯事先协调了讲话内容，也没有证据显示两人的发言经过沃什统一安排。
尽管如此，华尔街多家机构仍认为，两位高官的表态传递了相对一致的政策信息。高盛经济学家表示，杰斐逊与威廉姆斯的讲话进一步强化了他们对美联储不太可能在10月加息的判断。Evercore ISI经济研究主管Krishna Guha及其同事周四在报告中指出，两位官员共同传递的信息具有相当分量。
摩根大通首席美国经济学家Michael Feroli则认为，这两次讲话意在调整市场预期。他指出，两位官员传递的核心信息是，美联储不必在每次会议上连续加息，而是可以适当拉长政策调整之间的间隔，以便评估经济数据和此前加息的影响。
沃什淡化前瞻性指引 美联储转向更加依赖经济数据
值得注意的是，美联储高官此次对市场预期产生明显影响，正值沃什试图改变央行与投资者沟通方式之际。与过去通过前瞻性指引引导市场利率预期的做法不同，沃什倾向于避免提前暗示未来政策调整方向。
他不参与美联储季度利率预测，也尽量避免在公开讲话中透露下一步利率行动，而是鼓励投资者根据经济数据自行判断政策前景。
这种沟通方式获得了一些经济学家的支持。前瞻性指引的批评者认为，在金融危机等特殊时期，明确的政策承诺有助于稳定市场预期；但在经济数据快速变化、决策者难以准确判断未来走势的环境下，过度依赖前瞻性指引可能限制政策灵活性。
本周公布的经济数据就体现了这种复杂性。一方面，通胀和就业数据均弱于预期，降低了美联储立即进一步加息的紧迫性；另一方面，美国消费者支出仍然保持韧性，经济增长也呈现加速迹象。这意味着，美联储既需要防范通胀持续高企，也必须关注就业市场可能出现的疲软。
曾长期担任美联储理事会顾问的杜克大学经济学教授Ellen Meade认为，杰斐逊和威廉姆斯的讲话未必属于传统意义上的前瞻性指引。她指出，提前承诺某次利率调整，与表示需要更多时间收集数据、审慎作出决定，两者之间存在微妙但重要的区别。
耶鲁大学管理学院教授、前美联储部门主管William English同样认为，两位官员的讲话未必经过协调，而更可能是分别表达各自对经济形势及货币政策的判断。
多位官员强调耐心等待 但内部仍存在加息分歧
除了杰斐逊和威廉姆斯，其他美联储官员本周的表态也显示，决策层目前更倾向于等待经济数据提供进一步指引。
在北卡罗来纳州阿什维尔举行的一场会议上，里士满联储主席巴尔金、波士顿联储主席柯林斯以及堪萨斯城联储主席施密德，均未明确透露对今年最后两次议息会议的政策判断。
当被问及未来利率路径时，三人均强调需要关注即将公布的数据。巴尔金表示，应先观察经济形势如何发展。随后，美联储理事、负责银行监管事务的鲍曼也表示，目前没有迫切需要再次调整利率。
不过，美联储内部并非所有官员都对进一步加息持相同态度。今年以来一直积极主张提高利率的达拉斯联储主席洛根本周表示，为使通胀最终回到美联储2%的目标，可能仍需要多次加息。但她同时指出，债券市场期限溢价正在上升，这也可能对经济形成一定的抑制作用。
华尔街重新评估加息路径 10月14日通胀数据成关键
美联储官员本周接连发表讲话后，市场对今年剩余时间货币政策路径的判断发生明显变化。
Clocktower Group首席宏观策略师、曾担任前美联储理事米兰顾问的Eric Wallerstein认为，杰斐逊和威廉姆斯的讲话意在纠正市场对近期加息节奏的预期。他表示，当市场定价与官员所理解的经济及政策现实出现偏差时，美联储通过公开沟通影响投资者预期，并非新鲜事。
不过，官员们释放的观望信号并不意味着本轮加息已经结束。一方面，美联储9月的政策预测仍显示，决策者预计今年可能需要再加息一次；另一方面，近期美国国债收益率显著上升，也使官员们需要评估金融环境收紧对经济的影响。
与此同时，10月14日即将公布的消费者价格指数将为美联储提供新的通胀线索。如果物价压力持续高企，进一步加息仍可能成为政策选项；如果通胀继续降温，决策者则可能获得更多观察经济变化的空间。
值得注意的是，周五公布的美国9月就业报告显示，非农就业人数仅增加2.9万人，进一步强化了市场对美联储暂缓加息的预期。根据当天公布的市场定价，10月加息概率已进一步降至约14%，低于周四讲话结束时约25%的水平。
总体来看，美联储高层本周释放的核心信号并非结束加息，而是无需在连续两次会议上急于采取行动。尽管沃什正在淡化传统前瞻性指引，杰斐逊和威廉姆斯的讲话表明，美联储官员的政策表态仍能显著影响市场预期。
随着就业数据走弱、通胀压力尚未完全消退，美联储下一步利率调整的时点，仍将取决于未来数周经济数据所反映的增长与通胀形势。

title: 美债收益率居高不下！高借贷成本持续冲击美国经济 AI投资热潮与实体经济表现分化加剧
content:
持续数周的美国国债抛售潮令华尔街面临新的挑战。尽管周五公布的美国9月就业报告意外疲软，一度推动美债收益率回落、美股反弹，债券市场的涨势未能持续。随着10年期美债收益率维持在5%以上，投资者开始关注一个可能比短期市场波动更重要的问题，如果美国借贷成本长期居高不下，经济和金融市场将面临怎样的影响？
周五公布的数据显示，美国9月非农就业人数仅增加2.9万人，失业率小幅上升，明显疲软的就业表现促使交易员削减对美联储进一步加息的押注。不过，美债收益率随后重新企稳，10年期美债收益率在周五尾盘仍徘徊于5.27%左右。
与此同时，美股主要指数与实体经济之间的表现分化日益明显。尽管住房市场持续低迷、消费信贷成本攀升、信用状况较弱的借款人面临更高融资压力，但强劲的企业盈利和人工智能（AI）投资热潮仍支撑主要股指接近历史高位。
Hirtle & Co．首席投资官Brad Conger指出，美国普通消费者和企业的处境，与AI及资本支出相关领域形成了巨大反差。
美债收益率维持5%以上 高利率压力已向多个行业蔓延
过去数周，美债收益率持续攀升，引发市场对金融环境进一步收紧的担忧。虽然疲软的就业数据一度缓解了债券市场的抛售压力，投资者仍需面对高利率可能长期持续的现实。
Conger认为，目前尚未出现某个会令所有资产突然承压的明确临界点，但部分行业已经开始感受到高利率的影响。他特别提到住房、汽车、消费贷款和信用卡等领域。这些行业对融资成本变化较为敏感，借贷利率上升会直接影响消费者的购买能力和企业经营活动。
这种压力也反映在股票市场内部。尽管大型AI科技股持续支撑主要指数，市场上涨的覆盖面正在收窄，银行、工业和公用事业等板块表现相对疲弱。截至周五，标普500指数当周累计下跌0.3%，而科技股占比较高的纳斯达克100指数则上涨0.7%，反映出不同板块之间的明显分化。
Conger指出，当前市场面临的风险并不一定来自收益率突然突破某个特定水平，而是高借贷成本持续侵蚀部分行业的需求和盈利能力。
AI资本开支热潮支撑美股 科技巨头对高利率敏感度较低
尽管高利率给部分经济领域带来压力，华尔街仍有投资者认为，当前收益率水平未必会阻碍股市继续上涨。
Laffer Tengler Investments的Nancy Tengler表示，债券收益率上升有时也可能反映经济基本面强劲，并不必然意味着股票市场将受到严重冲击。她指出，如果一家企业能够以5%的成本融资，同时通过投资获得15%至20%的回报，那么继续扩大投资仍然具有经济合理性。
基于这一判断，Tengler近期增持了英伟达（NVDA.US）、美光科技（MU.US）和Meta Platforms（META.US）等科技股，同时增加了对GE Vernova（GEV.US）、伊顿（ETN.US）和Quanta Services（PWR.US）等电力基础设施相关企业的配置。
这类企业的共同特点是能够受益于AI基础设施建设及相关资本支出增长。
Gallo Partners创始人Michael Alfaro也指出，尽管借贷成本处于高位，美国私人部门的数据中心投资热潮仍没有明显放缓迹象。他认为，市场正在关注未来就业增长放缓以及能源价格压力减轻的可能性，并预期这些变化最终有助于缓解通胀。这在一定程度上解释了为何美国股市能够在融资成本持续高企的环境下保持韧性。
Alfaro目前仍看好部分与AI及航空航天产业相关的企业。不过，AI资本支出持续扩张也使美股对少数行业的依赖程度进一步提高。一旦相关投资回报不及预期，市场可能面临新的调整压力。
资金加速流入债券ETF 投资者重新调整资产配置
随着美债收益率升至多年高位，投资者的资产配置策略也开始发生变化。
根据数据，今年9月，债券交易所交易基金（ETF）吸收的资金占全部ETF资金流入的42%，创下一年多以来的最高占比。这一变化表明，随着债券收益率提高，固定收益资产对投资者的吸引力正在增强。
与此同时，部分机构开始调整此前对债券市场的低配策略。BMO Wealth Management的Carol Schleif近期将投资级信用债的低配幅度缩减了一半，但仍维持对美国高质量成长股的超配立场。这意味着，部分投资者正在重新增加固定收益资产敞口，同时继续持有基本面较强的成长型企业。
不过，不同债券资产之间的风险仍存在差异。对于信用状况较弱的借款人而言，高利率可能增加再融资压力，而信用质量较高的发行人通常拥有更强的融资能力。
因此，在当前环境下，债券收益率上升既为投资者提供了更高的潜在利息收入，也使信用风险和利率持续时间成为资产配置的重要考量因素。
企业债务短期压力可控 真正考验在于高利率持续时间
富兰克林邓普顿投资解决方案部门的Max Gokhman认为，市场需要关注的不仅是美债收益率上涨的速度，更重要的是收益率最终会稳定在什么水平，以及高利率将持续多长时间。他指出，美国经济中的部分借款人目前仍受到既有融资安排的保护，因此利率上升的影响可能需要较长时间才能充分显现。
例如，美国多数现有房贷借款人持有固定利率抵押贷款，平均贷款利率约为4%。相比之下，美国新发放抵押贷款的利率已升至7.28%，创下2023年末以来最高水平。这意味着，现有房主暂时不需要承担与新贷款相同的高利率，但准备购房或需要重新融资的消费者则面临明显更高的成本。
企业部门同样存在类似情况。数据显示，美国非金融企业债务中，只有约13%将在2027年到期，规模约为5700亿美元。由于多数债务尚未进入再融资阶段，企业不必立即按照当前较高的市场利率重新借款。
Gokhman认为，正因如此，只有当高收益率持续相当长一段时间后，借贷成本上升才可能对企业和整体经济造成更显著的冲击。在投资策略方面，他更关注债券久期配置机会，对信用债则相对谨慎。
值得注意的是，即使AI行业未来需要进行大规模融资，其受到高利率冲击的程度也可能相对有限。Gokhman预计，大型云计算企业及其他AI相关公司可能发行约3000亿美元债券。
不过，他指出，这些企业中有不少拥有投资级信用评级、充足资本以及较强的财务实力。由于企业正争相建设算力基础设施，其融资决策对利率成本的敏感程度可能低于其他行业。
因此，高利率对美国经济的影响可能呈现明显分化，即财务实力较强的科技巨头能够继续扩大投资，而住房、消费信贷及部分中小企业则可能承受越来越大的压力。
经济放缓与通胀高企风险并存 美股与美债或面临双重压力
尽管部分投资者认为美国经济仍能承受当前利率水平，如果高收益率长期持续，风险可能逐渐累积。
Gokhman认为，5%的债券收益率本身未必足以立即对经济造成严重冲击，但它会进一步增加已经承受压力的经济部门的负担。他指出，最新就业数据和消费者信心表现已经显示出经济面临的部分压力。
相比单纯的高利率环境，更值得警惕的是经济增长开始减弱、但通胀却未能同步回落的局面。在这种情况下，美联储可能难以迅速放松货币政策，而高债券收益率则可能继续压制经济活动和资产估值。
Gokhman特别提到，伊朗战争可能使能源价格长期维持高位，从而增加通胀持续的风险。为对冲这一可能性，他和团队近期已在投资组合中增加大宗商品配置。
他认为，如果经济增长放缓与通胀顽固并存，股票和固定收益资产可能同时承压，出现类似2022年的市场环境，而大宗商品则可能成为少数具有避险作用的资产类别。
整体来看，周五疲软的就业数据虽然短暂缓解了美债市场的抛售压力，但并未消除高利率长期化的风险。
对于华尔街而言，真正的问题已不再只是10年期美债收益率是否突破5%，而是这一水平会持续多久，以及实体经济能否在融资成本居高不下的环境中保持增长。
在AI资本开支继续支撑大型科技股的同时，住房、消费信贷和财务实力较弱的企业已经开始承受压力。如果未来经济增长进一步放缓，而能源价格又令通胀难以回落，美股与债市都可能面临更加复杂的投资环境。

title: 日本央行加息仍难提振日元 对冲基金重新建立空头押注 美元多头仓位持续增加
content:
尽管日本央行上个月如期加息，由于其政策立场未能达到市场预期的鹰派程度，加之美日利差仍然显著，日元持续面临贬值压力。美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）最新数据显示，对冲基金已重新建立日元空头仓位，逆转此前连续两周的看涨押注。与此同时，投机资金进一步增加美元多头头寸，并自2024年以来首次转为净做空英镑，反映出外汇市场对美元的看涨情绪有所增强。
根据CFTC数据，截至9月29日当周，杠杆基金持有的日元净空头头寸对应的名义规模约为2100亿日元（约合13亿美元）。具体来看，杠杆基金的日元净持仓由前一周的净多头4472份合约转为净空头16809份合约，意味着短短一周内净持仓变化达到21281份合约，此前连续两周积累的看涨仓位被全面逆转。
日元兑美元汇率已连续第三周走弱，尽管日本政府官员近期就日元持续承压及其潜在影响发表了相关评论，仍未能有效扭转日元的疲弱走势。日本央行上个月按照市场预期提高利率，但其政策表态未能让交易员相信后续将采取更加激进的紧缩措施。与此同时，日本与美国之间仍存在较大的利率差距，继续对日元构成压力。
值得注意的是，不同类型投资者对日元的判断出现明显分化。虽然杠杆基金重新转向做空日元，资产管理机构却进一步增加日元多头仓位。数据显示，截至9月29日当周，资产管理机构将日元净多头头寸增加9463份合约，至51961份合约，表明机构投资者对日元后续走势尚未形成一致预期。
与此同时，投机资金对美元的看涨情绪进一步升温。CFTC数据显示，截至9月29日当周，杠杆基金增加了美元多头押注，同时扩大对欧元和加元等主要货币的净空头仓位。其中，欧元净空头头寸增加23640份合约，至82445份合约；加元净空头头寸增加23396份合约，至72519份合约。
英镑的仓位变化同样值得关注。数据显示，杠杆基金的英镑净持仓由此前的净多头6519份合约转为净空头5377份合约，为2024年以来首次转为净看跌英镑。与此同时，英镑兑美元汇率本周跌至三个月低点，反映出英镑近期持续承压。
其他主要货币方面，杠杆基金将澳元净多头头寸减少570份合约，至55114份合约；纽元净空头头寸减少3762份合约，至1454份合约；瑞郎净空头头寸减少1603份合约，至17017份合约。相比之下，墨西哥比索仍受到部分投机资金青睐，其净多头头寸增加1417份合约，至80677份合约。
从资产管理机构的仓位变化来看，其对主要货币的态度也存在明显差异。除增持日元多头外，资产管理机构还将欧元净多头头寸增加487份合约，至245160份合约。不过，这类机构同期明显增加了对英镑和澳元的看跌押注，其中英镑净空头头寸增加11740份合约，至125424份合约；澳元净空头头寸增加17845份合约，至73073份合约。
此外，资产管理机构将纽元净空头头寸增加9743份合约，至21228份合约；加元净空头头寸增加3116份合约，至25949份合约；瑞郎净空头头寸增加888份合约，至36411份合约。墨西哥比索方面，资产管理机构则大幅削减净多头29255份合约，至16251份合约。
整体来看，最新CFTC持仓数据表明，日本央行加息尚未扭转日元的疲弱走势，美日利差仍是影响日元表现的重要因素。在此背景下，对冲基金重新建立日元空头仓位，并进一步增加美元看涨押注。不过，资产管理机构继续增持日元多头，也显示不同类型投资者对日元前景仍存在分歧。未来日元能否企稳，仍将受到日本央行后续政策立场、美日利差变化以及美元整体走势的影响。

title: 克利夫兰联储行长：美联储下次会前有时间权衡更多数据
content:
克利夫兰联邦储备银行行长贝丝·哈马克表示，决策层在10月下旬再次召开议息会议之前有大量经济数据要考虑。
“我们在月底的会议召开之前还会有大量的信息，所以我们有很多时间来决定什么是正确的政策立场，来确保我们履行职责的两个方面，” 哈马克接受PBS NewsHour采访时说。
“我认为我们在实现充分就业方面做得相当不错，” 她说，“我真正担心的是通胀。”
“我们已经搓过通胀目标五年半以上了，所以把通胀拉回到2%的目标是至关重要的。”
美联储主席沃什淡化前瞻指引 核心副手讲话仍牵动市场预期。

title: The vanishing world of India's street magicians
content:
Sitting in his cramped Delhi home, Ishamuddin Khan can still make a rope appear to rise into the air.

The 55-year-old magician spent decades performing a trick once dismissed as legend, and still keeps photographs and newspaper clippings from his years of international fame.

These days, he spends more time looking back at those memories than performing the trick.

"The times have changed," he says. "Street magic is dying a slow death. It is on a ventilator."

Khan's story reflects a wider change in India, where traditional street performers are finding it increasingly difficult to make a living from their craft.

Magicians, jugglers, puppeteers and acrobats once made a living from crowds in public spaces. Changing entertainment habits and tighter restrictions have made audiences harder to find, pushing many out of the profession.

Khan, one of India's best-known magicians, comes from the Madari community, which has a long tradition of performing in public spaces.

There are no official figures, but Khan says community records identify about 400 Madari families in Delhi, with hundreds more in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Telangana.

Despite their small numbers today, the Madaris trace their roots back centuries.

Historian Ashok Mathur says Madari traditions have roots in Indian folklore, mythology and the long history of travelling performers.

"For generations, these skills were passed through families," he explains.

Khan followed the same path, learning magic from his father and uncles and performing from the age of 12. By his early 20s, he had mastered the rope trick that would later make him famous.

The trick – in which a rope appears to rise into the air before a boy climbs it – was long associated with the mythology of Indian street magic and widely considered impossible, until Khan performed it.

He says it took six years to master the trick, which he first performed publicly in 1995 outside Delhi's iconic Qutub Minar. Two years later, he performed it before 30,000 people on a beach in Karnataka.

His trick brought international attention, and that led to tours to the UK, France, Germany and Japan.

Khan hoped the fame would shine a light on India's traditional performers. For a while, it did. But the attention faded.

As audiences turned to new forms of entertainment and public performance opportunities dwindled, many magicians found it harder to make a living from skills passed down through generations.

One of them is 40-year-old Imam Khan.

Once a magician, Imam now makes a living collecting bottles and recyclables from Delhi's streets. He spends much of his time rag-picking near a western Delhi dump, earning about 200 rupees ($2; £1.57) a day.

Experts say the decline in street performance has multiple causes, chief among them the changing nature of public spaces.

Anurupa Roy, founder of Katkatha Puppet Arts Trust, says performers increasingly struggle to find audiences as public spaces shrink.

"Closed parks and residential societies that bar outsiders are limiting spaces for performance."

Researcher and performer Komita Dhanda says changing attitudes to public spaces are also driving the decline.

"With tighter security, especially in busy town and city centres, there is little space left for street performers," she says.

It is not just individual artists who struggle to get permission. Dhanda says her well-known street theatre group, Jana Natya Manch, often faces hurdles performing in public spaces.

For many artists, the challenge is not just finding a venue but navigating unclear rules over what is allowed.

Most street performers rely on voluntary payments, but experts say the line between performing for money and begging can blur.

Unlike the UK, India has no federal busking framework. Performers instead navigate state-level rules on public order, obstruction, noise and public land.

"This is why street performers often have to face municipal and police regulations governing public spaces, as well as state-specific anti-begging laws," says lawyer Kaushik Mitra.

For many artists, Covid made a bad situation worse.

When India imposed its 2020 lockdown, public performances stopped. Many magicians returned to their villages; some never came back.

"We saw a decline in public performances after this period," Dhanda says. "The brunt was especially harsh for street magicians and performers, many of whom did not return to cities."

For the artists who did return and continue the trade, the challenges only increased.

Shahim Khan, 42, still performs magic on Delhi's streets, sometimes with his 12-year-old daughter, Alia.

Much of his work is now confined to industrial areas, far from the busy public spaces where he once performed, hitting his earnings hard.

Before the pandemic, he could stage four or five shows a day, earning 1,000-1,200 rupees.

"Now I barely manage two shows and earn 200-400 rupees," he says.

The rise of short-form digital entertainment has added to the pressures on traditional performers, experts say. So have changing attitudes towards street arts.

"There was a lot of Western interest in things like the rope trick decades ago. But forms and tastes have changed, and so has what India chooses to showcase," Dhanda says.

For Khan, the loss is about more than money. He fears an art passed down generations could disappear if no-one learns it.

"A trick can survive only if someone learns it," he says.

His son, Altamash, began performing with him as a teenager but now works decorating parties with balloons. In his 30s, he has largely left performing behind.

Years without regular practice have dulled his skills. When he demonstrated his juggling for the BBC, he struggled to find the rhythm.

"I am slowly forgetting all the tricks," he said.

Khan had hoped his son would carry on the family tradition. Altamash had hoped to make a name for himself too, but it did not work out.

"I knew I may not achieve the fame my father has, but I did not think there would come a time when performing would not remain an option," he says.

title: 高盛据悉助客户早期布局SpaceX 上市后斩获数亿美元奖励费
content:
高盛 的银行家在6月操办SpaceX轰动市场的首次公开募股（IPO）时赚取了巨额费用，但与此次上市相关的一笔可观收益在数年前就已埋下伏笔。
据知情人士透露，逾五年前SpaceX估值还只有数百亿美元时，高盛就曾帮助富裕客户安排对埃隆·马斯克旗下这家公司的投资。后来SpaceX以1.77万亿美元估值上市，卖出股票的高盛客户获得巨额收益，并由此向高盛支付了数亿美元的奖励费。
因讨论未公开消息而要求匿名的知情人士表示，高盛合伙人能够与客户一起投资，这意味着一些现任和前任高管可能也实现了可观收益。
高盛发言人拒绝置评。

title: 海湾局势叠加全球变暖，北极航运热度飙升
content:
通过北极航运的规模已达到创纪录水平。随着海冰融化，以及全球关键航运咽喉要道面临压力，船东正寻求替代航线。
据劳氏船级社旗下的 Lloyd’s List Intelligence 数据，北方海航道上个月的航次达到133次，是2022年的四倍多，比8月增加46%。
其中，近一半航次由悬挂俄罗斯国旗的船舶完成。
Lloyd’s List 海事情报与研究主管布里idget·迪亚昆表示：“随着各国政府和运营商越来越多地寻找受地缘政治风险影响较小的替代航线，北方海航道的发展趋势值得关注。”
9月通常是北极航线最繁忙的月份，因为此时海冰面积降至最低，没有破冰能力的船舶也可以通行。
南安普顿大学研究人员表示，2025年北极海冰经历了有卫星记录以来最大的单年冬季下降，此后一直处于历史低位。
海冰减少，加上曼德布海峡等关键航运通道面临更大压力，使北方海航道对船东的吸引力不断上升。曼德布海峡位于红海入口，目前受到也门胡塞武装威胁。此前，伊朗因美国袭击伊朗而限制船只通过霍尔木兹海峡，导致曼德布海峡成为沙特阿拉伯石油出口的重要通道。
与此同时，巴拿马运河今年也遭遇干旱。
液化天然气运输船经常利用这条航线前往俄罗斯的亚马尔和北极液化天然气二号工厂。不过，散货船的数量也有所增加，这类船舶通常运输谷物或铁矿石等大宗商品。
数据显示，9月通过北方海航道的散货船达到29艘，高于8月的18艘，也超过去年9月创下的12艘此前最高纪录。
此外，投入该航线运营的原油油轮数量也创下纪录。
北方海航道被划分为28个区段。俄罗斯国家原子能公司控制的北方海航道管理局会根据冰况，为不同区段制定相应航行规定，并负责签发通行许可。
保险公司和环保组织警告称，航道使用率不断上升，可能导致重大事故，而该地区的搜救和污染清理能力十分有限。
1989年，超级油轮“埃克森·瓦尔迪兹”号在阿拉斯加沿岸发生重大漏油事故，清理工作至少持续了四年；然而，事故残留物至今仍滞留在附近海滩。
Tara海洋基金会执行主任罗曼·特鲁布莱表示，即使是小规模漏油，也可能加剧全球变暖，因为黑色油滴会吸收阳光，促进海冰融化。
对于船员而言，北极航行同样存在重大危险，因为当地天气难以预测，环境条件极其恶劣。
英国海道测量局技术合作负责人汤姆·梅勒表示，在极高纬度地区，导航设备可能无法正常工作。
他说：“在这条纬度线以北或以南，地球曲率会明显增大，必须采用不同的方法显示数据，才能确保其在海图上的定位准确。”
他还表示：“如果船上没有一套能够正确显示海图的系统，我可不愿意登船。”

title: Which clubs did Man City's 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?
content:
The money flowed around football. It made a lot of other clubs richer. It helped teams everywhere and especially in the Premier League.

These have been some of the arguments used by those backing Manchester City in the media and online since the verdicts declaring the club guilty came in and an appeal was announced. The suggestion is that there was a net benefit to the game as a whole, and in particular the clubs to whom Manchester City paid big transfer fees.

The more than £900m by which the independent commission found the club had "inflated" its accounts was not all spent on transfer fees.

Clubs have many bills, including wages for players and other staff, utilities, insurance, infrastructure costs, commercial fees and much more.

But the roughly £1.2bn Man City spent on players between 2009-2018 (about £900m net spend) was more than anybody else in that period.

That outlay was vital in making them England's most successful club, and would surely have been heavily reduced had they not knowingly broken the rules, as the independent commission concluded.

So where did City's money flow to in the transfer market, and what impact did it have?

Who did Man City pay most money to between 2009 and 2018?

Football transfers include many costs.

The amount required to sign the player is the most obvious, but there are also agents' fees, legal expenses, administration money and potentially signing-on bonuses.

That means the money dished out by Manchester City during the 'asterisk era' will have reached people and bodies who work in the background of football deal-making and is difficult to track.

But what can be done is analysis of the fundamental interactions between City and other clubs.

Below is a list of every club to whom Manchester City paid transfer fees between summer 2009 and winter 2018, in descending order from the most money to the least.

The list is for senior players and does not include free transfers, loans or academy graduates.

That is 46 different clubs in 19 national league systems.

For some of them, the fees paid by City were the highest the clubs had ever received at the time.

Looking at the spread of money among clubs demonstrates just how far and wide Manchester City's money was spent.

The split in money spent on transfer fees by City during the timeframe is relatively even across some of the highest-ranked leagues in Europe, though the Premier League is higher than any other.

Just over a quarter of their total transfer outlay was paid to clubs in the English top flight.

They signed players from eight Premier League clubs, and the same amount in La Liga.

A combined £13m was spent on two players in the Championship.

Did the money really help football?

Manchester City's spending power unquestionably changed the world football transfer market - their willingness to pay higher fees and wages meant prices rose for everybody else too.

And once the world knows that a club has a wedge of cash burning a hole in its pocket courtesy of City, it can be difficult to spend it.

Asking prices may rise, and having an influx of money is no guarantee of it being well spent.

For many of the teams to whom City paid the most during this time, the money did not work out particularly beneficially.

Let's take a look at some of the more interesting cases.

First up, Wolfsburg. They immediately signed winger Julian Draxler for about half the fee received for Kevin de Bruyne in 2016, as well as others including veteran defender Dante.

Having lost De Bruyne, they dropped from second to eighth in the Bundesliga before narrowly avoiding relegation in the subsequent two seasons.

And things did not go particularly well for second highest-ranked club Monaco either.

The most direct replacements they signed following the sales of Benjamin Mendy and Bernardo Silva in the same summer to Manchester City - Terence Kongolo and Keita Balde - did not work out in the long run, and the team went from winning Ligue 1 and reaching the Champions League semi-finals to almost being relegated within two years.

The club City purchased most players from in the 2009-18 period - Arsenal (four) - did not mount a serious Premier League title challenge during that time.

Some clubs who did not receive payments from City could also argue that the spending of money from their "inflated" accounts compromised their chances.

For example, Manchester City paid very similar totals to Benfica and Porto during the era, but nothing to Sporting, the club which makes up the big three in Portugal.

Sporting did not win a title between 2009 and 2018. There are many reasons for that, but could one of them be the fact that their direct rivals received money from City that would perhaps not have been on offer had they followed football's financial rules?

Of the 12 clubs who received the highest amount of money from Man City, only the two Portuguese clubs won a top division league title or European trophy within less than four full seasons of the player sale(s).

In all the years since, the only other clubs in the top 12 who have managed to do so are the four Premier League sides.

There are also some ancillary fees which reached clubs whom Manchester City did not deal with directly.

Some players were subject to sell-on clauses, where the club City where buying the player from owed money to the previous team who owned the player.

For example, Queens Park Rangers earned roughly £9m from Raheem Sterling's move to City from Liverpool in 2015.

Barnsley took about £7m of the transfer fee paid to Everton for John Stones in 2016, and the Toffees also had to pass on about £2.5m to Wolves when Joleon Lescott moved to Manchester in 2009.

The Sterling and Stones clauses were worth more than most players operating in the English Football League at that time, significantly strengthening the financial positions of QPR and Barnsley.

To this day Barnsley have not sold a player for a higher amount than the fee they are believed to have received for Stones.

But QPR have not returned to the Premier League and Barnsley dropped down to League One from the Championship after two seasons.

Manchester City's spending during the time in which they were breaking the rules certainly had an enormous impact, on their own upward trajectory, the futures of other clubs around the world and the wider football economy.

But the reality is that it is impossible to unweave the tapestry of football history during that time and since - too much has happened and there are too many indirect consequences.

The effects of that spending will reverberate for years to come.

title: Pretorius breaks Gayle's T20 record score
content:
CSA T20 Challenge, Bloemfontein

Titans 267-3 (20 overs): Pretorius 188* (79); Boast 1-46

Knights 143 (17.2 overs): Cloete 39 (25); Ferreira 3-16

Titans won by 124 runs

Scorecard

Lhuan-dre Pretorius has broken Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.

The 20-year-old South African's knock off 79 deliveries, including 13 sixes and 15 fours, helped Titans post 267-3 against Knights in the CSA T20 Challenge.

It eclipsed the 175 not out made by Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore (now Bengaluru) against Pune Warriors in the 2013 Indian Premier League.

Pretorius, who has played 17 T20s, three one-dayers and two Tests for South Africa, finished with a strike rate of 237.97.

He made his half-century off 24 balls but only required 16 more balls to get to three figures and then got to 150 off just 58 deliveries.

Titans then bowled out Knights for 143 to wrap up an emphatic 124-run victory at the Mangaung Oval in Bloemfontein.

title: Two Iranian small-boat migrants charged with plotting attack on Jewish targets in Manchester
content:
Robert Wright in London

Published October 2 2026

Updated October 2 2026

Counterterror police on Friday charged two Iranian men who arrived in the UK by small boat with terrorism offences over an alleged plot to attack Manchester’s Jewish community, in a plot that officers said might have been directed from Iran.

Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool, and Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, were charged on the first anniversary of the attack on Manchester’s Heaton Park synagogue , which took place during Yom Kippur and left two worshippers and the attacker dead.

It also comes two days after Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were “strong indications” that Iran had a hand in Sunday’s alleged plot to target RAF Fairford air base in Gloucestershire. Tehran has categorically denied any involvement in the incident.

UK authorities have previously alleged that Iran had a role in multiple attacks on Jewish, Israeli and Iranian dissident targets in Britain.

The men were arrested in Manchester on September 20, hours before the start of this year’s Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar. The men arrived by small boats in 2020 and 2023, according to the Home Office. Without saying which was which, the department said one had been granted asylum while the other had a live asylum claim.

Counter Terrorism Policing said on Friday: “They were both charged on Friday October 2 with engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts. It is alleged that the two men were in contact with an overseas third party who may be in Iran in relation to the plot.”

The two men will appear in court on Saturday at Westminster Magistrates’ Court.

The charges allege that the men acquired instructions and equipment to assemble improvised explosive devices and conducted reconnaissance of potential targets.

Vicki Evans, senior national co-ordinator for CTP, said: “This investigation has led to the disruption of what we believe to have been a plot targeting the Jewish community in Manchester.”

She added: “I’m aware that the news of this alleged plot coming during the High Holy Day period has caused a great deal of concern to the Jewish community, as well as the wider public.”

Referring to the RAF Fairford incident, when five people were intercepted by local police, Evans said the past week had brought “into sharp focus” some of the potential threats from Iran.

She added: “While this incident and the investigation into the RAF Fairford incident are not connected in any way, I want to reassure the public that CTP, working with our national security partners, is using the full range of our capabilities to protect the UK from any hostile acts.”

The men’s arrivals on small boat crossings are likely to further increase pressure on the government to be seen to be acting decisively to stop clandestine arrivals and to enhance security screening of people seeking asylum.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said on Friday evening that the latest developments would be “deeply distressing” to Jewish communities.

She added: “I know this will be especially true in Manchester, as we mark one year since the terrorist attack at Heaton Park Synagogue. The fact both suspects arrived by small boat several years ago is a reminder of the importance of our relentless work to tackle illegal migration into this country. While numbers are down, I know there is more we must do.”

Nigel Farage, leader of the anti-immigration Reform UK party who has long campaigned on the risk of terrorists arriving on small boats, accused the government of inviting “terror and horror into our communities”.

“We now have a state of national emergency on our borders, and this government is trying to open them to even more unknown individuals,” he added, referring to plans to reopen a resettlement scheme .

He suggested Mahmood “must resign” if she “disagrees”.

Additional reporting by David Sheppard

title: Why thousands of couples are choosing Scotland to say 'I do'
content:
Hayden Kuhn and Savannah Aanderud had never set foot in Scotland before they decided it was the perfect place to get married last May.

The couple, from Pennsylvania in the US, wanted a destination wedding that would take their family and friends on an adventure with them.

They considered locations across Europe, before deciding on Scotland after Savannah saw photographs of a castle wedding online.

"I think it was on Pinterest," she said. "Somebody got married in a castle and I was like 'Oh, I have to do that'."

The pair are far from alone in seeing Scotland as the ultimate romantic destination.

Nearly a quarter of all marriages registered in Scotland last year involved couples who did not live in the country.

Figures from National Records of Scotland show that 6,596 of the 27,191 weddings recorded in 2025 involved neither partner being a Scottish resident.

But what is it about the country that persuades these couples to travel hundreds and sometimes thousands of miles to get married here?

The Gretna Green tradition

Nowhere attracts more visiting couples than Gretna Green.

Of the 6,596 marriages involving non-Scottish residents last year, 3,492 took place in the Dumfries and Galloway town, meaning it alone accounted for more than half of Scotland's destination weddings.

The town's association with romance dates back to 1754, when changes to marriage laws in England prompted young runaway couples to cross the border into Scotland, where they could marry without needing parental consent.

More than 250 years later, it remains one of the world's best-known wedding destinations.

It was this reputation that appealed to Patryk and Angelika Klimorowski, both 27, who travelled from north-west England to tie the knot there.

The couple said Scotland had long been woven into their relationship.

They first met when they were 15, when Patryk's parents moved to England from Poland, and one of the first things they bonded over was the 1996 movie Loch Ness.

Years later, that shared childhood favourite took on new significance when Patryk proposed on its shores.

Their connection to Scotland first started on a road trip in 2021, and they have regularly returned to explore the Highlands and celebrate their anniversaries in Edinburgh.

This year alone, they have travelled north of the border every two months.

So Scotland felt like the natural place to say "I do", they said.

Both Angelika and Patryk are history lovers and said they were drawn to the centuries-old tradition of a Gretna wedding.

"It meant something to us being part of that heritage." Angelika said.

Patryk said that his favourite memory was watching his bride walk down the aisle to the sound of Flower of Scotland played on the bagpipes.

"That sort of music just creates such a whimsical and romantic atmosphere that really can't be recreated in many countries outside of Scotland," Angelika said.

Those moments left a lasting impression on their families who had travelled from Poland.

"They hadn't really experienced anything like that before," she said.

The appeal was not just Gretna's history, Angelika said.

Less than an hour‘s drive from where they got married, the couple found themselves surrounded by dramatic scenery for their wedding photographs.

"There's not a lot of places in the world where you can do that," she said.

Although neither bride nor groom is Scottish, both say they feel a deep connection to the country.

"It's not home, but it feels like a home away from home," Angelika said.

Islands and Highlands

Chihon Ley Polanco, from Chile, and Ana-Maria Bucatari, from Moldova, came to Scotland to study, but the country quickly became the backdrop to their love story.

The couple first met in 2018 through a dance society at the University of Edinburgh, when Ana-Maria was on an Erasmus exchange and Chihon was completing his postgraduate studies.

They they spent years as friends, and it was not until Ana-Maria returned to Edinburgh in 2024 that their relationship became something more.

And their romance blossomed in the same place their friendship had years earlier.

"Everything happened again on the dance floor," Ana-Maria said.

Just four months after getting engaged, the pair walked down the aisle on the Isle of Arran.

The couple said they "fell in love" with the island at first sight, due to it having the "complete scenery of Scotland".

"You feel that you're in a magical place", said Chihon. "It's very unique."

The couple said Scotland felt like the natural choice.

"We're from two different continents," Chihon said. "Scotland is where we met and where we built our life together."

Their wedding brought together family and friends from across the world, with parts of the ceremony translated live into Spanish and Russian for relatives travelling from Chile and Moldova.

Chihon said friends from all over the world joined the couple for their celebrations.

The highlights of the night included a traditional ceilidh and a final group karaoke singalong of Sunshine on Leith, led by their Scottish wedding guests.

While some of their international guests were unfamiliar with Scottish wedding traditions, that did little to dampen their enthusiasm.

"We had people saying, 'We have no idea what's going on, but we're going to join in'," Chihon said.

He said Scotland would always hold a special place in their lives.

"Like Robbie Burns said, 'my heart's in the Highlands wherever I go'," he said.

"I think Scotland will be with us forever. I couldn't be more grateful. It was already special to me before, but now that I'm married to the woman of my dreams, it's like I owe everything to Scotland."

Heritage, history and castles

The same experience was echoed by Hayden and Savannah.

Despite arriving in Scotland just two days before their wedding, the couple said the country's wedding industry made planning from abroad remarkably straightforward.

They chose a castle near Edinburgh, and were drawn not only by the scenery but also by the sense of history they felt was harder to find back home.

"Scotland has this combination of this lovely countryside beauty and history," Savannah said.

"You don't get a lot of the historical venues like you do here, in the United States."

The couple also wove Scottish traditions into their ceremony, taking part in a Celtic handfasting ritual, using pieces of fabric provided by both of their grandmothers.

They said an important part of their decision was the chance to share the experience with loved ones.

"We wanted to go somewhere that would take our whole family on an adventure with us," Hayden said.

Many of their guests turned the wedding into a longer holiday, extending their stays to explore Scotland and even joining the couple on their honeymoon in the Highlands afterwards.

Looking back, the newlyweds say Scotland exceeded every expectation.

Savannah said: "Scotland is like nothing we've ever seen before. We were just blown away by how beautiful everything was."

title: 七国集团同意释放紧急储备后 特朗普称美国不会禁止柴油出口
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他不会禁止美国柴油出口。此前，七国集团（G7）及其合作伙伴同意释放部分紧急燃料储备，以压低飙升的价格。
“欧洲有大量柴油，他们将为全球作出重大贡献——我们也会，”特朗普周五在白宫对记者表示。“我们不会实施出口禁令。”
在特朗普政府大力施压后，包括欧洲、北美和亚洲主要经济体在内的G7周五同意释放最多1亿桶紧急石油和柴油储备。
“我确实问过他们，我们将会有大量石油，”特朗普还表示。“他们做得很好。”
特朗普作出上述表态之际，柴油价格正经历创纪录的飙升。柴油是现代经济的重要燃料，不仅驱动农业机械和美国航运业，还为农村社区提供供暖与电力。

title: 巴西大选在即 美国和澳大利亚突然以安全关切为由暂停当地领事服务
content:
在周日即将举行大选的巴西，美国和澳大利亚以“安全关切”为由暂停了当地的领事服务。
美国大使馆指示寻求紧急援助的公民切勿前往外交机构，要求他们通过电话联络值班官员。澳大利亚使馆则通知其公民联系位于堪培拉的应急中心。
两个使馆均未公开安全关切的性质。
巴西联邦警察周五晚些时候发表声明称，在对可能威胁美国外交设施的可疑行动计划进行调查时，他们在圣保罗和巴西利亚附近执行了两项搜查令。
警方表示，目前调查人员尚未发现任何证据证实最初认定的威胁，也未发现任何嫌疑人与犯罪组织存在关联。调查仍在进行中，包括对缴获的通讯设备和其它媒体资料进行分析。
据一位不愿公开身份的知情人士透露，美国驻巴西所有外交机构的工作人员已接到指示从周五开始在家办公。
美国政府表示，正与巴西当局合作“应对安全问题”。
巴西外交部尚未对此作出回应。
巴西将于10月4日投票，左翼总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦与他的保守派挑战者弗拉维奥·博索纳罗目前势均力敌。

title: 大宗商品综述：燃料价格大跌 铜价微升 金价走低

柴油价格大跌，此前七国集团（G7）释放信号称将释放紧急储备，以缓解能源成本飙升给消费者带来的部分压力。
欧洲柴油价格一度暴跌逾8%，随后收窄跌幅，而美国柴油期货一度下跌5.6%。

尽管如此，分析师和交易员表示，最新的储备投放可能不足以抵消持续的供应损失。
TP ICAP Group能源专家Scott Shelton表示：“我认为这削弱了柴油价格进一步上涨的逻辑，但投放的柴油数量没有大到足以对市场形成压倒性影响”。
本周油价波动，一方面中东石油供应状况改善，另一方面美国与伊朗未能在达成持久和平协议方面取得明显进展。

title: 纽约汇市：美元创一个月最大跌幅 就业数据疲软扰乱了利率预期
content:
纽约汇市周五美元创下一个月来最大单日跌幅，此前一份报告显示，美国9月份新增就业人数低于预期，一度令交易员对美联储今年是否会再次加息的押注出现动摇。
彭博美元现货指数下跌0.3%，之前美国政府公布的数据显示上月非农就业人数增加2.9万人，而彭博对经济学家的调查所得预测中值为9万人。失业率从4.1%小幅升至4.2%。
数据公布后，交易员一度下调对美联储加息的押注，不再完全预计年底前会再次加息。不过，到交易日结束时，市场又再度预计年底前会有一次加息，但美元仍维持下跌。
美元本周早些时候上涨，原因是美国与伊朗的对峙推动油价维持高位，同时市场对法国财政和政治风险的担忧加剧，提振了对美元这一避险资产的需求。周五，几乎所有G10货币兑美元都上涨。
富国策略师Erik Nelson表示：“这是一份喜忧参半的报告，足以抑制市场对美联储加息前景的定价，但又没有糟糕到削弱对美国经济增长的预期。美元走弱的反应应该会消退，市场注意力将重新转向欧洲的风险溢价。”
本周，法国政府公布了通过限制支出和增加税收收入来缩小预算赤字的计划，加剧了投资者对该国债务的担忧。
欧元周五上涨0.1%，但全周兑美元仍下跌逾1%。 法国兴业 银行首席外汇策略师Kit Juckes表示，推高能源价格的中东局势迟迟未获解决，“显然在短期内对欧元不利、对美元则是利好。”
美元本周仍上涨约0.8%，连续第三周走高，为2025年1月份以来最长连涨。
美国商品期货交易委员会的数据显示，截至9月29日当周，投机交易员连续第二周增加美元看涨头寸。

title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
content:
The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.

The party said it would cost £2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.

On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early, under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.

Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.

Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.

Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.

Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.

The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.

The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.

An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "A violent criminal doesn't become less dangerous just because the government has run out of prison cells."

She added: "[Labour's] answer is to let dangerous offenders out even earlier instead of building the prison spaces we need."

Labour Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said: "The Tories are taking the public for fools. Across 14 years in government, they added just 500 prison places and closed 23 prisons.

"Now Kemi Badenoch expects the British people to believe they'll build 50,000."

The Liberal Democrats also criticised the Tory plan, describing it as "fantasy numbers funded by breaking promises".

"Much like their economic plans, something doesn't add up," added the party's justice spokesperson Jess Brown-Fuller.

Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy told BBC Breakfast the 50,000 extra places would be built within six to seven years "and the vast majority of them will be built in the first parliament".

Meanwhile, the Prison Governors' Association said "long-term investment" was needed and warned a "staffing crisis" would pose challenges to delivering new prisons.

If the party wins power, the Tories said they would introduce legislation early in the new Parliament to override planning and procurement barriers, allowing the process to be "fast-tracked".

It said the use of private finance would help speed up delivery and control costs.

There are currently around 89,000 useable prison places in England and Wales, according to the latest government figures.

The Tories said their proposals would increase this figure by more than 50%, with the vast majority of new places expected within the party's first Parliament in government - up to five years - and the full increase delivered within seven years.

The £2bn a year cost would be funded through savings in other areas, including cutting the aid budget by £1bn and reducing the budget of the Department for Culture Media and Sport by £1bn.

The Labour government has promised to add 14,000 extra prison space by 2031.

The Tories argued increasing prison places would cut crime and prevent reoffending by keeping serious criminals off the streets.

Timothy said: "Prison works. It works by punishing and deterring, but most importantly by incapacitating.

"Prison should keep violent and repeat offenders away from the law-abiding public."

The prison population has risen significantly in recent decades, partly as a result of longer sentences and more people being returned to prison for breaching the conditions of their release.

Successive governments have pledged to increase the number of prison places - but delivery has often fallen short of those promises.

New prisons take years to build, often facing local opposition and obstacles in the planning process.

The Prison Governors' Association said: "Building 50,000 cells is one thing; finding the thousands of experienced officers, governors and specialists needed to run them safely is quite another.

"Politicians have spent years announcing prison places while the service struggles with overcrowding, ageing infrastructure and staffing shortages. The real test is not how many places can be promised, but how many prisons can be operated safely, effectively, and sustainably."

title: 10月3日外盘头条：沙特计划对胡塞武装发动攻势 科技公司推出萌系吉祥物 道明证券推迟美联储加息时点预期
content:
全球财经媒体昨夜今晨 共同关注的头条新闻主要有：
1、 七国集团将释放多达1亿桶柴油和石油储备以遏制价格上涨
2、 报道：沙特计划对也门胡塞武装发动攻势
3、 谷歌一直在追赶OpenAI与Anthropic，其全新旗舰模型真能跻身前沿梯队吗 ？
4 、 科技公司推出萌系吉祥物，以缓解AI焦虑
5、 迈克・库乌：遭债券抛售冲击的板块有望迎来反弹
6、 道明证券推迟美联储加息时点预期 料下次行动在12月
七国集团将释放多达1亿桶柴油和石油储备以遏制价格上涨
在特朗普政府一周来不断施压要求遏制燃料价格上涨之后，七国集团（G7）及其合作伙伴周五决定将释放多达1亿桶紧急石油和柴油储备。
法国总统马克龙周五表示，此次释放将由国际能源署协调，将在未来四个月内进行，初期的重点是柴油。他说，此举旨在“向市场发出明确的信号”。
消息公布后，欧洲和美国柴油期货价格大跌，布伦特原油期货最初也走低不过之后出现反弹。
报道：沙特计划对也门胡塞武装发动攻势
据媒体援引未具名海湾地区和也门官员以及西方外交人士报道，沙特阿拉伯正计划对也门胡塞武装发动攻势。
这项行动预计将在未来数周内启动，由受利雅得监督的也门地面部队主导，并获得沙特空袭支援
盟友预计不会直接参与作战行动。
“乔治·H·W·布什”号和乔治·华盛顿”号航母将继续留在当地。在4月针对伊朗的军事行动之前，美国上一次在中东同时部署三个航母打击群还是2003年。
谷歌一直在追赶OpenAI与Anthropic，其全新旗舰模型真能跻身前沿梯队吗 ？
谷歌 本周发布最新旗舰大模型 Gemini 4 Argon，希望在前沿 AI 赛道与 OpenAI、Anthropic 同台竞争。
分析师看好 Argon，该模型在基准评测榜单取得顶尖成绩。
新模型将谨慎分阶段落地，优先向网络安全合作方开放；但分析师认为，真正考验在于企业大规模投产部署之后。
科技公司推出萌系吉祥物，以缓解AI焦虑
AI公司正尝试发起一场新的“魅力攻势”：它们使用看起来像毛绒玩具般可爱的角色，试图让自己的技术显得不那么令人恐惧。
OpenAI 的最新 AI 代理由戴着领结和眼镜的彩色卡通角色化身而成；Meta 的 Muse 助手的吉祥物则是一个双颊红润的蛋形角色；而 Anthropic 也有自己友好的像素风橙色螃蟹“Clawd”。
随着公众对AI导致失业以及给人类带来生存风险的焦虑日益加剧，科技公司正效仿消费品公司和制药企业的营销策略，推出一系列萌系吉祥物。
其目的是让这些正在为我们编写代码、搜索互联网并代为预订日程的AI助手显得更加平易近人、个性鲜明且值得信赖。既然“绿巨人”能让孩子们乖乖吃蔬菜，那么一个甜美的拟人化三角形或许也能赢得AI怀疑论者的青睐。
迈克・库乌：遭债券抛售冲击的板块有望迎来反弹
公用事业板块正在上演一场耐人寻味的多空博弈。
一方面，一轮规模空前的 AI 基建建设，让这个原本走势沉闷的板块迎来前所未有的盈利爆发。另一方面，美债收益率走出 1994 年以来最迅猛的上涨行情，给该板块的高光表现蒙上阴影，板块股价应声走低。各大科技企业高管不断强调巨大的能源需求，但一旦出现利率上行、信贷环境收紧的信号，资本密集型的公用事业股票会首当其冲受到冲击。
公用事业板块的股息对追求收益的投资者具备吸引力；但随着债券收益率走高，债券相对分红股票的吸引力提升，形成直接竞争。
收益率曲线大幅飙升之时，公用事业板块 ETF（XLU）已经从近期高点出现大幅回落。
道明证券推迟美联储加息时点预期 料下次行动在12月
美联储副主席菲利普·杰斐逊表示，决策者可能需要更多时间，才能判断是否有必要进一步加息以遏制通胀。
杰斐逊警告称，通胀过高的时间已经太久，并认为通胀存在持续处于高位的风险。但他也表示，自己和同僚正在权衡一系列经济冲击，需要仔细评估未来公布的数据，然后决定下一步行动。
杰斐逊在预定周四于弗吉尼亚州Charlottesville发表的讲话稿中表示：“展望未来，我认为今后任何政策调整都应通过仔细考察数据趋势、不断变化的前景以及风险平衡来决定。我和我的同事需要作出自己的判断，这可能需要更多时间。”

title: US justice department will not reopen criminal probe of Fed’s Jay Powell
content:
Ella Lee and Claire Jones in Washington

Published October 2 2026

The US Department of Justice will not reopen its criminal probe of Jay Powell over the Federal Reserve’s $2.5bn renovation project, after an investigation by the central bank’s watchdog cleared the former chair of criminal wrongdoing.

The long-awaited report from the Fed’s independent inspector general found “deficiencies in the management” of the project but stopped short of identifying “administrative misconduct”.

“Making mistakes and not having any sort of oversight over the folks doing billion-dollar projects isn’t necessarily a crime,” US attorney-general Todd Blanche said in an interview with Bloomberg Television on Friday.

The watchdog said in the report that at no time during its evaluation “did we find reasonable grounds to believe that a violation of federal criminal law had occurred” that required a referral to the attorney-general.

Following the release of the report on Wednesday, Donald Trump revived his attacks on Powell, who has remained on the Fed’s Board of Governors after his term as chair ended in May. The president pointed to the blowout cost of the renovation as proof of Powell’s incompetence and suggested he should “be forced to resign, IMMEDIATELY”.

Blanche told Bloomberg that he was satisfied with the report but did not think Powell had appropriately overseen the renovation project, which has run over budget by several hundred million dollars. Blanche also did not rule out future action if evidence of wrongdoing was uncovered.

The DoJ earlier this year dropped its criminal probe into Powell’s handling of the renovation after a group of Republican lawmakers refused to support Trump’s nomination of current chair Kevin Warsh until it was resolved.

However, Jeanine Pirro, the US attorney for the District of Columbia, raised the prospect of reopening it should the inspector general find evidence of wrongdoing.

Powell had vowed to remain at the US central bank as a governor until the DoJ investigation was “ well and truly over , with transparency and finality”.

The former chair, who was repeatedly criticised by Trump over his refusal to slash interest rates as the president desired, has the right to remain on the Fed’s board until early 2028.

The Fed did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Hawaii's iconic 550-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch collapses
content:
Hawaii's famous Hōlei Sea Arch, a 90-foot-tall (27.4m) lava rock structure that formed about 550 years ago, has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean.

The collapse's exact time is not known. The arch was still projecting into the water from the coast of Volcanoes National Park on 23 September, but was gone by 27 September, the National Park Service (NPS) said.

"The coastline flanking the sea arch has shown signs of instability for years," NPS, which warned in 2021 that the arch would eventually crumble, said in a statement.

Located at the end of Chain of Craters Road on the island of Hawaii, also called "the big island", the formation was a popular - and heavily photographed - tourist destination.

The arch is believed to have fallen when the park was temporarily closed during Tropical Storm Nolo last weekend.

The park service said earthquakes during the 2018 Kīlauea volcano eruption and summit collapse had damaged the cliffs near the arch.

Its ultimate collapse marks "the latest transformation of the park's remote and rugged coastline".

In January 2020, new cracks and instability in the cliffs led the park to close the original arch viewing area, and a few months later, a new viewing area opened at a safer distance, NPS said.

Waves from a tropical storm later that year broke off a chunk of rock from the bottom of the arch.

"This formation is beautiful, but temporary, and has a limited life span," the park service said in 2021. "The sea arch will eventually crumble into the sea. However, others will replace it as the cliff slowly migrates inland."

Thousands of people have liked and commented on the NPS social media post about the arch's collapse, including sharing their memories of visiting the arch and posting photos of it.

"Nothing and no one is here forever," one Facebook user commented. "Millions of years from now the sun will die. Appreciate the good, the beauty, now."

title: 原油：燃料价格大跌 七国集团计划释放战略储备
content:
柴油价格大跌，此前七国集团（G7）释放信号称将释放紧急储备，以缓解能源成本飙升给消费者带来的部分压力。
欧洲柴油价格一度暴跌逾8%，随后收窄跌幅，而美国柴油期货一度下跌5.6%。
法国总统马克龙早些时候表示，G7将释放多达1亿桶紧急石油和柴油储备。
特朗普政府正采取多种手段压低燃料价格，白宫此前敦促欧盟释放库存，旨在防止美国被迫出台柴油出口禁令。
尽管如此，分析师和交易员表示，最新的储备投放可能不足以抵消持续的供应损失。
TP ICAP Group能源专家Scott Shelton表示：“我认为这削弱了柴油价格进一步上涨的逻辑，但投放的柴油数量没有大到足以对市场形成压倒性影响”。
本周油价波动，一方面中东石油供应状况改善，另一方面美国与伊朗未能在达成持久和平协议方面取得明显进展。
令供应形势更加困难的是，中国出口商取消了部分原定于10月出口的成品油货物以优先保障国内供应。

title: US backs down from fuel export ban threat as G7 agrees to release 100mn barrels
content:
Ian Johnston and Henry Foy in Brussels, Malcolm Moore in London and Myles McCormick in Washington

Published October 2 2026

Updated October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

The US has backed down on a threat to stop exporting fuel to the world as part of a deal in which European countries agreed to release more diesel from their strategic reserves on Friday.

The decision comes as US President Donald Trump attempts to douse a surge in diesel prices for American industry and farmers ahead of November’s midterm elections , which will determine control of Congress.

G7 leaders said after a meeting on Friday that they would release 100mn barrels of crude and diesel, co-ordinated by the International Energy Agency, “in light of ongoing market pressures”.

In a joint statement, they did not give full details of the plan but said the release would be carried out over a four-month period, beginning “immediately”, and including a “substantial” release of diesel reserves within the first 20 days.

The intervention will take into account “commitments that have already been fulfilled” under a pre-existing 400mn-barrel pledge made in March, of which 325mn barrels have already been released, according to the IEA.

Three people familiar with the details of the release said 40mn barrels would come from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, while Europe would contribute about 50mn barrels of diesel, with the remainder coming from Asia.

The agreement comes after Trump had faced intense pressure from Republican legislators representing America’s agricultural heartlands to impose an export ban to ease the strain on farmers ahead of next month’s elections.

European negotiators — and the US oil industry — had raced to avert a suspension, which would have sent global fuel prices soaring.

“We’re not going to be doing the export ban,” Trump told reporters on Friday, describing Europe’s commitment to release diesel stocks as “a great thing”.

“Europe has a lot of diesel and they’re going to be making a major world contribution and so are we,” he said. “We’re going to have a lot of oil.”

Two diplomats familiar with the discussions said the White House had asked Europe to unlock at least 100mn barrels and threatened to go ahead with the ban on US diesel exports if European countries failed to meet Washington’s demand.

The joint statement included a commitment from the signatories — including the US — “to refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products between G7 countries and call on all producers to refrain from imposing bans that could exacerbate market tensions”.

Asked if Washington had ruled out a diesel export ban as part of the G7 release, the White House pointed to the pledge in the joint statement.

French President Emmanuel Macron said G7 members had agreed “not to take any measure to restrict the exchange of oil and energy products between partner countries”.

European diesel futures extended declines after the announcement, with the benchmark down 8 per cent to $1,337.75 a tonne, the lowest level since the start of September. Wholesale diesel for sale in New York harbour fell almost 2 per cent to $4.56 a gallon.

The G7 leaders said they would “convene in the context of the IEA in the coming days to discuss the possibility of additional diesel releases as necessary”.

The release is a big win for the US oil industry, which had lobbied hard against an export ban and encouraged the administration to lean on allies to dump stocks as an alternative.

“We welcome the administration’s efforts to secure a co-ordinated G7 release of 100mn barrels of crude and refined products, along with a commitment not to impose export restrictions between parties,” said Bethany Williams, spokesperson for the American Petroleum Institute, an industry lobby group.

Macron said on Friday that the release would “send a clear signal to markets”.

France had earlier proposed a plan in which Europe would release 50mn barrels of diesel and for IEA countries to unlock a further 50mn barrels of crude, according to several diplomats familiar with the matter.

In March, Europe committed to release 73mn barrels of refined fuels as part of a 400mn-barrel strategic stock draw co-ordinated by the IEA in response to the conflict in the Middle East.

The US has largely completed its share of that programme, but some European countries have not yet met their obligations, according to Fatih Birol, head of the IEA.

Diesel prices have been trading above $200 a barrel in the US, Europe and Asia for several weeks because of several shocks to the world’s refineries, including from the Iran war, Russia’s conflict with Ukraine and China’s decision to limit fuel exports.

Additional reporting by Sarah White in Paris and James Politi in Washington

title: 10月3日收盘：美股周五收涨 就业数据走弱提振市场
content:
美国9月非农就业报告意外疲软，提振市场预期，认为美联储将在10月议息会议上按兵不动。
道琼斯 工业平均指数上涨250点，涨幅0.5%；标普500指数涨0.7%； 纳斯达克 综合指数攀升1.2%。纳指盘中一度创下历史新高，不过美债收益率随后反弹，带动美股从日内高点回落。
尽管周五迎来反弹，道指本周仍累计下跌约1.3%；标普500基本持平，小幅下跌0.3%；纳指本周上涨0.6%，周五实现三连涨。
9月就业数据公布后，美债收益率早盘下行，但后续反弹，拖累美股脱离日内高点。
华尔街风险偏好回升，科技股集体走强。英伟达股价创下5月以来新高，不过收盘未能守住历史最高收盘价； CrowdStrike 、Palo Alto Net works、 AMD 同样触及历史高位，AMD收盘涨幅近3%。
上月非农数据显示，美国新增就业仅2.9万人，失业率升至4.2%。道琼斯调查的市场预期为新增就业8.4万人、失业率维持4.1%。
Osaic首席市场策略师菲尔・布兰卡托表示：“从劳动力市场角度看，这正是市场想要的数据。不热也不冷，不算强劲，也没有大幅走弱。”
这份就业数据令交易员重新评估美联储后续政策路径。CME美联储观察工具显示，联邦基金利率期货定价，美联储本月维持利率不变的概率达到77%。
Nuveen首席投资官赛拉・马利克称，财报季即将开启，这份就业数据有望给市场提供支撑，她预计本轮财报季表现将“非常强劲”。
“我认为这或许就是大家一直期待的圣诞老人行情的开端。”她说。
有消息称，受特朗普政府施压，部分欧盟国家考虑释放战略燃油储备，受此影响油价回落，利好股市。
10月开局首个交易日（周四）美股小幅收高。但受全球债券抛售潮拖累，道指与标普500本周一度面临收跌压力，纳指是唯一有望周线收涨的主要股指。

title: 美国债市：美债回吐非农数据后涨幅 曲线中段领跌
content:
美国国债日内下跌。中期美债领跌，此前疲软的非农就业报告一度推动美债上涨，但投资者随后逢高卖出，导致各期限收益率日内最高上升5个基点。尽管如此，市场对美联储10月加息的定价降温，隐含的加息幅度从周四的约8个基点降至约6个基点。
纽约时间下午3点过后不久，美国国债收益率全线上升2个基点至5个基点，中期美债领跌，推动5s30s利差日内收窄3个基点，2s5s30s蝶式利差较周四收盘扩大4.5个基点。10年期美债收益率收于接近盘中高点的5.28%，接近本周5.15%-5.34%区间的上端。
非农数据公布后美债涨势最强时，短端和中段收益率一度下降多达10个基点，空头回补放大了这一走势。随着交易推进，收益率回到持平水平，继而转为上升。
数据公布后的市场波动逐渐平息之际，油价脱离盘中低点，加之法国与德国10年期国债利差收窄，给美国国债带来下跌压力。WTI在尾盘明显脱离盘中低点，但仍下跌约2%，此前G7国家释放信号称将投放紧急储备，以缓解能源成本飙升给消费者带来的压力，欧美柴油价格大跌。
截至纽约时间下午3点，美国国债期货成交量较20日均值高约30%，其中收益率曲线中段合约的交易尤为活跃。

title: Italy and Greece seek leeway on EU fiscal rules
content:
Paola Tamma in Brussels, Amy Kazmin in Rome and Eleni Varvitsioti in Athens

Published October 2 2026

Updated October 2 2026

Italy and Greece have asked Brussels for more fiscal wriggle room as surging fuel prices and rising inflation add to budgetary pressure on the bloc’s two most indebted countries ahead of elections next year.

Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni and Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis each wrote to the European Commission this week to plead for further room to manoeuvre under the EU’s fiscal rules, which are meant to limit a country’s annual deficit to 3 per cent of GDP.

Rising diesel and petrol prices, triggered by the war in Iran, have increased the cost of many national fuel price support measures, adding to mounting pressure on public finances around the world.

The EU’s fiscal rules were already adjusted in June to temporarily allow countries to spend up to 0.6 per cent of GDP until 2028 on energy investments that reduce dependency on imported fossil fuels.

This is part of a broader exemption allowing countries to spend up to 1.5 per cent of GDP on defence and energy, which both Italy and Greece are using, without the spending resulting in punitive measures.

The new requests made this week go further. Athens has asked for permission to exclude “temporary measures” from its net spending indicator, which analysts say are a reference to fuel subsidies.

Rome has requested that inflation be taken into account when assessing whether its budget complies with EU spending ceilings.

EU officials privately caution that markets may react negatively to granting additional flexibility under the fiscal rules.

Meloni sent a letter to Commission president Ursula von der Leyen on Thursday requesting that the matter be discussed at a meeting of EU finance ministers next week.

In her letter, seen by the FT, she argued Italy should be permitted to use the additional tax revenues it collects as a result of inflation to limit the impact of higher prices for households and businesses without this breaching the fiscal rules.

Part of this extra revenue should be used “to dampen the increase in energy costs in a temporary and targeted manner”, she wrote.

The letter also appealed to Brussels to treat inflation as a mitigating factor if Italy’s 2027 budget projections exceeded the annual EU expenditure thresholds.

Unveiling Italy’s new financial planning document on Friday night, finance minister Giancarlo Giorgetti projected this year’s fiscal deficit would fall below 3 per cent of GDP, while growth would hit 1 per cent, up from 0.6 per cent forecast in April.

However, Giorgetti said Italy’s deficit would rise to 3.4 per cent of GDP in 2027, as Italy activates the so-called national escape clause and requests 0.6 per cent of GDP in additional leeway from the EU for additional spending on energy and defence for next year and 2028 — a total of €29bn in extra resources over the two years — provided parliament agrees.

The deficit would drop to 3.2 per cent in 2028 — still utilising the EU’s extra flexibility — then drop to 2.3 per cent in 2029.

Growth will remain below 1 per cent a year from 2027 to 2029, ranging between 0.8 and 0.9 per cent. Italy’s public debt is projected to peak at 138.5 per cent of GDP next year — when it will replace Greece as the EU’s most heavily indebted economy — before gradually declining.

Giorgetti confirmed that Italy had decided not to spend quite as much on defence over the next two years as it had originally been considering, given an economic context he described as “particularly complex”.

Since taking power in 2022, Meloni’s coalition has won accolades from debt investors and credit rating agencies for its fiscal prudence and restraint, cutting Italy’s fiscal deficit from 8 per cent in 2022 to 3.1 per cent in 2025.

However, Rome has spent an estimated €2.8bn this year on fuel excise tax cuts. Last week Italy’s state-controlled energy group Eni said it would put a temporary price cap on pump prices for at least one month to support the government’s efforts.

Mitsotakis has also pleaded with Brussels for greater flexibility, calling for more “breathing room” in a letter to von der Leyen on Wednesday, also seen by the FT.

He proposed allowing member states to use the additional tax revenues generated by higher prices to fund temporary support measures that would shield households and businesses from rising energy costs.

He also criticised the Commission’s recommendations to reduce energy demand as being “not politically acceptable”.

The intervention comes as the cost of living has emerged as a key concern for Mitsotakis’s government, which faces national elections in spring.

The Commission declined to comment.

title: US economy adds just 29,000 jobs in September as hiring slows sharply
content:
Myles McCormick in Washington and Kate Duguid in New York

Published October 2 2026

Updated October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

The US economy added just 29,000 jobs in September as hiring slowed sharply from the previous month, raising doubts over the resilience of the labour market and the outlook for interest rate rises.

Friday’s figure from the Bureau of Labor Statistics marked an abrupt reversal from the downwardly revised 133,000 jobs added in August and was well short of the 88,000 job gains anticipated in a Bloomberg poll of economists.

Hiring decelerated across multiple sectors, with healthcare, a big driver of job gains in previous months, slowing sharply. Employment in the financial sector continued to contract.

Payrolls for July and August were revised lower by a combined 60,000 positions. The July figure fell to a loss of 10,000 jobs. The unemployment rate climbed to 4.2 per cent in September from 4.1 per cent in August.

“Today’s soft payroll report demonstrates that the labour market is simmering, not boiling,” said Jeff Schulze, head investment strategist at Franklin Templeton.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

The data came as the Federal Reserve weighs whether to raise interest rates further to tackle inflation after officials voted last month to increase borrowing costs for the first time in three years.

Treasury yields initially dropped following the report as traders lowered their expectations of additional rate increases.

Adam Schickling, senior economist at Vanguard, said the report “strengthens the case for the Federal Reserve to remain patient”, adding that “the labour market has not deteriorated sharply, but there is also little evidence that it has meaningfully strengthened”.

The two-year Treasury yield, which moves with interest rate expectations, fell as much as 0.09 percentage points to 4.69 per cent immediately following the release of the data. It later recouped that move and sat 0.05 percentage points higher on the day at 4.84 per cent.

Market bets on an October rate rise fell from 29 per cent before the data was released to about 23 per cent. They had fallen sharply this week after senior central bank officials signalled that policymakers would probably need more time to consider the data before taking further action. As the Treasury sell-off resumed on Friday, traders attached a roughly 85 per cent chance to the prospect of interest rates being higher by the end of the year.

“For the Fed, this number should be the nail in the coffin for an October hike,” said Thomas Simons, chief US economist at Jefferies.

US stocks were higher on Friday, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.7 per cent and the Nasdaq 100 climbing 1 per cent to a record closing high.

Fed chair Kevin Warsh had pointed to the labour market being in “good shape” as a factor behind the central bank’s decision to raise borrowing costs by 25 basis points in the face of inflation he said had been “too high . . . for too long”.

Traders said that while Friday’s report should cause the central bank to re-evaluate that position, they still expected the Fed to raise borrowing costs further in the coming months.

“Overall the data pour a little bit of cold water on the narrative that rates should be running dramatically higher,” said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US interest rates at TD Securities.

title: Arctic sea routes boom as Gulf war and global warming divert shipping
content:
Alice Hancock in London

Published October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

Shipping through the Arctic has reached record levels as melting sea ice and pressure on global chokepoints push shipowners to find alternative routes.

Voyages via the Northern Sea Route hit 133 last month, more than quadruple what they were in 2022, according to Lloyd’s List Intelligence, and up 46 per cent compared with August.

Almost half of the transits were made by Russian-flagged ships. Voyages have also been made by Chinese ships seeking another way to European markets given the disruption in the Middle East and in the Red Sea. “It’s worth watching how the use of this route develops as government and operators increasingly look for alternative shipping lanes with less exposure to geopolitical disruption,” said Bridget Diakun, maritime intelligence and research director at Lloyd’s List.

The Chinese container ship Dubai Tower travelled from Qingdao to the UK port of Felixstowe via the Arctic in September, trimming its voyage time to 24 days as opposed to the 40 or more days it would take to sail via the Suez Canal or Cape of Good Hope.

Another ship belonging to the same company set out from Ningbo to Felixstowe using the same route on September 27.

September is typically the busiest month for Arctic sea routes as the ice is at its lowest ebb, allowing ships without icebreaker capabilities to transit.

The northern sea ice suffered its largest single-year winter decline in 2025 since satellite records began and has remained at historic lows since, according to University of Southampton researchers.

The lower sea ice and increased pressure on chokepoints such as the Bab al-Mandeb Strait at the entrance to the Red Sea, which is currently threatened by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, are making the Northern Sea Route more appealing to shipowners. The strait has become a vital route for Saudi Arabian oil exports since Iran throttled shipping through the Strait of Hormuz in response to US strikes on the Islamic republic.

Meanwhile the Panama Canal has suffered drought conditions this year.

Liquefied natural gas carriers often use the route to reach Russia’s Yamal and Arctic LNG 2 gas plants, but there was also an uptick in bulk cargo vessels that typically carry commodities like grains or iron ore.

The number of bulk carriers transiting the route was 29 in September, compared to 18 in August and a previous high of 12 in September last year.

A record number of crude oil tankers were also deployed on the route, Lloyd's List data showed.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

The Northern Sea Route is broken up into 28 sections with different guidelines set by the Rosatom-controlled Northern Sea Route administration depending on the ice conditions. The Russian state-controlled company issues permits to sail through the area.

Insurance companies and environmentalists have warned that increasing use of the waterway could result in a major accident, with few search and rescue or clean-up capabilities in the region.

A major oil spill from the supertanker Exxon Valdez off the Alaskan coast in 1989 took at least four years to clean up, but residue from the accident is still lingering on nearby beaches. Romain Troublé, executive director of the Tara Ocean Foundation, said there was also a risk that even minor oil spills would accelerate global warming effects as black drops on the ice would absorb sunlight and increase melting.

“The people who will use this route are not only Russia and China . . . any companies that can go through this route in the future will have an impact on the Arctic,” he said. “If you and I are buying goods that are using this path, we are contributing to the dangers of it.”

There are also significant dangers for mariners given the unpredictable weather and harsh conditions.

Tom Mellor, head of technical partnering at the UK Hydrographic Office, the main provider of geospatial data to ships, said that navigational equipment could fail to work at far-northerly latitudes.

“Above or below that the world becomes much more curved and the display of that data requires a different methodology to make sure it is positioned correctly on that chart.”

“I wouldn’t want to go on board if you didn't have a proper system that was showing the chart correctly,” he said.

title: US murderer Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after failed execution, lawyers say
content:
Warning: This article contains details that readers may find distressing

Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator on Thursday night after authorities failed to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyers have said in court filings.

Pike, 50, was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance.

Pike remained critically ill and was being treated at a Nashville-area hospital.

Lawyers for Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, are seeking to have her sentence commuted after the failed execution attempt.

Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her botched execution.

Hospital staff are working to save her life and clear the drug used, pentobarbital, from her system, the filing states.

During the execution attempt, prison officials tried to start intravenous (IV) lines by using at least seven needles on Pike, according to her lawyers.

At one point, Pike herself offered guidance of where they could try.

"One needle was bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed," the filing states.

While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent review into Pike's botched execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.

The state's department of correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Authorities are yet to say whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have not not offered any explanations about what went wrong.

Pike's attorneys previously warned that her conditions, including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

In the latest filings, her lawyers allege that "at no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms Pike's body".

They are requesting that all relevant physical, written and electronic evidence is preserved.

Dr Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team, said two doses of pentobarbital was enough that "she would have surely died" had it entered her bloodstream in normal circulation.

The only possible explanation for her survival, Zivot said, "is that the pentobarbital blood level was never high enough to cause death" and that blisters on her arm after the botched execution indicated a ruptured vein.

So, instead of entering Pike's bloodstream, he said, the pentobarbital was more likely to have spread across the tissue under her skin.

Pike's medical condition of thrombocytosis may have also played a role, forming blood clots at the injection site that would potentially block pentobarbital from entering her veins.

Regarding the possibility the pentobarbital was degraded, Zivot explained that if this was the case, it could be due to factors including poor manufacturing or improper storage.

The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.

The US Supreme Court thwarted two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.

Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.

She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

Before the killing, Pike had accused Slemmer of insulting her and trying to steal her then-boyfriend.

Pike's boyfriend and co-defendant Shipp was 17 at the time so was spared the death penalty under state law. He was given a life sentence with the possibility of parole and remains in prison.

title: 美海岸警卫队称拦截一艘向古巴运送燃料的货轮
content:
美国海岸警卫队2日发布消息说，9月初在加勒比海拦截了一艘美方指称正向古巴“非法运输”燃料的货轮。
消息说，海岸警卫队登上这艘货轮进行检查，随后将该船押送至墨西哥尤卡坦半岛北部的普罗格雷索港。墨西哥海军确认“该船的压载舱内装有大量燃料”。此外，船上还载有若干个据信装有美方所指“非法燃料”的集装箱。
消息还说，美国海岸警卫队今年夏初登船并扣押了另一艘被认为正向古巴运送“非法燃料”的货船。
有分析认为，这些举措表明，美政府正在动用军事力量来强制执行对古巴的燃料封锁。这一政策已严重影响古巴的经济并导致当地居民饱受苦难。
美国长期对古巴实施经济、金融封锁和贸易禁运。继今年相继对委内瑞拉、伊朗发起军事行动后，美方又对古巴发出威胁，并进一步加大对古巴施压，实行石油封锁，扩大对古制裁。
古巴外长罗德里格斯9月7日表示，美国对古巴实施的贸易禁运已造成“创纪录”的经济损失，并加剧了古巴贫困家庭实际收入的下降和生活成本的上升。此外，能源供应的限制和对航运公司的威胁也破坏了水电供应及其他公共服务。（总台记者 史跃）
