title: 美联储主席沃什淡化前瞻指引 核心副手讲话仍牵动市场预期
content:
美联储主席凯文·沃什已承诺避免就利率走向向投资者发出明确信号。本周沃什的主要副手表明他们仍愿意有所回应，而投资者也在认真倾听。
美联储副主席菲利普·杰斐逊和纽约联储行长约翰·威廉姆斯本周的讲话清楚表明，他们认为美联储有时间评估经济状况，然后考虑是否再次加息。这些言论促使投资者下调对10月加息的预期。
两人的讲话仅相隔两天，但这并不意味着美联储不会进一步调整政策。官员们仍不断警告通胀过高，而定于10月14日公布的消费者价格数据可能在这场讨论中发挥重要作用。
不过，密切关注美联储的人士表示，两场讲话传递出的信息很清楚：在美联储9月16日加息后，交易员押注再次加息有些操之过急，尤其是在债券收益率大幅跃升、推动借贷成本急剧上升之际。
威廉姆斯周二讲话前，根据联邦基金期货定价，交易员认为美联储在10月27日至28日会议上加息的概率为70%。到杰斐逊周四结束讲话时，这一概率已降至约25%，期间低于预期的通胀数据也起到推动作用。
作为纽约联储行长，威廉姆斯不仅拥有永久的货币政策投票权，而且按惯例还担任联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）副主席。这一职位长期以来与美联储主席和副主席一道，被视为货币政策领导层的“三驾马车”。
在一些前任美联储主席任内，投资者曾认为，副主席或纽约联储行长的讲话是用来传递整个“三驾马车”观点的。不过，目前没有证据显示杰斐逊和威廉姆斯彼此协调了讲话内容，或与沃什进行了协调。
尽管如此，高盛经济学家表示，杰斐逊和威廉姆斯的讲话结合起来，进一步坚定了他们认为10月不太可能加息的判断，其他机构也得出了类似结论。
Evercore ISI经济研究主管Krishna Guha等人在杰斐逊周四讲话后给客户的报告中写道：“我们认为，杰斐逊和威廉姆斯共同传递的信息具有权威性。”
摩根大通首席美国经济学家Michael Feroli表示，这两场讲话显然意在管理市场预期。他说：“两人的信息都是，你不必一次会议接一次会议地不断加息，可以把加息的间隔稍微拉开一些。”
前瞻指引
美联储决策者9月一致投票决定加息25个基点，这是2023年以来首次加息，因为有迹象显示整体经济在加速，而通胀依然顽固高企。在会议后公布的预测中，官员们暗示支持年内再加息一次。
不过，沃什已经不再通过所谓的“前瞻指引”来引导市场的利率预期。他不参与季度利率预测，也避免在公开讲话中暗示未来政策行动，而是鼓励投资者从经济数据中寻找信号。
这种转变获得了不少支持。批评前瞻指引的人认为，这种做法在危机时期有其作用，但在经济数据快速变化、决策者对经济前景能见度有限时，价值不大。
一个例子是：本周低于预期的通胀和就业数据降低了再次加息的紧迫性，但消费者仍在支出，经济增长似乎正在加速。
杜克大学经济学教授的Ellen Meade表示，杰斐逊和威廉姆斯的讲话未必达到前瞻指引的标准。Meade曾在美联储理事会任职数十年，为美联储官员提供建议。
“我认为，锁定一次利率调整的前瞻指引，与告诉市场我们会花时间作决定并收集大量数据的前瞻指引是有区别的。区别很微妙，但确实存在，”她说。
耶鲁大学管理学院教授、前美联储部门主管William English认为，杰斐逊和威廉姆斯的讲话并非经过协调。
他说：“他们只是发表自己认为适当的讲话，阐述各自对经济和政策的看法。”

title: Low-profile hedge fund smashes record for New York office rent
content:
Zehra Munir and Amelia Pollard in New York

Published October 2 2026

A skyscraper in midtown New York has smashed rent records by leasing its top two floors to a low-profile hedge fund for up to $21.2mn a year.

Castle Hook Partners will move into the penthouse of 625 Madison Avenue, an office tower owned by real estate developer Related Companies, in the second half of 2029.

The fund’s willingness to pay between $350 and $400 per square foot in yearly rent for 53,000 square feet of space, according to people familiar with the matter, signals the boom at the high end of Manhattan’s office market is accelerating.

The previous reported record for office rent was set earlier this year when a private international family office signed a 10-year lease averaging $327.50 per square foot in a Midtown tower owned by the Soloviev Group.

While Related had originally planned to build a luxury residential high-rise on the site, purchased from SL Green in early 2024, it decided instead to tap into the “real premium” that exists for “new, properly amenitised, high-end office with incredible views”, Related chief executive Jeff Blau said in an interview.

A war for talent in the financial services and technology sectors, combined with a drive to attract workers back to the office, has resulted in a golden era for the city’s luxury offices .

The 53-storey high-rise overlooking Central Park has been designed by British architect Lord Norman Foster and will feature private dining facilities and wraparound terraces on its penthouse and “amenity floor”, said Blau.

Castle Hook, founded by Soros Fund Management alumnus David Rogers in 2016, is currently headquartered in the General Motors Building on Fifth Avenue. The firm counted legendary hedge fund manager Stanley Druckenmiller among its early investors and has kept a low profile on Wall Street. It manages about $11bn with 35 employees, according to its most recent regulatory filing.

The firm is among so-called global macro hedge funds — which trade macroeconomic trends in currencies, commodities, bonds and stocks — that have benefited from a volatile few years in markets. Macro funds were up 6.8 per cent for the year through the end of August, according to research firm PivotalPath.

Castle Hook has posted high returns in recent years. The firm reportedly gained about 50 per cent last year and made more than 60 per cent the year prior.

A spokesperson for Castle Hook did not respond to a request for comment.

The battle for talent among hedge funds has become fierce, with lavish offices and amenities emerging as ways to compete for top portfolio managers beyond huge cheques. Hedge funds and other financial firms were among the first companies to require employees to return to their desks after the pandemic.

Prominent hedge fund managers such as Bill Ackman and Dan Loeb have been among the loudest voices decrying New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s populist policies and their potential impact on the city’s real estate market. After Mamdani won the Democratic primary, some Wall Street executives privately warned his ascent would drive financial firms out of the city.

“People might have their views on where New York politics are, but I think people believe in the future of New York City,” said Related’s Blau.

Related’s building on Madison Avenue would be 67 per cent leased by the end of the year, mostly to financial services companies, said Stephen Winter, the company’s executive vice-president. Private equity firm General Atlantic will take five floors as the anchor tenant.

JPMorgan Chase’s headquarters, unveiled in 2025, features a state of the art health and wellness centre and 19 dining options, and has set the tone for new office amenities around the city.

The value of Castle Hook’s lease has not been previously reported. The 15-year tenancy agreement was reported earlier by the New York Business Journal.

title: Widdecombe suspect charged with planning terror act against Farage
content:
The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe has also been charged with preparing acts of terror including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Counter terror police said Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged on Friday with one count of preparation of terrorist acts.

The charge relates to activity which is alleged to have taken place between May 2024 and July 2026.

Kerry was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said she knew the fresh charge would be "extremely concerning" and her "profound sympathies" were with Farage and his family.

"Let no one make any mistake: an attack on anyone in politics is an attack on us all.

"This case raises serious questions about the security of those in public life. We must use this as an opportunity to reset. Once parliament returns, I will update on our work to strengthen protections for those who choose to serve."

The BBC contacted Reform UK for comment and a party source said: "This is exactly why Nigel needed £5m to protect his security for life."

Farage is currently facing a parliamentary standards watchdog probe into a £5m gift from a billionaire donor before he returned as an MP in 2024. The Reform leader has previously said the money was for his personal security.

Deputy leader of Reform UK, Richard Tice, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the murder of Ann Widdecombe had made everyone take security more seriously.

"What's particularly upsetting for those of us in and around him [Farage] is sometimes he's not been believed, not been listened to."

Tice added that he personally had security arrangements in place and his habits had changed which was a "consequence of the world we live in" arguing the "online world has clearly hindered this whole process".

Asked if Reform had done enough to dial the temperature down and whether comments from politicians added to public anger, Tice said "the passions that flow through democratic debate should be completely separate to the way that people respond

"It's the nature of democracy... it's part of the joy of it is that there will be robust debate but at the end of it one should be able to shake hands."

Counter Terrorism Policing Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said the charge on Friday was the result of a "hugely intensive and complex investigation".

"This investigation has been led by a dedicated team of detectives, analysts, and forensic experts, working on multiple lines of enquiry, which has resulted in this very serious charge," she added.

Kerry, from Rotherham, is due to appear in court over the terror charge on Wednesday, police said.

Frank Ferguson of the Crown Prosecution Service's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division said prosecutors "worked closely" with police to bring the charge and would continue to work alongside them as the investigation continued.

Widdecombe was found dead on Thursday 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.

She served as Conservative MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

Following her departure from the Commons, Widdecombe appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing and would later become a Reform UK spokeswoman.

title: 欧洲股市反弹 得益于债市压力缓解以及科技股上涨
content:
欧洲股市周五反弹，得益于油价回落使得债券收益率上升带来的压力有所缓解，科技股表现领先。
斯托克欧洲600指数收盘上涨0.8%，但全周仍下跌1.1%。
数据显示美国9月份新增就业人数低于预期且失业率小幅上升，缓解了美联储加息的压力，推动该指数进一步扩大涨幅。
Tikehau Capital资本市场策略主管Raphael Thuin表示：“很明显，这是‘坏消息就是好消息’的情况。这给经济强劲、从而迫使美联储过快加息的说法降了温。”
欧洲科技板块领涨，阿斯麦控股和英飞凌科技均上涨超过3%。随着有消息称欧洲国家正在讨论释放战略储备以缓解燃料价格飙升，布伦特原油跌至每桶约100美元。
个股方面，尽管几个月前才上调业绩展望，但IG Group Holdings Plc第三季度营收意外下滑，股价暴跌23%。开云集团股价下跌3.2%，分析师在与管理层进行收盘前沟通后指出，奢侈品行业环境正在恶化，市场持续疲软。
尽管周五反弹，欧洲股市在连续数日债券收益率上升以及经济前景担忧的影响下仍承受压力。法国的政治和财政挑战尤其受到关注。斯托克欧洲600指数仍低于8月份创下的纪录高位。
Natixis IM全球市场策略主管Mabrouk Chetouane表示，经济增长乏力和利率上升可能会对该地区股市构成压力。他补充说：“此外，目前的政治局势意味着，绝对没有人预计法国会进行任何形式的财政整顿。”

title: 七国集团将释放多达1亿桶柴油和石油储备以遏制价格上涨
content:
在特朗普政府一周来不断施压要求遏制燃料价格上涨之后，七国集团（G7）及其合作伙伴周五决定将释放多达1亿桶紧急石油和柴油储备。
法国总统马克龙周五表示，此次释放将由国际能源署协调，将在未来四个月内进行，初期的重点是柴油。他说，此举旨在“向市场发出明确的信号”。
消息公布后，欧洲和美国柴油期货价格大跌，布伦特原油期货最初也走低不过之后出现反弹。
这项协议将有助于缓解市场对美国总统特朗普此前威胁实施柴油出口禁令的担忧。七国集团成员国重申承诺，将避免在成员国之间对能源和能源产品实施出口限制。美国若实施禁令，可能引发全球供应紧张，并可能给欧洲和拉丁美洲带来严重经济后果。
柴油对交通运输、农业和工业至关重要，而在伊朗和乌克兰的战争已经扰乱了供应并推动柴油价格飙升。随着11月份美国中期选举临近，柴油价格高企成为特朗普面临的一个政治问题。
两名欧洲外交官表示，实际上，新增供应量可能只是所宣布规模的一小部分，因为此前的紧急储备释放计划下仍有相当大规模尚未投放市场。两人因讨论敏感事项而要求匿名。七国集团声明没有说明将释放多少原油和柴油，也没有列出新增承诺和此前已承诺供应的具体构成。
伊朗战争爆发后不久，国际能源署已在3月份协调了一项释放4亿桶储备的计划，但特朗普批评欧洲没有足够快地将这些储备投放市场。本周美国施加的压力进一步加大，促使欧洲官员周四举行紧急会谈，因为欧盟寻求就华盛顿的要求作出协调回应。
国际能源署署长法提赫·比罗尔周二表示，最初的储备释放计划中约三分之一尚未进入市场。截至当天，德国已承诺释放的储备中约77%仍未投放市场，而西班牙仅释放了其承诺规模的大约三分之一。相比之下，美国本周又批准从战略石油储备中释放4000万桶，从而完成其在3月份协议下的承诺。
根据七国集团声明，该计划设想在20天内“大规模”释放柴油储备，如果有必要，国际能源署还将讨论进一步释放柴油。知情人士称，此次最新释放将包括3月份协议下已经承诺、但尚未投放市场的储备。
目前担任七国集团轮值主席的马克龙说：“我们已经共同承诺，按照我提到的比例释放这些战略储备，并重点释放柴油。我们也都承诺确保不会实施出口禁令，特朗普总统尤其明确了这一点。”
特朗普周五在社交媒体发文称，他欢迎这一最新行动。
特朗普说：“欧洲刚刚同意释放庞大数量的大量储备的柴油。相关过程将立即开始。”
一名知情人士表示，欧盟各国大使周五开会讨论支持此次释放，但提出两个条件：一是不能危及战略储备，二是美国必须承诺避免实施能源出口禁令。该人士因相关讨论不公开而要求匿名。
汇编的公允价值数据显示，作为衡量市场强弱的一项备受关注的指标，欧洲市场柴油相对原油的溢价一度跌至每桶69美元，低于周四的76.77美元。
尽管伊朗战争推高了原油价格，但柴油和汽油等成品油价格承受的压力更大，加剧了俄乌战争导致正常运转炼油厂不足造成的影响。
美国加油站的柴油价格已飙升至每加仑6.53美元的高位，给美国农民带来压力。在欧洲，柴油期货价格有时已升至每桶200美元以上，交易员称，这一水平足以对需求构成压力。

title: G7 to release millions of barrels of oil and diesel after Trump threat
content:
The G7 has announced 100 million barrels of oil and diesel will be released to ease supply concerns that have caused prices to skyrocket.

It includes a "substantial release" of diesel within 20 days, with discussions around "additional diesel releases as necessary", G7 leaders said in a statement.

The group of advanced economies, including the US, said the move would begin immediately and would last for four months.

Under the measures, which come after US President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports, there will not be any "export restrictions on energy and energy products" between G7 members.

The G7 includes the US, UK, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France, with the EU also represented at its meetings.

Donald Trump had warned he would ban diesel exports from the US if European countries did not agree to put more of their own stocks onto the market. That would have eased pressure on prices for US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections, but pushed up prices elsewhere.

On Friday, he said on social media: "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately."

His Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had argued US farmers, truckers, and businesses "should not be left carrying the burden" as prices soar.

Speaking later at the White House, Trump said an export ban on diesel was "never really on the table".

Referring to the decision by the G7 to release fuel from reserves, he added that "what Europe did was a great thing."

"Europe has a lot of diesel and they're going to be making a major world contribution - and so are we," he said.

"And we're not going to be doing the export ban, we're going to be doing what we're supposed to do."

Trump had first said he backed a diesel export ban early last week, and was still considering it on Thursday, as his administration put pressure on Europe to tap its supplies.

Diesel is used heavily by the haulage industry and in agriculture, meaning rises in the cost of the fuel feed through into essentials such as food.

Following a meeting of G7 leaders, French President Emmanuel Macron said the bloc had agreed to release reserves of "up to 100 million barrels" within four months under the co-ordination of the International Energy Agency (IEA).

The UK was represented at the meeting by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who said the measures would "stabilise energy supplies, build resilience in supply chains and shield households and businesses from price shocks".

Macron said the co-ordinated action would "bring down the prices of petroleum products, particularly diesel". Highlighting the agreement not to pursue export bans, Macron said "President Trump, in particular, was very clear on this point".

In the joint statement, G7 leaders said: "We will implement our commitments with a co-ordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over four months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G7 members and partners."

It is not yet clear which partner countries will release stocks, nor how quickly.

The 100 million barrels will comprise a mix of diesel and crude oil. The price of global benchmark Brent crude oil briefly dropped below $100 a barrel, but rose back to around $102 by Friday evening. Before the US and Israel invaded Iran, it was trading at around $73.

Matt Smith, director of commodities research at Kpler, said oil had risen again due to renewed strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.

"Oil prices were selling off strongly due to the announcement of strategic stock releases in Europe, but they reversed course on rumours of Saudi Arabia planning an offensive into Yemen as it looks to re-establish a safe path via Bab-Al Mandeb," he said.

European countries had pushed back against US threats to turn off American diesel, against a backdrop of the US-led war in the Middle East and reduced supplies from Russia and China.

The G7 leaders said they will also co-ordinate maintenance schedules to avoid multiple refineries being shut down at the same time, while encouraging countries with the capacity to do so to ramp up refining of diesel in particular.

Avoiding a ban on US diesel exports will offer significant relief to countries which are reliant on imports of the fuel, including the UK, where prices at the pump topped £2 a litre for the first time on Friday.

Over half of the UK's diesel is imported, with 31% of those imports coming from the US.

The US is one of the world's leading diesel suppliers, with domestic refineries churning out roughly four to five million barrels every day, according to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA).

Americans consume about 3.6 million barrels of that. Refiners export the remaining 1.2 to 1.5 million barrels per day, making the US a vital supplier to the global market.

Supplies of diesel internationally have been heavily constrained by the conflict in the Middle East, which has restricted the flow of both crude oil and refined diesel onto global markets.

Russia, which is also a major producer, has implemented its own export ban on diesel, following attacks on its refineries by Ukraine, further limiting supply. The G7 leaders stressed that they will maintain sanctions against Russia amid its ongoing war in Ukraine.

Diesel is harder to refine than petrol and, because of its use in the haulage industry and agriculture, it is very difficult to reduce demand.

title: 隐私币ETF近一月大涨60%，跻身2026年表现最佳基金行列
content:
灰度 Zcash ETF（代码 ZCSH）过去一个月涨幅超 60%，年内涨幅约 253%。市场重新重视隐私叙事，投机资本从 AI 板块轮动流入该产品，推动其大涨。
Zcash 原生代币 ZEC 今年涨幅超 170%；相比之下，比特币今年价格基本停滞。Zcash 在设计上可以实现用户金融交易完全隐私化。该币种 2016 年问世，但后来隐私叙事热度消退 —— 隐私币给监管机构与交易所带来合规难题。
加密货币主流投资越来越机构化、越来越透明；与此同时，人工智能让大规模金融监控、交易分析能力大幅增强。两种因素叠加，令隐私主题再度受到市场追捧，也促成灰度 Zcash ETF 在 8 月正式上市交易。
对比来看，热门比特币现货 ETF IBIT 今年下跌约 1%；跟踪十大加密货币的 BITW 下跌 5%。而标普 500 ETF（VOO）上涨 12%，纳指 100 ETF（QQQ）涨幅接近 22%。

title: 百奥明公布庞贝病五年临床数据：运动功能具备持久获益
content:
核心要点
周五，百奥明公布 Ⅲ 期临床试验的五年随访数据，试验药物为 Pombiliti 联合 Opfolda，用于治疗晚发型庞贝病（LOPD）。
数据显示，该组合疗法能够帮助成人患者在连续五年用药过程中维持步行距离，长期来看呼吸功能也保持相对稳定；本次分析未识别出新的安全警示信号。
百奥明于 2025 年 12 月收购了销售这套组合疗法的阿米库斯治疗公司（Amicus Therapeutics），借此扩大自身在罕见代谢病领域的布局。
本次分析共纳入 82 名受试者，其中包含既往未接受酶替代治疗的初治患者，以及入组前已经使用酶替代疗法的经治患者。
晚发型庞贝病是一种罕见的遗传性溶酶体贮积病，病情可较为严重，全身肌肉会出现进行性、随时间不断加重的肌无力，不少患者的呼吸控制肌肉也会受到损伤。
该研究结果已于日本举办的第 31 届世界肌肉学会年会上对外公布。

title: 欧洲债市：法国国债相对于德国国债的收益率溢价收窄
content:
尽管欧洲债券周五上涨，但在对法国财政状况以及明年总统大选结果的担忧持续之际，基准法国10年期国债收益率连续第五周走高，也是过去八周中第七周上升。
随着法国国内买家重返市场，法国10年期国债相对德国同期限国债的收益率溢价收于141个基点。
收益率溢价从周五盘中159个基点的高点回落，为一周来首次收窄。
不过，本周债券利差累计扩大32个基点，创纪录最大单周升幅。
欧洲债券市场剧烈波动，投资者涌向优质资产避险，引发市场对风险蔓延以及欧洲央行是否可能采取行动的担忧。
周五局势略有缓和，意大利和西班牙国债相对德国国债的利差也有所收窄。
弱于预期的美国就业数据公布后，交易员下调了对英国央行和欧洲央行的加息预期。
市场更倾向于预计欧洲央行加息两次而非三次，英国央行加息三次而非四次。
随着市场对风险蔓延的担忧减弱，加息押注随后有所回升，尽管能源价格下跌。

德国10年期国债收益率下跌5个基点，至3.46%；
德国国债期货上涨70.00个点，至121.04；
意大利10年期国债收益率下降9个基点，至4.61%；

title: Stockpickers: AG Barr, Redcentric, Saga
content:
Dan Jones , Investors’ Chronicle

Published October 2 2026

Rising costs and hard-pressed customers mean many consumer staples companies find themselves less essential than they had assumed.

In the US, staples now make up a record-low 4.6 per cent of the S&P 500, according to investment manager Bespoke Invest.

The sector’s ability to keep producing the steady, reliable growth on which its reputation was built is being called into question. Worries about the impact of weight-loss drugs on appetites have not helped.

UK businesses have rolled out turnaround strategies, with varying degrees of success. While investors had warmed to Unilever’s plan to focus on its core divisions, the proposed merger of its food business with sauces maker McCormick left some asking whether it had gone too far.

Diageo has pinned its revival hopes on a plan to cut costs and put more marketing resources behind bright spots, such as Guinness, while making a bigger push into canned cocktails. Its smaller peer AG Barr is already feeling the impact of pre-mixed drink competition, given that its cocktail brand Funkin saw sales struggle again in the first half of 2026.

But things look more positive for the group elsewhere. The Irn-Bru maker has diversified via a series of recent soft drink acquisitions and is making market share gains.

Another attraction is its valuation: a price/earnings ratio of just 11.6 times January 2027’s estimated earnings is near bargain-basement territory, according to FactSet.

The depressed valuation means the company is nowadays more akin to a smaller company than a mid-cap stock and there are recovery stories to be told in this part of the market.

Personal care business PZ Cussons and cleaning products manufacturer McBride have both seen their shares rebound, notably as their businesses stabilise. In AG Barr, investors who focus on larger companies may be missing out on another potential winner.

AG Barr has spent the past 18 months focused on diversifying its portfolio beyond the famous Irn-Bru for which it is known, writes Erin Withey . This has translated into a string of recent acquisitions, which the group is now bedding in.

Today, the Cumbernauld-headquartered company’s product lines span Rubicon juices, MOMA oat-based beverages, Boost energy drinks and, more recently, Fentimans and Frobishers premium mixers.

These purchases helped drive sales for the half-year to August 1 up by 8.5 per cent to £247mn. Adjusted pre-tax profit rose by 2.6 per cent to £36.1mn. The group ended the period with net bank debt of £47mn.

The shares trade near a 12-month low, and after a successful period of expansion into premium soft drinks, we think this could present a buying opportunity. AG Barr must now squeeze the most out of what it has bought.

In July, Redcentric’s share price dropped after it returned £90mn to its shareholders by acquiring 35 per cent of its issued capital at 160p per share, writes Arthur Sants .

The cash came from the sale of its data centre business. Most of this went back to shareholders, with the rest being used to pay down its debt.

This has left a more streamlined business. Redcentric used to own data centres as well as provide the managed service, but now it mainly just does the latter.

Management believes the company is at a turning point. It forecasts revenue growth to be flat in full-year 2027, but adjusted cash profit (ebitda) is expected to rise slightly.

Given that this is a business cutting its way to profit growth, its valuation does not reflect this. It trades on a forward price/earnings ratio of 13 times, according to FactSet analyst consensus.

Saga raised annual guidance and said it expects to deliver medium-term targets ahead of schedule, after the travel and insurance group delivered double-digit revenue growth in the first half of the year, writes Christopher Akers .

As profits and the state of the indebted balance sheet improve, the group’s goals for an annual underlying pre-tax profit of £100mn and leverage under two times are in sight before 2030.

Key earnings generator Ocean Cruise’s underlying profit climbed 38 per cent to £47.7mn.

River Cruise profit rose by 54 per cent to £6mn, helped by the launch of new ship Spirit of the Moselle, while holidays profit more than doubled to £6.6mn.

On the insurance side of the business, broking profit was up by 75 per cent to £15.9mn.

The shares trade on 13 times forward consensus earnings and have risen more than 165 per cent over the past year.

title: Treasuries are losing their moneyness
content:
Brendan Greeley

Published October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

The writer is the author of The Almighty Dollar: 500 Years of the World’s Most Powerful Money

In 1981 the economists Tom Sargent and Neil Wallace wrote a brief article for the Minneapolis Fed’s Quarterly Review, “Some Unpleasant Monetarist Arithmetic”. Unpleasant, that is, for monetarists. The ideas in the article have become the basis for considering one of the most important trade-offs in political economy: monetary dominance against fiscal dominance.

Under monetary dominance, the government is constrained as it spends money. It can’t sell more debt than the public demands. When the public stops demanding, interest on government bonds rises, and the government stops borrowing. This leaves the central bank a free hand to manage inflation by buying and selling government debt.

Under fiscal dominance, the government simply borrows what it wants, spends what it wants, and leaves the central bank with an unpleasant choice. It can buy bonds, bringing the government’s cost of interest down but risking inflation, as the Federal Reserve did during the second world war. Or the central bank can let the politicians fight it out with the market, risking collapse in the value of the bank’s own portfolio and . . . inflation.

It’s a useful model. But as Sargent and Wallace already hinted in their 1981 article, there’s a wormhole the government can slip through. If the demand for sovereign debt can’t be sated, then the government isn’t constrained. It can borrow and spend and borrow and spend. Its cost of debt remains low, and the central bank holds on to its own discretion to manage inflation.

Since about the time that article came out, the US has been slipping through exactly that wormhole. Washington was both fiscally dominant and not constrained by the cost of debt, a condition so solid and stable it seemed like the result of a physical law, and indeed as it continued it encouraged a new discussion. Were Treasuries debt or money? Did the Treasury sell its bonds, like a security? Or did it simply issue them, like currency?

Certainly Treasuries had what economists call moneyness. They were liquid like money. They were risk-free like money, a stylised fact that became an empirical truth. They were even referred to as money. Traders called them “cash,” historically a maddeningly flexible word that can accommodate anything in any century people think of as money. Commercial banks and the Fed haggled over whether Treasuries had the same secure status as America’s base money, the Fed’s own reserves.

It was difficult to find the limits of global demand for dollar-denominated assets with moneyness, which gave economists and politicians the luxury of treating Treasuries like they were both securities and money, a special phenomenon with its own properties.

The distinctions used to be clearer. In the 18th century, assemblies in the American colonies borrowed directly from their own colonists, paying their debts by issuing small-denomination, liquid bills — currency. Under the Constitution, however, this practice was forbidden. Alexander Hamilton followed by building a liquid market for federal debt, just like the one in the United Kingdom. The early American republic would sell its debt to investors for banknotes and silver, and not issue it to citizens as currency. The Hamiltonian system was built on the assumption that Washington’s debt is a bond, not money.

The idea of government debt as cash money lingered. During the Civil War, Confederate States began issuing their own currencies again, and the Union government began paying for things with greenbacks, paper slips tied to a vague promise that they would be bought back eventually with gold. Periodically during financial crises until the Great Depression, cities would pay for things with their own “hard-times money”, currencies that worked a lot like the old colonial bills.

Each time, however, the old Hamiltonian system reasserted itself: bonds were securities, sold to investors for the ready cash of banknotes and bank deposits. That appears to be happening again. As I write, yield on the US 10-year note is 5.25 per cent. It is not normal to have to add an as-I-write to the 10-year. Not normal, unless Treasuries are no longer special.

There are many explanations for the rise in yields on Treasuries. Yields are going up for government debt around the world. The US has no apparent plans to reduce deficits. A war has raised the price of gas, feeding into inflation. Debt for data centres is competing for cash. All of these are real, but they don’t completely explain the slope of the rise in Treasury yields right now.

One of the things that made Treasuries so money-like is that yields changed slowly, stabilising their value. It’s possible that after several decades, all of these problems together have suddenly eroded the money-like liquidity of US debt; the moneyness is getting squeezed out of Treasuries again.

Sargent and Wallace were always right. Under fiscal dominance, inflation is coming one way or the other, and the central bank has no good choices. America’s Treasuries are just bonds. The wormhole is closing.

title: Motörhead guitarist Phil Campbell died from multi-organ failure, inquest hears
content:
Motörhead guitarist Phil Campbell died from multi-organ failure after suffering complications following "necessary" surgeries, an inquest has heard.

The Welsh rock star, who was the band's guitarist from 1984 until it disbanded in 2015, died aged 64 on 13 March.

Campbell's death could not have been prevented, St Pancras Coroner's Court heard on Friday.

The guitarist from Pontypridd, Rhondda Cynon Taf, underwent two liver transplants and bowel surgery at the Royal Free Hospital in London earlier this year.

The inquest heard he had previously drunk alcohol to excess but had been sober for seven years by the time of his death.

Campbell had suffered from Hepatitis C, external, but the inquest heard this had been treated.

While the second of the two liver transplants was successful, Campbell suffered further complications.

He underwent bowel surgery and was moved to intensive care, where he deteriorated rapidly.

He died in hospital on 13 March, with coroner Dr Richard Brittain recording his cause of death as multi-organ failure.

Brittain said: "My view is that there is nothing here to suggest his death could have been prevented."

He said Campbell died from "recognised complications of necessary surgical procedures".

Campbell's family previously described him as a "devoted husband, a wonderful father, and a proud and loving grandfather, known affectionately as Bampi" who had faced a "long and courageous battle in intensive care following a complex major operation".

"He was deeply loved by all who knew him and will be missed immensely," they added.

Motörhead was founded in 1975 by the bass player and singer Lemmy, whose real name was Ian Kilmister.

The group helped pioneer heavy metal music in Britain with a string of top 10 albums including 1980 hit Ace Of Spades, 1981's No Sleep Til Hammersmith, and Iron Fist in 1982.

Campbell was the second longest serving Motörhead band member, after Lemmy, and went on to record music and tour with his sons, Todd, Dane and Tyla.

title: 法国财政困局冲击债市 欧洲央行的噩梦场景日益逼近
content:
随着法国国债收益率飙升，给欧洲央行带来了越来越大的被迫采取行动的压力，该行面临着被卷入法国债券市场困境的风险。
投资者持有法国国债相对于同期限德国国债所要求的溢价已升至欧洲债务危机以来的最高水平，市场越来越多地猜测，动荡需要恶化到何种程度，欧洲央行才会动用其迄今尚未使用的救市工具。
这正是欧洲央行希望避免的局面。2022年意大利国债遭遇剧烈抛售时，欧洲央行决定设立“传导保护工具”，这一工具存在的本身就是为了防止金融市场动荡。
更令官员尴尬的是，他们设计这一工具是为了应对不合理且无序、并扭曲货币政策传导的市场波动。但考虑到法国未能实现赤字目标以及预算僵局使其成为市场关注焦点，目前的情况可能很难符合这些条件。
丹斯克银行首席策略师Piet Christiansen表示：“鉴于财政立场和政治不确定性，利差扩大是有理由的。但这也正是导致市场对欧洲央行的判断变得复杂的原因。如果这妨碍货币政策传导，那就是欧洲央行要处理的问题。如果没有，那就让市场在不受干预的情况下为这些驱动因素定价。”
欧洲央行及其他央行面临的一个关键问题是，它们希望避免给人一种正在帮助政府为财政赤字融资的印象。
由于官员们已经公开表示，传导保护工具只用于应对不合理的市场波动，因此，如果动用这一工具来缓解市场对法国债务的担忧，可能会损害欧洲央行的信誉。
另一个问题是，受中东冲突影响，欧元区通胀率正接近4%。乌克兰战争爆发后价格飙升时，官员们停止了所有债券购买，如果现在改变方向、从而放松融资环境，将与他们在6月和9月实施的加息相矛盾。
一些人仍然认为，结束所谓的量化紧缩可能是稳定市场的第一步。在量化紧缩期间，欧洲央行允许其持有的债券到期而不再进行再投资。
Allianz Trade经济主管Ana Boata接受采访时表示：“显然，在这方面是可以有所作为的。例如，对法国来说，每月是50亿欧元，实际上相当于新发行规模的20%。所以这并非微不足道。”
另一些人则相信，欧洲央行最终将别无选择，只能动用其政策火力，尤其是传导保护工具的启用条件确实给予了欧洲央行一定裁量空间。
Fidelity International固定收益首席投资官Marion Le Morhedec表示：“欧洲央行一直在密切关注此事。他们一直在与市场参与者沟通，包括对冲基金。他们确实希望了解正在发生什么，并且已经准备好采取一切必要措施，避免出现任何重大失控局面。”
到目前为止，欧洲央行决策者尚未释放任何愿意采取行动的信号。本周被问及是否可能使用传导保护工具时，德国央行行长Joachim Nagel表示，欧洲央行唯一关注的是使通胀率达到2%。
他说：“我在管理委员会的职责是履行我的使命。你提到了一个工具，但我们还有其他几个工具。不过，这与某些利差水平或者类似事情无关。关键是价格稳定。”
与此同时，欧洲央行行长克里斯蒂娜·拉加德上个月在都柏林发表讲话时，对于法国面临的压力似乎仍较为淡定。当时债券利差还没有目前这么大，不过她同时强调了更广泛的背景。
她说：“我们没有看到任何无序波动，也没有看到任何紧张局面。这是一种全球性走势，影响所有债券，尤其是收益率曲线长端，背后有多种原因，但并不存在无序运行的情况。”
如果有迹象显示，法国的情况正外溢至债务水平同样较高的邻国，那么这一立场可能会越来越难以维持。意大利国债相对德国国债的利差也有所扩大，不过仍远低于过去的水平。

title: 疲软非农报告弱化美联储短期内加息的可能 美债收益率显著走低
content:
债券交易员下调了对美联储本月加息的预期，此前美国劳动力市场显现疲软迹象。
美国9月新增就业人数低于预期，失业率小幅上升，推动美国国债周五上涨。对美联储政策路径最为敏感的两年期美债收益率一度下跌10个基点至4.69%。
利率互换显示，交易员目前预计美联储在10月会议上上调基准利率的概率约为20%，低于数据公布前的近30%。市场也已不再完全计入年底前还会加息一次的情景。
Marlborough Investment Management基金经理James Athey表示：“这基本排除了美联储10月加息的可能性。从目前来看，很难再提出有力的周期性理由。所谓‘美国经济强劲’的说法根本站不住脚。”
他表示，自己一直看多债券，并称这份就业报告“的确进一步增强了我们对这一判断的信心”。
作为抵押贷款等其他贷款定价基准的美国10年期国债收益率，本周一度升至2002年以来最高水平。
美国劳工统计局周五公布的数据显示，9月非农就业人数增加2.9万人，且此前两个月数据被向下修正，增幅低于彭博调查中所有经济学家的预期。10年期美债收益率周五一度下跌8个基点至5.15%。
American Century Investments全球固定收益首席投资官Charles Tan表示：“从边际上看，这给了美联储更多理由维持利率不变，而不是加息。反过来说，只要再有一两个通胀数据偏强，市场就可能重新转向更鹰派的预期。”

title: 欧洲债市动荡加剧 欧盟据悉担忧成员国寻求更多财政空间
content:
一位欧盟官员表示，随着债券市场下跌，欧盟政策制定者越来越担心各国政府要求放宽预算约束。
因讨论敏感消息而要求匿名的这位官员表示，各国没有意识到形势的严重性，仍不断要求布鲁塞尔放宽欧盟财政限制，但市场寻求的是可预测性。
该官员补充称，如果欧盟国家遵守支出目标，目前为遏制伊朗战争引发的通胀而进行的加息仍将处于可控范围。另一名欧盟官员表示，未来几个月欧元区各国政府可能面临金融市场的巨大压力。
在各国政府应对欧洲能源价格高企之际，要求获得更多预算空间的呼声不断出现。受中东冲突影响，布伦特原油目前徘徊在每桶100美元附近。意大利和希腊近期均要求欧盟委员会给予更多灵活性。欧盟委员会负责监督各国的赤字和债务水平。
欧盟委员会发言人没有立即回应置评请求。

title: 美国航空推出现金 + 里程混合购票功能
content:
核心要点
美国航空（AAL）将加入一众同行行列，向旅客开放现金叠加里程的混合购票模式。这是该航司为做大利润丰厚的客户忠诚度计划推出的最新改动。
美国航空表示，旅客在结算页面会看到滑动调节条，可以把 AAdvantage 会员里程和现金搭配起来支付机票。
如果用户手里的里程不足以兑换整张机票，但希望用里程抵扣一部分票价，这项功能就十分实用。
美国航空的主要竞争对手联合航空（UAL）、达美航空（DAL）等其他航司早已支持飞行里程搭配现金购票。举例：11 月第一周，从新泽西纽瓦克自由国际机场飞往巴黎的联合航空单程机票，有三种选择：消耗 40000 英里 MileagePlus 里程（另加 5.6 美元税费）；全额现金 428.50 美元；或者支付 369 美元现金外加 6000 里程。
美国航空将于未来几天上线的滑动调节工具，旅客可以选择多消耗里程，换取更大幅度票价减免。
各大航司正为争夺高消费旅客展开激烈竞争，战场已经延伸到全新机场贵宾休息室、升级高端客舱，以及会员等级匹配活动，美国航空此次更新工具正是这一大背景下的举措。

title: 脸书吹哨人弗朗西斯・豪根质疑AI企业能否实现行业自我监管
content:
核心要点
脸书（Facebook）吹哨人弗朗西斯・豪根表示，AI 企业必须 “拿出担当、切实遵守” 本周与特朗普总统签署的白宫 AI 协议。
豪根称，灵活的制度体系会让企业表面遵守白纸黑字的条文，却绕开规则背后的立法本意。
豪根泄露的内部文件催生了 2021 年《华尔街曰报》“脸书文件” 系列报道，该事件也成为 10 月 9 日上映电影《社交清算》的故事蓝本。
周五，脸书前吹哨人弗朗西斯・豪根在接受《财经早间》节目采访时表示，就在 Meta 首席执行官马克・扎克伯格及其他科技企业 CEO 签署白宫 AI 自我监管协议数日后，AI 公司必须拿出担当，恪守这份协议的 精神内核 ，而不只是停留在纸面。
“回顾科技公司应对监管的过往就会发现：面对弹性极大的制度规则，企业往往严格遵守书面条文，但想方设法规避规则背后的初衷。” 豪根说道。
她提出质疑：这些企业是会恪守规则的精神内核，还是会钻那些没有明文禁止的漏洞，“绕开监管围栏”？
豪根曾任脸书公民虚假信息治理团队产品经理，2021 年她泄露大量内部文件，催生著名的 “脸书文件” 系列报道。部分文件显示，公司清楚自家平台会对青少年心理健康造成负面影响。
由艾伦・索金编剧执导的新片 《社交清算》 ，10 月 9 日正式上映，影片故事就取材于这一事件。豪根本人也撰写书籍《一人之力：我鼓起勇气说出真相，以及我为何揭发脸书内幕》，讲述自己曝光内部文件的经历。
近几周，围绕人工智能对人类社会潜在风险的讨论已经白热化。豪根表示，相较于过去，如今 AI 企业对待安全风险的态度 “更加主动”。她同时提到，Anthropic 公司及其首席执行官达里奥・阿莫代伊积极呼吁引入独立第三方审计，这是一个积极信号。
豪根称：“这至少说明，达里奥心里很清楚，一旦有投机取巧的空间，即便是本性向善的人，也会开始走捷径。”

title: Our healthy obsession with fitness trackers
content:
The editorial board

Published October 2 2026

In 2014, Marc Benioff told the World Economic Forum in Davos that his friend, the computer magnate Michael Dell, had called him, worried that data shared from the Salesforce chief executive’s Fitbit monitor showed he had not been working out.

Benioff explained he had skipped the gym because he was suffering from a cold. But his enthusiasm for wellbeing wearables was infectious. Many more people have equipped themselves with Fitbits, Apple Watches, Whoop bands and other trackers since then.

Benioff and Dell have gone on to invest in Oura Health, maker of a fitness ring that promises in its initial public offering prospectus to “empower people to live healthier, longer”.

Oura this week delayed its flotation , which could have valued the Finnish-American company at about $16bn . The official reason was market uncertainty. But such is Oura users’ devotion to the $400 trackers that it is always possible executives and advisers synced their data that morning and decided to wait until their collective heart rates, sleep numbers and step counts heralded a more propitious outcome.

The company, and others like it, will be back. Some early leaders in the market, such as Jawbone, have dropped out or been absorbed by rivals, as Fitbit was by Google. But the runners still in the race are part of an overall market for consumer wearables forecast to generate $1tn in revenue between 2026 and 2032.

This is good news, and not just for investors. Healthy life expectancy is the metric that really matters for most people, and if we are to live longer, healthier lives then anything that nudges us to pay greater attention to our wellbeing is worth backing. Our health is our wealth, as the saying goes.

Silicon Valley’s billionaires are not the only ones banking on this connected future. In the US, Oura subscriptions and devices are already part of an insurance package for patients who share their sleep data with doctors, helping them detect, monitor and treat conditions such as obstructive sleep apnoea.

In the UK, insurer Vitality offers points to active customers who share fitness data which can help them qualify for lower premiums. Diabetes sufferers increasingly benefit from wearable glucose monitors, linked to apps. A 2022 analysis in The Lancet Digital Health of multiple studies of fitness trackers found that wearing one increased activity, to the tune of 1,800 extra steps per day.

The list of potential unwanted side-effects is long. As Benioff pointed out in 2014, the shared vital signs of listed company executives could become tradeable insider information. If insurers were to link protection too strictly to fitness goals, the unfit might be unable to buy cover at all.

The maxim “what gets measured gets managed” also has a flipside. Some important and hard-to-measure areas — mental rather than physical health, for instance — may be neglected, in an example of the McNamara fallacy, named after the bodycount-obsessed Vietnam-era US defence secretary Robert McNamara.

Fitness trackers can focus effort on restrictive targets , such as the quest to clock 10,000 steps daily, while some users’ cult-like dedication to hitting their goals (and bragging about it) could take a toll on their overall health, not to mention the patience of their friends.

Still, the gap is narrowing between fitness bands as faddish fashion accessories and as the serious healthcare tools some developers and doctors hope they can become. There is much further to go, but, to adapt the Chinese proverb, a journey of 1,000 miles begins with 10,000 steps.

title: EU pushes Ukraine for further reforms to unlock funding
content:
Paola Tamma in Brussels and Christopher Miller in Kyiv

Published October 2 2026

Brussels has rebuffed Ukraine’s request for additional financial support this year, demanding that Kyiv implement promised reforms before receiving further EU funding.

The decision comes as Ukraine grapples with intensified Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure, while its parliament struggles to pass the reforms required to unlock support from the EU and other donors.

This summer, Kyiv identified an additional $27bn in military needs and asked the European Commission to help cover the gap by bringing forward tranches from a €90bn EU loan agreed late last year .

That loan was intended to cover most of Ukraine’s financing needs in 2026 and 2027, allocating up to €45bn each year if certain reform milestones were met. However, only €15.7bn of this has been disbursed this year, partly due to delays in complying with reform requirements.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said further funding is urgently needed, in part to boost production of drones and interceptors as Moscow intensifies its aerial attacks on Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure ahead of the winter.

But Brussels rejected the request to frontload 2027 funding, instead pressing Kyiv to meet conditions that could unlock about €34bn in EU support this year.

In a joint statement on Thursday, Ukraine and the European Commission said they had “identified the means to cover Ukraine’s budget and defence needs for 2026. We have also reconfirmed the steps needed to ensure their timely release.”

The reforms Ukraine must deliver to receive the funds include the abolition of a VAT exemption for small parcels and the introduction of new taxation rules for digital platforms.

Both measures have passed in parliament, but include a controversial amendment that weakens the rules governing politically exposed persons (PEPs), which had been requested by the EU to strengthen anti-corruption efforts. That amendment, if signed into law, could threaten Ukraine’s compliance with the conditions attached to EU funding.

European commissioners Valdis Dombrovskis and Marta Kos wrote a letter to the Speaker of Ukraine’s parliament, underscoring that additional financial assistance in 2026 was still available to Ukraine if it fulfilled the requested reforms.

“Avoiding any weakening of Ukraine’s framework on PEPs” was “essential”, they wrote in the letter, which was seen by the FT.

In an interview with the FT on Thursday, Zelenskyy pushed back against media reports of tense discussions with Commission president Ursula von der Leyen over reform conditions.

“We had a very good meeting with Ursula and with her team, and she understands that they have to help Ukraine,” he said.

Europe should help close Kyiv’s financing gap “because we are defending them”, he added. “They have to do it for them also, not only for us.”

He said he had told von der Leyen that wartime pressures meant reforms could not always proceed according to a normal timetable.

“We have to defend [ourselves] now, and some decisions, financial decisions, you can’t wait ,” he said. “Because it’s a question of our stability.”

The Commission is also assessing Ukraine’s yet-uncovered financing needs for 2027, which officials said could total about €70bn in military and budgetary support. The assessment is expected to be presented to EU leaders meeting in mid-October.

Ukraine is in discussions with the IMF about further disbursements from its $8bn programme, a review of which is due later this year. Those disbursements are contingent on funding agreements from the EU and Kyiv’s other allies that will help cover Ukraine’s financial needs in 2027.

title: Riot police clash with students as education protests rage in France
content:
Riot police have clashed with protesters as thousands of students demonstrating over education standards disrupted more than 700 schools in France.

Fires have burned in the streets as high school pupils and others objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 1,747 people were arrested on Friday.

The protests began last week in the capital Paris and have spread across the country, with cities including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille affected.

French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said things had "gone from high-school student demonstrations to a public order disturbance".

Darmanin said that 735 of France's 3,700 schools were now affected "one way or another" by the violent protests.

Announcing the arrests late on Friday, Nuñez told France's TF1 television network: "We are sliding into riot and urban violence, and we are using all intermediate means to put an end to it."

Meanwhile, Education Minister Édouard Geffray said the movement had been hijacked by non-students.

He told French broadcaster BFMTV that teachers had said "the people in front of me were not my students".

Earlier on Friday, a 17-year-old was arrested on suspicion of attempted homicide after protests in Belfort, north-eastern France, where a police officer was targeted.

BBC Verify has now authenticated two videos that show the man, who was later identified as an officer by a minister, being beaten up.

In the graphic footage, a group of young men are seen chasing him. The officer falls to the ground, and is subsequently punched and kicked multiple times in the head.

At least 65 staff members have been injured in the unrest, the education ministry said.

In the Paris suburb of Pantin police charged at protesters and made arrests after projectiles where thrown at officers.

Meanwhile, in Strasbourg tear gas was deployed as police feared conditions would become more hostile, according to the Reuters news agency.

Rubbish bins have also been set on fire in Rennes and Paris.

"As far as we're concerned, we've won - our school is closed this morning," Lola, a 16-year-old protester, told the AFP news agency on Friday.

She said police actions had made things worse.

"It makes us even angrier - the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us," she added.

Police published pictures of some of the items they had seized from demonstrators, including petrol bombs, an axe and so-called mortar fireworks.

"Significant damage" had been done to school facilities, the education ministry said, after attacks on school gates, entrances and fences.

Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes suffered more than €2m (£1.7m) damage, according to the regional government, after fire destroyed its glass entrance and some areas inside the school.

The blockades and protests started last week before spreading to hundreds of schools across the country.

Students say school hours are too long, classrooms too hot and too many members of staff are off work.

It comes at a crucial time for French President Emmanuel Macron, six months before next year's presidential election.

Budget cuts planned, which will impact on education funding, have infuriated the young protesters.

Parents have also been worried that their children have become caught up in a wave of violence and unrest.

At the Claude Monet school in southern Paris, 53-year-old Anya was looking for her son.

"We banned him from coming. I hope he isn't here, but he did leave the house," she told AFP. "We're afraid the situation might escalate."

Darmanin said prosecutors had been asked to hold parents liable for damage caused by their children and "pay for repairs".

Many French unions have given their support to the protesting students.

Education union SNEP-FSU, public services union SNUEP-FSU and Solidaires have all called for members to support them.

Solidaires Trade Union Federation said in a statement: "Let's not let them fire on our children.

"Secondary school pupils have the freedom of assembly, association and demonstration."

title: Investors seek refuge from bond rout in haven German debt
content:
Emily Herbert and Ian Smith in London

Published October 2 2026

Updated October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

German government debt has emerged as the pre-eminent haven in the global bond rout, as concerns about an overheating US economy and fiscal worries elsewhere in Europe leave investors with few other places to turn.

The yield on 10-year Bunds has fallen 0.17 percentage points this week, even as borrowing costs have continued to rise elsewhere. French and Italian 10-year bond yields have risen 0.14 and 0.07 percentage points respectively this week, while US yields gained 0.07 percentage points over the week, even after a recovery following weak jobs data. Yields fall if the price of the bond rises.

“Demand for safety — Bunds — is on the up,” said Reinout De Bock, head of European rates strategy at UBS, amid a bond sell-off caused by an “[economic] cycle like no other with resilient growth, energy price risks and a broadening demand for capital”.

“Core Europe is emerging as the safe-haven allocation,” said Ales Koutny, head of international rates at asset management Vanguard, pointing to Germany but also the Netherlands and Switzerland, which have enjoyed almost as large falls in borrowing costs this week.

“First, it’s the historical benefit that they get from lower debt to GDP, better fiscal credibility and lower policy uncertainty,” he said. He added that the “amount of trade unwinds that we have seen has been wild”, as hedge funds have been forced to dump popular trades such as betting on Italian bonds outperforming Bunds.

Data pointing to powerful US economic growth has triggered a sharp sell-off in Treasuries in recent weeks, as investors have bet that the Federal Reserve will need to keep interest rates higher for longer to stop the economy from overheating. US government bonds posted their worst month since 2022 in September.

At the same time, a looming French budget and a fraught presidential election next year have brought investors’ attention back to the question of unsustainable debt piles in the region. Government bonds in Italy and Greece, both formerly the focus of market worries over debt, sold off in sympathy with French bonds on Thursday.

A big drop in German yields on Friday further drove up the additional interest rates that countries such as Italy and France pay on their 10-year debt relative to Germany’s.

France’s so-called spread over Germany hit 1.5 percentage points on Friday, its highest level since 2012, before narrowing later in the day to 1.4 points. Evelyne Gomez-Liechti, a multi-asset strategist at Mizuho, described 1.5 per cent as a “psychologically important” level.

The “violent” widening in Eurozone spreads on Thursday has “triggered an aggressive flight-to-quality bid into Germany”, she said.

There has been a particularly sharp move in so-called swap-spread trades, such as when investors buy French bonds and bet against euro interest rate swaps of the same maturity, typically using leverage.

The broader bond sell-off has sent the additional yield on five-year French bonds relative to the equivalent euro interest rate swaps surging to 0.8 percentage points, the biggest gap since 2011. That has led to losses for those betting on bonds against swaps.

Such idiosyncratic risks among several European countries had whittled down the options for investors looking to allocate outside the US, de Bock said.

“There has been rising demand for diversification” away from US Treasuries, he said. “People want to allocate into Europe” but there were “weak links, countries with higher deficits . . . the universe [of safer bond markets] is smaller than you thought”, he said.

De Bock said on Friday he was recommending that clients buy German debt and bet against Italian debt after the recent sell-off. He said he had previously used EU bonds, issued by the bloc as a whole, as the portion that clients should buy, but “I prefer to have a long that is really focused on the safest asset, which is Bunds”.

Investors were reassessing the risks around so-called peripheral Europe, including France, said Peter Schaffrik, global macro strategist at RBC Capital Markets.

“The market has figured out that for the slower-growing economies, these yield levels are unbearable; the economy can’t live with it,” whereas “Germany is still growing decently,” he added.

title: 美国股市早盘温和走高 非农数据令加息预期降温
content:
美国劳动力市场增幅显著放缓，市场猜测美联储无需很快被迫加息，债券收益率走低，推动美股早盘上扬。
纽约时间10：12，标普500指数上涨0.9%，纳斯达克100指数涨1.4%，道指走高0.5%。
货币市场目前已不再完全计入美联储2026年还会加息一次。此前美债遭遇抛售、收益率升至多年高位，如今反弹进一步扩大。原油价格下跌也改善了市场情绪。七国集团（G-7）计划释放至多1亿桶柴油和原油。
美国劳工统计局周五公布的数据显示，9月非农就业人数增加2.9万人，前两个月数据被向下修正。这一增幅低于预期。失业率升至4.2%，一定程度上反映出劳动力人口增加。
Principal Asset Management的Seema Shah表示：“就业报告弱于预期，应会明显压低美联储10月加息的可能性。非农就业增长减弱、工资增速放缓以及失业率上升，都表明劳动力市场正在降温，而不是重新趋紧。”
高盛资产管理的Lindsay Rosner表示：“今天疲软的数据不支持劳动力市场正在重新趋紧的观点。我们的基本情景仍是12月再加息一次；不过，如果市场压力持续、能源价格进一步上涨，也可能迫使美联储本月采取行动。”

title: 财长贝森特与美国国税局打击富人用来规避资本利得税的ETF策略
content:
核心要点
美国财政部和国税局本周发布警示，矛头直指富豪投资者，以及协助他们利用 ETF 策略规避资本利得所得税的金融、税务与投资顾问。
财政部长斯科特・贝森特表示，税务部门 “将严厉打击旨在逃税、钻联邦税法空子的交易”。
税法第 351 条款一般允许投资者将资产转入一家公司，并换取该公司股份，满足条件时 无需确认资本利得 （存在限制条件）。富人把一篮子证券组合转入新设立 ETF，借此规避收益纳税，已经演变成一种精巧避税手段。
ETF 一大卖点，就是可灵活管理资本利得与亏损。但在美国国税局与财政部发布最新指引后，富豪投资者必须重新审视部分 ETF 递延纳税策略。
争议焦点是 第 351 条款 ETF 转换 的某些使用场景：富豪个人通过中介机构，用一篮子大幅升值股票新设 ETF，目的是递延资本利得税。税务当局的新指引称，该机制本身仍属于合法策略，但增加了附加约束条件。
贝森特本周早些时候在 X 平台发文表示，这份指引 “清晰释放财政部信号：我们会严肃打击刻意逃税、钻联邦税法漏洞的交易”。
针对依托 351 条款、借 ETF 转换避税的配套税收裁定文件，他补充道：“对于这类转换，我们的态度很明确：按照现行法律，这套操作 不能实现避税效果 。”
这份《2026‑20 税收裁定》与《2026‑62 通知》，列举了税务部门认定有问题的情形，包括 ETF 仅充当 “通道” 转移证券以避税。税收裁定是国税局针对特定事实，对税法与法规作出的官方解释，可用于预判国税局如何认定同类交易的税务性质；而税务通知则针对更广场景给出通用性指引。
税法 351 条款规定，满足特定条件时，投资者把资产转入企业换取股权，可以不确认资本利得。例如，单一资产不能超过投资组合市值 25%，前五大持仓合计不能超过组合总价值 50%。合规前提下，这类操作目前仍然被认可。
福特汉姆法学院税法与政策方向教授杰弗里・科隆表示：“国税局与财政部的目标，是他们认定属于滥用的税务筹划手段。”
税务当局认为，投资者通过不当方式规避收益征税，违背该法规的立法初衷。
对于把 ETF 当作税务盾牌的富豪投资者及其投资、税务顾问而言，税务新规发布之后，整个游戏规则或将改变。
监管出手的缘由
国税局这份税收裁定，针对的是将证券投资组合转入新设立 ETF 的交易模式。在这类筹划交易中，ETF 收到转入证券后很快就将其分配出去；投资者最终拿到一个 “实质性不同” 的新组合，而原始持仓的账面增值完全不用确认缴税。
Gursey Schneider 税务合伙人布莱恩・格雷称：“本质就是不用交税，直接完成资产分散配置。”
税务部门指出该操作存在问题，但监管行动并非突发。
去年 7 月彭博的一份可视化报道显示，市场上已有总额 220 亿美元的 ETF 专门为此目的设立，递延的资本利得税最高可达 65 亿美元；自 2024 年起，这类交易规模显著加速增长。
贝森特曾在 7 月 22 日 X 推文写道：“税法应当奖励投资，而不是纵容滥用金融工程的避税行为。” 他补充，监管机构 “不会对华尔街滥用式避税视而不见，也不会容忍专门钻联邦税法空子的产品。如果一项税务方案听上去好得不真实，那大概率有陷阱，投资者务必三思。”
本周的公告中，他再次引用了 7 月的警告。
7 月，国税局与财政部官员曾会见华尔街税务协会成员，沟通政府重点关注的交易类型，包括存疑的 351 条款置换交易。本次税务通知覆盖了当时讨论的多种筹划方案。
谁在用 351 置换？基本都是顶级富豪
一般只有高收入人群使用 351 置换策略。
成本是重要门槛。波士顿 TwinFocus 律所管理合伙人兼总法律顾问约翰・潘特基迪斯表示，设立一支这类 ETF 成本可达 20 万–30 万美元。部分机构建议，投资者至少要有 2500 万美元升值股票放入 ETF，这套方案才具备可行性；潘特基迪斯的门槛更高，他认为持仓低于 1 亿美元的投资者，做这笔筹划没有意义。
这份通知 并非认定全部 351 交易都涉嫌违规 。
通知原文写明：“本通知不涉及，也不对下述交易发表意见：通过 351 交易，向新设立 ETF 注入与其投资策略匹配的资产；若无重大环境变化，这些资产原本就打算长期由 ETF 持有。”
Cerity Partners 肯塔基州巴德斯顿办公室负责人约书亚・诺曼表示，高净值个人与家族采用 351 置换，确实存在合理场景。例如富豪想把 ETF 份额赠与他人，但对方不想直接接收单只个股；另外，将独立管理账户转入 ETF，也可以降低富豪持续承担的税务压力，提升税后收益。
部分 ETF 专家认为，通知中的措辞甚至可能推动该策略被更广泛采用。ETF 管理人 Cambria Funds 创始人梅布・费伯在 X 上称：“非主流观点：监管本周打开口子，设计规范的 351 筹划有望进入主流应用。”
ETF 领域尚存疑问
税务监管机构增设多项限制条件，交易才能够享受递延纳税待遇。
诺曼表示： 交易的时间点至关重要 。
税务通知明确，转入升值证券后 短期内 发生的相关交易属于可疑行为。
但国税局没有对 “短期内” 作出细化定义，税务从业者与法律界普遍预期后续会发布更多指引。
诺曼称，在监管机构补充细则前，“短期内” 的界定会持续处于灰色地带，其他税务专家也认同这一看法。
专注税务与资产组合策略的 Tax Alpha Insider 博主在 X 上写道：“针对 ETF 种子注入的 351 条款税收裁定，我重点看三点，以此判断激进筹划：1）事先筹划证据；2）种子注入后快速赎回；3）转出组合与转入资产差异巨大。这里存在大量灰色空间，未来数月乃至数年，我们会看到大量‘结合具体事实与情形’的个案分析。”
国税局与财政部征集公众对这份通知的意见，截止日期为 10 月 28 日。
监管并不会彻底废除证券换份额这套机制，因为所有大型 ETF 日常申赎单元本身就是免税操作，这是一个数万亿美元规模的行业，潘特基迪斯说道。
但他补充，监管大概率会给那些小型 ETF 增设更多约束 —— 这类产品注入资产后立刻分散组合，纯粹为获取税务优惠。
更多税务筹划手段或将被监管盯上
通知显示，税务部门还在密切关注其他筹划方案，包括搭配 351 转换的合伙制资产转移，以及使用期权、帮助投资者递延资本利得税的 ETF 产品。
会计师事务所 Thomas， Zollars & Lynch 税务合伙人埃德・佐拉斯撰文写道：“税务从业者必须吃透这些被点名的筹划手段，才能给客户提示潜在审计风险。”
科隆提到，国会也可能介入，修改现行 ETF 监管规则，例如收紧 ETF 分配升值证券获取税务好处的适用范围。
格雷建议，想要管理资本利得税的投资者，可以考虑 交换基金 。这是一类私募投资载体，通常采用有限合伙架构，让持有高度集中升值股票的投资者把股份打包进一个分散化组合，同时递延资本利得税；缺点是参与者需要持有满 7 年才能赎回份额。
他还提到，投资者也可以使用 慈善剩余信托 管理资本利得与亏损。

title: 俄称打击乌基础设施 乌称袭击俄炼油厂
content:
俄罗斯国防部10月2日通报称，俄军当天凌晨打击了为乌军服务的基础设施和海上船只。通报说，俄军打击了乌南部敖德萨州伊兹梅尔港一处接收、储存、运输军用物资和燃料的设施。俄军还打击了一艘运送乌军军用物资的干货船、一座为乌军提供后勤保障的公路铁路桥，以及基辅州一座变电站。过去24小时，俄军还控制了哈尔科夫和苏梅地区的三个居民点。
2日，乌克兰武装部队总参谋部发布截至当天8点战况信息称，过去一天前线地区发生207次战斗，乌空军、导弹部队和炮兵部队对俄军无人机控制点、兵力集结区等重要目标实施打击。此外，乌克兰武装部队总参谋部通报称，乌军当天凌晨袭击了俄罗斯伏尔加格勒州的一个炼油厂。（总台记者 郝薇 王晋燕）

title: 联合国：中东局势或致全球新增2200万人面临粮食不安全
content:
当地时间10月2日，联合国妇女署发布报告称，中东地区局势持续紧张导致霍尔木兹海峡航运受阻，推高全球食品价格，并对民众生计造成压力。报告预计，到2026年年底，全球可能新增约2200万人面临粮食不安全状况，其中约53%、即1170万人是女性。
报告指出，苏丹、南苏丹、也门、巴勒斯坦和海地等国民众面临较为严重的粮食不安全风险，其中女性受到的影响更为明显。在苏丹，可能面临粮食不安全的人群中，女性比例接近56%。报告还显示，在苏丹、埃及、伊拉克、叙利亚等国，约80%的女性处于劳动力市场之外，这进一步增加了女性面临粮食不安全的风险。
联合国妇女署在报告中敦促有关各方寻求外交解决方案，缓和地区局势，以促进地区及国际和平与安全。（总台记者 赵远方）

title: 一艘油轮在霍尔木兹海峡遭不明发射物击中
content:
当地时间10月2日，英国海事贸易行动办公室（UKMTO）通报，已收到一份关于霍尔木兹海峡内发生安全事件的报告。
据一艘油轮船长报告，该船在执行出港航行任务时遭到一枚不明发射物击中，导致船上发生小规模火灾并全船停电。火势随后已被扑灭，船只目前正在航行中。
UKMTO表示，目前没有人员伤亡或环境影响的相关报告。有关部门正在展开调查。
UKMTO建议各船只谨慎通行，并向该机构报告任何可疑活动。（总台记者 陈占升）

title: 债券抛售行情或将落幕的隐秘信号
content:
周四美国债券市场企稳，TLT 债券 ETF 录得至少一个月以来最强日内反弹。与此同时，在期权市场的两个细分领域，出现一些不那么引人注目，但对债券多头同样意义重大的交易信号。
据芝加哥期权交易所 LiveVol 以及 SpotGamma 的数据，股票市场中，周四开盘约一小时后，公用事业板块 ETF（XLU）出现一连串期权押注，该基金期权成交量飙升至 30 日均值的十倍。
核心是一笔 100 万美元规模的交易，押注该板块将止跌，甚至迎来反弹。债券持续下跌推高收益率，高股息的公用事业板块因此遭受重创 —— 固定收益产品收益率走高，对公用事业的分红形成更强竞争。
具体来看，该交易方卖出 5 万张 1 月中旬到期、行权价 39 美元的看跌期权，获利 69.5 万美元；同时卖出同等数量、同一到期日、行权价 42 美元的看涨期权，获利 40 万美元。交易发生时 XLU 价格略高于 39 美元。这笔交易意味着，交易方押注到期时，该基金价格会落在 39‑42 美元区间，以此博取最大收益。
这笔交易并非激进押注公用事业板块大幅上涨，但它表明部分交易员认为该板块跌势已经结束，利率或许已经见顶。此外，这也是该利率高度敏感板块期权资金流向持续一周转向的集中体现。据 ThinkOrSwim 数据，XLU 与 10 年期美债收益率的 30 日相关系数为‑0.94。
道富公用事业精选行业 SPDR ETF（XLU）实时报价：39.94 美元，+0.26（+0.65%）|美东时间 11：40
Barchart 数据显示，看跌期权与看涨期权的成交量比率在上月末触及 2.67，为 5 月以来最高，随后上周该比值回落，交易资金开始转向看涨期权。SpotGamma 统计，周四市场约买入 74000 张看涨期权，而看跌期权仅 4500 张。
其他预示利率见顶的押注
公用事业板块的期权交易，并非唯一暗示债券抛售正在降温的隐秘期权信号。当日晚些时候，芝加哥商业交易所债券交易场内，有交易者投入 440 万美元押注短期利率将会反转下行。
一位不愿具名的场内交易员透露，有交易者买入 10 万份 SOFR（担保隔夜融资利率）期货 3 月合约的 96/96.12 看涨期权价差组合，当时合约价格约 95.51。这笔交易押注隔夜利率将回落至 6 月以来未曾见到的收益率水平。
该交易员表示：“就业报告发布前夕，今日出现大规模看涨期权买入，成交量巨大。10 年期美债收益率突破 5.3% 之后，市场就迎来反弹。”

title: 科技公司推出萌系吉祥物，以缓解AI焦虑
content:
AI公司正尝试发起一场新的“魅力攻势”：它们使用看起来像毛绒玩具般可爱的角色，试图让自己的技术显得不那么令人恐惧。
OpenAI 的最新 AI 代理由戴着领结和眼镜的彩色卡通角色化身而成；Meta 的 Muse 助手的吉祥物则是一个双颊红润的蛋形角色；而 Anthropic 也有自己友好的像素风橙色螃蟹“Clawd”。
随着公众对AI导致失业以及给人类带来生存风险的焦虑日益加剧，科技公司正效仿消费品公司和制药企业的营销策略，推出一系列萌系吉祥物。
其目的是让这些正在为我们编写代码、搜索互联网并代为预订日程的AI助手显得更加平易近人、个性鲜明且值得信赖。既然“绿巨人”能让孩子们乖乖吃蔬菜，那么一个甜美的拟人化三角形或许也能赢得AI怀疑论者的青睐。
“人们对AI的恐惧与日俱增，而面对可爱的东西很难产生恐惧感，”资深品牌顾问艾伦·亚当森表示，“人们更容易信任友好的事物。”
市场研究机构 Morning Consult 近期对1300名消费者进行的一项在线调查显示，超过半数的受访者认为AI对社会构成了生存威胁，近70%的人担心AI会取代人类的工作。
在AI巨头们争夺用户的背景下，关于“流氓AI代理黑客攻击政府网站”的新闻标题以及“AI发展速度过于危险”的警告层出不穷。用卡通形象来代表强大的算法，标志着这些公司价值近十亿美元营销努力的最新篇章。
此前，企业已经尝试通过更温和的方式来缓解AI恐惧，并消除人们对依赖自动化系统可能导致认知能力下降的担忧，例如投放强调AI能赋能人类、提升生产力的广告。
据广告追踪公司 MediaRadar 估计，自2023年以来，包括 微软 、OpenAI、 谷歌 、Anthropic 和 Perplexity 在内的科技巨头已在美国为其AI产品累计投入了9.36亿美元的广告费。其中，超过一半的支出发生在今年的前八个月。
这场最新的AI品牌重塑甚至延伸到了政府最高层。特朗普总统最近签署了一项行政命令，将“人工智能”更名为“超级智能”（super intelligence），以凸显其广阔前景。
周一，OpenAI 宣布出于安全考虑取消发布其下一代AI模型。一天后，该公司推出了名为 Dots 的新AI代理。
OpenAI 的 Dots 是全天候在线的助手，旨在处理工作任务和日常琐事，如安排会议或预订航班。在旧金山的一场活动上，OpenAI 展示了一组粉色、蓝色、绿色、黄色和紫色的角色阵容，它们的名字包括 Iggy、Felipe、Jojo、Todd 和 Alfred。
用户可以自定义其专属 Dots 的外观和名称。
“人们不会害怕自己命名的事物，反而会接纳它，”亚当森（Adamson）说。
OpenAI 表示，Dots 预计将出现在该公司针对该新产品的后续广告宣传中。
上个月，Meta 在 Meta Connect 大会上推出其AI代理 Muse 时，其吉祥物 Jolly 的真人等身模型还在现场与参会者共舞。
如今，Jolly 的形象不仅出现在纽约和旧金山的 Muse 广告牌上，还客串了 Muse 的电视广告。在在线广告中，它有时戴着发带、穿着运动服充当健身助手，有时则戴着耳机陪伴用户网购。
Anthropic 员工 Sam McAllister 使用 Claude 的代码创造了这只复古像素风螃蟹“Clawd”，并在2024年的演示中用它来展示产品的部分功能。开发者们非常喜爱这只甲壳类动物，它也因此成为了 Claude Code 的吉祥物。虽然 Anthropic 并未在面向消费者的营销中使用 Clawd，但会在开发者活动上分发相关的周边商品。
在在线交易平台 Etsy 上，充斥着各种非官方的 Clawd 周边产品；其中一位商家甚至在售卖一款未经授权的9.4英寸螃蟹毛绒玩具，售价高达148.23美元。
吉祥物过去曾帮助推销过其他可能缺乏吸引力或具有潜在危险的产品。几十年来，卡通角色“骆驼老乔”（Joe Camel）为香烟增添了一层酷酷的色彩。
资深广告人谢丽尔·伯曼表示，随着时间的推移，一个有效的角色形象能让品牌在众多相似的选择中脱颖而出。她曾参与过包含多个标志性吉祥物的广告制作，如 麦当劳 叔叔、品食乐面团小子和老虎托尼。
“角色化身为品牌本身，将抽象的技术变成了人们熟悉的朋友，”她说。

title: The Ellison credit complex gets a bit more complex
content:
Toby Nangle

Published October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

We’ve joked before that Warner takeovers are the harbingers of financial apocalypse . So those of a superstitious disposition should mark next week — when the latest takeover is set to close — in their diaries, thanks to the willingness of bond investors to part with their cash.

But Paramount Skydance, the bond issuer and Warner Bros acquirer, is a big investment-grade company, isn’t it? And while $52bn is still a lot of corporate bonds for debt capital market teams to find homes for, big investment-grade companies seem like they sell large slews of bonds on a weekly basis.

S&P Global Ratings, 24th September:

We lowered our issuer credit rating on PSKY [Paramount Skydance] to ‘BB’ from ‘BB+’, as we expect leverage to increase when the acquisition closes shortly.

Wait, what? Double-B flat isn’t investment grade, it’s junk.

Luckily for investment-grade bond investors, Paramount Skydance didn’t let a little thing like being junk-rated get in the way of issuing a monster consignment of investment-grade rated bonds.

Somewhat unusually for a public debt transaction of this size, they threw in extra credit support in the form of a special first-lien charge. And as S&P Global Ratings explains in its ‘recovery rating’ report ($) :

Depending on the recovery assessment for a given debt issue, the issue rating is derived by notching up, down, or not at all from the issuer credit rating on the issuer of the debt.

The rating analysts reckon that, in the event of default, noteholders who have the benefit of this first-lien charge will recover 90–100 cents in the dollar. At least this is what they reckon if their 2031 default scenario comes to pass.

The 2031 default scenario imagines a world in which the company runs into difficulty, decides it needs to restructure its debt, but is still churning out $10.2bn of ebitda, giving it an enterprise value of around $63bn (after accounting for all the costs of bankruptcy administration).

Bondholders with the first-lien charge are close to having first dibs on this imagined $63bn enterprise value, and these dibs push the bond ratings up to BBB-, despite being issued by a BB-rated company. Nice.

Are there any other credit supports that help the company squeak over the IG rating line ($) ? Our emphasis:

Our ratings on PSKY reflects [sic] the commitment by the Ellison family , the company’s controlling entity, to take all steps necessary for it to deleverage below 3.75x on a net-debt basis (per the company’s definition) by 2028 and to 3.0x by 2029.

Of course.

David Ellison is the CEO of Paramount Skydance. He is also the son of Larry Ellison. And Larry Ellison, according to Bloomberg’s Billionaires Index , is worth $187bn — largely based on the value of his holdings of Oracle Corp common stock. Having the owner of 40 per cent of the global AI hyperscaling heavyweight committed to taking all steps necessary to deleverage has got to be pretty reassuring to credit investors.

We checked in on how investors are pricing the global AI hyperscaler’s creditworthiness. We also threw the new Paramount Skydance bonds, and every other triple-B-rated US corporate bond in the ICE BofA corporate bond index into the chart.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

Increasingly, it looks like two large issuers are being priced as having far higher risk credit premia than the rest. Both sit on the lowest rung of the investment-grade ladder, and both are Ellison family companies.

Moreover, as Chris Whittall of IFR noted today , the cost of insuring Paramount debt against default using credit default swaps has skyrocketed. And that Ellison family commitment doesn’t look like it has helped (h/t to Dec Mullarkey, who also flagged this correlation):

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

Partly, this could be unhappy holders of the new PSKY bonds seeking to lay off risk. An IFR article ($) reports that the new 10-year bonds fell close to five points shortly after issuance, suggesting that maybe not everyone was in it for the long haul.

But, given its long history, the cyan Paramount CDS line most likely references obligations issued specifically by the Paramount subsidiary of Paramount Skydance to whom the commitment has apparently been given. S&P rates unsecured debt from this subsidiary a lowly single-B plus.

Still, if the new PSKY debt doesn’t look like it has been absorbed that well, at least we won’t be muttering about indices being gamed and passive bot-run funds getting stuffed. Because the weird timing of the bond deal all but guarantees that the victims have, so far, all been active human decision-makers.

As MainFT reported Wednesday , Paramount Skydance rushed to sell bonds to close the acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery “before a third-quarter deadline to avoid hefty penalty fees”. And this rush saw them sold on 30th September: not a great day for any wannabe corporate bond index constituent.

The cut-off for inclusion in Bloomberg indices — think the big US and Global Agg indices — is two business days prior to the last business day for the month, so Monday 28th September. For ICE BoA corporate bond indices , the cut-off for month-end rebalancing is three business days ahead of month-end, so Friday 25th September. And the iBoxx USD Liquid Investment Grade Maturity Indices require new issues to settle by the last day of the month. The new Paramount Skydance bonds settle on the 5th October.

So quasi-passive or actual index-replicating investors are unlikely to have piled in. And active managers needn’t have worried about any relative-to-benchmark performance cost of missing out on a deal that performed strongly, at least for the next month.

title: 道明证券推迟美联储加息时点预期 料下次行动在12月
content:
道明证券调整了对美联储加息时点的预期，目前预计将在12月和明年3月加息，此前预计的时间分别为10月和明年1月。
首席美国经济学家Oscar Munoz等人在报告中写道，对美联储加息次数的预期不变。
他们写道：“虽然即将公布的CPI和PPI报告可能成为最终决定因素，但鉴于美联储官员似乎看法一致，我们现在认为美联储要在10月再次收紧政策的门槛很高”。
不认为周五的数据改变了美联储的预测，但近期利率的上升可能“影响了其谨慎态度”。

title: 美国就业增长逊于预期 企业招聘保持谨慎
content:
美国9月份新增就业人数低于预期，薪资增速放缓，显示随着成本上升，雇主在招聘方面趋于谨慎。
美国劳工统计局周五公布的数据显示，9月份非农就业人数增加2.9万人，此前两个月的数据被下修。这一增幅低于预期。失业率升至4.2%。
稳健的消费者支出和强劲的企业投资为招聘提供了支撑，但许多注重成本控制的雇主仍不愿扩大员工规模。不过，裁员仍较为有限。
由于失业率从历史水平来看仍然较低，美联储官员在考虑何时再次加息时，可以继续将注意力集中在通胀上。数据公布后，交易员削减了对美联储10月加息的押注。
Jefferies LLC首席美国经济学家Thomas Simons在报告中表示，“对美联储而言，这一数据应该会彻底打消10月加息的可能性。现在看来，那些强调距离再次需要加息还有一些时间的决策者，更有可能继续保持耐心。”
这份最新就业报告是11月中期选举前的最后一份，预计经济状况将成为影响美国人投票选择的核心因素。劳动力市场是其中一部分，但外界的很大一部分焦点仍集中在挥之不去的生活成本担忧上，尽管消费者仍在持续支出。
行业表现
地方政府就业人数下降，一些受人工智能影响程度较高的行业也出现就业下滑，包括信息业、专业和商业服务业以及金融活动等行业。与此同时，数据中心及其他人工智能相关基础设施投资为建筑业和制造业增加就业提供了支撑。
医疗保健以及休闲和酒店业就业人数也有所增加。与此同时，平均时薪较8月上涨0.1%，弱于预期；同比上涨3%，为2021年以来最慢的同比薪资增速。平均每周工时持平。
Oxford Economics首席美国经济学家Michael Pearce表示，“劳动力市场依然稳健，但它并没有带来通胀压力。”
经济研究观点：“9月份非农就业数据表明，在8月份数据异常强劲之后，招聘步伐有所放缓。加之失业率上升，这份报告不足以支持美联储10月加息。我们预计美联储今年余下时间将维持利率不变。”——Anna Wong、Andrew Sacher和Eliza Winger
就业报告由两项调查构成：一项是企业调查，用于统计非农就业人数；另一项是家庭调查，是失业率和劳动参与率等数据的依据。家庭调查也有自己的就业人数指标，该指标当月大幅上升。
9月份劳动参与率（即正在工作或积极寻找工作的人口占比）升至61.8%，为四个月高点。

title: 以色列中央选举委员会要求国家安全部长删除争议视频
content:
据多家以色列媒体报道，以色列中央选举委员会2日要求国家安全部长本-格维尔删除其发布在社交媒体上一段引发争议的视频。
以色列《国土报》报道，本周早些时候本-格维尔发布的一段视频显示，本-格维尔与一名巴勒斯坦被囚人员对峙，本-格维尔还宣称，他为让后者监禁条件更加艰难而“自豪”。本-格维尔还威胁这名巴勒斯坦人“我要杀了你”“我要处决你”。
报道说，涉事被囚人员名叫哈桑·萨拉梅，系巴勒斯坦伊斯兰抵抗运动（哈马斯）成员，因牵涉1996年针对以色列人的袭击事件而被判处终身监禁。
批评这段视频的请愿者认为，在监狱内拍摄视频的行为违反了“禁止将公共资源用于竞选活动的禁令”。以中央选举委员会接受了这一观点并于2日裁定，本-格维尔发布这段视频的目的是“选举宣传，而非像本-格维尔所称的那样起到威慑作用”。
该裁定还说，本-格维尔应以个人名义向请愿方支付2万新谢克尔（约6500美元）的法律费用，他所在政党还须承担相关费用。
以色列议会选举定于10月27日举行。按以色列媒体说法，这将是以色列近40年来首次按计划而非提前举行议会选举。

title: Why does Anthropic’s IPO feel so weird?
content:
Richard Waters

Published October 2 2026

For fast-growing tech companies, initial public offerings are an important rite of passage. From Google’s declaration that it wanted to “make the world a better place” to SpaceX’s ambition to “extend the light of consciousness to the stars”, they are a moment to capture the world’s imagination. The best IPO narratives fuse an idealistic vision of the future with a sense of inevitability about why this company will win.

Selling shares to the public for the first time is also seen as a milestone on the path to corporate maturity. There is an expectation that products have been honed and business models perfected.

Perhaps all of this goes some way towards explaining why the looming IPO of AI company Anthropic has felt so . . . weird.

Details from its draft prospectus leaked out this week, suggesting the share sale is close. If it hits the $2tn valuation investors are expecting, it would set a record for a new public company.

Compared to other blockbuster tech IPOs, though, the build-up to Anthropic’s stock market debut has felt discordant, even creepy. What other company, after all, would think to warn shareholders that its main product might go off the rails and resort to blackmail?

The most obvious cause of the weirdness has been the predictions from former and current employees that AI might lead to human extinction. Far from trying to stamp out such talk, CEO Dario Amodei agreed that the technology could cause “catastrophic damage” and regulation was urgently needed.

It isn’t only the doomerism that has struck a jarring note. Like the rest of its industry, Anthropic has struggled to convince the public that its technology is actually going to make the world a better place. AI executives such as Amodei like to talk about the economic “abundance” it will create and the diseases it will cure, but such utopian musings are out of tune with the wariness many people feel.

Then there are the mishaps. The extinction warnings relate to a future version of AI that might escape human control. Even at this stage, though, Anthropic can’t seem to keep a grip on the technology it is already building. Echoing problems at rival OpenAI, it confessed recently to three cases in which its AI had escaped on to the internet and hacked into other companies’ systems.

Ultimately, none of this may matter much to investors, given the company’s astounding growth. Even here, though, things are not straightforward. There is a lively debate among AI investors over whether makers of so-called frontier AI models like Anthropic will be able to maintain any kind of performance advantage. If not, it is likely to struggle to maintain pricing power and be forced into an overhaul of its business model.

To Anthropic’s critics, much of this reflects the immaturity of a five-year-old research lab that has, almost overnight, been propelled to global prominence.

Countering the extinction warnings, tech figures like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, former White House AI tsar David Sacks and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg argue that there is nothing inherently dangerous about developing more advanced AI or releasing the technology to a mass market. It just takes the same kind of engineering experience, product design and quality control that characterise other technologies — disciplines that Anthropic is still learning as it mutates from ambitious start-up into mature product company.

Before it sprang to wider attention, Anthropic was the product of a culture that seems singular even by the standards of Silicon Valley. Its founders were heavily influenced by a branch of the effective altruism movement known as long-termism, which is fixated on the risks of human extinction from technologies like advanced AI. To critics, that has led to a speculative and self-indulgent doomerism that overstates the more prosaic work needed to control AI.

This is certainly how things are seen in Washington. After a lunch at the White House this week, a number of AI executives — including Anthropic’s CEO — signed an “accord on super intelligence” that promises the kind of things you would expect from normal, mature companies: “Robust internal controls”, special board-level committees and outside audits to contain the risks.

It’s hard, though, to see this erasing the weirdness from the Anthropic IPO. Investors still need to grapple with voluminous warnings that take up fully a third of the company’s draft prospectus (including the one about blackmail). There are apparently so many things that could go wrong that Anthropic’s lawyers would be forgiven for suggesting the company instead issue a single, blanket statement: This technology will do crazy stuff we can’t even imagine yet.

Nor has the official line in Washington, exemplified by President Donald Trump’s insouciance, done anything to end the division in Silicon Valley. Technologists without an obvious axe to grind, like Bill Gates, have been sounding increasingly alarmed about AI, which they warn is much too dangerous to be left in the hands of private companies without serious external controls.

As its big moment on Wall Street nears, Anthropic’s unintended IPO narrative is hard to dispel: the hypergrowth AI company which, according to its own employees, might just kill us all.

title: 谷歌一直在追赶OpenAI与Anthropic，其全新旗舰模型真能跻身前沿梯队吗？
content:
核心要点
2026 年，谷歌（GOOGL）在 AI 领域的发展之路跌宕起伏。
开局尚好。2025 年末推出的 Gemini 3，让谷歌重回前沿 AI 的讨论中心。
但今年大部分时间里，AI 技术突破的主角是 Anthropic 和 OpenAI。
谷歌无疑希望，全新旗舰模型 Gemini 4 Argon 的发布能够扭转这一局面。
前沿 AI 赛道
今年 8 月，DeepMind（谷歌 AI 实验室）原 CEO 德米斯・哈萨比斯卸任。我当时撰文提到，新任负责人科雷・卡武库乔卢肩负重任，需要追赶山姆・奥尔特曼与达里奥・阿莫代伊执掌的两家公司。
如今谷歌宣称，该模型在部分基准测试中，性能优于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的顶级产品。
综合评测指数 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index（AAII）榜单显示，Gemini 4 Argon 排名仅次于 Claude Opus 5.5 与 Claude Sonnet 5.5。
IDC 人工智能研究总监蒂姆・劳表示：“基准测试表明，谷歌 Gemini 4 Argon 在关键任务上具备高级推理能力，尤其在法律推理、金融以及其他企业知识类工作，也包含长周期任务场景。”
Omdia 首席分析师连杰・苏认为，虽然谷歌 “入局网络安全、代码领域的时间偏晚”，但 Gemini 4 把谷歌带到 AI 前沿，网络安全领域表现尤为突出。
网络安全
谷歌也在重点宣传这项优势。
公司计划分阶段推出新模型：首先面向可信网络安全合作伙伴开放，同时配合美国政府开展发布前安全评估。
Gemini 产品负责人图尔西・多希接受 采访时表示：“以这种方式启动上线，能增强我们的信心，也可以尽快把这套经过训练、擅长网络防御的模型交到安全防护人员手中。”
苏提到，OpenAI 与 Anthropic 的模型曾出现失控风险事件，这给谷歌创造了机会，使其有望 “树立可信模型供应商的定位，提供安全可靠的 AI 服务”。
Futurum Group 的 AI 业务负责人尼克・佩申表示，虽然 Argon 让谷歌重新具备 AI 竞争力，但这款模型还不足以让谷歌成为行业 “领头羊”。
蒂姆・劳称：“但至少，Gemini 4 Argon 在企业知识工作场景开辟了新的竞争战线，可与其他顶尖前沿模型一较高下。”
谷歌在公告中表示，新模型已经投入内部使用，用于优化谷歌数据中心内存资源，无需额外采购硬件，就释放出数百 TB 存储空间；量子计算研究人员也已使用该模型。
但和所有新模型一样，真正的考验是正式广泛上线、投入实战之时。谷歌尚未给出全面开放的时间表。
“虽然谷歌宣传内部落地案例的成果，但最终验证，要等模型全面发布后，在企业生产环境中才能见分晓。” 蒂姆・劳说。
补充趣闻
美国总统特朗普将 AI 重新命名为 SI（Super Intelligence，超级智能），这件事带来一个出人意料（但某种程度上可预见）的后果：欧洲小国斯洛文尼亚的域名注册量迎来 “前所未有的暴涨”，没错，它的国家域名后缀就是 ．si 。
斯洛文尼亚域名注册管理机构 Register.si 发言人向 BBC 表示，9 月新增 44000 个．si 域名，而 8 月新增不足 2000 个。
这不是 AI 概念第一次引爆小国域名热潮。
加勒比海岛国安圭拉人口不足 2 万，近些年它的域名 ．ai 也曾迎来注册爆发。

title: 营收展望疲软叠加裁员计划公布，耐克股价大跌6%
content:
专题：聚焦美股2026年第二季度财报
核心要点
耐克股价周五继续下跌，连续第二个交易日走低，此前公司发布 2027 财年第一季度财报，同时给出悲观的业绩展望。
这家运动服饰巨头周四披露，第一财季营收下降 4%，至 112 亿美元；大中华区业务收入下滑，北美板块的增长起到部分对冲作用。本季度净利润 7.12 亿美元，同比去年的 7.27 亿美元下降 2%。
耐克总裁兼首席执行官埃利奥特・希尔在公告中表示：“耐克运动生活线、乔丹品牌以及大中华区业务仍有大量待改善之处。我们正在采取审慎举措，以符合长期发展的正确方式夯实这些业务。”
耐克预计 2027 财年营收将出现 高位个位数百分比的下滑 。周五早盘，耐克股价最新下跌约 6%；今年以来累计跌幅接近 45%。
公司同时推出名为 “Pace（节奏）” 的全新运营模式，目标到 2031 年实现 25 亿美元成本节约，并计划自 2027 年起进一步裁员。
希尔周四在致员工的内部公告中写道：“这项改革会造成耐克整体岗位缩减。我清楚这类消息会带来不确定性，我对此十分重视。”“受影响岗位的相关决策将从 2027 年及之后才会启动。”
该改革项目还包括：升级全球供应链、重组为三大区域业务板块、在印度建设全新园区，以及进一步精简组织架构以压缩成本。
“降本成为主旋律”
耐克今年已经实施两轮裁员：1 月在美国配送中心裁撤 775 个岗位；4 月再度裁员 1400 人，主要集中在技术部门。
花旗分析师周五发布研报，因销售指引低于市场预期，维持对耐克 “中性” 评级。
“耐克正在演变为降本叙事。管理层推出 25 亿美元降本计划，来应对运动生活线、乔丹品牌以及中国业务面临的巨大现实压力。” 花旗分析师写道。
分析师提到，管理层会在投资者日活动上披露更多五年展望，但 Pace 改革真正看到实质性成效要等到 2029 年。
“耐克存在超出当前指引的可能性，但在我们看来，耐克并不应当相比同行享有估值溢价。” 分析师补充道。

title: Pedro Sánchez loses vote on Spanish housing reform
content:
Barney Jopson in Madrid

Published October 2 2026

Spanish lawmakers have rejected Pedro Sánchez’s signature effort to address a ballooning housing crisis, in a major setback for the prime minister that could push him to call an early election.

Spain has been rocked by public anger over rising rents, which boiled over last week after an 87-year-old was evicted from her Madrid apartment because she could no longer afford it.

But Sánchez’s attempt to quell the fury with a legislative reform failed on Friday as his minority leftwing government could not corral enough support to pass the bill.

Junts per Catalunya, a Catalan separatist party whose votes helped Sánchez return to office in 2023, said it would not support the housing bill, arguing that it would reduce the supply of rental properties and drive up prices further.

The legislation included a prohibition on evictions until 2030 and a ban on the purchase of residential property by investors the government called “vulture funds”.

One of the EU’s few remaining socialist leaders, Sánchez has struggled to pass major legislative changes or a budget in his second term. The rightwing opposition — the conservative People’s Party (PP) and the populist Vox party — voted against the bill and renewed its calls for snap elections to break the gridlock.

Opinion polls carried out before Friday’s vote suggested the PP and Vox could secure enough votes to oust Sánchez and form a governing alliance.

But some analysts said the premier could still turn this defeat in his favour and mobilise his base, especially if he calls early elections. Pablo Simón, a politics professor at the Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, said: “He has to call elections within nine months or so. So the question is: is he going to have a better moment than this in three or six months’ time? That is the question he will be asking himself. And the answer is probably no.”

The premier’s standing has been hit by an influx of thousands of unauthorised migrants into Ceuta, a Spanish African exclave, and by a series of corruption allegations, including charges against his wife, who denies wrongdoing.

Addressing the PP and Vox, Isabel Rodríguez, Spain’s housing minister, condemned them for opposing the bill. “Whilst people are protesting in the streets, you’re off to Miami or a vulture fund conference encouraging them to colonise us,” she said. The legislative push began when Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was evicted from her Madrid flat after her landlord introduced a rent increase she could not afford when a longstanding rent cap expired.

Following street demonstrations to support her at the weekend, hundreds of people set up a protest camp in central Madrid. The small company that owns her apartment subsequently struck a deal to let her return home.

title: 柴油补给受阻 扎波罗热核电站拟减少待命应急发电机数量
content:
国际原子能机构当地时间10月2日表示，由于柴油燃料储备持续偏低，扎波罗热核电站正考虑进一步减少处于自动待命状态的应急柴油发电机数量。
应急柴油发电机主要在外部供电中断时，为核电站关键安全系统提供电力。国际原子能机构介绍，今年8月至9月，扎波罗热核电站曾因长时间失去外部电源，连续近三周依靠应急柴油发电机供电，导致柴油储备明显下降。受周边军事活动影响，近期补充柴油的工作仍受到阻碍。
与此同时，扎波罗热核电站的外部供电也较为脆弱。国际原子能机构称，扎波罗热核电站自今年6月以来已10次失去外部电源，目前仅依赖一条330千伏外部输电线路，备用电源的可靠性因此尤为重要。
国际原子能机构总干事格罗西表示，持续缺乏柴油补给正在加剧扎波罗热核电站本已脆弱的核安全形势，并呼吁有关方面尽快保障燃料运抵核电站。（总台记者 张云帆）
