title: 福特险胜现代，保住美国市场第三大销量席位
content:
核心要点
福特在第三季度以微弱优势保住美国市场销量第三的位置，此前市场普遍预计现代汽车将会超越这家底特律车企。
福特周五公布，第三季度轻型车辆销量同比下降 6.6%，达到 507395 辆，该统计口径不含归类为其他品类的重型大型皮卡。
与之对比，这家韩国车企（统计包含现代、起亚、捷尼赛思三大品牌）本季度销量增长 5.4%，达到 506200 辆。
两家企业实际表现均好于此前预期。考克斯汽车此前的预测曾认为，现代将首次实现季度销量超过福特。
现代集团（含豪华品牌捷尼赛思以及姊妹品牌起亚）今年在美国市场销量势头强劲。反观福特，受去年事故影响，其核心 F 系列皮卡的生产与销售遭受冲击，生产端一直承压。
根据两家企业本周披露的数据，截至第三季度，福特今年累计销量依旧领先现代约 89700 辆。
周五，福特淡化了现代销量紧追不舍的态势。福特表示，尽管同属一个集团，但起亚与现代在美国是独立运营的两个品牌。
除 F 系列皮卡的生产问题之外，锐际等车型销量下滑，也让福特的同比数据对比压力陡增。
福特美国销售负责人罗布・卡夫尔周五表示，本季度，包含 F‑150 在内的 F 系列皮卡的销量与库存水平持续改善。
他在媒体电话会上表示：“年初我们遭遇的部分阻力已经基本过去，这为我们第四季度的强劲表现打下基础。”
第三季度 F 系列皮卡整体销量仅下滑 1.9%；但已经停产的电动皮卡 F‑150 Lightning 销量暴跌 97.1%。
这家底特律车企旗下福特品牌本季度销量约下滑 6%，豪华品牌林肯销量下跌 18%。
截至 9 月，福特电动车累计销量同比大跌 67.5%；其中第三季度同比降幅接近 80%。该品类同比基数压力较大：去年同期，在特朗普政府取消最高 7500 美元电动车联邦补贴前夕，福特电动车销量曾创下历史新高。

title: 高盛因客户提前投资SpaceX股份退出斩获巨额收益
content:
高盛 集团投行在承办SpaceX这场规模盛大的6月IPO时赚取巨额费用，而这笔上市相关的更大收益，早在多年前就埋下伏笔。
知情人士透露，早在五年多前SpaceX估值数百亿美元阶段，高盛就安排高净值客户投资这家公司。这家航空企业上市时估值达1.77万亿美元，出售股份的高盛客户斩获巨额收益，同时给高盛带来数亿美元的激励费。
不愿具名的知情人士称，高盛合伙人可与客户一同参与投资，这意味着部分现任及前任高管也获得大额收益（信息涉及隐私）。
高盛发言人拒绝置评。
高盛规模达4万亿美元的资管与财富管理业务板块手握令人羡慕的资源，可为客户拿到稀缺机会，投资尚未上市的企业。这类优质标的往往伴随高风险，但也展现出企业登陆公开市场之前，早期投资蕴藏的巨大上行收益空间。
该部门目前由Kristin Olson主管，面向高净值人群开展另类投资业务，还曾协助客户参与支付巨头Stripe、设计软件公司Canva的早期融资轮次，这两家企业均被视作潜在IPO候选企业。
高盛投行部（独立业务板块）作为SpaceX上市的主顾问，收取约1亿美元服务费。该行全力烘托本次上市热度，包括在纽约总部大堂摆放火箭模型。上市当日，高盛投行员工脚穿印有SpaceX标识的 耐克 绿色鞋款，这是对“绿鞋机制”的呼应——该条款允许承销商在市场需求旺盛时增发股票。
知情人士（因信息涉密要求匿名）表示，这笔激励费带来的意外收益并未纳入此前财务预估。高管团队决定动用这笔收益，提前拨付部分慈善捐赠用于高盛公益项目，以此获取更优的税务效果。
今年早些时候生效的一项税制修订，设置了慈善捐赠抵扣的最低门槛，以此激励企业提前捐赠。只有超出该门槛的捐赠款项，才能享受税收减免。
上月，高盛首席执行官戴维·所罗门暗示了该行这一操作。他在一场投资者会议上提到财报中或将出现一些特殊项目，其中一项尤为突出：银行正以一种“税务效益极高”的方式，把未来数年的慈善捐赠提前兑现。
他同时提示，这项操作叠加科技投入等领域开支增加，将推高非薪酬类费用，相关数据会体现在10月13日发布的三季报中。

title: 埃里森表示，派拉蒙与华纳兄弟探索合并后的新公司将命名为天空之舞（Skydance）
content:
核心要点
派拉蒙‑天空之舞（PSKY）首席执行官戴维・埃里森于周五宣布，下周完成与华纳兄弟探索（WBD）的合并交易之后，合并主体将命名为 Skydance（天空之舞） 。
过去 18 个月，这家企业接连完成两笔重大收购，此番更名也形成一个完整的发展时点。
埃里森周五在 X 平台发文写道：“派拉蒙与华纳兄弟塑造了一个多世纪的流行文化。将两家企业整合，我们并非改写历史，而是为这两家标志性制片厂配备更强大的发展引擎。合并之后，我们就是 Skydance：一个以创意为先，承载大胆、优质故事内容的大本营。”
埃里森指出，新的集团名称，可以让派拉蒙、华纳兄弟继续作为相互独立的制片厂保留下来。
“我们绝不希望一个全新的企业品牌，削弱、改变或是掩盖这两家制片厂任何一方的光芒。” 他表示，“恰恰相反，我们希望这个名字能够赋予合并集团独有的身份，同时让派拉蒙、华纳兄弟以及我们旗下所有杰出品牌继续站在聚光灯之下。”
根据 Rentrak 的数据，派拉蒙制片厂与华纳兄弟制片厂合计计划明年推出 35 部电影。
2025 年 8 月，曾出品《碟中谍》系列、《壮志凌云 2：独行侠》的制作公司 Skydance 完成对派拉蒙的收购。几周之后，埃里森便把目标瞄准华纳兄弟探索，开启收购进程，并最终促成这笔重磅交易。
今年 2 月，派拉蒙‑天空之舞与华纳兄弟探索公布交易，企业估值约 1100 亿美元。
在多州总检察长提起相关诉讼之后，派拉蒙‑天空之舞本周表示，这笔交易预计将于周二完成交割。
交易完成后，埃里森以及即将卸任美泰 CEO 的伊农・克雷兹将出任联席首席执行官。

title: 英伟达股价自5月以来首次创历史新高 市值迈向6万亿美元
content:
英伟达股价自5月以来首次创下历史新高，在两个月的抛售导致市值蒸发逾1万亿美元后，投资者重新涌入该股。
这家全球市值最高的上市公司股价周五上涨2.9%，较7月底低点累计反弹近25%。当时，对人工智能前景的担忧一度令英伟达股价承压。
近几周，市场乐观认为Meta Platforms的Muse等AI智能体可能推动半导体需求增加，为英伟达股价上涨提供了支撑。英伟达周一宣布将股票回购计划规模增加创纪录的1，500亿美元后，股价进一步获得提振。
英伟达此次反弹之前，市场对AI行业前景的情绪数月来迅速变化，其中包括对企业斥资数千亿美元建设AI基础设施是否合理，以及这项技术可能给人类带来的安全风险等问题的担忧。
这家总部位于加州圣克拉拉的芯片开发商周一发布了一套新的双层AI安全系统，旨在防止AI智能体失控。英伟达表示，这套新系统有能力阻止近期OpenAI的AI模型导致Hugging Face遭侵入的事件。
英伟达股价今年迄今上涨约27%，有望连续第四年实现两位数涨幅。目前公司市值约为5.7万亿美元，距离成为历史上首家市值达到6万亿美元的公司不到3，000亿美元。

title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski
content:
Zack Polanski has urged voters to back the Greens to force changes from Andy Burnham, arguing his party has the power to move Labour in "the right direction".

In his speech to the party's annual conference, the Green leader said that "sustained pressure" from his party had made forced Labour into changing its stance on issues including climate and its stance towards Israel.

He told activists in Brighton that Labour had failed to take action on housing, as he called for a three-year cap to limit rent rises in the private sector.

And he said that voting for the Greens would force changes from the government, telling members: "Vote Green, and watch Labour move".

Polanski arrived in Brighton facing questions over his leadership of the party amid signs the Greens' rise in popularity last year may have waned, and how he would respond to Labour's change of leadership under Burnham.

In his half-hour address, he did not mention the Conservatives or Reform UK but launched repeated attacks on Labour's record in office.

He criticised Labour for making "slogans without action" on the cost of living and vowed only his party would end "Rip Off Britain".

And he was particularly critical of Labour's record on housing, where he accused the party of failing to take on the "powerful vested interests of developers and big landlords".

Instead, he urged the government to enact an "emergency brake" on private rents, under which they would be prevented from rising above the lowest of consumer price index measure of inflation, wage growth or 2%, for three years.

'Sustained pressure'

He argued that pressure from the Greens in the face of government "inaction" had forced Burnham into calling an emergency Cobr meeting this summer amid record-breaking hot and dry temperatures.

The Greens, he added would not "hesitate" to tax "extreme wealth", as he repeated the party's call for a so-called windfall tax on back profits - an issue where the government has faced pressure from unions.

"Through our sustained pressure – and our historic wins – we have held the worst instincts of the Labour government in check.

"And we have started to move them in the right direction. But we can't wait for them to get there on their own."

He also sought to draw a clear dividing line with the government on the issue of oil and gas, ahead of looming decisions for the government on whether to approve the Rosebank oil field and Jackdaw gas field.

Burnham has stuck to Labour's manifesto commitment not to issue new oil and gas licences, but has left open the possibility of approving the two sites.

This summer's wildfires, Polanski told the conference hall, should prove the "final nail in the coffin for new oil and gas".

Zionism motion

He began his address by celebrating his party's surge in membership since his election as party leader a year ago, and electoral successes including the hundreds of councillors it gained in May's local elections in England.

But his speech did not touch on an issue that could divide the membership over the weekend, ahead of a probable vote on a motion put forward by members that describes Zionism as a form of racism.

The motion defines Zionism as an ideology in support of "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and seeks to shift the party's position to supporting a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".

The current form of the motion has drawn criticism from senior figures, including deputy leader Rachel Millward, who earlier described it as "problematic".

Former leader Caroline Lucas told the BBC: "I think there is no single definition of Zionism and, irrespective of the intentions of those who put that motion, I think there is a real risk that it will be divisive and could be seen as a sign that Jewish people aren't welcome in the party."

It has also attracted criticism from some Jewish groups including the Board of Deputies and the Jewish Leadership Council.

Green MP Sian Berry would not confirm how she planned to vote on the motion but said she could "absolutely see and feel how strongly many members feel we should be saying even more".

Under Green Party rules if the motion passes it would officially become party policy, but would not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto.

Polanski has said he wants to see the motion amended to specify that it should not be used to discipline Jewish members attending synagogues that consider themselves Zionist.

He is also supporting a change that would replace the call for a single Palestinian state with backing for a "lasting settlement granting equal rights for all" to be "shaped and determined by Palestinians themselves".

Asked by the BBC if he believed that Zionism is racism, Polanski said it would depend on how the term was defined.

"If your Zionism is the displacement of the Palestinian people then that is clearly racist, and I say that as a Jewish leader of a British political party."

Asked whether the conference motion was calling for the eradication of Israel, Polanski said: "That's why I'm calling for an amendment."

"I don't believe we as a Green Party of England and Wales or even the British government should be deciding what the future settlement looks like," he added.

When asked if he believed Israel had a right to exist, Polanski said: "I believe people have a right to exist."

Asked the same question again, he said: "Both Israelis have a right to exist and Palestinians have a right to exist."

Pushed for a third time on whether Israel had a right to exist, he said: "Our job as political parties is to defend the rights of people, not the rights of nations."

Polanski also said he wanted to focus on what the party could "materially do to make a difference" such as campaigning for the UK government to stop selling arms to Israel and sharing intelligence with the Israeli government.

title: Rivian三季度交付超预期，确认2026全年业绩指引
content:
核心要点
Rivian 周五公布第三季度交付量同比大涨 46%，超出华尔街预期，同时确认 2026 年全年汽车交付目标。
这家电动车企业 7‑9 月合计交付 19248 台车辆，去年同期为 13201 台。FactSet 汇总分析师平均预期为 18000 台。
Rivian 在今年早些时候上调全年交付指引，目标区间为 65000‑70000 台 。想要达成该目标，公司第四季度交付量需要较第三季度至少提升 20.5%，达到 23193 台。
交付量增长的背后，是入门级 SUV 车型 R2 产能持续爬坡。R2 于今年早些时候上市，定位低于旗舰 R1 SUV，尺寸更小、售价更低。

title: 特斯拉公布第三季度交付486532辆汽车，超出市场预期
content:
核心要点
消息公布后，埃隆・马斯克旗下这家电动车制造商的股价上涨约 2%。
关键数据
交付量同比去年的 497099 辆下滑约 2%，但相比第二季度的 480126 辆有所回升。
StreetAccount 统计分析师预期约 461100 辆；特斯拉周二自行发布的市场一致预期为 461974 辆。
特斯拉并未披露各车型、各地区的精确交付数字，但表示入门级 Model 3 轿车与销量最高的 Model Y SUV 占总交付量的绝大多数，比例达到 98%。
交付量是特斯拉对外披露中最接近 “销量” 的指标，但在面向股东的公告文件里，“交付量” 并没有严格的统一定义。
这家马斯克执掌的车企正面临激烈竞争，来自比亚迪、 小米 等中国电动车厂商的产品价格更低、创新亮点颇多。特斯拉正试图扭转连续两年汽车销量下滑的局面。销量下滑部分源于消费者对马斯克的负面情绪，同时美国联邦电动车税收抵免政策到期也带来冲击。
拜登总统 2022 年签署的《通胀削减法案》原本将电动车税收优惠延续至 2032 年。而特朗普政府的支出法案提前终止该政策，补贴已于 2025 年 9 月 30 日到期。
截至周四收盘，特斯拉年内股价下跌 21%，跑输全部大型科技股同业。
摩根士丹利 分析师在周三研报中表示，特斯拉三季度交付量对比去年同期和上一季度，“基数对比压力较大”。去年第三季度是特斯拉的 “交付创纪录季度”；而今年二季度， 交付量比产量高出约 2.8 万辆 。
特斯拉周五同时公布，本季度储能产品（含 Megapack、Megablock 储能系统）部署量 13.7 吉瓦时；去年同期为 12.5 吉瓦时，今年二季度为 13.5 吉瓦时。
Megapack 面向工商业与公用事业储能项目；新款 Megablock 由四套 Megapack 搭配一台变压器组合而成。这套储能系统使用锂离子等电池，帮助数据中心与公用事业企业规避停电风险，储存太阳能、风能等可再生能源电力。
马斯克旗下太空探索技术公司 SpaceX 是特斯拉备用储能电池的大采购方，也采购了价值数百万美元的赛博皮卡。
国际能源署《2026 全球电动汽车展望》报告显示，尽管特斯拉交付量出现同比回落，但全球电动车需求今年整体走高。国际能源署认为，伊朗冲突推高油价，进一步凸显电动车在保障能源安全、降低燃油开支方面的价值，刺激市场需求。
2020 年，电动车与混动车型仅占全球新车销量的 5% 不到；2025 年，全球每四台新车就有一台是新能源车。
特斯拉将于 10 月 21 日盘后发布第三季度财报。

title: 特朗普经济顾问哈塞特：鲍威尔的未来由他自己决定 而非白宫
content: 当被问及白宫是否应该在决定杰罗姆·鲍威尔是否继续担任美联储理事一事上发挥作用时，白宫国家经济委员会主任凯文·哈塞特表示：“不。目前这是鲍威尔要作出的决定。”

title: 美国8月工厂订单环比增长0.1% 预期增长0.2%
content:
美国普查局数据显示，8月份工厂订单环比增长0.1%，预估中值为增长0.2%。
35位经济学家的预测区间为下降0.2%至增长0.7%。
7月份工厂订单增幅从0.9%下修至0.8%。
8月份扣除运输设备的工厂订单增长0.3%，7月份为增长0.7%。
8月份耐用品订单下降0.1%，初值为持平；扣除运输设备后增长0.2%，初值为增长0.3%。
扣除飞机的非国防资本品新订单增长1.6%，与初值一致；出货量增长0.5%，初值为增长0.6%。

title: 特朗普称欧洲将释放“庞大规模的”柴油
content:
在美国政府施压欧洲、要求其帮助在11月中期选举前缓解高油价后，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，欧洲已同意释放柴油供应。
特朗普周五在社交媒体发文称：“欧洲刚刚同意释放庞大规模的储备柴油。释放过程将立即开始。”他没有提供更多细节。
这一决定降低了特朗普政府为压低柴油价格而实施美国柴油出口禁令的可能性。在柴油价格近期触及纪录高位的背景下，出口禁令可能导致全球供应紧张，并给欧洲和拉丁美洲带来重大经济影响。

title: 美联储传声筒：就业数据好坏参半，美联储后续政策仍要看通胀
content:
美联储传声筒Nick Timiraos发文称，9月就业报告几乎不会促使美联储官员改变其对经济的核心判断，同时也扫清了本月维持利率不变的一大潜在阻碍。
这份报告几乎没有释放出劳动力市场再度收紧、进而加剧物价压力的信号，这是其中最为关键的变化。美联储高层官员本周释放信号：自上月加息之后，他们希望留出更多时间评估通胀的演变态势，而周五出炉的就业报告，给了他们观望等待的空间。
9月招聘步伐放缓，数据修正结果显示，夏季的就业增长略低于此前公布水平。失业率从4.1%升至4.2%，但该涨幅实际没有看上去那么明显：未经四舍五入的原始数据显示，失业率仅从4.14%微升至4.18%。
相较于月度非农新增岗位，美联储官员更为关注失业率。倘若失业率出现显著下行，就意味着劳动力成本上行压力升温，这将令凯文・沃什主席及其同僚在本月是否再度加息的抉择变得更加棘手。而周五的就业报告并未传递出这类信号。
将于10月14日公布的9月消费者物价指数，或将对后续加息时点以及本轮紧缩周期的终点产生更大影响。

title: 七国集团将释放多达1亿桶柴油和石油
content:
在特朗普政府施压要求遏制燃料价格上涨后，七国集团将释放多达1亿桶紧急石油和柴油储备。
法国总统马克龙周五在记者会上表示，此次释放将由国际能源署协调，并将在未来四个月内进行。马克龙目前也是七国集团轮值主席。
他说，七国集团希望借此推动燃料价格下跌。

title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference
content:
When Kemi Badenoch arrived for her first Conservative conference as leader last year, a member of her entourage overheard somebody wonder aloud: "Who's that?"

This baffled member of the public was actually working at the Conservative conference. Badenoch had been the party's leader and the leader of the opposition for almost a year.

It is an anecdote which underlines the scale of the challenge Badenoch faced at that conference, an event her allies are now with distance willing to acknowledge was make or break for her leadership.

And it is an anecdote which also underlines that, far from break her, that conference represented the start of a major turnaround for Badenoch.

Twelve months on, Badenoch will arrive in Birmingham this weekend in total command of a party whose leading lights are beginning to permit themselves the occasional flicker of optimism after years of misery preparing for, and then experiencing, a brutal election defeat.

Yet for all that Conservatives now believe their leader is an electoral asset, they still face an existential threat from Reform UK and the challenge of how to adjust their strategy to face a new prime minister, Andy Burnham.

The answer to both those issues for Badenoch is a focus on the economy. "Stronger economy, stronger country" will be the party's conference slogan, with the two speeches Badenoch gives - one on Sunday, the other on Wednesday - building on announcements she has made in the past two weeks about cutting benefits for the long-term unemployed.

'Traditional left-right split'

Welfare spending is increasingly seen by the Conservatives as a core battleground with Labour.

During Labour conference they derided the event as the "Welfare Party Conference". Whereas Sir Keir Starmer sought to cut welfare spending before backing down in the face of a rebellion by his own MPs, Burnham has made clear that he believes the way to reduce the benefits bill in the long-term is more up-front investment in support for those out of work.

This is a clear ideological difference which both parties are happy to embrace. Conservative strategists believe there is a broader lesson there.

"The differences between the parties have been quite muddled for a while," one says. "Now that Burnham is prime minister we have a more traditional left-right split."

Another area where Badenoch will embrace that divide in the coming days is the pensions triple-lock.

The policy currently guarantees the state pension goes up each year in line with either inflation, wage increases, or 2.5% – whichever is the highest.

Badenoch will make clear that the Conservatives continue to support that policy in its current form, breaking with some generally supportive think tanks and policy experts who believe Badenoch should follow Burnham's lead.

In his conference speech on Tuesday, Burnham set out plans to end the existing triple lock from 2030, so the state pension increases at least by inflation or 2.5% - but remove the automatic annual link with average earnings.

The Conservatives hope the sharpening left-right split leaves Reform UK in a strategic bind, occupying a less obvious place on that spectrum.

A year ago some senior Conservatives feared being usurped by Reform as the leading party of the right was a near-inevitability, but now they are optimistic that Nigel Farage's party is on an inexorable slide.

That bullishness is fuelled in large part by the difficulties Reform has faced over Nigel Farage's £5m gift from Christopher Harborne and the fallout - including a police inquiry - from the recent Channel 4 News investigation.

"I find more and more voters raise concerns about Reform with me - people who weren't previously giving us the time of day," one MP said.

"These are successful people with big garages and good jobs who do not necessarily pay that much attention but want a small-c conservative government.

"They were switching to Reform because they were fed up with us and thought Farage was now the main option on the right. But they are starting to come back."

Others are less positive, pointing out that Reform still often record higher shares than the Conservatives in the polls — and more importantly have now won far more votes than them in successive years of local and national elections.

Whether or not there is indeed a long-term trend of the Conservatives regaining ground at Reform's expense, Badenoch may not have long enough to wait.

She has told her team to prepare for this conference as if it is the last before the general election. While not all of her aides agree, Badenoch is convinced that Burnham will go to the polls within the next year.

Party high command started weekly election planning meetings shortly after Burnham succeeded Starmer.

Neil O'Brien, a member of Badenoch's shadow cabinet, has begun work on a manifesto alongside the party's head of policy. It is intended to be a more concise set of pledges than the usual sprawling manifestos.

Also with an eye to the election, the Conservatives will present new faces at the conference who have applied to be candidates at the next election.

Badenoch's ambivalence in some cases, and opposition in others, to ex-MPs who lost their seats in 2024 standing for the party again has attracted some controversy, especially when it comes to the high-profile former cabinet ministers Grant Shapps and Penny Mordaunt.

The leader's supporters are unrepentant, arguing that the party "needs to show we have changed".

Things have certainly changed since last year, at least. That may prove the easy part.

title: I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's
content:
Reporter Michael Graczyk has covered nearly 500 executions carried out in Texas, continuing even after his 2018 retirement from The Associated Press.

He remembers two instances where needles popped out before reinsertion for successful execution - but never one in which an inmate survived.

That's what happened this week in Tennessee, when 50-year-old inmate Christa Pike remained breathing and audibly snoring after two separate doses of pentobarbital, the barbiturate used in the state's lethal injection protocol.

Graczyk, 76, says he wasn't entirely surprised to hear of the anomaly - and had actually thought about the possibility during his decades-long career as a Texas journalist.

"It seems to me it was just a matter of time," he told BBC News.

Tennessee's execution protocol calls for a secondary set of pentobarbital-filled syringes in case the person being put to death does not die after the first set, according to AP, but does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set.

Governor Bill Lee halted executions in the state after Wednesday night's failure, ordering an independent review into procedures. Botched executions have come under scrutiny over the past decade, since a shortage of the drugs used led some states to change the formula, or procure drugs from more questionable sources. Some states even brought back death by firing squad as an alternative.

The secret hunt for lethal drugs used in US executions

Pike is now in hospital where she is receiving "life-saving care", according to her lawyer.

It's not uncommon for lethal injections - the most frequently used form of capital punishment in the 27 US states where the penalty is legal - to be "botched". The Death Penalty Information Center, a think-tank that does not take a stance on the death penalty, describes a botched execution as one with "unanticipated problems or delays that caused, at least arguably, unnecessary agony for the prisoner or that reflect gross incompetence of the executioner". The organisation has compiled a list of 64 botched executions since 1982, 51 of them lethal injections. In at least seven of those cases, the executions were halted because the IV line could not be set.

But Graczyk has never seen an execution fail after the injection was delivered.

"That has never happened here," Graczyk said of the Lone Star State.

Graczyk, who covered a wide range of topics for the AP during his 46 years with the news service, considers his prolific attendance at executions to be an important part of the job.

"There is no [greater] authority, power, or whatever you want to call it, that state or federal government has over us than the power to take our life," he said.

There have been 1,683 executions in the US since 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre, which is when the US Supreme Court re-instated the death penalty. Texas has carried out by far the most of any state, with 602 executions. In 1982, it became the first state to use lethal injections to execute people.

Why the death penalty is on the rise in US

"I always thought it was important for someone who has no stake in the outcome of a case to be there and to see the law being carried out and to make certain that it is done properly," Graczyk said.

"That someone is there to see it and tell others: Here's what I saw. Here's what happened."

Although he is technically retired, he still works freelance for AP covering executions in his home state.

He feels a particular responsibility to remember victims in his coverage and it's especially disheartening when he writes a story about an execution that doesn't make big news.

"I feel bad for the victims in the case," he said. "They are the forgotten folks. They always have been."

"Today, all the emphasis is on the inmate in Tennessee," he said. "No tears are being shed, other than the victim's immediate family, for the victim … and I understand that's the business we're in, but it doesn't mean it's right."

Pike's victim was Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old originally from Florida who loved to roller skate, smile and help others, according to descriptions given by her friends and family. Slemmer was tortured and killed by Pike, then 18, and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, after they met her at a job training camp.

Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, was present in Tennessee on Wednesday for the execution attempt, telling NBC News afterwards that it "was a mess".

Texas, where Graczyk lives and works, does not allow observers in the execution chamber when the IV is being inserted, he said.

"So when we get into the chamber, the inmate's already hooked up."

In a lethal injection execution, the IV would typically be inserted in the crook of the person's arm, Graczyk said. But if that didn't work, sometimes it would go into the top of their hand, their leg, neck or other sites.

During successful executions, Graczyk said inmates become "visibly unconscious after just a few seconds". They are usually pronounced dead 20 to 40 minutes after the fatal dose is given, he said.

He still remembers the death of Jonathan Nobles, who was executed by lethal injection in Texas in 1998. He'd been handed the sentence after his conviction for the brutal 1986 stabbing murders of two Austin women, Kelley Fraquhar and Mitzi Johnson-Nalley.

Nobles sang "Silent Night" as his last words.

"He gets to 'Round yon virgin' and he stops talking," Graczyk told BBC News. "That's how long it took for the drug to kick in so he wasn't conscious anymore."

That scene has stuck with Graczyk for nearly 30 years.

"To this day, when I'm in church on Christmas, and the choir is singing Silent Night, and all the congregation is joining in Silent Night and they're all, you know, in the spirit of the season and the joy of the season, and I'm thinking of this execution, I'm sure I'm the only one in that congregation that is having that kind of recollection."

When people hear about his career covering executions, he said, they are usually curious.

"Most people don't get to watch someone die," he said.

But when people ask him about what he has witnessed, he tells them "it's not the only thing I did or do or have done".

title: Dolly Parton sings Jolene in Welsh in recording released after her death
content:
A new version of Dolly Parton's Jolene is set to be released, with parts of the song sung in Welsh by the legendary country artist.

The song was recorded before her death on 25 August, and is a collaboration with Welsh singer-songwriter Bronwen Lewis as well as Parton's niece, Jada Star.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote more than 3,000 songs.

The single will come out on 9 October, and is the second posthumous release from Parton - who was of Welsh descent.

In a teaser video released on social media, Star and Lewis explained how the song came to light.

As a proud Welsh speaker, Lewis, from Neath, had started translating some of her favourite tunes, and soon landed on the Parton classic, Jolene.

"Two years ago I posted a video of me singing the Dolly Parton classic Jolene in Welsh, external," said Lewis.

"I never expected it would go viral and definitely didn't expect it to attract the attention of Dolly's family - especially her niece Jada."

A friendship was born, and Star came over from Nashville in the US to Wales to meet Lewis, joining her at Pride Cymru.

"Pride Cymru was such an amazing experience and I learned so much about my family lineage," said Star.

"I cherish the time I spent with Bronwen exploring one of the most beautiful places I have ever seen."

The teaser revealed it was Star's suggestion to record Jolene in Welsh, which Lewis "jumped" at the chance to do, with Star then saying she would get her aunt involved too.

"Jada told me that her Aunt Dolly would like to sing with us on our version of Jolene. I think I fell to the ground," said Lewis.

"Definitely cried happy tears, and called my mother immediately."

BBC Radio Wales presenter Lewis said she had always loved Parton's music.

"To hear Dolly sing in another language, and in Welsh for the very first time, was unbelievable."

After understanding the phonetics of Lewis' translation, Parton recorded her parts at her studio in Nashville, in early 2025.

Lewis had planned to go over to meet her to release the music, but Parton passed away before the meet-up could happen.

"It was devastating, not just for myself and our family, but for the entire world," Star said.

Lewis said the pair realised what a privilege it was to have recorded and collaborated "with one of the greatest musicians and women to grace this Earth".

"We did what she always told us to do. We got ourselves together and decided to finish what we started," Star added.

Star and Lewis said Parton was "proud" to sing in Welsh.

This is not the first time Parton has featured on songs in another language.

She has appeared on several Latin songs and also collaborated on a track with an Irish folk band in 2011.

Before her death, Parton revealed she had recorded a song with U2 which is set to be released in November. She also teased fans about a track which has been kept in a time capsule until its planned release in 2046.

In 2008, during a concert at the Cardiff International Arena, Parton reportedly revealed her Welsh ancestry to fans in the crowd.

"Some of my mother's people, the Owens, are from there [Wales]," Parton later told Wales Online.

"I've been there about three times and it always feels good because it feels like family."

Star had also previously spoken about the family's Welsh connection.

She said the Owens side of the family, coming from Parton's mother Avie Lee Owens, was believed to have come from Conwy.

Speaking to BBC Radio Wales in 2024, Star said discovering that part of the family's history had been "really extraordinary".

Star suggested some of Parton's music, and her own, may have been inspired by her Welsh roots.

Parton's death brought renewed attention in Wales to the country music legend's Welsh links, with her heritage explored in a 2025 documentary.

Following the singer's death, research by staff at Conwy council's archives suggested Parton's ancestors were from Machynlleth, not Conwy as previously thought.

title: 特斯拉第三季度销量高于预期 显示汽车业务趋于稳定
content:
特斯拉 第三季度销量好于预期，显示在电动汽车市场面临挑战之际，该公司核心业务趋于稳定。
根据周五发布的声明，这家汽车制造商当季在全球交付486，532辆汽车。相比之下，分析师预期均值为463，761辆。
这一业绩对特斯拉而言是一大利好。此前，该公司经历了一段汽车销量下滑、股价表现落后的时期，面临竞争以及美国需求疲软也给其带来压力。首席执行官埃隆·马斯克正努力推动特斯拉转向人工智能、无人驾驶汽车和人形机器人等未来业务领域。
第三季度销量较去年同期有所下降。特斯拉去年第三季度交付497，099辆汽车，创下纪录，当时消费者赶在美国取消联邦激励措施之前争相购车。尽管如此，华尔街预计，在连续两年销量下降后，特斯拉今年将能够实现销量小幅增长。
特斯拉股价在周五早盘上涨超过4%。尽管该股今年以来下跌，但最近几周有所反弹，市场寄望于马斯克可能将特斯拉与其掌管的另一家大型公司、火箭制造商SpaceX合并。
这家汽车制造商正按计划在今年投入逾250亿美元，用于扩建工厂并建立无人驾驶出租车业务。该公司本周在一份申报文件中表示，已筹措300亿美元的新贷款 和信贷 额度，以支持增长。
特斯拉最近停产了价格较高的Model S和Model X，从而缩减了产品阵容。目前，该公司销售三款面向消费者的车型：广受欢迎的Model Y和Model 3，以及颇具争议的Cybertruck。
周五公布的结果再次证实，Model Y和Model 3占其绝大多数销量。除这两款车型外，该公司“其他车型”的交付量仅为8，295辆。
特斯拉还有更多车型即将推出，包括承诺已久的新版Roadster跑车。目前，该公司也已开始生产Cybercab，这是一款没有方向盘或踏板的无人驾驶出租车型，同时还在销售Semi电动重型卡车。

title: 美国9月非农仅增2.9万人远低于预期 市场下调10月加息预期
content:
美国9月仅新增2.9万个就业岗位，招聘环比大幅放缓。这一结果引发市场对劳动力市场韧性的质疑，交易机构随之下调对美联储加息的预期。
美国劳工统计局周五公布的数据，较8月下修后的13.3万新增岗位出现急剧回落，同时远低于彭博经济学家调查预期的8.8万人。
多个行业招聘降温。医疗行业作为近几个月就业增长的重要引擎，招聘大幅走弱；金融业就业规模持续收缩。
7月与8月非农就业合计下修6万岗位，7月修正为就业减少1万人。
9月失业率由8月的4.1%小幅上行至4.2%。
施罗德高级经济学家乔治·布朗表示，这份报告“弱于市场预期”，但他提醒：单月非农数据疲软，尚不足以让政策制定者认定劳动力市场正在持续恶化。
他补充道：“今年非农就业数据如同坐过山车，各月之间波动剧烈。”
上月美联储三年来首次加息，以对抗顽固 高通 胀。这份数据将激起一场讨论：劳动力市场是否还能承受进一步加息。
数据发布后美债收益率下行，交易商下调加息预期。期货市场不再完全定价年底前会完成一次完整加息。
跟随利率预期变动的两年期美债收益率下跌0.08个百分点，报4.71%。此前市场已完全定价2026年12月会加息，如今该概率回落至88%。
美联储主席凯文·沃什上月表态，美联储双重使命中的就业指标目前“状态良好”；即便通胀“长期居高不下”，美联储仍有空间加息25个基点。
近几周，市场押注美联储最早10月再度加息的赌注显著上升。但两位美联储高官——副主席菲利普·杰斐逊、纽约联储主席约翰· 威廉姆斯 本周释放信号：政策制定者可能需要更多时间研判数据，再采取下一步行动。

title: 就业报告数据疲软，交易员认为美联储10月加息概率已微乎其微
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
核心要点
受 9 月就业报告的影响，投资者目前认为美联储 10 月再度加息的可能性极低。
基于 30 天利率期货交易数据的 CME 美联储观察工具显示，美联储加息 25 个基点的概率仅为 17%；一周前该概率接近 36%。预测交易平台 Kalshi 的数据显示，10 月加息概率仅 18%，而一周前该概率将近 70%。
美国 9 月仅新增 2.9 万个就业岗位，低于 8 万以上的市场预期。此前美联储为对抗顽固的通胀已经实施加息。如今劳动力市场降温，或将促使美联储重新权衡其双重使命 —— 保障充分就业与稳定物价。
本周三公布的美联储偏好通胀指标显示物价降温，也推动 10 月加息概率在周中就出现下滑。8 月剔除食品与能源的核心物价同比上涨 3%，低于市场一致预期的 3.3%。
先锋集团高级经济学家亚当・希克林表示：“这份报告进一步支持美联储保持耐心。劳动力市场并未急剧恶化，但也没有明显走强的迹象，政策制定者有理由等待更多数据。”
尽管交易员认为 10 月加息基本无望，但市场依旧预测央行将在 12 月加息。 美联储观察工具显示 12 月加息概率高于 75%；Kalshi 平台给出的加息概率为 65%。
美联储为期两天的政策会议将于 10 月 28 日落幕，并公布下一次利率决议。

title: Tesla deliveries fall 2% as US consumers buy fewer electric vehicles
content:
Kana Inagaki in London and Stephen Morris in San Francisco

Published October 2 2026

Tesla’s deliveries fell less than expected in the third quarter, as a recovery in European sales helped offset softening demand for electric vehicles in the US.

The US carmaker delivered 486,532 vehicles in the three months to the end of September, above analysts’ forecasts of 461,974 but down 2 per cent from 497,099 in the same period last year. Shares in Tesla rose nearly 4 per cent on Friday.

Tesla’s US sales have been suffering after President Donald Trump ended a $7,500 tax credit for EV purchases and cancelled federal emissions trading schemes that had become an important source of income for the carmaker.

The carmaker’s sales hit a record in the third quarter of last year as US consumers rushed to buy EVs ahead of the expiry of the tax credits.

Tesla does not provide a regional breakdown of its deliveries but quarterly sales in the US were likely to have fallen 31 per cent year on year to 123,880 vehicles, according to estimates by Cox Automotive.

Other US carmakers also reported lower sales for the third quarter. Ford said US sales for the period fell 6.6 per cent year on year to 509,764 vehicles as it phased out its Escape and Corsair models. General Motors reported a 6 per cent decline in US sales to 670,974 units due to a “much smaller EV market”.

Rising fuel prices have helped lift demand for EVs elsewhere, with sales in Europe continuing to recover following a consumer backlash against Tesla chief executive Elon Musk’s political activism last year.

New registrations in the UK and the EU increased 43 per cent year on year to 191,787 vehicles during the first eight months of 2026, according to European car industry body Acea.

Still, Tesla has faced intense competition from BYD and other Chinese manufacturers that are rapidly making inroads into the UK and other European markets.

The EU has also delayed a long-awaited vote on allowing Tesla’s supervised “Full Self-Driving” software across the bloc, from October to December at the earliest, though it is already allowed in certain member states.

Despite its name, FSD still requires humans to sit in the driver’s seat and pay full attention — unlike Google’s Waymo taxis. Musk has repeatedly promised that Tesla’s FSD software will be approved for fully autonomous driving soon, but it has yet to gain regulatory approval in any countries.

In a filing this week, Tesla said it had secured $30bn of new credit lines as Musk prepares to pivot the group from EV manufacturing to focus on autonomous driving, robotics and AI. In April, the company raised its guidance for annual capital expenditure from $20bn to $25bn.

In January, Musk discontinued Tesla’s premium S and SUV X models as the group shifted to the development of the Cybercab, a golden self-driving taxi, and a humanoid robot called Optimus. Both experimental products have started production, but are yet to generate any income through sales.

title: 以总理：将对迪拜航空航班遇袭事件幕后主使进行报复
content:
当地时间10月2日，以色列总理内塔尼亚胡就迪拜航空航班遇袭事件发表声明称，这是一起险些出现的重大恐怖袭击，并表示将对潜在的幕后主使进行报复。
内塔尼亚胡称：“我们目前正在调查他是否是受人指使。无论幕后黑手是谁，都将付出极其沉重的代价。”
9月30日，载有以色列乘客的迪拜航空FZ1073航班从阿联酋迪拜飞往以色列特拉维夫途中发生安全事件。据沙特内政部声明，该航班载有174名乘客和8名机组人员，在飞行途中宣布进入紧急状态，沙特有关部门批准其在位于该国西北部的塔布克机场紧急降落。该航班于9月30日9时45分安全着陆。当天17时40分，所有乘客搭乘迪拜航空调派的替代飞机继续行程，机长和副驾驶以外的机组人员搭乘该航司另一架飞机返回迪拜。
据阿联酋方面消息，该航班副驾驶涉嫌在驾驶舱内持刀刺伤机长，导致飞机突然急降。其他机组人员和乘客制服袭击者后，机组重新控制飞机。

title: 美国上月仅新增2.9万个就业岗位，失业率小幅升至4.2%
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
美国劳工统计局周五发布的最新数据显示，9 月就业增长不及预期，美国经济仅新增 2.9 万个岗位，失业率升至 4.2%。
9 月就业增速较 8 月有所放缓，8 月新增就业数据已被下修至 13.3 万人。不过经济学家提醒，8 月那份看似亮眼的就业数据，可能受到部分季节性因素影响，夸大了实际招聘规模。
市场此前预期 9 月新增就业约 9 万人，失业率维持在 4.1%。
近几个月就业增长持续不及预期，7 月与 8 月就业估算值合计被向下修正 6 万个。修正后，8 月新增就业 13.3 万人（初值 16.2 万）；7 月数据转负，就业减少 1 万人（初值为新增 2.1 万人）。
劳工统计局数据显示，截至 9 月，美国经济月均新增就业 6.8 万个。相比去年，就业增量有所回升 —— 去年是有记录以来就业表现最弱的年份之一，月均新增不足 1 万人。但当前招聘节奏仍远低于疫情前月均 12 万的水平。
尽管面临多重压制招聘的不利因素，包括人口老龄化、人工智能快速普及、油价走高、政策不确定性以及伊朗冲突，就业市场大体上依旧扛住了压力。

title: US jobs market sees sharp slowdown ahead of midterm elections
content:
The US jobs market saw a sharp slowdown in September, with employers adding just 29,000 jobs in the final update before the midterm elections.

Headcounts were little changed in major sectors from tech to retail as hiring fell significantly from August, according to figures from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

Meanwhile, the unemployment rate rose slightly from 4.1% in August to 4.2% in September.

The figures signal a cooling US economy, which experts said reduced the likelihood of a series of further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

The 29,000 jobs created in September was down from a figure of 133,000 in August, according to revised BLS figures for the month.

But George Brown, senior economist at Schroders, said while job gains have been a “rollercoaster“ this year, a single soft report is unlikely to point to a lasting collapse.

And Bradley Saunders, North America economist at Capital Economics, said the lower figure was “not disastrous“, adding that a drop in government roles and temporary visa policy changes weighed on overall growth.

Jeffery Roach, chief economist at LPL Financial, added that the data showed tension between “goods producing sectors that support the AI boom” and service industries feeling the effect of changes brought about by the tech.

“Given the overall softness of the labour market, the likelihood of two Fed hikes is going lower,” he said.

The BLS report stands in sharp contrast to President Donald Trump's insistence that America's economy is booming and it is the "hottest" nation in the world.

The disconnect is likely to present significant challenges as the president and his fellow Republicans hit the the campaign trail with just a month to go before the midterm congressional elections.

According to an AP/NORC poll released on Thursday, just 17% of Americans approve of the president's handling of cost-of-living issues, while 26% approve of his handling of the economy overall.

Both are new lows for Trump, surpassing the lowest mark for Democrat Joe Biden during his presidential term.

There have been some indications that the president understands that his views of the American economy are out of step with those of most Americans.

"I've done a very bad job of explaining how good the country is doing," he said at a White House event earlier this week.

title: 美国9月非农就业大幅低于预期，美债收益率下行，美股期货上涨
content:
来源：华尔街见闻
美国劳动力市场意外降温，令美债收益率下行、股票期货走高，并进一步削弱了市场对美联储10月加息的预期。
美国劳工部周五公布数据显示，9月非农就业人数仅增加2.9万，远低于市场预期的9万，且低于所有预测区间下限。失业率从8月的4.1%小幅升至4.2%。受此数据影响，美国国债收益率全线下行，美股期货走强，利率市场对美联储10月加息的定价大幅回落。
利率互换市场显示，数据公布后交易员对美联储10月会议加息的概率预期从此前的29%降至17%，年内剩余两次会议的累计加息溢价降至约21个基点。两年期美国国债收益率单日下行约10个基点，触及4.69%。标普500指数期货上涨0.8%，纳斯达克100指数期货涨幅达1.1%。
日历效应或是主因，就业市场未见实质性恶化
经济学家普遍认为，9月就业数据的异常疲软很可能主要源于季节性调整因素失真，而非劳动力市场的实质性转向。
今年劳动节假期落在月末，据报道，这一情形历史上往往导致非农就业数据偏低。与此同时，政府采用的季节性调整模型被认为既压低了9月的就业增量，也导致8月数据遭下调至13.3万——低于此前公布的16.2万。9月就业预测值的分布区间为3.5万至18万，离散度本身也反映出分析师对数据扰动的预判。
当前就业市场的基本面仍具韧性。首次申请失业救济人数持续徘徊在57年来的低点，企业利润稳健，国内需求表现强劲，尚无大规模裁员迹象。
就业结构分化，部分行业仍在扩张
从行业构成看，9月就业的疲软主要由政府部门、信息业、专业和商业服务业以及金融活动等领域的就业减少所拖累。
与此同时，医疗保健、建筑和制造业仍实现了就业净增长，显示部分实体经济领域的用工需求依然稳定。
据报道，失业率上升至4.2%，部分原因在于劳动力队伍的自然扩张。退休潮持续以及特朗普政府对移民的严格管控压缩了劳动力供给，客观上对失业率形成了一定支撑。经济学家估计，当前经济每月需新增5万至8万个就业岗位，才能跟上劳动年龄人口增长的步伐。
战争、能源价格与关税构成后续隐患
尽管当前劳动力市场整体稳健，经济学家对未来数季度的前景仍持审慎态度。
据报道，美国与以色列对伊朗的战争带来的能源价格上涨和供应链紧张，预计将在今年年底至2027年期间开始对就业市场形成实质性冲击。柴油价格已创历史新高，潜在的传导压力正逐步向交通运输和农业以外的行业扩散。
此外，持续的关税摩擦亦令企业感到忧虑。供应管理协会（ISM）周四公布的调查显示，制造商对与加拿大贸易争端的担忧情绪持续升温，这可能进一步抑制企业的扩产和招聘意愿。
通胀数据走软叠加就业降温，加息预期再度承压
就业数据公布前，美联储于上月将基准隔夜利率上调25个基点至3.75%至4.00%区间，为三年来首次加息，并释放了进一步收紧的信号。
然而，7月和8月通胀数据相继低于预期，已令10月再度加息的概率有所回落。芝商所FedWatch工具显示，就业报告发布前，市场对美联储10月27日至28日会议加息的定价约为22%，较一周前的约69%大幅下降。9月就业数据公布后，这一概率进一步降至17%左右，市场对年内完成一次加息的预期也已不再完全定价。

title: 交易员加大押注：美联储将维持利率不变
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
芝商所（CMEGroup）数据显示，期货交易员目前认为，美联储在10月下旬议息会议上维持现有利率水平的概率为86%。而在美国劳动力市场数据不及预期公布前，该概率为72%。
CME数据显示，市场押注12月加息25个基点的概率小幅升至64%，数据公布前为61%；交易员认为美联储12月维持利率不变的概率为25%，高于数据出炉前的19%。

title: 美国9月就业增长降温，失业率小幅走高
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
美国 9 月雇主新增 2.9 万个岗位，失业率升至 4.2%。通胀持续给市场带来压力，推高各项成本。
美国联邦政府周五公布数据显示，上月雇主仅新增 2.9 万个工作岗位，失业率升至 4.2%。近几个月劳动力市场原本展现出出人意料的韧性，但本次就业增速不及预期。
自伊朗冲突爆发以来，通胀不断走高，强劲的就业表现与物价上行带来的压力形成矛盾。对绝大多数劳动者而言，工资涨幅没能跑赢物价。9 月平均时薪增长乏力，同比仅为 3%，显著低于当前通胀水平。
近些年，美国企业与劳动者接连遭遇多重冲击：先是新冠疫情，随后是通胀，再到各类战争与关税进一步推高物价。受中东能源供给瓶颈影响，柴油价格创下历史新高，货运与供应链承压。
尽管波动不断，但美国整体经济并未陷入失速。劳动力市场依旧具备韧性，不过求职者与应届毕业生的就业处境面临挑战。背后一大原因在于劳动力供给发生变化：招聘节奏放缓的同时，婴儿潮一代大规模退休，叠加特朗普政府实施移民限制，进入劳动力市场的新增人口有所减少。
其他关键要点： 中年群体劳动参与率维持高位，说明市场对劳动力仍有需求，支撑就业率保持在较高水平。自 2021 年 10 月以来，失业率一直维持在 4.5% 及以下，创下现代历史上最长的一段时期。
人工智能的影响：目前很难精准统计由人工智能造成的岗位流失。但 9 月，受 AI 冲击风险最高的多个行业出现岗位缩减：信息行业减少 1 万个岗位，金融业减少 7000 个岗位，专业及商业服务业就业人数下降 9000 人。
过去数年，就业增长高度集中在部分行业，其余行业增长停滞甚至岗位流失。9 月，医疗与建筑业成为就业增量的主要来源。还有一个小幅亮点：此前整体呈下行趋势的制造业新增 9000 个岗位；自 2025 年 12 月至今，制造业累计新增岗位已达 7.2 万个。

title: 美国9月新增2.9万个就业岗位，劳动力市场降温
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
失业率小幅升至 4.2%
美国经济 9 月新增就业岗位 2.9 万个，不及市场预期。通胀高企、移民政策收紧等因素正在给劳动力市场部分领域带来压力。
美国劳工部周五发布报告显示，失业率小幅升至 4.2%。
此前预测认为 9 月新增就业约 8.4 万个。对比新冠疫情过后就业市场的火热行情，当下劳动力市场整体平稳，但增长乏力。近几个月就业数据起伏不定，一些突发事件（例如海地籍劳工失去受保护身份而大规模失业）扰动非农就业数据。
求职平台 ZipRecruiter 劳动力经济学家妮可・巴绍表示：“今年劳动力市场大概率会出现更多波动。影响劳动者流动和企业招聘预期的因素纷繁复杂，而且这些因素的变化速度极快。”
薪资增速放缓成为一个日益凸显的隐忧。9 月平均时薪达到 37.81 美元，同比上涨 3%，该增速跑输通胀。数月以来物价持续上涨，很大程度源于特朗普政府对伊朗开战推高汽油价格。
医疗、建筑以及制造业实现岗位增长；其余多数行业岗位几乎零增长甚至出现岗位流失，白领行业也未能幸免。
这份数据反映出当下劳动力市场的特征：裁员不多，但新增岗位供给不足。这对大学毕业生冲击尤为明显 —— 企业正在采用人工智能处理入门级工作任务，而毕业生正涌入就业市场。
除人工智能发展之外，多重因素交织给劳动力市场带来不确定性：伊朗冲突推高油价、特朗普推动加征关祱、收紧移民政策。这些经济压力也让消费前景变得难以预判。作为美国经济主要驱动力的消费者，面对生活必需品价格飙升，对经济的感受愈发糟糕。
目前居民消费依旧保持韧性，但经济学家表示， 价签冲击（sticker shock） 中国日报网．．．最终会迫使消费者缩减开支。此外，薪资增长疲软的态势预计将在今年延续，进一步加重家庭财务负担。
巴绍称：“薪资增速大概率会持续走弱。在职员工不愿跳槽，保住现有岗位已经成为劳动者的首要选择。因此企业缺乏涨薪压力。中低收入家庭面临的支付压力会进一步加剧。”
为对抗 高通 胀，美联储已于 9 月加息，预计今秋至冬季劳动力市场会进一步降温。倘若继续加息，2027 年就业市场增长将继续承压。
咨询机构毕马威首席经济学家黛安・斯旺克在本周的经济研报中写道：“ 货币政策存在时滞效应 澎湃新闻。通往物价稳定的道路布满坎坷；步入 2027 年，招聘就业是需要重点观察的核心领域。”

title: Obama’s red herring
content:
Edward Luce

Published October 2 2026

This article is an on-site version of our Swamp Notes newsletter. Premium subscribers can sign up here to get the newsletter delivered every Monday and Friday. Standard subscribers can upgrade to Premium here , or explore all FT newsletters

I am not among those who think Barack Obama should take on Donald Trump. Some have urged all the former presidents, including George W Bush, Bill Clinton, Joe Biden and Obama, to link arms and denounce Trump. What would happen then? My bet is that such a coming together would play straight into the hands of a president who claims he is the scourge of the establishment “uniparty”. Having spent their capital to no effect, or worse, the ex-presidents might find their accounts are empty. The same would apply to Obama. Though he has higher approval ratings (60 per cent plus) than anyone else in US politics, retired or active, that would buy little in today’s polarised arena. But he can have a real impact on the Democratic Party’s direction.

He could, of course, make the wrong kind of effect. At a recent event in New Hampshire, Obama said that Democrats should focus less on the “mechanical and instrumental and materialist” questions (chiefly economic) to tell a larger narrative about what brings Americans together. “What people are starved for at the moment is an ability to tell a moral, an ethical, story about how we live together,” Obama said. “All that stuff [the economy, inequality, power, AI] is important but there is an underlying moral foundation about how we see each other, that so often came out of a church, or a temple or a mosque . . . our leaders have to be able to speak that language in a serious way.”

It is hard to think of worse advice. Politicians should not aspire to be religious or spiritual leaders, though it is easy to see why Obama might think so. He shot to national prominence in 2004 with his Democratic convention speech saying there was no red state America, or blue state America, but the United States of America. He presented himself as a healer who delivered hope. Some might say that strategy worked. Having travelled with his 2008 campaign, I think there were other factors involved in his historic victory. He beat Hillary Clinton to the nomination on the strength of his opposition to the Iraq war and his superior ground game in states that hold caucuses. He defeated John McCain in the general election partly on the back of the Lehman Brothers-induced financial meltdown. Through both, he was a brilliant campaigner who packaged his story and biracial background to fit the larger moment.

We are living in a very different moment today. Moreover, Obama’s diagnosis does not really fit the facts. Far from focusing on the economy and other supposedly mechanical issues in the 2024 presidential election, Kamala Harris made her campaign about democracy. She made a larger bet on an ethical narrative that was repudiated. Her economic message was incrementalist and jumbled. Obama would have done it far better and might even have won. But when it boiled down to a choice, people voted for Trump because they thought he would put more money in their pockets. As Nancy Pelosi keeps reminding people, “democracy is saved at the kitchen table”. Obama’s second error is to presume he can be reproduced. He did tell a larger story about America. Reasonable people can disagree about how critical it was to his success. But both he and his moment were unique.

There is no doubt that Obama can move the needle. He helped persuade Joe Biden to drop his re-election campaign in 2024 after that disastrous debate. How people wish Obama had intervened sooner, though it might not have worked given Biden’s stubbornness. Likewise, Obama was probably decisive in persuading California’s voters last year to pass Proposition 50. That measure enabled Gavin Newsom, California’s governor, to gerrymander five extra Democratic seats in the state in retaliation for Trump asking Texas to do the same. The fruits of that could be critical in next month’s midterm elections. These are the kinds of practical interventions that can have a decisive effect. Talking about the arc of history bending towards justice once sounded good. Nowadays it sounds like pie in the sky.

I am turning this week to my colleague, Brooke Masters, the FT’s US managing editor based in New York. Brooke, it is easy for Washingtonians such as me to miss what people are thinking outside the Beltway bubble. Am I underestimating Obama’s national influence? He recently appeared with your mayor, Zohran Mamdani, a figure he clearly admires. Indeed, Mamdani’s ability to speak to the young and across some fairly improbable divides reminds me of the younger Obama. But their politics, and economics, are very different. From what you have seen of Mamdani, could he be the one who changes Democratic politics?

My column this week argues that the upcoming likely Republican midterm defeat will generate ripples, not earthquakes. “Loss of control of Congress — the switch to divided government — used to mean that the president’s room for manoeuvre would be roughly halved,” I write. “For the most part, however, Congress has been largely irrelevant in the last 20 months.”

I was both riveted and unnerved by this probing Ezra Klein interview with Bill Gates in the New York Times. Gates is a life-long techno-optimist. The vast risks of AI seem to have changed his mind.

Talking of AI, three cheers to Dan Drezner, dean of Tufts’ Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy, and author of a great Substack, who comes out swinging in defence of writing as an activity essential to thinking. I’m also with Joan Didion, who said, “I write to find out what I’m thinking”.

Hi Ed. I think you are being very clear-eyed about the limits of what Obama can accomplish in this election. His soaring oratory about unity resonated in 2008 in part because the economic situation seemed so dire. Today, voters feel financially squeezed and they are worried about the long-term problems posed by AI, but they aren’t nearly as scared.

Where I do think he can make a difference is on turnout.

The latest FT election poll shows Trump’s approval rating has fallen to the lowest level yet, but national disaffection does not guarantee a blue wave. I talked this week to canvassers in one bellwether congressional district, the 17th in the northern suburbs of New York City. It generally votes Democratic but elected a Republican to Congress in 2024. The door-knockers found potential voters are generally split and not particularly excited to turn out.

That tracks with history. Fewer than half of eligible voters usually vote in midterm elections, and the share has fallen as low as 36 per cent (in 2014). Given the efforts by the Trump administration and some states to make it harder to vote by mail, getting supporters to the polls is going to be absolutely critical in this election.

If Obama motivates Democratic voters who would not otherwise make the effort to take time out of work and stand in line, he can help change the outcome in closely fought states.

His enduring popularity with Black Americans means that he could play a particularly important role in states with close Senate races such as North Carolina, where 20 per cent of voters identify as Black, and Michigan (13 per cent) and Texas (13 per cent).

It is worth remembering that when midterm turnout set the modern record of 49 per cent during Trump’s first term in 2018, Democrats gained 40 seats and flipped control of the House of Representatives, but they still lost seats in the Senate.

title: 美联储加息预期生变，美股期指短线拉升
content:
北京时间10月2日晚，美国劳工统计局公布9月非农就业报告。作为美联储10月28日议息会议前的最后一份重磅就业数据，市场对该报告的关注度持续升温。
数据发布后，美股期指短线拉升，截至发稿，纳斯达克100指数期货涨1.06%，道指期货涨0.85%，标普500指数期货涨0.8%。 美元指数 小幅走低，截至发稿，下跌0.13%至101.91。
9月非农报告出炉
美国劳工统计局数据显示，美国9月非农新增就业人数为2.9万人，市场此前预期为9万人。
失业率方面，9月失业率为4.2%，市场此前预期为4.1%，8月为4.1%。
薪资数据方面，9月平均时薪环比上涨0.1% ，同比上涨3% ，市场此前预期分别为上涨0.3%和3.2%。
值得关注的是，美国9月非农就业人数增加2.9万人，远低于市场预期的9万人，前值为增加16.2万人，显示出劳动力市场降温幅度超出预期。巴克莱此前测算，若以今年的季节性因子重新调整，8月数据存在被高估的可能，市场对此已有充分预期。
美联储加息预期降温
当前市场对美联储10月加息的预期已较一周前大幅降温。据CME“美联储观察”工具，截至10月2日记者发稿，美联储10月维持利率不变的概率为71.8%，加息25个基点的概率仅为28.2%。而就在早些时候，市场对10月加息的概率一度接近80%。
这一转变主要源于美联储官员近期的密集表态。纽约联储主席威廉姆斯日前表示，鉴于美联储早些时候已经加息，目前没有迫切采取行动的必要。美联储副主席杰斐逊此前表示，决策者可能需要更多时间来判断是否有必要进一步加息。美联储负责监管的副主席鲍曼也表示，目前不认为进一步加息有迫切性，需要更好理解经济趋势。
分析人士认为，强劲的非农数据本身并不意味着更“鹰”派的货币政策立场。只有当强劲的就业增长同时伴随更高的参与率、稳定的失业率和更高的薪资增长时，才构成真正的“鹰”派信号，三者缺一不可。若后续CPI数据未大幅超出预期，美联储在10月会议上暂停加息仍是阻力最小的路径。
高盛预计下次加息预期时间为今年12月，并预计美联储将在10月会议上按兵不动。

title: 多家银行继续明确房贷贴息操作细节：已审未发贷款可办理，5年期满需正常计息还款
content:
来源：财联社
财联社10月2日讯（记者 彭科峰） 自9月30日国内主要银行发文响应“929”房贷新政后，近两日包括农行、工行、浦发、 宁波银行 等多家银行进一步发布了居民购房贷款贴息政策常见问题的解答。
工行等部分机构明确指出，对于部分在政策实施前已经受理尚未发放的个人住房贷款，如符合贴息条件，请客户联系贷款经办行提供后续服务。但是，对于10月1日前已经发放的个人住房贷款，则不进行追溯。另外，目前部分银行正主动联系客户补签贴息协议，确保新政惠及更多人群。
多家银行明确：10月1日前已审未发贷款可贴息 不溯及过往
今日晚间，记者注意到， 10月1日、2日，农行、 邮储银行 、宁波银行等多家国有大行、股份行、上市城商行，通过官方微信公众号等渠道相继发布实施个人住房贷款财政贴息政策的客户问答公告，就“929”房贷新政执行过程中的一些常见问题作进一步解答。
对于申请程序问题，邮储银行在通知称，客户在申请住房贷款时，无需单独向该行申请财政贴息，在贷款办理时，银行将根据您所购房屋面积、房屋总价、是否属于首套住房等条件进行初步判断，并告知客户贴息比例、贴息期限、贴息额度等要素，确保客户知晓政策内容并授权银行办理贴息。对贷款审批通过并经审核符合贴息条件的贷款，在正常还贷时，自动在每期应还款金额里扣除贴息金额，实现“免申即享”。同时，为了让客户“心中有数”，对符合贴息条件的个人住房贷款，后续银行将通过手机短信、APP消息等方式，及时告知客户贷款满足财政贴息条件。
宁波银行在通知中表示，对经审核符合贴息政策要求的贷款，采取“免申即享”办理方式，即按月收息时，在每期应还款金额里自动扣除对应贴息金额。如需帮助，客户可通过宁波银行手机银行、贷款经办机构、95574客服电话咨询。
对于贴息标准问题， 浦发银行 在公告中表示，按照《通知》要求，财政部门按照贷款本金给予年化1个百分点、期限不超过5年的贴息支持，单户可享受贴息的贷款规模上限为100万元。其进一步举例称，如果客户的房贷利率为3.05%且符合贴息条件，在贴息期间贷款将按照年化利率2.05%计算利息。如果客户的房贷规模为120万元且符合贴息条件，则可享受贴息的贷款规模上限为100万元。
对于近期新发房贷能否享受财政贴息的问题，工行明确指出，具体有三种情况。其一，对于部分在政策实施前已经受理尚未发放的个人住房贷款，如客户符合贴息条件，请联系贷款经办行为您提供后续服务。其二，按照《通知》要求，本次购房贷款贴息政策自2026年10月1日起实施；对于10月1日前已经发放的个人住房贷款，不进行追溯。其三，对于贷款期限大于或等于5年的，最多可享受5年的贴息优惠；对于贷款期限小于5年的，按照实际贷款期限享受贴息优惠。
宁波银行也明确，对于2026年10月1日前在该行已经放款的存量住房贷款，不享受本次贴息优惠。
对于套取“财政贴息”的问题，农行在通知中指出，有关部门发现通过违规操作套取骗取贴息的，将收回贴息资金。该行将依规开展贷款审批，对符合要求的予以贴息。对于各类“包装贷”、“职业背债人”等，该行严格予以禁止。
有银行提示：贴息非银行贷款利率下调、5年期满后正常计息
记者了解到，一些银行已经于10月1日向购房客户及时发放相关贷款。
建设银行 方面介绍，新政后总行迅速响应，第一时间形成操作细则、完成贴息相关协议文本和系统改造，并开展行内培训。据了解，10月1日政策实施首日，建行四川分行下辖成都双流分行、宜宾分行、南充分行等机构迅速行动，首批为4名购房客户发放贴息贷款210万元，涵盖新建商品住房和二手住房。
另有地方银行人士向记者介绍，目前该行已经在和相关房贷客户进行接洽，贷款投放等相关流程正在快速推进中。这些客户基本属于前期已经有购房意向、符合条件但未正式发放贷款的人群，属于刚好赶上了这一次的政策红利。
记者注意到，在进行相关政策解读和客户宣传时，部分银行也相应加大了相关提示，以更好保护消费者权益。宁波银行方面就指出，本次优惠方式为财政贴息补贴，不属于银行贷款利率下调，贷款合同执行利率保持不变。并且，贴息优惠最长享受5年，期满之后客户需要按照原贷款合同利率政策计息还款。并且，按照政策要求，大面积、高总价住房贷款不予办理贴息。
记者了解到，对于部分已签约、未放款且满足条件的客户，一些银行正在抓紧进行工作，确保财政贴息惠及相对应的人群。有银行内部人士向记者表示，对于10月1日前已经“收单”且符合条件的客户，该行正要求信贷经理主动联系客户，在放款之前完成贴息协议的补签工作。
（财联社记者 彭科峰）

title: 美国9月非农仅新增2.9万个岗位，失业率小幅上行
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
招聘形势低迷，远不及市场预期，但失业率仍处在历史低位附近
美国 9 月新增就业 2.9 万个岗位，大幅低于市场预期。这表明劳动力市场整体尚且平稳，但已经难以像过去一样持续实现大规模就业增长。
核心数据
新增就业数据远低于分析师 8.4 万人的预期。
月度就业数据本身波动较大，因此投资者与政策制定者通常更关注失业率，而失业率今年整体一直维持低位。
美国劳工部周五公布，失业率小幅升至 4.2%，高于上月 4.1%，但依旧处于历史低位，反映劳动力市场大体保持健康。经济学家此前预期失业率维持 4.1%。
对美联储意味着什么
美联储的政策重心已经从提振就业转向对抗通胀。
上个月，美联储三年来首次加息，试图压制居高不下、顽固高于目标水平的物价涨幅。政策转向背后的一大理由：央行判定就业市场状况良好，不再那么需要货币刺激。
美联储主席凯文・沃什在 9 月的发布会上表示：“包括劳动力市场在内的一系列广泛数据都显示，经济已经走强。”
今年的就业市场现状
大型企业公开释放裁员信号的情况有所减少。职业再就业咨询机构挑战者、格雷与圣诞节的数据显示，8 月对外公布的裁员规模创下 2022 年以来同期最低水平。受移民人数大幅下滑影响，想要维持失业率稳定，社会所需要新增的岗位数量也随之变少。
很多企业进入 “少招聘、少裁员” 模式：既不愿大规模辞退现有员工，同时也不积极招入新人。
债券市场暴跌背景
在债券市场遭遇抛售的大环境下，投资者格外关注本次就业数据。本周早些时候，美国国债收益率触及 24 年新高，随后出现回落；抵押贷款利率飙升，创下四年最大单周涨幅，大量潜在购房者因此选择观望。
对中期选举的影响
周五公布的数据，是 11 月 3 日中期选举之前的最后一份就业报告。多项民调显示，选民对经济的悲观情绪不断加重，这种情绪通常会对执政党造成冲击。密歇根大学调查显示，消费者信心接近历史低位。与此同时，大量美国劳动者已经不再轻易跳槽。
人工智能带来的影响
部分经济学家担忧人工智能即将带来大规模失业潮，但目前尚无确凿证据表明自动化正在大量消灭白领岗位。与之相反，数据中心领域的巨额投入反倒拉动了劳动力市场。
领英的估算显示，2023 年初至 9 月末，美国新增了数据标注员、数据中心运维等相关岗位，这还尚未统计建筑类岗位。电工、水管工的工时与收入都出现大幅上涨。
摩根日兴证券美国经济学家鲁奇尔・夏尔马表示：“有明确迹象表明，数据中心投资对就业市场产生正向外溢效应。”

title: I’m even more bullish about stocks than a year ago
content:
Stuart Kirk

Published October 2 2026

Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter.

A year ago, I wrote that greed would be my fourth-quarter investment strategy . We were in a bubble, I reckoned, but it had a way to go. Besides, US stock returns had been positive 80 per cent of the time in the last three months of the year since my mum was at kindergarten.

So much for that. By the end of October I had sold every equity fund in my portfolio and ran a 100 per cent cash position for the next five months. Does being greedy make sense again now? Will I ignore my advice regardless?

Part of the reason I threw my shares out of the pram was how well they had performed in 2025 up to that point. Everything felt too perfect. I was up 17 per cent since January, comfortably ahead of the S&P 500 – even though I had no US stocks.

This year, my portfolio has risen in value by 11 per cent, in line with the S&P 500 in dollars, but four percentage points behind in pounds. I will take that every time, of course. But it doesn’t seem as frothy and overheated as this time last year.

Yes, there’s been SpaceX, the frothiest and most overheated company listing in the history of finance. And the size and growth in borrowing to fund the artificial intelligence boom is off the charts — $340bn by the hyperscalers alone next year, according to Goldman Sachs.

So what do I mean when I say that equities feel less exuberant to me than 12 months ago? And does that necessarily make them more attractive? As an investor you want the va-va-voom. You just don’t want to overpay.

For earnings, that is. And one of the most extraordinary developments since my column a year ago is how much more profit I receive for my money. In every one of the markets I’m invested in, forward price-to-earnings ratios are lower today.

I read once about a hedge fund manager who used to scream at analysts: “Don’t bring me stocks on eight times price-to-earnings ratios and tell me they’re cheap. Show me something that you think is undervalued on 50 times!”

Like Nvidia, I suppose. In 2023, its forward price-to-earnings ratio was exactly that (its trailing multiple was 180 times). I would have told my boss it was ridiculously expensive and only a moron would buy it.

It turns out it was cheap — as defined by the fact that Nvidia’s share price subsequently sextupled. And indeed its earnings grew by even more, such that the consensus forward price-to-earnings has dropped to just 19 times, according to Capital IQ data.

It grew into its valuation, as the pros say — and then some in Nvidia’s case. A milder version of this is what has been going on in equity markets more broadly. In the US, Japan and Latin America, forecast earnings are a third higher than a year ago. For the UK, it’s 27 per cent. LatAm earnings will nearly double.

Thus, if I had known last October that US profits would be what they are forecast to be this year, the 25 times forward price-to-earnings back then was actually closer to 18 times. Japan’s was 13 rather than 17. The FTSE 100’s was more like 11 than 14.5 times.

The surge in earnings didn’t come until long after I sold out of equities. It was only after Iran kicked off that profits began accelerating almost everywhere. But you need to look at a long-run chart to appreciate just how unusual this is — especially in the US.

So much so that not only are forward price/earnings ratios lower today than a year ago for every stock market I own but they are all — save the US — beneath the levels they dropped to when I bought back into equities as missiles were flying over the Gulf.

Even the S&P 500’s ratio is only a smidgen higher — 21.3 times today compared with 20 in late March. And yet the index is up by a fifth. Asia ex-Japan has performed even better, while its price/earnings ratio fell by as much as the US’s rose. It’s a similar story, to a lesser degree, for the UK.

If investors are receiving way more profits per share compared with the price of each share versus a year ago, it goes without saying that we should be more bullish today — right? Other things being equal, I suppose so.

Any expected-return calculation takes current values as a starting point. The higher the valuation relative to the past, the lower the expected returns — and vice versa. Share prices can veer off trend for years, though. I’ve been waiting for some ratios to mean revert for decades.

But history shows that the future performance of equity markets has tended to be better the lower the valuation is now. In that case, if I were happy to own stocks when I wrote my end-of-third-quarter review a year ago, I should be keener still.

And I am. There are risks aplenty, of course. There always are — even if the young ’uns out there believe a rocky investment landscape is a new phenomenon. What is different, however, is that whereas last time a re-rating (down) in valuations was the risk, today I would argue that missing out on earnings is the worry.

What does that come down to? Three things: whether your mum thinks using ChatGPT is useful or not (demand); whether the price of compute plummets due to intense competition (supply); and whether AI can stay unregulated without a rogue agent spurring a worldwide backlash.

For now I’m hopeful, especially given the resilience of equity markets to rising bond yields. But you know how long my bullish moods can last now, don’t you?

The author is a former portfolio manager. Email: [email protected]

title: Car crashes into viral shop shutters where gran was hoisted into the air
content:
A shop made famous when a grandmother got caught on its shutter and was left dangling in the air has hit the headlines again after a car crashed through the front of it.

The Best-One shop in Tonteg, Rhondda Cynon Taf, caught the dramatic moment on CCTV when a Jaguar smashed through its doors after mounting bollards and crashing into the shop's coffee machine.

In March 2024, the shop went viral after staff member Anne Hughes got caught on the shutter while waiting for the shop to open to start her shift.

Anne, who died in 2025, was left dangling 7ft (2.1 metres) in the air and shouting for the owner to help her, with CCTV footage of the incident viewed tens of millions of times.

People working in the shop could not believe the latest incident on Friday and were left "scared" when the car ploughed into the shop's entrance.

Donna Davies, who has worked in the shop for several years, said: "The car just came straight through, it was a loud noise and we didn't know what was happening but thought it could have been ram-raiders. It was scary."

She said she ran out and saw an elderly driver and passenger, who are both regulars to the shop, in the car.

"The driver said his foot slipped when he went to get out the car and the car came straight in," Donna said.

Anne's viral moment was previously immortalised by local graffiti artist Tee2Sugars on the shutter she was caught on.

He has now updated the shutter to include the car smashing through the front of the shop.

Donna said she had worked with Anne before her death.

"Anne would be laughing at this, I think she'd like the updated shutter," she said.

"People are coming in the shop this morning and finding it amusing. It wasn't at the time, but looking back we can smile."

The shop front was badly damaged in the crash but the owner and family worked late on Friday and Saturday to fix the front and keep the shop open for customers.

Hakim Akram, who is the nephew of the shop owner and works in the store, said: "It was a bit of a shock, he just came flying through - I didn't even know what happened until I saw the car.

"It was surreal and very loud. People thought it was a prank and AI when they first saw it on social media."

One customer, Shaun, said he could not believe it.

He said: "It's just crazy after the incident with the lady on the shutter and now this."

The family of Anne Hughes told BBC Wales they were very glad no-one was seriously hurt. Her son Ceri joked: "We can't believe the shop's luck, we are starting to wonder if all of this is an inside job.

"Tonteg Best-One - the only shop in the UK where you can be lifted 7ft in the air on Monday and driven through on a Friday."

They said they were pleased the artwork of Anne was not damaged.

Her grandchildren Lilly and Alex said their nan would be happy with the new addition on the shutter and joked: "Nan always preferred a Bentley but would settle with a Jag next to her on the shutter."

title: 美国9月新增就业人数远低于预期 8月数据下修
content:

美国9月新增就业人数远低于预期，显示劳动力市场乃至整体经济意外走弱。
美国劳工统计局周五公布，经季节性调整后，当月非农就业新增2.9万人，失业率升至4.2%。
道琼斯 调查的经济学家此前预期新增就业8.4万人，失业率4.1%。
除9月数据疲软外，8月就业数据被下修，新增就业修正为13.3万人；7月数据由正转负，非农就业减少1万人。整体修正后，就业人数较此前公布值合计少增6万人。

title: 美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万个就业岗位，失业率升至4.2%
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
美国经济 9 月新增就业岗位远低于预期，暴露出劳动力市场乃至整体经济一处出人意料的疲软环节。
美国劳工统计局周五公布，经季节调整后，当月非农就业新增 29000 人 ，失业率升至 4.2% 。 道琼斯 调查的经济学家此前预期新增就业 84000 人，失业率维持 4.1%。
除 9 月数据表现疲软外，8 月就业数据被下修至新增 13.3 万人；7 月数据由正转负，非农就业减少 1 万人。两次数据修正合计，较此前公布值少计 6 万个就业岗位。
市场迅速对这份报告作出反应。交易员将疲软就业数据视作利好消息，认为这大概率进一步确认美联储将在 10 月议息会议维持利率不变。
数据发布后股指期货走高；美债收益率应声回落，此前美债收益率一度攀升至本世纪初以来的高位。市场隐含概率显示，美联储在 10 月 27‑28 日会议按兵不动的概率飙升至 83.7%。
相较于非农新增就业的 headline（头条）数据，美联储官员更加关注失业率。
用于统计失业率的住户调查数据表现，要好于统计非农岗位的机构调查。 住户调查显示，当月家庭口径就业增加 7.8 万人；劳动力规模扩大 48.5 万人；劳动参与率上升 0.2 个百分点至 61.8%，创下 5 月以来最高水平。劳动参与率统计的是就业或积极找工作人群占总人口的比重。
包含灰心丧气劳动者以及因经济原因从事兼职人群的广义失业率小幅回落至 7.6%，为 2025 年 1 月以来最低。
该报告出炉之际，美联储官员正在评估经济现状，研判其将如何影响下一步利率决策。
结合央行政策官员近日的表态，市场重新调整预期，目前预计美联储公开市场委员会（FOMC）将推迟至 12 月才会再次加息。FOMC 已于 9 月将基准利率上调 25 个基点。
政策制定者普遍认为，通胀对经济的威胁大于劳动力市场；近几个月劳动力市场整体展现韧性。数据勾勒出一幅 “少招聘、少裁员” 的经济图景：每周初请失业金人数处于低位，一项指标显示裁员规模处于四年低点。
但通胀水平持续大幅高于美联储 2% 的目标。央行偏好的最新核心通胀指标显示，核心通胀年化率为 3%。
薪资方面持续显现通胀降温迹象。
9 月平均时薪仅环比上涨 0.1%，12 个月同比涨幅为 3%。华尔街此前预期环比 0.3%、同比 3.1%；该同比薪资增速为 2021 年 5 月以来最低。周平均工时维持 34.6 小时不变。
当月新增岗位主要来自医疗行业，新增 1.7 万个岗位；建筑业新增 1.1 万；制造业新增 9000。
政府部门就业减少 1.7 万个岗位；临时援助服务业岗位减少 1.1 万；受人工智能对就业冲击的担忧影响，信息服务业岗位流失 1 万；金融行业岗位也减少 7000。
尽管就业增长疲弱，但经济其他领域不乏强劲信号。
宏观层面经济增长势头强劲。
本周早些时候，美国商务部上调一季度、二季度国内生产总值（GDP）增速，修正后分别为 2.2% 与 2.5%。亚特兰大联储预测三季度 GDP 增速可达 3.7%。

title: 美国9月份非农就业人数仅增加2.9万 失业率小幅攀升
content:
专题：美国9月劳动力市场走弱，仅新增2.9万非农岗位
美国9月份新增就业人数低于预期，失业率小幅上升，显示在成本不断上涨之际，雇主在招聘方面持谨慎态度。
美国劳工统计局周五公布的数据显示，9月份非农就业人数增加2.9万人，此前两个月的数据被下修。这一增幅低于所有经济学家的预期。失业率升至4.2%。
就业增长放缓主要受到政府、信息、专业和商业服务以及金融活动等行业就业人数下降的拖累。医疗保健、建筑和制造业则增加了就业岗位。
稳健的消费者支出和强劲的企业投资为招聘提供了支撑，但许多注重成本控制的雇主仍不愿扩大员工规模。不过，裁员仍较为有限。
由于失业率从历史水平来看仍然较低，美联储官员在考虑何时再次加息时，可以继续将注意力集中在通胀上。

title: School protests send shivers down French government's spine
content:
It is a piece of wisdom that all French leaders take care to heed: young people on the street equals trouble.

Since the student protests of May 1968 – memorably described by President De Gaulle as chienlit (bed defecation, in other words chaos) – every government has run scared of angry French youth.

Why? Because youth movements are unpredictable and shapeless, often with no clear structure to negotiate with. Because when they protest, other groups join in.

Also: because as they're young, the public tends to sympathise. And because if the police mess up and cause injury or worse, then the consequences are incalculable. And presidential elections are only months away.

For all these reasons, when la jeunesse en colère (angry youth) is at the barricades governments tread very carefully indeed.

Right now, French teenagers are at the barricades and if they are not visibly angry (the mood is more excitement), they certainly have the government of President Emmanuel Macron in what Le Monde called on Friday "the cold sweats".

A movement that started nearly two weeks ago in the low-income Seine-Saint-Denis area of northern Paris has in the last few days spread across the country.

On Thursday – the high point so far – hundreds of lycées (where 15-18 year-olds finish their schooling) were being blockaded. On Friday, the situation had improved but around 400 lycées were closed in order to protect staff and students. Universities are beginning to join in.

Violence has erupted. On Thursday the main hall of a lycée in Nantes was destroyed by fire. Smaller fires too numerable to mention were lit at school entrance gates around the country. The cost of the damage is millions of euros.

According to Education Minister Édouard Geffray, 65 teaching staff including 40 school heads have been injured. "Most of the staff who were hurt said that the people they were facing… were not their own pupils," he said.

In addition, the government says that around 300 police and firefighters have been treated for injuries, and some 2,000 people – mainly minors – taken into custody. For their part, student groups say they have a long list of people injured by police. Two teenagers have serious eye injuries and one has lost many of his teeth.

The problem would be hard enough if it was just a question of meeting the protesters' demands. But there is another dimension – a political and social one – which makes this student crisis far more dangerous than in the past.

The demands do exist, even if they remain vague. They are about money – the lack of it – and the need for more teachers, smaller classes and better buildings.

On such matters, many in France would agree with the teenagers. Certainly using protest to demand money from government is such a national habit that even governments agree it's legitimate. And of course, things are indeed getting worse in the education system – because money is so tight.

This week Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu published his draft for next year's budget. The motif is "More cuts – and this time we're serious!"

Whether or not he manages to remove €54bn (£46bn) from state spending, as he promises, remains open to question.

But it is surely obvious that the era of public largesse to defuse social unrest in France is now in its twilight. Students demanding an extra school nurse or insulation in the dining-block are likely to be disappointed.

But that is the lesser of the worries.

The far greater fear is that these student protests are being manipulated by the hard left – and that the violence of recent days is a foretaste of what awaits a dangerously polarised society in the year of elections that is coming.

For the right and centre, there is no doubt that behind the student trouble lies the cunning hand of the France Unbowed party (LFI) and its popular presidential candidate, Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

LFI leaders have regularly appeared next to the students – notably in the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis whose mayor Bally Bagayoko was criticised for saying that "violence can sometimes be legitimate."

An internal report prepared for the Paris police department which was leaked to the media analysed the opening of the movement in Seine-Saint-Denis. It concluded that students were being "egged on by far-left elements from students unions… and political groups such as… LFI."

It said the tensions "could be part of a flame-kindling strategy… aimed at imposing their ideas ahead of the national elections".

In support of its conclusion, the report's writers cited the presence of protesters who are not themselves lycéens, the vagueness of the demands, the flying of Palestinian and Algerian flags, and the use of tactics – like calling for supplementary protests at police-stations - that come from the radical-left playbook.

The LFI strongly denies doing anything more than lending its natural support to a movement it regards as legitimate. On Thursday Mélenchon called on students to avoid violence "which only serves our enemies' interests".

But his opponents believe that the 75-year-old veteran – who stands a good chance of making it to the second round of the presidential elections in May, probably against the hard-right's Marine Le Pen – knows exactly what he is doing.

Polls show he has massive support – some 40% -- among 18-24 year-olds in France, and that this is concentrated in the populous, high-immigration city suburbs where his talk of a "new France" and "creolisation", to reflect France's changing language and population, are highly appreciated.

But young people are also the biggest abstainers in French elections, so the strategy – as the elections approach – will be to give constant reminders to this part of the population that the LFI is at their side, and that their vote can count.

Whether this will be enough to ensure victory for Mélenchon is another matter. He must surely take seriously the polls which all show him losing massively in a run-off against Le Pen.

If that happens, France will be in very unstable territory - for which the young people's protests of recent days will indeed have been a harbinger.

title: Paris Fashion Week confronts luxury’s crisis of desire
content:
Elizabeth Paton

Published October 2 2026

Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter.

Front row conversations dissecting the state of the industry in Paris can feel rather heavy these days. Most of the starry creative hires made by big heritage houses a year ago, with a handful of notable exceptions, have failed to generate the magic — and sales momentum — hoped for in brand C-suites. Budgets are tighter, and some designers may be on the move again already, decisions that have a wider ripple effect across studios, head offices and people’s daily lives. A sharp luxury slowdown in China is another cause for concern. And it is heaping the pressure further on creatives to make people dream about and spend again on goods they do not aspire to in the way they once did.

It is interesting to see how designers respond to the moment. Some keep clients fully front of mind, like Daniel Roseberry, who built a subterranean velveteen nightclub for his latest Schiaparelli ready-to-wear show based on sexy deconstructions of the “Schiap jacket” — to the delight of his couture clients, many of whom sat at tables drinking champagne in support. Others opt for shock factor, like Matières Fécales, which shut down Place de la République, a square famous for public demonstrations, for its show titled “The 99 per cent”. Featuring 99 non-Caucasian models of different ages and sizes, it was a personal and political rallying cry from co-founders Hannah Rose Dalton and Steven Raj Bhaskaran to those they feel are left behind by the system. It generated a huge outpouring of support on social media — even if critics asked whether such fashion statements empower the masses if it’s only the 1 per cent who can afford to own the garments.

Pushing the boundaries of possibility comes in many forms. At Anrealage, Kunihiko Morinaga offered incredible colour-changing skirts and dresses via rippling 3D-printed scales, LED lights and E Ink paper scales, playfully stretching ideas of what clothes can or should be. Here are some other takeaways from the biggest shows of the week.

This season it was all about glamour at Dries Van Noten. Julian Klausner, the brand’s creative director since 2024, explained backstage that he and his team took cues from the little flourishes that made them feel glamorous when walking down the street: a cinched waist, a sparkling brooch or bold pops of colour. This brought to mind 1950s movie stars, which on the runway translated to movie poster prints inspired by the era splashed across dresses, skirts and car coats. Like Prada before it this season, this felt like an homage to skirts: a nod to the hyper-femininity of the 1950s, perhaps, but also reworked to relish the style’s versatility. Almost all falling to the knee, they came dripping in Indian crystal embellishments or with paper-bag waists, cargo pockets or with gauzy layers over stencilled prints. Matched up with everything from cropped jackets (everywhere at the moment) and sweater vests, and layered up with plenty of cocktail jewellery, it felt contemporary, fun and, most importantly, wearable.

Every so often, a fashion show transports you to another dimension. Such was the case at Rick Owens on Thursday, where the grand colonnades, reclining statues and supercharged fountain jets of the Palais de Tokyo plaza were recast as an otherworldly set, one where models in long stone-coloured ceremonial gowns strode their way down a huge ramp to electronic music that thudded like a heartbeat. The inspiration this season was, in fact, stones: from “elegant stoicism” to “stone-throwing, which I’ve made my life’s modest mission to oppose” and “the stone thrown aside during Christ’s resurrection,” read Owens’ show notes.

Some dresses had a sturdy, quilted quality like armour, while others in gossamer silk rippled in the breeze. Rompers with sharp edges, worn with crystalline rope boots, then acted as a turning point to tougher, more industrial layered looks including sulphur-dyed denim skirts and biker jackets, before closing with a series of strange structured head-to-toe harnesses, which Owens called his version of a négligée. Owens has been described by The New York Times as “fashion’s patriarch of freaks” — a title he would relish. His weird and wonderful universe feels ever more invigorating than the bulk of the industry mainstream.

Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen, founders of The Row, have long let their chic, minimalist clothes for very, very rich women do the talking. The duo rarely give interviews; famously, they also don’t allow guests to use social media at their Paris show. Logo-free, the brand’s calling card has generally been “if you know you know” when you see their clothes in the street. It hasn’t held them back, per se; their €5,000 Margaux bag has cult status and their €1,000 rubber flip flops spawned endless imitations.

Lately, however, there has been a quiet shift in the script, including (whisper it) advertising in glossy magazines, with a volume shift on the runway too. Amid the neat, neutral tailoring this season were even more beautiful and colourful fabrications than usual, bringing new verve: opulent vintage-esque materials in reds and turquoise, or broderie anglaise, elegantly fashioned into wrap tops and slips, next to floral ribbon belts, and fraying straps and hems. Bohemian, almost, until you remember the wild price tags.

The general consensus on the front row of the Chloé show on Thursday morning was that this would be the last from creative director Chemena Kamali. Rumour has it that she will take over from Anthony Vaccarello at Saint Laurent; and though this is not confirmed, her exit could prove an issue for parent group Richemont, which already has another vacant creative director spot to fill at Alaïa, where it is yet to find a replacement for Pieter Mulier who decamped to Versace. Anyway, back to business — and to the runway, where the show notes began: “May the love poured into this collection endure forever.” This collection certainly cycled through house archetypes; plenty of broderie anglaise dresses, cape-like outerwear in block colours (worn with fun fisherman’s hats), sorbet-hued, barely-there lingerie and vast floaty gowns. A romantic ode, then, and one that got a standing ovation. But that was likely more of a farewell gesture than directed at the clothes themselves, which felt more dutiful than truly spirited.

Pierpaolo Piccioli inherited a complex challenge when he took the reins at Balenciaga last year; a house with its own distinct heritage and even starker contemporary codes courtesy of Piccioli’s predecessor Demna. Thus far, his collections have yet to offer a cohesive view of what Balenciaga should be today. His Thursday show, however, was a step in the right direction. This season, he was motivated by the idea of putting couture-like cuts and techniques on everyday pieces of clothing, which included T-shirts with cascading trains, denim cut on the bias, peplum white-collar shirts, voluminous oversized cargo trousers and blazers finished with trailing ribbons. There were too many ideas at play. But Piccioli is also working hard to make his mark here. A coral-inspired textile totem structure at the centre of the runway was a nod to the coral necklaces he wears every day — and a personal touch.

title: Black metal mourns pioneering Venom frontman
content:
The co-founder, frontman and bass player of pioneering heavy metal band Venom has died at the age of 63, it has been announced.

For almost 50 years Conrad Lant, known by his stage name Cronos, led the Newcastle band credited with inventing the black metal genre and cited as a major influence by thrash metal bands including Metallica, Slayer and Anthrax.

In a tribute, the group said Lant's "voice, bass and vision were at the heart of Venom" and described their bandmate as "uncompromising, fearless and unmistakable".

His son Nathan thanked the band's fans down the decades "for all of the support you have given my dad over the years, I know he really appreciated you all".

Venom began in Newcastle in 1978, formed by musicians from three other bands, but it was their second album - Black Metal released in 1982 - that cemented their status in the rock world.

Playing a fast style mixed with Lant's dark imagery and lyrics, the album gave its name to an entire subgenre and influenced bands on both sides of the Atlantic.

'Filthy fifteen'

Speaking to BBC Newcastle, rock journalist Simon Rushworth said: "They were massively influential [and] spawned a whole genre of what I'd call extreme metal.

"The likes of Slayer, Metallica, Anthrax, they all cited Venom.

"Venom took Metallica out on the road in the mid-80s before anybody knew who they were. Then Metallica returned the favour and took Venom on the road with them.

"Cronos was right at the heart of it, not only with the music.

"He was the one who brought a lot of the early artwork to the table and kind of created this black metal image."

That imagery brought the band to the attention of the US government when the track Possessed was included on the "Filthy Fifteen" list of songs compiled by the Parents Music Resource Center, the committee behind the adoption of "parental advisory" warning stickers.

The original line-up began to break apart following Possessed and Cronos pursued solo projects until a short-lived and acrimonious reunion in the mid-90s.

With changing line-ups, but mainly led by Cronos, Venom continued to the present day, releasing a 14th studio album - Into Oblivion - this year.

In a tribute on social media, original guitarist Jeff "Mantas" Dunn said: "Despite the turbulent history of this band, it was at the end of the day the three of us, who started something so special and changed the direction, the movement and the history of metal as we know it.

"At times like this the thing I remember is the friendship that we had in those early days, that one for all, all for one mentality, that rebellious quality and the absolute driven urge to be something so different whether it was accepted or not."

Rushworth said the band were themselves influenced by the likes of Motorhead, Kiss, Black Sabbath and Alice Cooper, adding: "Cronos wanted Venom to be a more evil and flamboyant hybrid of all of those bands.

"Many would say he succeeded."
