title: Donald Quintin: ‘We’re entering a different market now’
content:
Robert Armstrong

Published October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

This article is an on-site version of our Unhedged newsletter. Premium subscribers can sign up here to get the newsletter delivered every weekday. Standard subscribers can upgrade to Premium here , or explore all FT newsletters

Good morning. The S&P 500 has been all but unchanged for four months. Look under the hood, and you will find that earnings expectations for the coming year have risen 7 or 8 per cent over that period — but that this has been neatly offset by the price/earnings ratio index falling from 22 to 20. This is exactly what one would expect to happen in an environment where a combination of real economic growth and inflation are driving interest rates up: future earnings increasing while the valuation of those earnings falls as the discount rate rises. Once in a while, markets make sense. If you spot anything else making sense, email us: [email protected] .

Donald Quintin joined Lone Star Funds in 2010 and became its CEO in 2024. Previously, he worked at Merrill Lynch and Salomon Brothers. Lone Star, founded in 1995, invests across private equity, credit, and real estate. Headquartered in London, the group has offices around the globe, from Dallas to Tokyo. It had about $36bn in assets under management as of the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings .

Unhedged: How do Lone Star’s three strategies — buyout, commercial real estate and credit — fit together?

Donald Quintin: The fund started in commercial real estate during the savings and loan crisis, and pivoted through time to respond to the Japan banking crisis, then moved to Europe. As investment opportunities expanded it made sense to break the fund into commercial real estate and an opportunistic strategy, which we did during the early stages of the financial crisis. Subsequently, we took the opportunity strategy and split it between credit and traditional buyouts. But across all those strategies we remain dedicated to value investing.

Unhedged: What do you mean by value?

Quintin: We focus on transactions where there is a preponderance of asset backing or some sort of reliable cash flow. So, being disciplined on entry price and looking at the companies where there are opportunities to make changes — where the return is predicated on what you can do to improve the business, rather than on market growth or multiple expansion.

We tend to focus on those situations where there could be, for example, a corporate carve-out, or you have a global corporation that is looking to shed a business. These are complex situations — they require a lot of work desegregating that business from the parent. Those situations require a lot of muscle memory, setting up new management teams, addressing technological shortfalls and really trying to define what the business should look like on a standalone basis.

Unhedged: Is it too crude to say that where a lot of buyout shops think about revenue growth, you think more about margin or return on capital?

Quintin: The broader market has historically focused on either revenue growth or multiple expansion. How we think about investing, that is really a small part of the value proposition. The real alpha is coming from either improving the underlying margins of the business, or focusing on the cash flow.

Unhedged: The last time we spoke you talked about how you made your bones picking through the wreckage of the great financial crisis — loans in distress, CDOs on the rocks. What did that teach you?

Quintin: Having gone through the financial crisis gives you an appreciation for things like excess leverage, and focusing on how things can go wrong . . . I started my career at Salomon Brothers in fixed income, in the mortgage division as a trader. I moved to Merrill Lynch just at the onset of the financial crisis and worked closely with management there — John Thain, Greg Fleming — culminating in the sale to Bank of America. That was a huge learning opportunity, with many sleepless nights and difficult situations during the day.

Unhedged: We’ve seen lower returns and longer hold times in the buyout industry. Are industry returns permanently lower now?

Quintin: I think what’s happening is a separation in the market, which will force a return to what private equity was in the beginning, in the nineties — where the quality of the business, the quality of the management and a realistic view as to what one can do to improve that business are really important. A respect for how you’re going to exit that business before you ever buy it. When money is cheap, rates are low and multiples are expanding, that kind of stockpicking attitude isn’t as relevant because a rising tide raises all boats. Now we have high interest rates relative to recent history, and those rates are likely going to be higher for longer. That puts pressure on the assumption that growth is what’s going to drive your returns . . . We’re entering a different market now.

Unhedged: 2021 was a euphoric peak in private equity. That’s five years ago now — time for that vintage of buyout to grow up and move out. Are they going to struggle to do so? And does that create opportunities for Lone Star — helping with companies’ balance sheets or on the equity side? Are you licking your chops?

Quintin: I think we are. It will create opportunities. Broadly, I agree with your timeframe, 2021, that period had really kind of peak multiples. And you had post-pandemic inflated Ebitdas, you had a significant amount of cheap debt available that wasn’t hedged at the operating company level from floating rate to fixed rate. Because nobody was anticipating that rates would go up — they’d only seen them stable to down. Those situations are now manifesting themselves into credit opportunities. You have good businesses that are under capital structure pressure . . . with companies where the purchase prices were elevated, the challenge is really if those positions haven’t been marked low enough. I’m struck by the fact that we’re in a time now where you have a huge amount of debt capital available through private credit and through the bank market. You have a healthy banking system, generally. And there’s a lot of dry powder. So you have the tools for transactions, right? You are starting to see asset-by-asset transactions happening, but you’re not seeing portfolio sales, and a lot of it is because those companies didn’t grow into the elevated prices they were acquired at, they didn’t hit their growth projections.

Unhedged: So if they mark to market, it crystallises a bad return.

Quintin: You could make that argument. If they’re willing buyers, and transactions don’t happen, it’s often because the expectations are not being met by the seller.

Unhedged: What about retail distribution of private equity investment? Lone Star hasn’t done it, but what do you think? Where is it appropriate? Is there an opportunity here?

Quintin: It’s not something we anticipate doing in the future. Raising money in the retail space requires a significant apparatus. And I think where you’re seeing a prevalence of that is in those institutions that have become quite large and they have many different channels for fundraising. It’s not something that we have spent time thinking about.

Unhedged: What’s the best deal you ever did?

Quintin: I feel quite proud of the Novo Banco transaction, which was the acquisition of the good bank from Portuguese central bank Fundo, the rescue vehicle. At the time, there were those calling for the liquidation of the bank, and the Portuguese state had difficulties selling the bank. It was a very complicated transaction. It required a significant amount of work on the balance sheet, the structure and the needs of the state. We presented them with a very novel proposal that enabled the state to sell the bank, and we bought a 75 per cent stake. What I’m really proud about is that we really refocused the bank, we improved the governance, we introduced technology, we expanded its lending footprint in Portugal. When you are buying a bank, particularly post-financial crisis, you have a lot of stakeholders, whether it’s the ECB, the Central Bank of Portugal, the Portuguese government. And an incredibly important stakeholder in the citizenry of Portugal. We successfully exited the bank, selling it to BPCE, a French bank. And I think it was a great success story for Portugal.

Unhedged: Lately there has not been a lot of distress in the credit world. So what’s keeping you busy in the credit business?

Quintin: Credit is something that we do on an opportunistic basis, and it hasn’t really been a big focus of ours given where we are in the cycle. That being said, there are opportunities coming up because some of it is a situation you described before — the high prices paid and the excess debt used in the 2019 to 2021 timeframe. I also think the elevated rates are creating issues . . . there are operating businesses that didn’t hedge their debt and where things were priced to perfection. Debt starts to impact cash flow. That’s something that we’re clearly seeing. Also, private credit has been a complement to the existing bank loan market and it complements private equity very well, but when you start to enter a credit cycle, if there’s an element of bad underwriting, you can’t escape that. And we’re starting to see instances of that crop up. But I still think it’s early days.

I do think that the market will start to separate between those that have experience handling stressed and distressed credit. Private credit that’s been assembled without proper workout teams, anticipating potential issues, will have to scramble to catch up, just to find the expertise.

Unhedged: Where are we in the credit cycle?

Quintin: It’s early days, but we are starting to see a trend. I think the reported figures from folks like Fitch and others are starting to increase. I think it is different than the financial crisis . . . to this point the economy has continued to do well, and in the industrial manufacturing space order books are still holding up fine. But there has been an impact from the prolongation of a higher-rate environment.

Unhedged: Turning to the real estate business, rates were nothing and now they’re 5 per cent. How does that change how you manage that business?

Quintin: We’re obviously not immune to the higher-for-longer interest rates. But I think those also create opportunities for investors in that opportunistic space, as higher rates put pressure on individual situations. In the financial crisis, we had a concentration of large pools of assets that are under stress at the same time. Now you have more idiosyncratic situations, and those in and of themselves are creating opportunities for investors. You also have a different banking environment, and private credit. The positive side of private credit is that it’s very patient capital.

Unhedged: When asset values are high and rates are rising, everybody wants to know, is there going to be a big dislocation? I’m not going to ask you that, but I will ask: if there is a dislocation, where will the opportunities be?

Quintin: I think it’s about being very disciplined, pragmatic and able to move quickly and handle complex situations. You don’t want to be learning on the job in those types of markets. You want muscle memory to kick in. That’s where experience comes into play. It prevents you from making decisions that you will come to regret later.

In yesterday’s letter we incorrectly stated that the 10-year Treasury yield was 4.29 per cent, rather than 5.29. This was a careless error — and one committed by Rob, not Katie, despite Katie’s byline being at the top of the letter. Rob regrets both misleading readers and damaging Katie’s reputation.

A tough guy .

title: 'I was terrified': Alex Ferguson on brain haemorrhage and games that shaped his life
content:
"I was terrified," says Sir Alex Ferguson, one of the fiercest, most explosive and most decorated managers in football history.

The legendary former Manchester United boss is recalling the day he returned to Old Trafford for the first time after suffering a brain haemorrhage in May 2018.

Four months after emergency surgery, Ferguson - famous for his 'hairdryer treatment' when United dominated English football - was back to watch his beloved club take on Wolves in the Premier League.

The man responsible for making the dreams of United fans around the world come true for once was unsure of the reception he would receive from supporters.

"I wish I could say I was comfortable. I wasn't," Ferguson tells BBC Breakfast.

He need not have worried.

Ferguson and his wife Cathy received a standing ovation when they took their seats in the directors' box before kick-off.

"My wife was with me, and she was nearly crying," he said. "When we sat down, she said: 'That's fantastic.'"

Ferguson had been retired five years - after winning 38 trophies during 26 years in charge of United - at the time of his brain haemorrhage, aged 76.

Now three months short of 85, he says: "I'm feeling quite good despite small injuries."

The Scot has a new book coming out - 'Games of My Life'. It tells the stories of 21 defining matches in his playing and managerial career, revealing fresh insights into his journey from working-class Glasgow to dominating the English game - and Europe - as United boss.

Ferguson is thankful he is able to talk about the games that helped shape him.

"I had lost my voice; I couldn't speak," he says about the days immediately after brain surgery. "That was a frightening moment.

"I remember my grandsons coming to see me and I had lost my voice.

"Then they brought in a therapist and she started doing things like asking me to write down the names of birds, names of animals, names of rivers.

"That way my voice came back."

'I almost quit football for Canada'

Ferguson won the lot during his time in charge of United between 1986 and 2013, including 13 Premier League titles.

He transformed them into a winning machine, and the history and tradition of United ran red through his veins.

As well as delivering two Champions League titles, Ferguson masterminded five FA Cup triumphs, won the League Cup four times and added the Club World Cup, European Super Cup, European Cup Winners' Cup and the Intercontinental Cup to the Old Trafford trophy cabinet.

In his book, Ferguson has picked standout games in his career, from winning his first cup final playing for Govan High School in Glasgow in 1955 at the age of 13 through to his retirement as a manager in 2013.

"That was my starting point," he says, holding the medal he received after that cup win 71 years ago.

"I played for Glasgow Schools, Scotland Schools and the Scotland youth team. The starting point of my career was there and I can look back with great satisfaction."

Ferguson describes growing up in Govan as "the making of me". He says he developed his inner confidence from his mother Elizabeth and a drive to succeed from his father Alexander, who worked in the Govan shipyards on the River Clyde.

"He was so proud of me and my brother," says Ferguson.

"He was a hard taskmaster because whenever I scored a hat-trick or a goal, my mother would say 'that's great, son'." His father, meanwhile, offered tough constructive criticism however many goals Ferguson had scored.

After making his debut as a 16-year-old striker for Queen's Park, Ferguson ended up at St Johnstone, where he endured a frustrating spell and nearly quit football for a new life in Canada.

"I wasn't enjoying it. I wasn't playing first-team football; I was in the reserves all the time," he says.

"I filled out all the forms and phoned my aunt in Canada, because you needed a sponsor then, and never told my mother and father."

The next day St Johnstone, decimated by a flu bug in the team, arrived at Ibrox to take on Rangers. A 21-year-old Ferguson was promoted to the starting XI and scored a hat-trick.

That life-changing performance in 1963 revived his playing career and set him on the path to becoming one of football's greatest managers.

"I would say this to young people - don't miss the biggest opportunity in your life. It's recognising it."

'Don't sell Ince to Inter - or you'll regret it'

Ferguson is sat in front of a table for the interview, which was conducted before the Premier League announced on Tuesday that Manchester City had been found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of financial regulations between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

On the table are several items from his career, including the Scotland cap he was finally presented with in 2021 - 54 years after appearing for his country.

Ferguson received the cap at Hampden Park on the night Scott McTominay - then a United player - scored a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 3-2 win over Israel in a World Cup qualifier.

"I remember signing McTominay at seven years of age," Ferguson says.

Also on the table are old letters addressed to Ferguson from disgruntled United fans amid speculation he was about to sell midfielder Paul Ince to Inter Milan in the summer of 1995.

One reads: 'Don't sell Incey to Inter - or you'll regret it'. Another reads: 'Every Red is disgusted with you'.

"Paul was a tremendous footballer, there's no doubt about that," says Ferguson.

"He had incredible ability, but I just had that feeling that he just got carried away a bit at the time.

"He then got this offer from Inter Milan. I'm trying to weigh up one thing against the other. I'm looking at Paul Scholes and I said 'should we?'

"Milan's offer went from £7m to £7.5m and I said 'do it'.

"That's what your job is as a manager. You have to make hard decisions, and some decisions don't suit everyone."

There is also a notebook on the table with a list of words scribbled down by Ferguson when he used to address his players.

The names of Bernard "Monty" Montgomery, the World War Two general who outwitted his arch rival, and former prime minister Winston Churchill are on the list. So too is Ince.

"I didn't notice that before. I couldn't escape him," laughs Ferguson, who once called Ince a "big-time Charlie"., external

"I regret saying that. That was a mistake," Ferguson would later say.

The pair have since reconciled.

"He's a good friend of mine," says Ferguson. "He used to come over and play snooker with me. He texted me not so long ago."

'Beckham thought I was trying to get rid'

"You can't win anything with kids," former Liverpool and Scotland defender Alan Hansen said after a youthful United side lost 3-1 at Aston Villa in August 1995.

Ince, 27, and forward Mark Hughes, 31, had been moved on in the summer to Inter and Chelsea respectively.

Meanwhile, Ryan Giggs, 21, Gary Neville, 20, Scholes, 20, and David Beckham, 20, were beginning to make a name for themselves.

By the end of the season, Ferguson's side had won the Premier League and FA Cup double.

"We'd worked really hard getting youth into the club again and this bunch of young lads became the spirit of Manchester United," says Ferguson.

"They added something. Apart from the great abilities they had, they had desire. I put Beckham out on loan at Preston [in March 1995] and he thought I was trying to get rid of him, which was not true.

"David was the last to really develop because of his physique. Although he grew to 6ft, he was small and thin as a young kid."

Did Ferguson ever fear that throwing his young players in at the deep end could backfire?

"I did exactly the same when I was in charge at St Mirren and Aberdeen," he says.

"I had belief in young people because if you give them an opportunity there are two things that happen - they become real stars and they can remain loyal to you as a manager."

title: 瑞士宝盛集团宣布6亿瑞郎股票回购计划
content:
瑞士宝盛集团宣布了一项价值至多6亿瑞士法郎（7.23亿美元）的股票回购计划，此前集团瑞士监管机构刚刚宣布结束对该公司长达数年的调查。
贷款方还提出了修订后的资本分配政策。
该公司在一份声明中表示，“在获得监管部门批准并考虑到集团雄厚的资本实力后，宝盛集团董事会已批准此次股票回购计划。 ”
本周早些时候，瑞士金融市场监管局（Finma）结束了对宝盛集团（Julius Baer）的执法程序，该公司股价创下逾一年来的最大涨幅。此举消除了长期以来拖累其股价的不利因素。
宝盛集团当天表示，在瑞士金融市场监管局（FINMA）做出决定后，该公司正在寻求回购许可。

title: 花旗：小米集团-W维持“买入”评级 目标价34港元
content:
花旗发布研报称， 小米集团-W （01810）公布9月电动车交付量超过4万辆，该行维持“买入”评级及目标价34港元。
小米YU7新款GT车型交期已缩短至介于1至5周，与基础/长续航/Pro/Max版本相近；新款SU7基础/Pro/Max交付期介于5至8周，Ultra则仅有12月交付。
该行指出，小米于9月7日正式推出SkyNomad系列，N70/90首月交付突破1万辆；N70 Pro/Max交期为6至8周，N90 Max交期超过12周。1至9月累计交付逾28.6万辆，相当于该行2026年预测交付目标45万辆的64%。
该行认为，在料为今年最弱一季的第三季业绩公布前，小米近期股价或受压，但亦视此为具吸引力的入市时机。

title: 大摩：吉利汽车维持“增持”评级 目标价27港元
content:
大摩发布研报称，近期每周汽车数据亦显示，9月行业销售存在下行风险，主要原因是10月1日假期。该行予 吉利汽车 （00175）目标价27港元，给予“增持”评级。
该行提及，投资者可能正在等待关于潜在欧盟插电式混合动力车（PHEV）关税及出口增值税退税削减的更明确消息，才会增加曝险。然而，以该行基准情境约6倍估值计算，吉利的估值似乎日益具吸引力。吉利的规模、成本领导地位，以及自筹资金/自由现金流（FCF）的财务状况，应能使其在行业下行期间进一步强化竞争地位，这使吉利成为该行覆盖范围内相对较低风险、较高品质的中国汽车股投资部位。

title: 美联储本月加不加息？美国9月非农今晚揭晓 全球市场严阵以待
content:
转自：财联社
财联社10月2日讯（编辑 卞纯） 北京时间周五晚20：30，美国劳工统计局将公布9月非农就业报告。届时，围绕美国劳动力市场现状的诸多疑问将得到解答。 这份报告也将成为投资者判断美联储是否可能连续第二次加息的重要依据。
根据市场共识预测， 华尔街预计美国9月非农就业人数增加8.4万人，失业率预计维持在4.1% 。
虽然新增就业人数料将较2025年前的趋势有所放缓， 但美联储官员更加关注的失业率预计仍将处于表明“充分就业”的水平 。
而在预测市场，交易员对就业增长的预期比华尔街经济学家更乐观。Kalshi数据显示，市场认为美国9月非农新增就业人数超过9万的概率接近60%，新增就业人数超过10万的概率则大约为50%。
周三公布的 “小非农”ADP数据显示，9月美国私营部门新增就业9万人，超出经济学家预期，较8月修正后的3.6万人大幅增加。ADP首席经济学家Nela Richardson称此为一份强劲的报告。
将如何影响美联储加息预期？
在8月非农意外强劲增长16.2万人（且前几个月数据也被上修）之后，今晚发布的9月非农报告备受瞩目。
美联储官员将通过这份数据确认美国劳动力市场的韧性。该央行的双重使命是实现充分就业和维持物价稳定。过去数月，由于劳动力市场表现稳健，美联储将政策重点放在抑制通胀上。
若周五公布的非农就业报告符合预期，将确认就业市场在各种经济压力下仍颇具韧性，包括各类贷款利率上升、伊朗战争导致燃油价格上涨等；若非农就业报告超预期，则美联储加息的可能性或有所上升；而如果就业市场意外走弱，美联储内部的鹰派声音可能会受到抑制。
罗素投资策略师日前表示，倘若美国9月非农就业数据超出市场预期，会构成阶段性利空，将强化美联储年内再度加息的必要性。
Plante Moran Financial Advisors首席投资官Jim Baird表示，市场可能更愿意看到一份“不错但并不过热”的就业报告。如果新增就业明显过强，可能进一步巩固10月再次加息的理由，并对市场造成短期压力。
“在劳动力市场方面，广泛的数据表明状况已经企稳。新增就业数据虽存在一定波动，但近几个月就业增长已扩展至多个行业，这令人鼓舞。裁员人数保持低位，职位空缺数量总体上略有回升。”美联储副主席菲利普·杰斐逊周四在演讲中表示。
此前，市场一度认为，美联储在9月加息25个基点后，很可能会在10月再次加息。不过，周三公布的较预期更为温和的个人消费支出（PCE）指数以及美联储官员本周的讲话削弱了这一预期。
纽约联储主席约翰·威廉姆斯周二表示，鉴于美联储本月早些时候已经加息了一次，目前没有迫切采取行动的必要。
美联储副主席菲利普·杰斐逊周四呼应了威廉姆斯的观点。他表示，决策者可能需要更多时间，才能判断是否有必要进一步加息。
支持美联储需关注通胀但不必急于再次加息的核心依据是，是美国劳动力虽相对稳定，但也不算特别火爆。此外，薪资增长也有所放缓，9月平均时薪预期同比增长3.1%，低于年初的约4%。
过去几天，美联储加息预期持续降温。据CME“美联储观察”，目前美联储10月会议维持利率在3.75%-4.00%不变的概率为75.6%， 加息25个基点的概率为24.4% 。而在PCE数据公布前，这一概率大约为50%。
（财联社 卞纯）

title: Travelodge review 'emotional read' for security victim
content:
A woman who experienced a naked man performing sex acts outside her Travelodge hotel room says a review into the chain's security was an "emotional read".

Wendy Griffith was one of dozens of people who shared their stories after the BBC revealed how a woman woke up to a man sexually assaulting her in her bed at the chain's Maidenhead branch in December 2022 after staff gave him a key card and her room number.

Griffith said she felt "sadness and frustration that women had to go through these experiences" for the review to happen and she wants lessons to be learnt across the industry.

Travelodge said it welcomes the recommendations from the report and changes have been under way since March.

Marketing consultant Griffith, from Norfolk, was staying at Travelodge London Stratford in July 2025 when she said a man started banging on her door.

She then witnessed him through the door's peephole performing sex acts.

She recalled "rising panic" over the hour as she was "essentially trapped" in the middle of the night, trying and failing "multiple times" to contact hotel staff.

With no room phone and no emergency contact number in her room, she used her mobile to try to call the Travelodge website number.

She said she was "incredibly traumatised and not able to summon help", then dialled 999 in desperation.

The man, Trevor Reece, 40, pleaded guilty to outraging public decency in September 2025.

He was sentenced by magistrates to four months of alcohol dependency treatment and ordered to pay £185 court costs and £50 compensation to his victim, which Griffith says has yet to be paid.

She subsequently discovered that during a lull in the hour she was targeted, her tormentor - who was also a hotel guest - had gone to reception and asked for a replacement room key. He gave her room number instead of his own.

She said he was only refused because the clerk told her he knew the man was a long-staying guest, and the number he gave was not his own room.

A review carried out by barrister Paul Greaney KC found room intrusions were reported at nearly one in 10 Travelodge hotels this summer and no policy was in place on violence against women and girls.

Travelodge interim chief executive Ray Reidy told the BBC the company was working with the Suzy Lamplugh Trust - a personal safety charity - to develop one.

'Sadness and frustration'

Griffith said she had found the review "quite emotional to read" and described it as "galling".

"I mean, there's validation in it, but there's also real sadness and frustration that women had to go through these experiences before the issues were taken this seriously," she said.

"It's terrible to think that it's just taken years and years for this to come to life and such serious incidences for people to realise what's been going on and how companies like Travelodge have been behaving."

The company, which is based in Thame, Oxfordshire, said in its response to the review: "Travelodge would like to unreservedly apologise again to the woman assaulted and to all guests where Travelodge has fallen short due to failures in its policies and procedures for room access security and in its response to complaints."

Griffith said prior to her ordeal, she would "regularly travel on my own".

"I treat travel now and security in particular in hotel rooms so differently," she added.

Carolyn Pearson, CEO of travel security company Maiden Voyage, said handing a room key to someone claiming to be a guest's boyfriend is an "incredibly basic" failure, but one that is "unfortunately very common across the industry".

"This is not just a Travelodge issue," she added.

Pearson said hotels "should never ever confirm whether or not a guest is staying at the hotel or not".

Dawn Brennan, CEO of women's safety charity Wise Women, said: "We would say that no one should be getting access to any rooms unless they're registered and also provide an ID.

"But even further than that considering women's safety, the hotel should have policies in place where they double check as well if it's a partner that's coming to the reception and they don't have the key."

Griffith said she believed security and safety at hotels was an "industry-wide problem" and has set up a petition calling on the government to implement minimum safety and guest security standards across all hotels in the UK.

As the law stands at present, primarily, the hotel and its management are responsible for the safety of guests.

Each hotel, or chain, will have its own security policy which staff should abide by.

Griffith said: "What has kept me speaking up about this is the fact that so many people have been affected, in particular women, and something positive has to come from these incidences.

"Change has to happen and I've said throughout a locked hotel room should mean exactly that. Locked, safe, yours.

"What I want now is for the lessons from this review to go beyond Travelodge and help create clear national standards across the hotel industry."

Your Voice

title: 芝加哥期权交易所拟推出“恐慌指数”VIX永续期货
content:
美国最大衍生品交易所芝加哥期权交易所（Cboe Global Markets）正探索上市挂钩Cboe波动率指数（VIX，“恐慌指数”）的永续期货。该产品若落地，这类无到期日的合约将首次让投资者能够直接押注VIX现货水平。
在纽约当地时间1日举行的彭博情报衍生品市场结构会议的永续期货专题研讨会上，Cboe全球衍生品业务主管罗布·霍金称：“举例来说，我们正在研究的方向之一就是VIX永续期货。”他表示，一旦美国针对永续期货的监管框架明朗，交易所就会推进上市工作。
VIX衡量标普500指数期权投资者对未来30天市场波动率的预期。它是金融市场引用最广泛的指标之一，但目前无法直接交易指数本身的现货点位。
“现在没有办法交易VIX现货，”霍金解释道，“一直有人问Cboe：我该如何投资VIX现货？迄今为止，还没有合适的工具。”
Cboe现已上市VIX期货与期权，市场上也有跟踪VIX的交易所交易基金（ETF）。但这类产品持有的是VIX衍生品，并非VIX本身，无法完美跟踪这一波动率指标；在常规市场环境下，产品还存在投资成本偏高的短板。事实上，ProShares VIX短期期货ETF2026年年内跌幅已达34%。
永续期货没有到期日，并设有资金费率机制，使合约价格贴近现货价格。由于自带杠杆，该产品既能放大收益，也会放大亏损。
霍金表示：“我认为永续期货会是非常好的解决方案。”
从加密市场走向传统资产
永续期货最初是加密货币市场的高杠杆品种。美国头部投资平台罗宾侠本周宣布，将面向美国客户开放比特币、以太坊永续期货最高10倍杠杆交易；其他加密货币永续期货最高杠杆为3倍。
Cboe此举，是美国传统交易所的大趋势：把已经在加密市场得到验证的永续期货，拓展到其他资产类别。
曾在高盛担任股票波动率交易员的霍金指出，期权相较永续期货仍具备显著优势。“期权也可以实现相近杠杆，但不同之处在于，期权拥有非线性收益结构，线性产品做不到这一点。”
他补充道：“买入期权，上行收益几乎可以呈抛物线增长，价格越是朝着对你有利的方向变动，利润增速就越快。”和永续期货不同，期权买方的最大亏损仅限于已支付的权利金，这是另一项核心差异。
与标普续约25年
本周，Cboe将与标普道琼斯指数公司（S&P DJI）的独家授权协议延长25年，有效期至2051年。这份协议保障Cboe在未来数十年拥有标普500指数（SPX）及其他标普道琼斯指数挂钩产品的期权上市权。
自1983年Cboe首次推出挂钩标普500的期权以来，双方合作已逾40年。2025年SPX期权成交量达创纪录的9.706亿张合约，同比上涨25%，机构与个人投资者都更多利用指数期权开展对冲与收益增强策略。
Cboe首席执行官克雷格·多诺休表示：“本次续约，让我们能在未来长期做大SPX与VIX两大核心业务。”标普道琼斯指数CEO卡瓦·克莱称：“投资者对美股的需求持续攀升，我们看到进一步深化合作的巨大空间。”
联合探索代币化期权
在续约之外，两家机构宣布计划联合研发代币化期权合约，这是将指数衍生品引入区块链结算体系的初步尝试。产品具体上线时间、合约结构、所使用的区块链网络均尚未确定。Cboe称代币化项目仅处于探索阶段，并非确定落地产品。
这一动作契合行业大势：传统交易所与指数服务商都在研究传统金融产品的区块链版本，包括代币化股票、代币化货币市场基金。随着美国监管机构对区块链市场基础设施态度趋于包容，这一转型势头不断增强。
这份长达25年的合约本身就极具意义。此前竞争对手曾在法庭挑战SPX期权独家授权的部分条款，将独家权益锁定至2051年，为Cboe锁定数十年业务稳定。对标普道琼斯指数而言，也获得一家长期合作方，在上市衍生品市场推广其基准指数。
Cboe旗舰产品标普500指数期权每日名义交易规模约4.5万亿美元。短期期权尤其受到愿意承担更高风险的个人投资者追捧；若永续期货成功上线，有望承接一部分这类投资者需求。
霍金呼吁监管机构出台更清晰的永续期货监管标准：“这类产品拥有巨大应用与创新空间，但我们需要监管层面的明确指引。在开局之前，你得先清楚游戏规则。”

title: 普京：很快所有人都得开中国车
content:
10月1日，俄罗斯总统普京在“瓦尔代”国际辩论俱乐部全体会议上表示，由于欧洲汽车市场正陷入深度衰退，很快所有车主都可能换开中国汽车。
普京表示： “欧洲的汽车工业在哪里？企业正在关闭。我们很快都将开上中国汽车。这是好是坏我不知道，但便宜且质量好。”
普京驳斥了西方国家关于中国汽车“产能过剩”的指责，并提醒市场的基本原则——最终结果永远由消费者需求决定。 他强调，如今不仅欧洲汽车工业处于深度危机和严重困境，欧洲的冶金、相关行业以及化工和制药工业也是如此。
“瓦尔代”国际辩论俱乐部是一个由外国和俄罗斯的政治学、经济学、历史学和国际关系领域的顶尖专家组成的协会。

title: Pro-Russian parties jostle with Kyiv supporters in crowded Latvian election
content:
Henry Foy

Published October 2 2026

Good morning. A scoop to start: Vladimir Putin has instructed his military leaders to abandon the rules of conflict, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the FT in an interview , citing intelligence briefings that the Russian president had told his generals: “There are no rules now.”

Today, we preview tomorrow’s parliamentary election in Latvia, and the Netherlands’ justice minister says a freeze on EU funds to Sierra Leone is a triumph for justice.

Have a cracking weekend.

This article is an on-site version of our Europe Express newsletter. Premium subscribers can sign up here to get the newsletter delivered every weekday and fortnightly on Saturday morning. Standard subscribers can upgrade to Premium here , or explore all FT newsletters

Latvians head to the polls tomorrow following a government crisis in May, in an election that’s likely to deliver further uncertainty for the Nato member on the alliance’s eastern flank as Russia escalates its threats, writes Paola Tamma .

Context: Polls open on Saturday and seven parties are forecast to clear the 5 per cent threshold necessary to enter the 100-seat parliament, according to a poll released last month and commissioned by Latvian public broadcaster LTV. The campaign has been dominated by socio-economic issues, although parties still largely position themselves around Latvia’s ethnic-linguistic divide.

United List, the party of Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, a staunch Ukraine supporter, has a comfortable lead, polling at 14.4 per cent.

Coming second and third, with over 9 per cent of the voting share each, are two parties courting Latvia’s substantial Russian-speaking minority — Sovereign Power and Latvia First — which are either openly pro-Russia or call for an easing of sanctions against Moscow.

Trailing them with around 5 to 6 per cent of the vote each come the Progressives, a green-affiliated party, National Alliance, a staunchly anti-Russian party, and the Union of Greens and Farmers.

In a spectacular fall from grace, New Unity, the centre-right party of former premier Evika Siliņa, is polling below the threshold at 4.3 per cent. Siliņa resigned following the mishandling of Ukrainian drones crashing into the Baltic country. Almost 15 per cent of Latvians polled said they would not vote.

Kulbergs has ruled out an alliance with Sovereign Power, the more outspokenly pro-Russia party, whose leader Jūlija Stepaņenko has faced scrutiny over financial gifts of €420,000 from her father, a Russian-based businessman whose company supplied concrete anti-tank barriers used by Russian forces.

But he has been more nuanced on other potential coalition partners. Analysts agree that no single party will win an outright majority; the most likely outcome is a coalition government built around Kulbergs’ party, although coalition partners depend considerably on who clears the 5 per cent hurdle for parliamentary representation.

Europe should take Donald Trump’s diesel ban seriously, if not literally, writes Lex — it is a sign that the continent can no longer rely on the US being an unconditional supplier of energy.

The EU has postponed aid for Sierra Leone after the Dutch government pressured Brussels to cut off money to Freetown unless it extradited a wanted drug lord, writes Laura Dubois .

Context: Dutch authorities have said Sierra Leone should not receive EU aid unless it extradites Jos Leijdekkers, a Dutchman who was sentenced for cocaine trafficking and other charges in the Netherlands and Belgium. The Hague believes he is hiding out in Sierra Leone under the protection of the authorities.

The European Commission this week said it would postpone €18mn in direct budget support to Sierra Leone’s government planned for this year — a move immediately celebrated as a success by Dutch justice minister David van Weel.

“I’m very happy with that,” van Weel told the FT. “I think that every pressure we can apply to Sierra Leone to finally co-operate on the extradition of Mr Jos Leijdekkers should be used.”

According to the Commission, the aid was suspended because certain conditions for it to be paid out could not be met. “It’s due to technical reasons that the disbursement for 2026 was suspended,” said home affairs commissioner Magnus Brunner yesterday.

Commission spokesperson Guillaume Mercier said the aid was “currently under assessment and no disbursement is currently planned” and added that the EU was “closely monitoring drug trafficking and, more broadly, trends in transnational organised crime in Sierra Leone and across the wider west Africa region”.

Van Weel, however, waved these technicalities away. “It’s up to the Commission to do their own spokesperson [work],” he said. “I consider this a very welcome event in light of the pressure that we’re trying to build up towards Sierra Leone.”

title: 美民主党参议员质询：五角大楼收购委内瑞拉石油公司合规吗？
content:
美国参议院民主党人正对五角大楼计划收购一家委内瑞拉石油公司股权的方案，质疑其合法性与审慎性，为后续可能开展的相关调查铺垫基础。
四名资深参议院民主党议员在致特朗普政府高层的信函中表示，五角大楼拟收购北美蓝能源伙伴公司（NABEP，委内瑞拉第二大石油生产商）股权的交易法律基础薄弱，还会损害该国走向民主转型的进程。
美国于9月初公布方案，五角大楼将取得NABEP公司35%的被动股权。该公司将获得17个石油区块的控制权，据称区块石油储量约650亿桶。委内瑞拉称本国已探明石油储量达3000亿桶，位居全球首位。作为交易安排的一部分，美国国务院将拥有按成本价采购该油田20%产量的优先购买权。
自1月尼古拉斯·马杜罗下台后，特朗普一直推动美国石油产业重振委内瑞拉油田。他将这笔与NABEP的交易称作“世界史上最大石油交易”。
这批议员包括参议院外交委员会民主党首席议员珍妮·沙欣（新罕布什尔州），他们要求特朗普政府在交易敲定前，提交协议文本与全部条款。
议员们同时要求美方说明，五角大楼战略资本办公室收购外国石油公司股权的法律依据，并询问国务院将如何支付采购该石油公司产出原油的款项。
特朗普政府称，这笔交易能够降低美国民众的燃油成本，原油将用于补充美国战略石油储备。目前该储备处于1982年以来最低水平。
参议员们在致国务卿马尔科·鲁比奥、国防部长皮特·赫格塞思、能源部长克里斯·赖特的信函中写道：“这份拟议协议很难降低美国高昂的能源成本，还存在破坏委内瑞拉人民摆脱独裁、推进转型进程的风险。”
美国国务院全球公共事务助理国务卿迪伦·约翰逊表示，民主党参议员数周前就知晓政府官员计划于周四向其通报情况并提供文件，但参议员取消了原定周四上午的会议。约翰逊称：“这纯粹是哗众取宠。”
另外三名议员也共同签署了该信函：参议院军事委员会民主党首席议员杰克·里德（罗德岛州）、参议院能源与自然资源委员会民主党首席议员马丁·海因里希（新墨西哥州），以及参议院银行、住房和城市事务委员会首席议员伊丽莎白·沃伦（马萨诸塞州）。
众议院民主党人也向政府发出了类似信函。
议员通常会向机构、企业或相关各方发函索要资料，以此为国会调查铺路。但任何后续调查大概率要等到11月中期选举之后才会启动，且取决于民主党选举结果。目前民主党属于少数党，相关委员会主席均不由民主党担任，无权召开公开听证会或签发传票。
参议员在信函中要求鲁比奥、赫格塞思与赖特说明政府的尽职审查流程，并披露特朗普家族或其捐赠者是否会从该交易中获益。议员同时质疑，由商人亚历杭德罗·贝坦库特执掌的这家委内瑞拉石油生产商，能否快速将产量提升至特朗普政府所暗示的规模。
NABEP方面推进迅速，已筹备60台钻井平台、30台用于输送重油的蒸汽锅炉以及数十套重型设备。公司希望到2028年末，原油产量实现翻倍以上，达到每日50万桶。
议员表示：“令人费解的是，为何美国公众应当支持这项交易，让美国与一家相对不知名的外国石油公司深度绑定。该公司缺乏开发如此规模油田的能力与公信力，其管理层还面临国际刑事调查。”
议员指出，贝坦库特虽未被提起刑事指控，但“曾在西班牙、瑞士和美国多次受到洗钱相关调查”。鲁比奥则称贝坦库特在美国并未处于正在进行的调查之中。
媒体报道，五角大楼战略资本办公室将通过低价认股权证完成对NABEP的投资，美国可在不投入大额资本金的前提下获得这家企业的股权。
民主党人认为，设立该五角大楼办公室的法律条文并未授予其收购私营石油公司股权的权限，这笔交易超出了该机构的法定权责范围。该办公室的权限本是发放贷款与提供担保，服务于美国国家安全利益。
不少参与委内瑞拉民主进程的人士批评这笔交易。他们担忧，该交易会让美国与德尔西·罗德里格斯领导的现委内瑞拉政府绑定，罗德里格斯曾是马杜罗政府的副总统。
议员在信函中写道，这项计划“只会给美国与委内瑞拉制造新的腐败风险，看似是在奖励那种损公肥私的行为，而正是这类行为最初摧毁了委内瑞拉石油行业。长期来看，此类举动会损害美国在委内瑞拉乃至整个拉美地区的公信力。”

title: 特朗普再喊话：必须推动永久夏令时法案
content:
特朗普在社交媒体发文称，参议院的共和党人必须行动起来，推进我所称的《不再调时钟法案》，正式名称为《阳光保护法案》。
特朗普表示，每年两次调整时钟这套流程十分荒唐，耗费国家巨额资金，还会推高犯罪率、增加民众压力，影响体育赛事，几乎方方面面都会受波及。就连备受敬重的美巡赛总裁布莱恩・罗莱普也支持这项法案——冬季办高尔夫赛事时，经常会早早天黑，赛事难以完赛。民众不想再反复调时钟。而且绝大多数人更希望傍晚能多一小时日照，而非清晨。
众议院已于2026年7月14日以308票赞成、117票反对通过该法案，获得跨党派大力支持。民主党与共和党都希望法案落地。现在轮到美国参议院，这有望成为又一场重大的两党合作胜利。遗憾的是，阿肯色州参议员汤姆・科顿不知出于何种理由，搁置了这项法案。
民众早已厌倦一年两次调时钟。就连大多数农民，也更希望傍晚有更长日照时间收割庄稼。调时既愚蠢又麻烦，有时成本高昂。设有瞭望塔、地处偏远的城市与州，为此要花费数百万美元。近期研究还表明，调时带来的焦虑会损害健康。
特朗普称，权威医学、犯罪学与经济学研究得出明确结论：取消一年两次的时间调整，让傍晚永久多一小时自然光，将有助于降低抢劫与谋杀案件，减少车祸（尤其是行人交通事故！），降低心脏病、中风与季节性抑郁症风险；让孩子放学步行回家更安全，增加家庭共处时间，大力支持课外文体活动；提振体育、健身、旅游、零售与餐饮等行业；还能节省电费，人人都能享受额外一小时日光。
简单来说，就维持当前时间，永久不再调钟。最重要的一点：几乎所有人都不想一年两次调整时钟。这是共和党、民主党和无党派人士可以共同支持的议题。

title: 美国能源信息署：上半年出口大增后，美国丙烷出口量高于五年均值
content:
美国能源信息署（EIA）称，受中东供应中断影响，2026年上半年美国丙烷出口量攀升，对印度等市场的出口持续维持在远高于五年均值的水平。
EIA周四在报告中表示，依托创纪录产量，加上对印度及其他南亚国家的出口，上半年出口量同比增长11%，达到每日200万桶。
4月出口量创下每日210万桶的纪录，“受石化产品需求上升，以及进口商寻求货源替代中断的中东供货所推动”。
丙烷产量提升，使得美国相对亚洲的价格更具优势，竞争力超过其他地区货源。
美国丙烷出口总量增长或将受到出口产能瓶颈，以及厄尔尼诺引发的巴拿马运河持续干旱问题制约。
另外，大型出口商企业产品伙伴公司预计将于今年完成休斯顿航道与尼德兰码头的扩建项目，新增每日30万桶出口能力。

title: Black voters rally against new electoral maps in the US South
content:
Guy Chazan in Baton Rouge, Louisiana

Published October 2 2026

Like many Black voters across the South, Asti Robins is furious. And the anger is so powerful, she says, it could shape the outcome of November’s midterms.

The cause: new Republican-backed electoral maps that critics say will dilute the voting power of African Americans. There would be a reckoning, Robins predicted. “Black voter turnout will be huge. People are energised.”

An environmental campaigner, Robins lives in Louisiana’s sixth congressional district, a majority-Black constituency that was redrawn by the state’s Republican-controlled legislature.

Louisiana was a bastion of the slaveholding economy before the civil war and Black people still make up 32 per cent of the state’s population. It had two majority-Black districts to represent them, out of the state’s total of six. Now it has just one.

“Without representation, what is citizenship?” asked Ashley Shelton, founder of Power Coalition, a Louisiana non-profit focused on voting rights and civic engagement. “What is citizenship when my values, my experience of this country as a Black woman aren’t reflected in the halls of Congress?”

The boundary change came after a landmark April Supreme Court decision, Louisiana vs Callais, that ruled Robins’ district was an “unconstitutional racial gerrymander”.

Critics said the ruling gutted the 1965 Voting Rights Act, a central achievement of the civil rights era, which prohibited racial discrimination in voting. Supporters said the US constitution did not allow states to sort voters by race .

Electoral boundaries were traditionally redrawn every 10 years based on the census, but recently Republican- and Democratic-controlled states across the US have been remaking their electoral maps with increasing frequency in a tit-for-tat race to derive maximum partisan advantage. This year the process has been accelerated by President Donald Trump.

Republicans have been the main beneficiaries of the changes and are projected to net about four seats, according to the Cook Political Report.

But with Trump’s approval ratings at record lows and Republicans trailing Democrats in the polls, that advantage may not be big enough to preserve the party’s House majority in November.

Redistricting has largely been driven by politics. But in the South, race is never far from the surface. Over the past few months, Black communities in Louisiana, Alabama and Tennessee were “cracked”, or broken up and combined with larger white populations into new gerrymandered districts that critics say will reduce their ability to elect candidates of their choice.

The process means Cleo Fields, the Black Democratic lawmaker representing Louisiana’s sixth district, which is now majority white and overwhelmingly Republican, will soon be out of a job. He is retiring from national politics and will seek a state senate seat instead.

Fields is convinced the gerrymander will backfire. “People are going to show up in greater numbers [in November], particularly African Americans,” he said in an interview. “They are determined not to let their voices be silenced.”

It is unclear how much impact a Black voter surge in the South will have. The region is deep red: even in 2008, when a rise in Black turnout helped propel Barack Obama into the White House, all but three southern states voted Republican.

Black voters do not always vote Democrat, however. Republicans made big inroads in 2024, when Trump received 15 per cent of their vote, according to Pew Research, compared with 8 per cent in 2020.

But this year Black Democrats, backed by a newly galvanised base, are running across the South in places that were long seen as impregnable Republican strongholds.

Keisha Lance Bottoms, the Black former mayor of Atlanta, is in a close race with Republican Rick Jackson for the governorship of Georgia, an office held by Republicans for the past 23 years. In Mississippi, limited polling has put Scott Colom, a Black state prosecutor running for Senate, within striking distance of Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.

Voter apathy has long been a problem in deep southern states such as Louisiana. But Shelton believes that might be changing.

“You’re giving people something to stand up for,” she said. “You’re giving them a reason to say, ‘I have to pay attention, I need to understand.’

“The only answer to people taking away your voice and your power is to show up.”

For Black community leaders, the gerrymandering evokes dark memories of Jim Crow, the system that enforced racial segregation after the end of Reconstruction in 1877.

Leona Tate personifies the struggle to overcome that legacy. As a six-year-old girl in 1960, she had to be escorted by US federal marshals into her newly desegregated school in New Orleans through a crowd of yelling and cursing white people held back by police.

She remembers not being able to eat in the school cafeteria. “[The white students] were going to either knock the food out of your hand or they was going to spit in it,” she said in an interview. “Every school that I went to was the same thing, all the way through high school.”

The civil rights movement overcame the worst excesses of Jim Crow. But with redistricting, Tate says its gains are threatened. “I see a regression,” she said. “It feels like they’re just trying to erase all people of colour.”

In its April ruling, the Supreme Court’s conservative majority argued that the US had fundamentally changed since the 1960s when Black voters were blocked from voting by literacy tests and other obstacles. The legacy of that unequal treatment, the justices said, was no longer enough to justify drawing electoral districts along racial lines.

Fields agrees that the lot of African Americans has indeed improved. “But have we overcome all of the vices of discrimination? Absolutely not,” he said. “They need to walk in my shoes one or two days . . . just come and live my experience.”

Critics said the court’s ruling marked the culmination of years of legal efforts to unpick the VRA, a law that Justice Elena Kagan said in her dissent was “born of the literal blood of Union soldiers and civil rights marchers”.

Conservatives insist that most of the VRA remains intact. But detractors say that in purely practical terms the court’s ruling makes it much harder to challenge electoral maps that diminish Black voting power.

Louisiana was quick to enforce the judgment. Jay Morris, a Louisiana state senator, was one of the architects of the state’s new map, which he has admitted was “drawn to maximise Republican advantage”.

In an interview, Morris accused Democrats of doing the same. There were some blue states in the north-east where “30 or 40 per cent of the population votes Republican”, yet “there are zero Congress members from the Republican Party” being elected there, he said.

Morris said there was nothing undemocratic about the way Louisiana had changed its map. “That’s how democracy is defined — majority rules,” he added. “And we’re a majority-Republican state.”

Robins said the dissolution of the sixth district was a “gut-punch”, both for herself and her relatives. Her family hails from Alsen, a small community just outside Baton Rouge settled by former slaves who fought on the Union side during the civil war. The childhood summers she spent there, among the chickens, cows and pecan trees, were idyllic. But in recent years, it has become a tougher place to live.

The community sits at the northern end of a heavily industrialised corridor along the Mississippi River nicknamed “Cancer Alley”. It is hemmed in by a massive Exxon polymer plant and a sprawling landfill site. Locals complain of respiratory problems. “The smell will burn your nose,” Robins said.

Residents often felt overlooked. That changed in 2024, she said, with the creation of the new sixth district, of which Alsen was a part. The community felt newly hopeful. “We were sending a hometown guy from Baton Rouge to Congress,” Robins said. “People thought their voice would be heard on the federal level.”

Then came the Supreme Court decision and the new map. Robins said she felt deceived. “The state sends six representatives to Congress and this now means that only one of them [will] care about people who look like me — the descendants of slaves,” she said. “It felt like we’d taken two steps forward and been pushed back six.”

title: 知情人士：博通着手筹集600亿美元 为Anthropic采购芯片提供资金
content:
据知情人士透露，博通公司的华尔街承销团正着手筹集600亿美元全新AI芯片融资，受益方包括Anthropic以及其他企业。
知情人士称，这笔巨额债务方案涉及的多家银行即将发放420亿美元A类优先担保债的承销邀约函。
消息人士表示， 黑石 集团牵头180亿美元B类次级债，黑石旗下多只基金承诺出资90亿美元，剩余部分计划对外分销。
博通的一名发言人拒绝置评。
这项融资方案已经筹备数周，正受到华尔街与硅谷专业人士的密切关注。在社会舆论对数据中心建设产生抵触的背景下，市场希望借此确认投资者仍愿意持续投入AI基建。博通希望销售更多芯片与数据中心设备，以此挑战英伟达；而Anthropic这类AI企业则需要持续扩容算力。
知情人士在8月的谈判中表示，这笔潜在交易将帮助Anthropic等企业获得芯片与其他关键AI基础设施。 这笔融资，是已募集的数千亿美元AI基建债务的新增部分。虽然大部分资金用于建设数据中心，但用于采购芯片与服务器的融资交易也在不断增多。
8月，英伟达同样宣布与黑石等六大金融巨头合作，拟调动超5000亿美元资金投向AI领域，其中包含协助客户融资采购英伟达芯片。
与此同时，黑石对Anthropic的投资，推高了其面向高净值客户的私募股权基金业绩。

title: 申万宏源：泉峰控股处于价值重估阶段 维持“买入”评级
content:
申万宏源 发布研报成， 泉峰控股 （02285）作为全球户外动力设备领军企业，泉峰控股以EGO构筑品牌护城河、深度绑定劳氏渠道，正迎来渠道补库与替换周期共振、锂电化加速渗透的业绩拐点，处于盈利底部反转与价值重估阶段。维持公司2026-2028财年盈利预测为1.6/1.5/1.7亿美元，同比+66%/-7%/+13%，对应PE为10/11/10X，维持“买入”评级。
申万宏源主要观点如下：
①2025年底渠道商主动补库，趋势延续；②上一轮房地产周期触发爆发式购买潮对应2025-2027年集中替换窗口；③锂电OPE渗透率提升趋势确定，26H1公司推出约130款新产品，其中约90%为锂电产品。
EGO品牌护城河极深，平台生态飞轮已形成
①26H1OBM收入占比进一步提升至79.6%，EGO品牌在北美锂电OPE多个细分品类（手推式割草机、扫雪机、骑乘式割草机）市场份额排名第一；②电池平台持续拓展，电池保有量越大、生态越宽，护城河越深。体现平台扩张的强大动能；③深度嵌入劳氏（Lowe‘s）供应链和货架体系，短期内竞争对手难以复制。
除北美基本盘外，区域拓展与客群拓展构成公司中长期第二增长曲线
①区域拓展：2025年收购比荷卢地区渠道SDL，26H1在欧洲推出首款自动无线割草机器人，反响出色；②客群拓展：2B专业渠道开拓，26H1美国市场商用骑乘式割草机推广成功，为商用渠道重要里程碑。
风险提示： 美国关税政策变化、汇率波动、美国市场终端需求不及预期。

title: 野村：上调阿里巴巴-W2027财年经调整后净利预测7%
content:
野村发布研报称，预计阿里巴巴（09988）（BABA.US）即将公布的2027年度第二财季业绩将进一步彰显其人工智能（AI）策略布局。该行将阿里巴巴2027财年经调整后净利预测调高7%，主要得益于电商业务盈利预期的提升。该行给予阿里巴巴“买入”的投资评级及目标价178美元。
野村指，阿里巴巴进一步聚焦AI与云端业务。在参加阿里巴巴年度云栖大会后，该行对其AI云业务的前景更具信心。在中国AI生态系统中，鲜有企业能像阿里巴巴一样，在AI价值链的几乎每一个关键环节——涵盖芯片、基础设施、模型及AI应用——都占据如此稳固的优势地位。
野村与阿里巴巴的交流进一步印证了其观点：管理层已将重心向AI云业务倾斜，该业务正逐渐成为营收增长的重要引擎；与此同时，公司更加注重其他业务板块的盈利能力，旨在为AI领域的投资储备现金流。

title: 东吴证券：珍酒李渡维持“买入”评级 有望步入再成长周期
content:
东吴证券发布研报成，维持珍酒李渡（06979）“买入”评级，渠道模式创新已经过验证，后续业绩有望加速修复，维持此前盈利预测，预计2026~2028年公司non-IFRS归母净利预测为8.8、10.6、12.0亿元人民币，对应2026-2028年non-IFRSPE为25.8、21.6、18.9倍，考虑到公司走出调整期后的增长具有较强可持续性。
东吴证券主要观点如下：
复盘李渡：罕见逆势成长的次高端白酒品牌
白酒行业需求承压下，上行周期累计较多库存的次高端白酒企业普遍面临战略困境：既定表端业绩约束下，若选择以价换量，经销商库存或面临较大的减值损失，长期或选择放弃代理权；若坚持挺价，高价下动销流速减缓，经销商库存去化周期被动拉长，库存越去越多、且品牌市占率下降。因此次高端酒企在下行期普遍或主动、或被动的放弃表端业绩要求。不同于其他次高端酒企，李渡品牌逆势成长，1H26营收创下历年来的新高，集团内营收占比亦从2020年的15%提升至1H26的31%。
李渡品牌高成长背后折射出公司强大的操盘能力
复盘历史，李渡品牌在核心人物汤向阳先生的主导下，开创白酒体验式营销模式实现破局，近年来锚定“全国化+次高端”战略扩张。（1）产品端看，品牌打造具备差异化的高线光瓶产品形象，并通过“液体古董”、“喝一瓶、少一瓶”等品牌叙事打造稀缺性心智，资源投放上“以高带低”，优先锚定高端价格带圈层心智，近年来价格带向下延伸，错位进入品牌势能释放期。（2）渠道端看，公司打造“总舵-分舵-小舵”互动体验架构，注重C端意见领袖培育。高端产品以配额制保障稀缺性，流通产品注重供需平衡、低库存运转以保障经销商利益。（3）区域端看，品牌江西省内势能已成，正逐步走向全国化。
新老模式共振，公司有望步入再成长周期
该行认为：（1）品牌势能释放下，李渡品牌仍有较大成长空间。省内若对标其他地产酒企业，李渡市占率仍有较大提升空间。省外参考地产酒品牌培育路径，李渡品牌有望快速突破10亿元规模。（2）珍酒“万商联盟”模式有望加速扩散至全价格带：异业经销商“亦商亦客户”的属性，在使用自身代理产品进行社交活动时天然有助于产品完成消费群体圈层内部的传播，辅以公司的强操盘能力，有望引领经销商预期持续向上。同时吴董事长个人IP价值亦被市场低估：微信视频号自身具备成瘾性，且优先推送朋友点赞的视频，董事长IP视频高播放量下可通过经销商、KOL的点赞快速完成品牌价值主张的圈层传播。
风险提示： 宏观修复不及预期，次高端价格及费用竞争加剧，渠道库存消化不及预期等。

title: 知情人士：亚马逊计划向投资者出售价值80亿美元的英伟达芯片
content:
据知情人士透露， 亚马逊 正计划通过一家新设立的特殊载体，向外部投资者出售价值约80亿美元的英伟达高端芯片，以此优化资产负债表。
该公司近几周已与投资者展开洽谈，评估市场对该交易的意向。根据方案，亚马逊将把数千枚部署在美国各地数据中心的格雷斯·布莱克韦尔（Grace Blackwell）芯片剥离，转入一家特殊目的载体（SPV）。
随后亚马逊再向该特殊目的载体租回这些高端人工智能芯片，载体将通过发债引入外部投资者。通过将这批高价半导体资产转移给投资者，亚马逊可在资产负债表上转向更轻资产的运营模式。
亚马逊拒绝就此置评。
科技巨头正寻找创新方式，为巨额的数据中心基建投入融资，本次拟议操作正是在此背景下推出。这类基建的大部分成本，来自用于训练先进人工智能模型的芯片。
科技企业正在采用多种手段将债务移出资产负债表，以维持自身信用评级。企业会提供残值担保，向贷方承诺芯片或数据中心的未来价值，而不是直接举债为项目融资。该模式掩盖了科技巨头实际承担的风险规模。
投资者预期，依托亚马逊当前的双A评级，该载体有望获得投资级信用评级，从而吸引保险、养老金等更广泛的投资者参与交易。
知情人士补充称，亚马逊还计划出让该载体最高10%的股权，这意味着亚马逊将不再持有该实体任何股份。亚马逊与投资者之间的谈判仍在进行，方案存在变动可能。
知情人士表示，本次交易涉及的芯片由亚马逊采购或租赁而来，已部署在美国五个州的十余个数据中心，包括内华达州与弗吉尼亚州。
英伟达的格雷斯·布莱克韦尔芯片属于该公司最先进的产品之一，但很快会被更新的Vera Rubin芯片所替代。
OpenAI、Anthropic等头部人工智能实验室（亚马逊承诺对二者最高投资830亿美元）使用最新一代芯片训练模型；上一代芯片则继续用于业务应用运行。根据监管文件，亚马逊预计每一代半导体产品至少可使用五年。
预计亚马逊今年资本开支将达2200亿美元，绝大部分将投向旗下云业务AWS，用于采购高端芯片以及扩建人工智能数据中心。
亚马逊已通过资本市场筹措资金支撑该项投资。今年3月，公司公布计划发行约500亿美元公司债；因市场需求旺盛，募资规模从原定370亿美元上调。但7月发行250亿美元债券时，长期债券市场需求转弱，投资者要求更高收益率。
由图形处理器作为抵押的融资模式在CoreWeave这类公司中十分流行，这类企业凭借稳定的芯片获取能力进行借款融资。
为帮助客户降低借贷成本，英伟达在8月联合华尔街大型机构设立5000亿美元融资平台，承诺为最高125亿美元此类债务提供兜底支持。

title: 港股午评：恒指跌2.64%失守24000点 科指跌2.45% 科网股普跌 赛力斯涨超8%
content:

title: Meet Man City’s powerbroker
content:
Published October 2 2026

One thing to start: Monzo Bank is stepping up its efforts to court private equity investors after takeover talks with the Brazilian fintech giant Nubank collapsed over the up-to £10bn valuation the UK group was seeking.

And a scoop: Petrol station empire EG Group is delaying plans for an initial public offering until next year, opening up the possibility that the group will explore a sale.

Welcome to Due Diligence, your briefing on dealmaking, private equity and corporate finance. This article is an on-site version of the newsletter. Premium subscribers can sign up here to get the newsletter delivered every Tuesday to Friday. Standard subscribers can upgrade to Premium here , or explore all FT newsletters. Get in touch with us anytime: [email protected]

In today’s newsletter:

Khaldoon al-Mubarak’s big test

Will UBS ever leave Switzerland?

The go-to firm for corruption scandals

For eight years, the Premier League ’s probe into Manchester City’s finances has cast a pall over the club. And this week, those inquiries broke into explicit charges and allegations.

So when longtime former coach Pep Guardiola posted a message of solidarity to supporters of the club, his choice of image was telling: a picture of him next to City chair Khaldoon al-Mubarak , in a warm embrace.

Mubarak has been the face of Abu Dhabi investment in the football club, as royal owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan has stayed in the shadows.

The FT’s Chloe Cornish and DD’s Arash Massoudi profiled Mubarak, the Abu Dhabi power broker, and how the scandal for City has forced him into a position of now having to defend both the club and his own reputation.

During Mubarak’s tenure, the club has gone from mid-table plodder to one of the most successful teams in European football. Mubarak has been there for all of it: he regularly attends games at the Etihad Stadium , where he’s been seen lifting trophies from eight Premier League title wins as well as the Champions League .

But after a damning verdict last week found City guilty of more than 100 violations of the Premier League’s financial rules, Mubarak must manage the firestorm of reputational damage to Abu Dhabi, whose image has become tightly intertwined with the club’s.

An independent commission found that the club had inflated its income and hidden its costs to the tune of more than £900mn over a period of almost a decade.

The club has until Friday to lodge a formal appeal against the findings of an independent commission. Meanwhile, Etihad Airways , the team’s biggest sponsor, has threatened legal action against the Premier League.

Mubarak and City have vowed to fight the charges, which they strenuously deny. And attention will return to the pitch soon. When the Premier League kicks off again on October 10, City will be sitting top of the table.

But chairing City is far from Mubarak’s only job.

He’s one of the United Arab Emirates’ most powerful non-royals as chief executive of Mubadala and as the point person for several important diplomatic relationships, including with China. As a sign of just how powerful he is, when Abu Dhabi secured a seat on Donald Trump ’s Board of Peace this year, Mubarak got the slot.

At Mubadala, Mubarak’s not only the world’s longest-serving head of a sovereign investment fund but one of the main figures overseeing Abu Dhabi’s more than $1.5tn in wealth.

For the heads of hedge funds and investment firms globally, that makes him one of the most important people to know.

“The power he holds is massive,” said one executive at a large global investment firm. “But he does it from behind the scenes.”

But despite all of the allegations levelled against the football club in recent days, Mubarak, at least personally, appears to have some protection. He was placed on the UK’s official list of approved diplomats in 2020, which automatically gives immunity from any criminal investigation and in most cases shields the person from civil proceedings on UK soil.

The political battle over UBS ’s future in Switzerland is already heated. Now one of its influential shareholders has entered the fray, with a simple suggestion: leave.

Artisan Partners , whose funds own 1.8 per cent of the bank, wrote to the Swiss bank’s board this week arguing that Switzerland was “no longer an attractive or desirable location” following moves to impose tougher capital requirements.

The Milwaukee-based asset manager reckons the rules could force UBS to hold an additional $16bn of common equity and cost shareholders as much as $36bn in foregone market value.

UBS politely pushed back, saying its “goal is to continue operating successfully as a global bank from Switzerland”.

But leaving is not entirely theoretical. UBS has explored contingency plans for moving abroad if the rules prove too onerous. Chair Colm Kelleher has even privately discussed with US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent what shifting the bank’s headquarters to the US could look like.

And Artisan is worth watching. It’s not an activist investor by trade, but the long-only fund manager has form when it decides to speak up.

In 2021, it publicly criticised Danone ’s strategy and governance and pushed for changes at the top. Chair and chief executive Emmanuel Faber was ousted weeks later from the French consumer goods company amid mounting shareholder pressure. Artisan has made itself heard in Switzerland before, too. That same year it backed activist investor Third Point ’s push for change at Richemont , arguing there was “significant unrecognised value” in the Cartier owner.

Artisan has not gone full activist at UBS — at least not yet. But its intervention adds another complication to an increasingly febrile debate over the bank’s Swiss future.

For corruption in the basketball world, Wachtell Lipton may now be the go-to law firm. In August, the report prepared by the firm for the National Basketball Association on the topic of alleged salary cap misconduct at the Los Angeles Clippers was so damning that the team’s owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for the year.

The FT on Thursday scooped that Wachtell had hired Joon Kim , a Cleary Gottlieb white-collar litigation partner who previously had a distinguished run at the US Attorney’s Office in Manhattan.

His famed cases as a federal prosecutor include the high-profile charges he brought in 2017 against US college basketball coaches accused of a wide-ranging kickback scheme.

In other Southern District of New York matters, Kim took on Steven Cohen , the hedge fund manager, and Ross Ulbricht , the mastermind of Silk Road , the illicit online marketplace.

Wachtell’s litigation group had been looking for a rebound.

Over the summer, its ace litigator and firm co-chair abruptly left for Gibson Dunn with several colleagues. Kim’s hiring shows the M&A powerhouse isn’t throwing in the towel when it comes to putting lawyers up for clients’ court fights.

The firm very rarely makes outside lateral hires so landing Kim is a big deal and shows that Wachtell wants to play offence.

The firm is down to roughly 20 litigation partners, almost half its corporate partner roster. Don’t be surprised if there are more free-agent signings at Wachtell coming.

KPMG’s global general counsel Anne Collins has left the firm as part of a wider executive reshuffle. She attracted scrutiny for her handling of whistleblower allegations that rocked the accounting firm in Australia.

JPMorgan executive chair of global investment banking Hernan Cristerna is retiring from banking after 30 years at the bank and will step down at the end of the year.

Linklaters has hired Mohammed Almarzouki as a corporate partner in Riyadh. He joins from Clyde & Co .

Houlihan Lokey has hired Jacques Bitton as a senior adviser in France. He previously worked at Société Générale .

Living large Changpeng Zhao, the former Binance chief executive who was jailed in the US, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates, the New York Times reports .

Who’s who In a deep dive about the secretive trading house Jane Street, Bloomberg digs into the relatively unknown people behind the firm, including the management committee, decision makers, founders and notable alumni.

title: UK universities comb records for China links after MI5 warning
content:
Michael Peel , Charles Clover and Lucy Fisher in London

Published October 2 2026

UK universities were racing on Thursday to meet an MI5-driven order to cut ties with a Chinese research organisation, prompting fresh calls for official help to cover national security compliance costs as geopolitical tensions rise.

The educational institutions have been combing their records since Wednesday’s espionage alert , which said the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) secretly channelled funding from Beijing’s intelligence apparatus to more than 100 UK-linked academics.

The UK domestic security agency’s unusually specific alert highlights growing pressure on the country’s leading universities to carry out deep vetting of collaborations with Chinese institutions, particularly in sensitive technological fields with potential military uses.

“[Universities] have become very much better at this over the past few years, but we still have to recognise that it’s patchy,” said Sir Peter Mathieson, the University of Edinburgh’s vice-chancellor. “Not every university has the same level of sophistication around national security — and not every university has the same needs.”

MI5 was “very respectful of academic freedom and institutional autonomy” but the security agency did not “necessarily show us its workings”, Mathieson added.

None of the universities or sector representative bodies contacted by the FT since the MI5 alert has said it has found evidence of a relationship with the CGTRI.

However, MI5 has not identified the more than 100 academics it cited nor said how many of the cases were current and which were historic, university representatives said.

The MI5 alert also acknowledged universities might have “engaged with CGTRI in good faith”, as the Chinese body had “obfuscated” its links to the Chinese Ministry of State Security.

The announcement triggered a letter by security minister Dan Jarvis to all UK university vice-chancellors asking them to end arrangements with CGTRI.

The security agency’s work on CGTRI had exposed Chinese intelligence efforts to “covertly benefit from the expertise and research of our academics, undermining our national security and that of our allies”, Jarvis said.

China’s embassy in London has condemned what it called “baseless allegations”.

“The accusations made by the UK intelligence agency against the relevant Chinese entity are imaginary and purely fabricated,” it said in a previous statement.

In 2024, the previous Conservative administration summoned university vice-chancellors for a briefing from the intelligence agencies on hostile powers targeting British academia.

It came after the creation in 2021 of the Research Collaboration Advice Team, a government unit that provides advice to universities on national security risks linked to international research.

George Freeman, an MP and a former minister for science, said a government review he commissioned in 2022-23 identified about 400 links between China and Britain’s research and innovation system. This included 40 collaborations that were “red-flagged” by the research collaboration advice team.

He said the MI5 public warning “suggests these red-flag exposures have still not been properly reviewed. They need to be, urgently.”

The current Labour government is planning to publish a fresh research security strategy, bolstered by a new research security fund, in the coming months.

The fund is a recognition of the increased compliance costs universities face in analysing proposed Chinese partners, including whether they have other affiliations with the country’s military and security agencies.

Ben Moore, associate director for international policy at the Russell Group of 24 research-intensive universities, said the association had long called for such a fund to “protect sensitive research and proactively tackle threats as they emerge”.

He added: “It’s encouraging to see government taking steps towards this and we’ll continue to work with them closely as more details are confirmed.”

title: Monzo courts private equity after Nubank walks away
content:
Laith Al-Khalaf

Published October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

Monzo Bank is stepping up its efforts to court private equity investors after takeover talks with the Brazilian fintech giant Nubank collapsed over the up-to £10bn valuation the UK group was seeking.

The digital bank has in recent weeks held early-stage discussions with the European buyout group CVC and US private equity firm Advent International about selling a significant stake in the group. People familiar with the matter said Monzo was seeking to sell a stake of up to 15 per cent.

They added that a sale to a private equity fund was now the preferred option for Monzo after takeover talks with Nubank fell through and that Monzo’s advisers would turn their efforts to engaging with more fund managers.

Monzo had been trying to clinch a sale to Nubank in a deal that would have valued the UK fintech at £10bn. New York-listed Nubank, which has a market capitalisation of about $65bn, said on Wednesday that it would not be pursuing a deal.

People familiar with the matter said that the sides were unable to agree a price and that Nubank had instead decided to concentrate on growing in its home market and the US, where it has recently secured a banking licence.

Monzo could yet pursue a third option: tapping venture capital investors for a more traditional fundraising round. However, one person familiar with the board’s thinking said Monzo would prefer the private equity option as it would probably be a far larger investment and give Monzo access to more cash for growth.

Monzo, Nubank, Advent and CVC declined to comment.

Monzo has endured a difficult year, with a bruising fight between its board and investors over the company’s international expansion plans and long-awaited initial public offering.

The fintech’s board ousted then-chief executive TS Anil because of concerns about the pace of growth and whether he was committed to the business for the long term — a move that angered the company’s biggest investors.

Anil ultimately remained on the board, but was replaced as CEO by former Google executive Diana Layfield. Since taking the helm in February, Layfield has closed Monzo’s US offices and switched the focus of expansion plans to Europe, opening offices in Spain and securing a European banking licence from Irish authorities.

Anil — who stayed on as an adviser to Layfield — along with Monzo’s chief financial officer and former Nubank executive Tom Oldham helped broker the takeover talks, according to people familiar with the deliberations.

When asked last month about whether there would be more consolidation among direct-to-consumer fintechs, Oldham demurred. “I’m not sure on the consolidation point,” he told the FT. “I think we’re really just focused on growing our customer base at pace.”

He added: “If we see other great companies that are delivering against one of our customers’ needs, and we think that’s a good cultural fit for us, that’s a company that we like, then for sure we would look.”

But behind the scenes, São Paulo-based Nubank had identified Monzo as providing a potential foothold in Europe.

“You cannot look at the deal without looking at Revolut,” said one senior technology banker of Nubank’s interest in Monzo.

“If you’re looking at it from a financial point of view, the deal doesn’t make sense for anyone. But Monzo as a platform could turbocharge Nubank into developed markets, handing them a banking licence and more customers than Revolut in its own market.”

Although Monzo is a similar age to Revolut, it has long since been overshadowed by its larger rival. Revolut has grown to become a global player with 80mn customers and a $115bn valuation. Monzo reported just 15mn customers this year.

Nubank, which launched in 2013, has 140mn customers. But they are mainly in Latin America, and the company is seeking to take on Nik Storonsky’s Revolut to become the world’s dominant fintech.

Both have already secured US banking licences in recent months, while Revolut has also made moves in Colombia, Mexico and Argentina.

John Cronin, an independent banking analyst, said there were “only two ways” for Nubank to expand in Europe: “You buy your way in . . . or you build organically, which takes ages, and you’re behind in the race versus Monzo, Revolut and others scattered around the continent.”

Nubank’s top executives are aware of the difficulties around European expansion. David Vélez, the company’s billionaire co-founder, told the FT last month that UK growth would be costly and posed its own challenges.

“I would say there are more digital banks, it’s a very big market, [but] you still have access and cost problems . . . there’s still a significant lack of access to certain products, specifically on credit.”

The price tag for Monzo attached to its talks with Nubank had sparked scepticism, however. In a note to clients, equity research company Autonomous labelled the deal “financially questionable”, noting that a valuation of between £8bn and £10bn would be seven times Monzo’s tangible book value, far higher than competitors.

Autonomous added that in the mature UK market, it would be hard to monetise Monzo’s customers to make the transaction pay off. The $9 per month Monzo generates from each customer is only half the monthly average revenue per Brazilian Nubank customer, Autonomous said.

“Nubank would be paying a premium to its own valuation to acquire something that doesn’t generate the same returns as it’s currently generating,” the independent analyst Cronin said.

A venture capital adviser said Monzo and Nubank also served starkly different customers, with Nubank providing lending and banking services to underbanked customers in Latin America.

“Nubank is more mass-market and not necessarily known for higher-value customers. There are not a large number of underbanked people in the UK or Europe.”

But if Nubank balked at Monzo’s desired valuation, private equity firms without the same strategic rationale for a deal or operations to merge were likely to be even more price sensitive, making a deal difficult to pull off.

That could mean that rather than cashing out via a sale to Nubank, Monzo’s existing investors have to inject more cash into the UK fintech to fund its growth plans in pursuit of an exit at a later date.

Still, speaking to the FT last month, Oldham seemed unperturbed. “We’re super hopeful about bringing that sort of Monzo magic, as we like to say, to other markets,” he said.

Additional reporting by Michael Pooler and Akila Quinio

title: IPO hopeful Zilch needs to prove it’s one of a kind
content:
Published October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

Part of valuing any company when it goes public is working out which existing stocks it most closely resembles. Investors gauge valuation multiples for the so-called peer group , add a discount or maybe even a premium, and presto — an IPO share price emerges. For Zilch, a UK fintech preparing for a London listing, this simple-sounding process poses a grave problem.

Zilch’s main product is a cheaper alternative to credit cards, offering customers a competitive interest rate that is, in effect, subsidised by selling advertising. Five years ago it was valued in a fundraising at $2bn. Peers included Sweden’s Klarna, which had rocketed to a $46bn valuation. But the peer group has gone from help to extreme hindrance: Klarna has shed 90 per cent of its value since then.

Value Zilch next to its Swedish counterpart now and it would be worth, well, close to zilch. True, Klarna had its own idiosyncrasies . But it’s not like other comparisons are less awkward. Affirm, a buy-now-pay-later specialist, still trades above its IPO price but is down 42 per cent from where it closed the day it went public, and 9 per cent this year. Upstart, which focuses on personal loans, has fallen 92 per cent over five years and halved this year so far.

What about earlier generations of consumer finance companies that Zilch hopes to usurp? There’s Vanquis, a subprime credit card lender that has been restyling itself as a fintech, but has been around in various forms since the 1800s. No luck there either: its shares are down almost 40 per cent over the past 12 months, and 80 per cent over five years.

Zilch may argue it isn’t really like any of these. It aims to mix the low interest rates and convenience of companies such as Klarna with the stickier customer relationship of credit card lenders. Since its service can be used anywhere — unlike products that are offered by retail partners at the checkout — it should not be reliant on a handful of large merchant partners, while the quick turnover of its loan book makes it less exposed to interest rate moves.

Its finances do seem to be on the up, too. Zilch reported a net loss of £10.5mn in the year to March 2025, but showed a route to profitability. Revenue nearly doubled, massively outpacing the mere 7 per cent growth in operating expenses, creating what financial analysts call “positive jaws”.

Zilch would be one of a kind in one important way: by listing in London. The City has not always been welcoming for tech groups, but scarcity can be a virtue. The listing of Raspberry Pi in 2024 with a valuation of just over £500mn would barely have registered in the US, but created a sizeable stir in the UK. Its shares have risen almost 150 per cent since.

By the same token, Zilch would be assured attention from exchange executives and politicians desperate to liven up the long-quiet IPO market. And other fintech IPO hopefuls such as Zopa are watching closely. If Zilch can secure a better reception than its ailing listed peers, it may not be a one-off for long.
