title: 棕榈油：产量超预期兑现，单边回调之后机会在哪里？
content:
来源：牛钱网
嘉宾介绍：徐超，大地期货油脂首席分析师，国内资深 “生柴”研究专家，农产品SQL数据库核心开发者。曾供职于油脂龙头企业，长期从事油脂油料等大宗商品交易策略研究。丰富的豆棕 菜油 供需分析经验及产业人脉资源为策略研发奠定扎实的基础。
一、前期上涨的三个驱动，如今在利空端全部兑现
过去几个月，油脂市场经历了一轮由预期驱动的上涨。回头来看，支撑那波行情的核心逻辑主要有三点：一是产区持续干旱，尤其是印尼加里曼丹中部地区的干旱程度不断加深；二是 原油 价格维持强势，没有触发加息预期；三是基本面没有出现超出预期的重大利空。
然而进入 9月中下旬之后，这三点在利空端几乎同时兑现。首先，产区降水明显增加，加里曼丹中部此前严重的干旱情况，尤其是接近北部和东部的区域，已经有所缓解。其次，原油价格触发了后续的加息预期，地缘冲突持续之下，宏观层面对于油脂的通缩交易开始集中体现。第三，也是最具冲击力的一点，马来西亚产量数据远超预期 。 两家准确性较高的机构都给出了接近 210多万吨的产量预期，环比增幅达到18%到20%，而往年9月份正常产量一般在189到190万吨左右，这已经算是不错的水平。
这意味着，市场此前一直期盼的回调不仅发生了，而且幅度可能比之前预期的更深。
二、产量超预期带来的连锁反应
单看产量数据本身，或许还可以用 8月假期工作日结转、后期干旱集中收割等因素来解释。但问题在于，当这样一个产量在9月底到10月兑现之后，对应的期末库存将从之前预期的270到280万吨，直接攀升到330到340万吨。这个量级对市场的影响是直接的。
第一，单边回调的幅度会比之前预期的更强。 上周市场还普遍愿意在原油企稳的情况下回调做多，但超预期产量数据出来之后，这种节奏被明显打乱。
第二，近月反套会加深。 如果 10月份之后的产量不给出环比下降，或者维持持平，甚至按季节性再增2%到3%，那么近月反套结构将进一步强化。此前印尼干旱给到了一定的马来与印尼价差范围，市场对于反套能否继续深化、尤其是在一五价差到-450这种位置，以及明年减产预期如何演变，存在从反套转向正套的节奏讨论。但产量数据出来之后，短期反套节奏被压制，结构上不太会往正套方向转，两套价差可能继续被往下压。
第三，库存高点出现的时间可能推迟。 最乐观的情况下，如果 11月左右产量整体出现非常大的减产力度，产地可能迎来去库节奏。但当前产量兑现之后，短期压力明显增强，后续对应的库存拐点预期需要重新评估。
三、后期做多单边需要重新找到三个驱动
既然此前的三个驱动在利空端已经兑现，那么行情若想重新上涨，也需要对应找到这三个驱动。
第一是天气。今年厄尔尼诺预计在四季度见顶， 10月开始进入四季度，到明年一季度产地降雨会增加，在干旱基础上出现一定降水增加没有问题。关键要看后边的降水是否具有持续性，或者整体偏干水平会如何。如果11月份继续切入干旱节奏，做多的第二波机会可能到来，尤其是针对远月合约。
第二是原油。原油价格需要保持相对稳定的结构，或者说不出现大幅度下跌，这是做多的第二个条件。
第三是产量和库存。需要跟踪 10月、11月马来西亚的产量能否给出对应的库存减少。如果这三个条件能够确定，那么后续单边会比较好做。
四、如果单边不好判断，正套结构可能是更稳妥的选择
如果单边确实不好判断，或者上述驱动无法兑现，那么明年在现有结构下仍然是减产的，可以关注库存拐点预期出来之后的反套合约，以及后续的正套合约。因为明年供给端出现问题，整体震荡行情或者月差走正的行情，相对来讲确定性更高，无非是定义时间和驱动的问题。
从厄尔尼诺情况来看，现有干旱可以对明年产量造成至少 300万吨左右的减产。但要想把减产幅度推到400到500万吨，还需要看到9月、10月马来西亚干旱明显减弱。对标15到16年的厄尔尼诺，去掉季节性趋势后整体减幅大概在9.23%左右。
今年印尼中加地区的干旱幅度远超 15到16年，因为这几年种植区域变化，中加地区产量占比已接近印尼总产量的四成左右，对应的产量影响比较强。但马来西亚这边看不到特别明显的干旱，只有在二三月份有一些，幅度完全无法与15到16年相比。
如果四季度能看到同比上来的干旱程度，那么明年 棕榈 油整体的库存收缩度会比较强。尤其是 10月份之后又要进入印尼的生物柴油阶段，虽然印尼官方给了156，但今年毕竟有一个季度，再加上明年，而且美国生物柴油这一边，26年给了一个好头，27年整体增量也给得很明确。与23年不同，27年的整体增幅要比23到24年的预期好很多，因为23到24年是一个累库到累库增量的过程，而经历了25年去库之后，目前的RINS价格以及到27年的生物柴油目标定量，对于油脂的整体需求增量是很强的，后面还有小额炼厂的一部分结转前期量的问题。
五、估值角度：棕榈油并不贵
从估值定价的角度来看，比较合理的美 豆油 定价大概在 70美金左右，73到可以放得更大一些。因为现在美豆油出现了明显的超跌，不管是从进口其他油脂的替代角度，还是从其他替代能源原料的价格来看，抑或是它本身的利润逻辑，都处于超跌状态。美豆油到70以下，本身对于海外的原料替代就比较强。从价格推导来讲，大概1200美金这一线，棕榈油换算一下大概在9600左右的价格，在生产逻辑上，尤其是国际油脂定价逻辑上的支撑是比较强的。
如果算一个最低价，假设回到打仗之前，所有事情都回到相对低位，柴油价格回到两块五这样的水平，虽然短期内、中期内可能都看不到，但对应计算的油脂价格也得在 8800左右。现在比较麻烦的一点是，前面的油脂因为利润端走出比较反季节性的价差之后，给到了过高的区间，能源以及天气的升水给到之后，确实需要有回调的作用。
每年在厄尔尼诺开始兑现到产量之前，因为产量毕竟要 8到10个月之后兑现，大概都会有这样一波炒作，今年节奏也非常像。一般来讲，到什么位置就再跌回去，跌回去之后再重新整理好整个基本面，再重新给出对应的减产逻辑。
六、需求端跟踪与操作节奏
需求端目前来看，印尼这边的产量此前因为加里曼丹的干旱，确实导致了一部分港口印尼与马来价差走平，看到了一点点印尼干旱对产量的影响。比较遗憾的是，印度也好，中国也好，整体的港口库存确实都比较高。
印度这次减税之后，港口库存会开始快速往渠道库存去转移，可能为后面的印度整体港口库存清出来之后的需求提供一定保障。马来与印尼本地的价差还没有拉得太开，至少从产量端还没有看到这两个国家，尤其是印尼遭受干旱之后的产量出现多大减幅。
所以需要跟踪两个点：一是印度需求，即马来 RBD价格能不能对应马来的出口增加，因为马来产量其实已经没有什么变化了，只能从印尼的减产推导到马来的产量变化；二是跟踪马来与印尼本地的实际月差会不会出现正套，即很明显产量出现问题了。
从现在估值角度来讲，棕榈油到底贵不贵？其实并不贵。远月的抛物价差，即过 5个月之后的柴油价格与棕榈油价格，已经跌到非常低的水平，棕榈油相对于柴油价格在远期来讲并不是一个很高估的区间。
经历这波大跌之后，无论跟柴油比价还是跟原油比价，整体价格都到了非常低的位置。从现在 1.9再跌到1.8，无非可能也就400到500个点的跌幅。如果现在这个位置去尝试，还是需要控制好仓位。如果前面没有仓位，现在想二次入场棕榈油，可以对着 01 的价格去做 05 ，或者对着 01 去做 09 都可以。但至少从现在来讲，仓位还是要控制好，临近过节，以及目前的利空还没有特别好的去反映，至少还没有看到天气继续干旱、产地产量目前这个利空肯定还是要等到 10月8号的整个数据出来之后，10月10号马来数据出来之后才会去落地。得等到这三个相对出现见底的节奏，可能才会比较适合上一些仓位。
七、总结
整体来看，棕榈油此前的上涨驱动已经在利空端兑现，产量超预期使得单边回调幅度加深，近月反套结构被压制。后期若想重新做多单边，需要重新看到天气干旱、原油稳定、产量库存减少这三个条件。
如果单边不好判断，明年供给端收缩叠加生物柴油需求增量，正套结构可能是更稳妥的选择。估值上棕榈油并不贵，远月对柴油比价已到很低位置，但各合约预期打得太满，操作上仍需控制仓位，等待利空落地后的见底信号。

title: Foreign bid highlights Australia’s battle to forge a gold champion
content:
Nic Fildes in Sydney

Published October 2 2026

Could you be the FT’s top trader?

Australia has created some of the world’s biggest mining groups — yet it has failed to produce a global gold champion.

Northern Star Resources, Australia’s largest gold miner and a stock market darling, was a candidate to rise to global significance as the booming gold price boosted its valuation to A$44bn ($31bn) earlier this year.

That was before a sharp downturn in its fortunes in recent months as production warnings eroded investor confidence and triggered an executive exodus.

The company is now in play after it two weeks ago rejected an A$39bn ($27bn) bid from South African rival Gold Fields. A deal would be the largest mining combination since the $38bn Xstrata-Glencore tie-up in 2012, according to Dealogic.

Activist hedge fund Elliott Management had called for a sale in June, leaving Northern Star Australia’s putative gold champion vulnerable to a takeover.

The rejection of the offer was made public just as executives from the gold industry arrived in Denver for the Mining Forum Americas 2026 conference this week. Some bankers landed after 15-hour flights from Australia to discover that the news had leaked when they turned their phones back on.

The conference provided Gold Fields with a chance to sell the combination to its investors in closed-door meetings and from the stage.

Mike Fraser, chief executive of Gold Fields, used a keynote speech in Denver to argue that the potential combination with Northern Star presented “a very compelling story”.

He picked through an estimated $5bn of potential synergies in the form of tax savings and cost cuts as maps of the Kalgoorlie region, where both companies own significant gold-mining and processing assets, were displayed.

“We continue to remain open for dialogue and believe this proposal warrants further consideration by the Northern Star board,” Fraser said, putting pressure on his target.

A Northern Star presentation in Denver by acting chief executive Ryan Gurner, its former finance chief, was less explosive.

The company’s new chief executive Suresh Vadnagra is walking into a bid situation when he joins the company from Glencore on Monday. Two board members proposed by Elliott, including former Anglo American chief executive Mark Cutifani, have also just joined.

One gold industry veteran said the timing of Gold Fields’ approach would put pressure on the Australian company to weigh its options.

A combined Gold Fields and Northern Star would create Australia’s largest gold producer, based on output, and the second largest globally to US miner Newmont .

Elliott has urged Northern Star to open talks with Gold Fields, which could move to sweeten its offer if talks resume, according to a person with direct knowledge of the situation.

Northern Star has said that the Gold Fields’ bid undervalues its growth potential. The offer means its shareholders would own a third of the Johannesburg-listed company, introducing more risk for cautious Australian investors.

Morningstar analyst Jon Mills said that there was a 50 per cent chance that Gold Fields would offer more: “We think Northern Star remains in play and a higher offer is likely.”

Mitch Ryan, a mining analyst with Jefferies, said there was “moderately low” risk of a counterbidder given the scale and premium required.

Australia’s mining industry has historical connections to South Africa but recent corporate activity has been tumultuous.

BHP took over Billiton in 2001 and acquired significant South African operations that were later spun out into South32. The “Big Australian” then tried to acquire Anglo American in 2024 but the deal was contingent on the demerger of two substantial businesses in South Africa — a plan that caused political uproar in the country.

Some in the industry remain puzzled that Australia lacks a gold producer in the same league as Newmont, Barrick Gold or Agnico Eagle given the country’s mining history, particularly in gold. Former domestic giants like Newcrest and Normandy have been scooped up by foreign buyers.

Australia’s largest miners historically mined gold but transitioned away from the precious metal in pursuit of high-value iron ore and copper production. BHP has remained a substantial gold producer in Australia but deems the yellow metal to be a byproduct of its copper mining rather than a core metal.

Company executives argue that Australian investors have been less comfortable with local gold companies pushing into high-risk overseas markets including Africa and the Pacific in pursuit of growth than international peers.

Jake Klein, founder and chair of A$27bn gold and copper miner Evolution Mining, said that Australia was adept at building great gold mining groups but not at turning them into global players.

“If Northern Star does fall to a foreign player, then it’s another missed opportunity for Australia’s gold mining industry,” he told the FT. “We grow companies very well, but we have not yet been able to take them to the next level and build a peer to the biggest global gold companies like Newmont, Barrick and Agnico.”

Australia’s original gold rush in the 1800s transformed Melbourne into the world’s richest city on a per capita basis. More recently, however, the focus of the industry has been around the rich “Goldfields” region of Kalgoorlie, 600km east of Perth, the Western Australian capital.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

The region has been a hive of consolidation for decades as companies trade assets to build gold empires. That includes Gold Fields, which bought a small player in 2001 and now produces 1mn ounces a year from the region.

Northern Star is itself a consolidation story. Its main asset is the gigantic “Super Pit” in Kalgoorlie, whose ownership was previously split between Newmont and Barrick Gold before they sold it. The mine now produces almost half a million troy ounces of gold a year — a figure that is projected to almost double by the end of the decade as a new mill comes online.

Northern Star has been a remarkable success story for Australian investors since it raised A$5mn in a late 2003 listing. The company earned a reputation for creating substantial value from unloved assets such as the Super Pit.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

A stock that was trading for less than A$0.40 in 2011 peaked at almost A$32 in March. The Gold Fields offer was pitched at an implied value of A$27 per Northern Star share.

Northern Star is likely to shed smaller gold mines whether or not it is sold, creating a knock-on effect for smaller companies with about $4bn of assets up for grabs. But the hopes of a global gold giant emerging from Australia still look far-fetched, with cautious investors unwilling to back the level of cross-border M&A that has defined the growth of US, Canadian and South African gold companies.

“Australia has all the ingredients to be the global epicentre for mining: investors, bankers, engineers, lawyers and analysts who have a deep understanding of the industry and are widely respected as best in class,” Evolution’s Klein said. “But for whatever reason, to date we have fallen short and not been able to create that global gold champion.”

title: 新世界发展盘中涨超10% 2026财年实现扭亏为盈
content:

title: 韩国加大口头干预力度以稳定债市，承诺必要时采取市场支持举措
content:
在全球债券抛售潮加剧之际，韩国决策者正加大口头干预力度以稳定国内金融市场，并承诺必要时将减少短期公债发行，采取市场支持举措。
韩国财政经济部长官李炯日周五表示，政府已准备好“在必要时考虑进一步减少（公债）发行规模”。
韩国财经部周四在一份声明中宣布，将10月公债发行规模削减5万亿韩元（36.7亿美元）。
李炯日强调，政府将与韩国央行密切协调，准备在市场抛售加剧时动用紧急市场稳定工具，包括大规模回购或提前赎回债务。
韩国指标三年期公债收益率周一升11个基点至4.11%，创2022年11月以来最高水平，追随全球债市跌势。
韩国官员本周加强了口头干预，以抑制市场波动。
李炯日周五警告称，长期高利率和信用利差扩大可能会严重损害信用状况较差家庭的再融资条件。
周五早盘，韩国三年期公债收益率报4.01%，徘徊在周一触及的四年高点附近。

title: NY's governor appoints special prosecutor in Cornell frat rape investigation
content:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed the state's attorney general, Letitia James, as a special prosecutor in investigating the alleged gang rape of a woman at Cornell University.

The woman has alleged she was drugged and raped by several men at a fraternity house. The case, which stems back to 2024, was reopened after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month that thrust the allegations into the national spotlight.

"New information has raised serious questions about how this case was handled, and I've lost faith in the Tompkins County DA's ability to fairly oversee it," Hochul said.

The announcement means District Attorney Van Houten is no longer overseeing the case.

The BBC has contacted Van Houten's office for comment.

He has defended his office's previous decision not to file charges in the case, arguing they were not given enough evidence to meet the legal threshold.

Van Houten reopened the case after the civil lawsuit and said much of the information released in recent weeks about the case was not passed to his office.

"The young woman at the center of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued," Hochul said in a statement.

James could prosecute any offences that might be found during her investigation and present evidence to a grand jury, Hochul said.

James, who is the state's chief legal officer, said on X, external that she stood ready "to lead a process guided by the facts and the law".

"The Governor has entrusted my office with this investigation, and we do not take that responsibility lightly," James added.

Hochul and James are scheduled to provide an update on the investigation on Friday morning local time.

The woman at the centre of the case, identified anonymously as Jane Doe in court documents, filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university in September.

Jane Doe is a placeholder name sometimes used in US law for privacy or anonymity reasons.

She alleged that she was drugged and raped by seven men at a fraternity house at the university in 2024.

She claimed that Cornell failed to protect her or adequately punish the men, who have now become known as the Cornell Seven.

The case was initially referred to Van Houten, the top prosecutor in the county, in 2024.

Van Houten said his office did not bring charges at the time because he had only seen a statement from Doe implying the incident was consensual and that she had not been drugged.

This week, his office announced it would be reopening the case - less than two weeks after Doe filed her civil lawsuit.

Cornell has said it provided evidence to the district attorney's office from its own investigation, including a Snapchat group chat in which fraternity members discussed a "free" sexual encounter with Doe on the night of the alleged assault.

Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, has accused the district attorney of repeatedly changing his story amid news coverage of the case.

title: Australia says platforms like Steam and Roblox have 'significant' child safety gaps
content:
Australia's online safety regulator has found "significant gaps" in how popular gaming platforms protect children online.

In a new report it found inconsistent approaches in how Steam, Roblox, Fortnite and Minecraft implement child safety measures as research shows nine out of 10 children aged 8 to 17 in Australia have played online games.

"Australian children have a right to play online without being exposed to predators, sexual extortionists, violent extremist content or other harmful material," eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said.

Roblox said it "prioritises the safety of our Australian community, especially the youngest users". The other platforms have been contacted for comment.

Weak safety on platforms allow "predatory adults" to make contact with children before grooming them, Inman Grant said, for sexual exploitation or radicalisation.

The report found that Valve - the US gaming giant that owns Steam and Steam Chat - was the only provider that did not use a type of technology widely used by the industry to detect and remove known harmful content.

Valve also did not "proactively" use tools to detect child sexual exploitation or violent material in chats, with current systems mainly flagging scams, the report found.

Roblox, along with Valve, were noted in the report as using only internal datasets to train language detection systems and for not regularly retraining these models.

"We expect these services to lift their game to identify and combat serious harms such as child sexual exploitation, sexual extortion and material and activity which promotes, incites or instructs violence," Inman-Grant said.

Minecraft and Fortnite, which does offer child accounts, generally let users self-declare their age, the report highlighted, meaning anyone who said they were adults could access "higher-risk communication features".

Steam also relied on users self-declaring their age but the report acknowledged the platform had recently introduced age checks using credit cards, and that Roblox had put in stronger age checks since last December.

Another issue raised by the report was the inconsistent manner in which the four gaming platforms shared information and participated in industry initiatives.

Mojang Studios, developer of Minecraft, and Roblox shared industry expertise in combating child sexual exploitation as well as violent extremism online, but Valve did not.

Elsewhere, Fortnite maker Epic Games failed to share instances of breaches with other platforms under a global programme that was designed to combat online child sexual exploitation and abuse.

The report was based on information collected by Australia's eSafety Commission on how the platforms were protecting users from serious online harm between October 2025 and March 2026.

Australia has made global headlines in recent years for its stance on online safety, after it introduced its world-leading social media ban for under-16s last December - which did not include gaming platforms - and a more recent push to force tech giants to offer users a chance to opt-out of social media algorithms.

A spokesperson for Roblox said it had "invested heavily" in its safeguards for children which include mandatory age checks.

Valve, Fortnite, and Microsoft - which owns Minecraft - have been contacted for comment.

title: 巨贪千亿，起底易会满的金钱帝国
content:
来源：猫笔刀投研社
谁都知道，易会满最疼他的儿子。他的那个学习成绩极差，无比顽劣的儿子。
当易会满在支行调研时向地方行长抱怨“儿子高考学习不好”时，他想不到，儿子也会成为 中金公司 意气风发的高管。
2014年，易晨阳揣着浙江银行学校（中专）的毕业证，走进瑞银香港办公室。
没人知道，他爸易会满，刚升任工行行长。
他没走后门——至少表面没有。
他只是比别人更早出现在饭局，更懂怎么递名片，更会笑。
18个月后，他跳槽香港中金公司。
2015年8月29日，他从瑞银离职。
第二天，他爸易会满，正式成为工行董事长。
2015年11月3日，他入职中金香港。
半年后，他爸调任证监会。
2019年，科创板开板。
易晨阳，成了中金最年轻的IPO操盘手之一。
2020年夏天， 蚂蚁集团 上市前夜。
他站在香港香格里拉酒店的落地窗前，手机屏保是那张庆功宴照片。
他没发朋友圈。
但那天，他给三个客户发了同一句话：“明天，我们改写历史。”
在2020年那个燥热的夏天，当蚂蚁集团估值突破3000亿美元时，易晨阳主导设计的“战略配售+超额配售权”方案，让中金公司狂揽28亿元承销费。
这笔世纪交易不仅让他在金融圈赢得“操盘小霸王”的称号，更成为其家族利益输送的关键点。
蚂蚁集团IPO期间，易晨阳团队曾将300亿元理财资金通过嵌套资管产品注入项目，而这笔资金的最终流向，竟与易会满堂兄易会强关联的浙江某私募基金存在隐秘关联 。
也没人知道，他爸在证监会的办公室里，正批着另一份文件——关于“支持科技创新企业上市”。
2022年，他升任中金香港RO。
那是合规负责人。
也是中金公司最后的防火墙。
易会满很得意：“没想到后来能进中金，在香港当保荐人，发展得相当不错。”
2023年6月26日，他升职当天，他爸易会满，被免去证监会主席职务。
三个月后，他爸的旧部、工行资管部总经理顾建纲，被查。
顾建纲的儿子，是易晨阳在中金的搭档。
2024年2月，易会满卸任。
2025年9月6日，中央纪委宣布：易会满涉嫌严重违纪违法，接受审查。
2025年9月9日，易晨阳消失。
他的1号、9号香港证监会牌照，全部失效。
系统显示：“无主事人”。
他不再是任何人。
2025年9月，当易晨阳在审讯室里交代出第17个离岸账户时，调查组意识到，这起案件涉及的金额可能超过千亿规模。
一位参与办案的纪委干部感慨：“我们查的不是简单的贪腐案，而是一个盘踞金融系统二十年的利益集团。”
------
他爸易会满，1984年从浙江银行学校毕业。
那年，学校还在杭州天目山路的老楼里，墙上贴着“为金融事业服务”的红字标语。
他不是天才。
他只是浙江苍南灵溪镇余桥村，最会读书的那个孩子。
家里五个孩子：大姐易爱珠，大哥易会取，二哥易会平，三哥易会坦，最小的是他。
村里人说，易会坦最彪悍。
初中时，他敢拎着板凳去打隔壁村的混混。
后来，他没进银行。
他在温州开了一家小公司，专接“难搞的融资”。
有人找他，说：“我项目要上市，但材料不齐。”
易会坦说：“你找我，不如找我弟弟。”
他从不提自己是易会满的哥哥。
但他知道，只要他开口，有人就会“配合”。
易会取，二哥，在杭州做担保公司。
他不放贷。
他只做一件事：介绍人。
“你找我，我带你见周某。”
周某，是易会满的表弟。
没人知道他全名。
但金融圈都知道，他是“白手套”。
他不持股。
不签字。
不露脸。
他只管一件事：把钱，从A账户，转到B账户，再转到开曼，再回流A股。
2020年，蚂蚁IPO那笔300亿，就是他经手的。
他用三个壳公司，三层离岸架构，把资金洗得干干净净。
没人查他。
因为没人敢查。
他背后站着易会满。
而易会满背后，站着整个浙江金融圈。
2024年，易会满卸任。
一个月后，杭州西湖区一家小公司注册成立。
名字叫：会满。
法人：易会强。
易会强，是易会满的堂弟。
他不是高管。
不是股东。
他只是个普通会计。
但他注册“会满”那天，正好是易会满离开证监会的第17天。
没人知道他为什么选这个名字。
但圈里人都懂。
这是挑衅。
也是告别。
也是——
“我还在。”
------
2026年3月，沈荣勤被查。
他是工行浙江分行原行长。
和易会满，同届，同校，同乡。
浙江银行学校，1984届。
他们一起在仙居支行熬过夜，一起在杭州分行喝过酒。
沈荣勤退休后，当了浙江钱塘江金研院的院长。
他还在管钱。
还在介绍项目。
还在用“易主席的老部下”这五个字，换回几千万的咨询费。
2026年9月30日，最高检通报：易会满涉嫌受贿罪，被提起公诉。
起诉书里，有这么一句：
贪污数额非常巨大
“纵容、默许亲属利用本人职权谋取私利。”
没提名字。
但所有人都知道，说的是谁。
没人提蚂蚁。
没人提300亿。
没人提离岸账户。
因为官方从不写小说。
它只写事实。
而事实是：
易会满，从一个中专学校毕业，从支行柜员，走到证监会主席。
易会满担任证监会主席的五年，是股民散户最受伤的五年。
他任职1760天，以融资为本，搞史无前例的扩容大跃进，发行1860只新股，募资2.2万亿，再融资9.6万亿，大小非减持7万亿，将二级市场的资金抽干。
同时，超越《证券法》，将场外股权转让系统的新三板变成北交所，440多只股直接到二级市场交易，其中有大量假冒伪劣公司；
放任券商搞衍生雪球产品，导致千股跌停式爆仓，将股指倒退到18年前，市值损失20万亿。
2026年10月1日，浙江金融职业学院官网更新。
校友名录里，易会满的名字，被划掉。
易晨阳的名字，从未出现过。
沈荣勤的名字，还在。
但后面，多了一行小字：
“涉嫌严重违纪违法，正在接受调查。”
没人再提“易家帮”。
没人再提“金融圈潜规则”。
因为真正的权力游戏，从不需要名字。
它只需要——
一个位置。
一个时间。
一个，没人敢问的沉默。
声明：本文绝不构成任何投资建议、引导或承诺，仅供学术参考，市场有风险，投资需谨慎。

title: South Korea brings powerful prosecution agency to heel
content:
Daniel Tudor and Song Jung-a in Seoul

Published October 2 2026

For 78 years, South Korea’s prosecutors were feared and admired for their broad authority to investigate crimes as well as to bring cases to court.

But this Friday the prosecution service will be abolished and its functions divided between two new agencies — a victory for reformers, but one that some fear could leave an investigative vacuum in areas such as financial crime.

The new Serious Crime Investigation Agency, under the interior ministry, will shoulder major investigations, with police handling the rest. The Public Prosecution Office, under the justice ministry, will decide whether to bring charges and represent the state at trial.

President Lee Jae Myung’s Democratic Party has long argued that the outgoing system enabled politically motivated investigations and gave prosecutors near-unchecked authority.

At a meeting of senior aides on Thursday, Lee said: “We are bringing an end to an era of wrongdoing—a time when the prosecution monopolised both investigation and indictment, exercising unchecked power and, even worse, acting as a ‘political prosecution’ to suppress and eliminate political rivals.”

Former president Yoon Suk Yeol , now imprisoned over his botched December 2024 martial law declaration, was himself a former chief prosecutor. His ascent to power in 2022 and appointment of old colleagues to senior posts revived criticisms at the time of a “prosecutors’ republic”.

Under the reforms, the Seoul Southern District Prosecutors’ Office, known as the “grim reaper” of Yeouido, the banking district, for the rigour of its financial crime investigations, will see its specialist operations dismantled and rebuilt inside the SCIA.

“White-collar crimes may be difficult to handle,” said Park Ju-geun, head of corporate research group Leaders Index. He believes the SCIA and police would need more time to build up expertise.

A serving prosecutor who wished to be identified only by their surname, Son, said that SCIA officers, of whom they estimate 70 per cent have come from the old prosecution service, “have a building with desks in it, but no computers or even pens yet”. Yet at the same time, the agency feels pressure to “go after a big target, to prove itself”, they added.

Handing more investigative power to the police is also coming under scrutiny because of recent scandals . In July, a police team leader was arrested over alleged evidence tampering in the murder of a schoolgirl; the accused killer’s father, himself a serving officer, was suspected of destroying evidence. Then just over a month ago it emerged that a police officer had allegedly falsified the closure of two missing-person cases, with both people later found dead.

Lee referenced such concerns at the Thursday meeting, stating police reform would also be a “key task” for his administration.

A particular flashpoint of the reforms has been the loss of prosecutors’ power to conduct “supplementary” investigations when their review of a police file exposes gaps before an indictment decision. Under the new system, prosecutors may identify missing facts but must ask police to investigate them again.

The uncertainty surrounding the changeover is the latest chapter in a long and controversial history. The prosecution service was founded in September 1948 — less than a month after South Korea itself — and accumulated power under successive autocratic governments.

Pro-democracy activists reviled the service both as an instrument for pursuing dissidents and as a pipeline into the authoritarian political elite. A young prosecutor named Kim Ki-choon embodied both: in 1972, Kim helped draft military ruler Park Chung Hee’s authoritarian Yushin Constitution, before rising to become justice minister and, decades later, chief of staff to Park’s daughter, then president Park Geun-hye.

The organisation survived democratisation in 1987, and its clashes with progressive leaders made reform a cause of the left. Supporters of former president Roh Moo-hyun viewed the corruption investigation preceding his 2009 suicide as politically driven; Lee has likewise portrayed cases against him as selective justice.

“The death of Roh was a great shock, and a tragedy. Prosecution reform is maybe a sort of holy grail,” said Park Ye-rin, a rank-and-file member of Lee’s Democratic Party. “But speaking less emotionally, it can’t be right to have all that power with one place.”

Prosecutorial prestige was cultural as well as political. Son said joining the service “overjoyed” their parents and meant both acquiring “a job with power” and being recognised as a “state-certified elite”. Prosecutors were “objects of aspiration”, they added, due to their authority, the future opportunities available to them in law and politics, and media portrayals that enhanced their mystique.

For Son though, regardless of how the system is structured, “any holder of power seeks to utilise the prosecution once they take office”.

title: 韩国财长称必要时将考虑进一步减少国债发行
content:
韩国财政部长官李炯日周五表示，如有必要，韩国将考虑进一步减少国债发行，并承诺继续密切关注市场动态。
李炯日发表上述言论之际，韩国已决定在10月份将国债发行规模削减5万亿韩元（约合36.4亿美元），同时政府也承诺在必要时采取包括紧急回购债券在内的稳定措施。
李炯日在与韩国央行行长申铉松、金融委员会委员长李亿远（Lee Eog-weon）、金融监督院院长李灿珍（Lee Chan-jin）及国土交通部长官洪志善（Hong Jee-sun）举行的会议上讨论了这一问题。
这是李炯日自上月就任以来举行的首次此类会议。
他在会上表示：“如果高利率持续，信用评级较低的企业可能面临更沉重的再融资负担。政府将继续与相关机构合作，密切监测债券市场。”
在会议期间，李炯日还强调了密切监测房地产市场的必要性，指出首尔公寓价格的涨幅已连续五周放缓，而江南富裕地区以外的房价则继续上涨。
李炯日还强调需要继续落实韩元国际化的后续措施，并承诺将很快宣布放宽相关监管规定的举措。

title: OpenAI fires workers for 'mishandling sensitive information'
content:
OpenAI has fired three researchers for allegedly mishandling information, including work which involved an external organisation analysing AI models.

"Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work," a spokesperson told the BBC.

The ChatGPT-maker did not name the sacked workers, but at least two of them were involved in safety research at the firm.

The firings come as the debate over AI safety and the risks the technology may pose to humanity intensified in recent months.

"We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," a spokesperson for OpenAI said.

Concerns over AI safety have made headlines after some researchers and industry executives called for more guardrails around the technology.

OpenAI has come under under intense scrutiny after its models went rogue and hacked several platforms, including Australian government websites.

In an incident in July, one of the firm's AI models accessed the internet and breached the open-source developer platform Hugging Face.

That incident led OpenAI to review the activities of its AI agents, which are designed to execute tasks autonomously based on simple instructions.

The firm said this week it has notified more than 100 organisations about incidents involving unauthoritised activity linked to its systems.

Being notified "does not mean that any private information was accessed" or that a system was compromised, it said.

In September, researcher Jacob Coxon, who left Anthropic, called for AI development to slow down so its potential risks could be properly assessed.

Anthropic boss Dario Amodei and OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman have also called for measures to address concerns over AI.

On Tuesday, US President Donald Trump hosted a meeting of top technology bosses - including leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta and Google - to discuss AI.

After the gathering at the White House, Trump posted a document that he called a "morally binding" agreement that would serve as a "form of protection" from AI's potential risks.

Some technology experts criticised the pact, pointing out that it allowed AI companies to regulate themselves.

Trump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI's risks in response to calls from some industry figures for tighter oversight of the technology.

title: 10月甲醇基本面供需情况简析
content:
来源：金联创化工
文 | 刘若娇
导语： 9 月 甲醇 价格上涨明显，并创下历史高位。内地市场，上旬受霍尔木兹海峡通航受限、国内装置检修及厂库偏低拉动期现货大幅冲高；中旬下游成本倒挂、CTO 企业外放货源后价格回落，货源偏紧限制跌幅；下旬地缘溢价回落，检修装置复产、节前备货收尾，成交转淡，仅少量刚需逢低补库。港口市场震荡上行，地缘扰动叠加低库存、内地补给有限支撑期现高位，基差极端偏强，持货商惜售，但港口MTO 开工低位压制需求，双节备货下成交以刚需为主。截至9月29日，江苏进口甲醇价格在4400-4610元/吨，3050-3085较8月底涨1350-1525元/吨；内蒙北线集中在3405-3500元/吨，较8月底涨580-650元/吨；山东地区在3830-3950元/吨，较8月底涨810-820元/吨。
就2026年10月甲醇供需基本面来看：
供应方面，国产来看， 9月产量环比窄幅增加，预计在738.40万吨左右。下月预计国内甲醇企业总体开工或增加，产量随之增量。10月来看，根据金联创统计显示，下月检修装置主要华中及西北地区少量企业，同时考虑9月份检修装置在10月份恢复并提负。
进口方面， 9月进口量预估在43-45万吨，较8月减量38万吨左右。主要因地缘因素影响，海峡实际通航偏低，中东装船量继续收缩。10月份进口量预估47万吨水平，具体以海关数据为准。9月中东装船量继续收缩，截止目前不足12万吨，据悉部分船只难以突破海峡封锁。外加部分非伊量，总进口量预期较低。
需求方面， 9月甲醇实际国内消费量有所回升。传统下游加权开工率环比增加 1.47 个百分点在50.63%。其中DMF开工出现下降，其余产品装置开工环比均有所增加。烯烃装置开工环比增加1.43个百分点在67.54%。预计10月甲醇需求表现偏强。具体来看，传统下游方面，截止9月底，传统下游开工环比小幅增加，10月传统下游依旧处于传统旺季，加之预计原料甲醇随着西北产区装置陆续回归，价格将有所下行，下游成本减低后需求有望回升。烯烃方面，截止9月底，烯烃开工虽仍不足7成，但中天合创装置中上旬恢复正常，延安能化、大唐多伦装置月下旬重启，烯烃需求继续增加。
后市来看，10月国内甲醇市场整体呈现内地先强后弱、港口高位震荡的格局。 内地市场方面，9月底上游持续超卖，上旬受产区偏低库存支撑价格偏强，但随着前期检修装置陆续复产，叠加宝丰新产能投产预期带来压制，供应压力逐步释放；需求端MTO利润偏弱，传统下游旺季表现不及预期，市场多维持刚需采购，需求支撑不足，内地甲醇价格阶段性承压回落，需重点关注新增装置实际投产进度与下游开工变动。港口市场方面，9月中东甲醇发运仍受限，低库存及偏低进口量形成底部支撑，但港口MTO开工持续低位，高价原料带来的需求负反馈限制上行空间；美伊局势暂无明显突破，地缘溢价短期仍存，但双方仍在谈判，若出现实质性进展，浮仓积压甲醇或集中释放，市场将在地缘情绪降温、进口恢复预期下承压，不过在港口低库存格局未实质改变前，价格回落空间相对有限。

title: 第一太平：MPIC拟124亿披索收购Meralco约1.9%权益
content:
第一太平 （00142）发布公告，于2026年10月1日，Metro Pacific Investments Corporation（MPIC）（公司的菲律宾联号公司，集团间接持有其49.9%经济权益）与San Miguel Global Power Holdings Corp．（卖方）订立该协议。
MPIC已同意购买，而卖方已同意于完成日期以特别大宗出售的方式出售出售股份，占Meralco（集团的联营公司Manila Electric Company）已发行及流通普通股本总额约1.9%权益，有关价格为每股出售股份580.99披索（相等于约9.27美元或约72.28港元），合共约124亿披索（相等于约1.98亿美元或约15亿港元）。
于紧接完成前，MPIC于Meralco中拥有约47.5%直接及间接股权权益，而卖方则于Meralco中拥有约4.13%股权权益。于完成后，MPIC于Meralco中将会持有约49.4%直接及间接股权权益，而Meralco将继续为集团的联营公司。Meralco乃菲律宾最大的公用配电公司，服务马尼拉大都会及周边省份部份地区。
该项交易为MPIC增加于Meralco的实际权益，并反映MPIC对Meralco的长远增长前景及其对集团的策略重要性依然充满信心。

title: 浦江中国拟折让约14.62%配售最多3300万股配售股份 净筹约1.3亿港元

title: 美国增派爱国者防空系统 保护沙特与卡塔尔能源设施
content:
两名美国官员及一名地区消息人士称，美军近几周额外部署两套爱国者导弹发射系统，用于保卫沙特阿拉伯与卡塔尔的油气设施。
美国希望向这两个盟友作出保证，一旦特朗普总统决定重启针对伊朗的大规模军事行动，美方会保护两国关键能源设施。
特朗普周四表示，他正考虑在未来数周重启轰炸行动。他称：“现在我必须做出抉择：要么伊朗签署协议，要么伊朗将不复存在。”
8月初，当时特朗普考虑发起大规模打击，目标包含伊朗能源基础设施。沙特与卡塔尔领导人向他游说，劝阻其采取该行动。两国领导人深切担忧伊朗会实施报复，袭击本国油气设施。
美方官员表示，两国的恳求，是特朗普当时放弃打击、转而采取经济施压手段的重要原因。
上月，美军向沙特增派一套爱国者防空系统，守护一处核心石油设施；另一套爱国者系统部署至卡塔尔，保护天然气设施。
如果大规模战事重启，美军需要获准使用沙特领空。但倘若沙特认为本国石油设施得不到保护，大概率不会放行。
美国中央司令部发言人蒂姆·霍金斯上尉拒绝置评。
自对伊战争爆发以来，爱国者防空系统，尤其是其拦截弹，已经成为紧俏装备。
美军从其他战区抽调防空系统与拦截弹药调往中东，引发外界对全球其他区域战备水平的担忧。
在战争可能重启的背景下，正向中东增派更多军舰、战斗机与地面部队。
一名美国官员透露，西奥多·罗斯福号航母及其打击群于周日“秘密”驶离圣迭戈，奔赴中东，预计11月中旬抵达。
罗斯福号将与已经自3月起部署在中东的乔治·H·W·布什号航母，以及夏季从日本调派、仅在中东部署约一个月的乔治·华盛顿号航母会合。
这名美国官员称：“这意味着中东地区最多可集结三支航母打击群，火力将大幅增强。”
但另一名美国官员表示，目前尚未确定罗斯福号是替换现有部署在中东的航母，还是作为额外增援力量。
一名美方官员称，马金岛号两栖戒备群已于周一启程前往中东，编队包含三艘两栖舰，搭载来自第13海军陆战队远征部队的数千名海军陆战队员。
该编队预计11月底抵达中东，与过去数月已经部署在当地的另一支两栖戒备群及陆战队远征部队汇合。

title: 对冲基金大鳄阿克曼称人工智能极大增加了颠覆性冲击风险
content:
传奇投资者比尔·阿克曼（Bill Ackman）数十年来一直在寻找优质企业和潜力股。人工智能及其应用场景的兴起改变了他审视企业的方式，因为新兴技术带来的颠覆性影响已成为一项现实风险。
这位潘兴广场资本管理公司CEO已投资于“七巨头”（Magnificent Seven）股票，其中 微软 、Meta和 亚马逊 占据了显著的仓位。
阿克曼近期关于人工智能及其所带来的风险增加的言论，或许能解释其中的原因。
阿克曼在做客“The Knowledge Podcast”节目时表示，在评估投资标的时，他会考量：即便股市停摆10年，自己是否仍愿意持有这家公司的股份。
阿克曼指出，关注公司创造的收入，并预判该业务在10年或20年后的前景，至关重要。
这正是人工智能可能发挥作用的地方。
阿克曼表示：“人工智能极大地增加了行业遭受颠覆性冲击的风险。”
阿克曼指出，投资者必须审视自己投资的企业，并思考人工智能可能会如何对其造成颠覆。
这位投资者表示，在评估企业的“护城河”及其宽阔程度时，他现在必须格外谨慎，因为有些企业可能会因人工智能的冲击而消亡。
人工智能的积极一面
阿克曼在采访中承认，潘兴广场利用人工智能进行投资研究。他还强调了人工智能助力实现的医学进步。
这位投资者表示，人工智能带来了机遇，使得创建以往无法实现的企业变得更有可能。
“其进步速度之快，远超我以往所见的一切。”
阿克曼表示，人工智能将使那些此前并非创业者的人能够成为创业者。
在谈及投资布局时，阿克曼特别提到了 Meta 近期推出的 Muse AI 智能体，尽管他本人尚未亲自试用过。他提到，潘兴广场办公室的同事已经使用过 Muse，并对其创建智能体的简便性赞不绝口。
潘兴广场重点关注的另一项投资是涉足实体基础设施领域的布鲁克菲尔德公司。
“布鲁克菲尔德无疑是人工智能领域的赢家，”阿克曼说。

title: 国际刑警组织称人工智能加剧网络威胁
content:
国际刑警组织（INTERPOL）警告称，人工智能助长了网络威胁，因为它增强了诈骗等既有的犯罪手段。
国际刑警组织全球首席信息安全官比约恩·瓦特内（Bjorn R． Watne）周四在新加坡科技周活动期间接受采访时表示，人工智能是对现有犯罪手段的强化，而非彻底变革。诈骗分子可以利用人工智能同时针对多名受害者实施诈骗；与此同时，翻译技术和数字身份验证手段的提升，也使得人们越来越难以区分欺诈性互动与真实互动。
“这是一个演变过程，而非一场革命，”瓦特内说道，并补充称人工智能主要是在提升现有技术的“速度与规模”。
企业应着重保护的对象
瓦特内指出，随着网络威胁不断演变，企业应优先采取保护措施。
企业应当首先识别其“核心资产”——即维持运营至关重要的资产——并确定哪些主体最有可能企图窃取或破坏这些资产。
随后，企业可以利用威胁情报来了解这些对手所采用的战术与技术，并据此量身定制防御措施。
瓦特内指出：“如果并未成为特定威胁的目标，企业无需试图同时防范所有类型的威胁。”他补充道，根据企业面临的是机会主义犯罪分子还是高级持续性威胁（APT）攻击者，所需的防御手段也会有所不同。
此外，他还提到，高层管理人员与网络安全战略之间的脱节往往也会阻碍企业的工作。
瓦特内补充道：“仍有许多行业尚未意识到，如今每一家企业其实都是 IT 公司。”
他还指出，尽管网络风险在企业风险清单上的重要性日益提升，但在许多公司，网络安全 议题尚未真正进入董事会的视野。
智能体AI带来新风险
瓦特内表示，随着此类AI技术获得代表用户采取行动的能力，他对这一技术持高度警惕态度。他警告称，一旦出错，后果可能不仅仅是提供错误信息，更可能引发涉及现实世界的严重后果。
“AI向你提供错误信息是一回事，”瓦特内说道，“但当AI实际执行操作并采取了错误行动——尤其是在物理世界中——时，就可能导致人员身体受到伤害。”
他指出，AI在汽车及自动驾驶车辆等设备上的广泛应用，正是令人担忧的领域之一。
瓦特内指出，与金融服务等领域相比，人们对技术的信任度相对较高，这进一步加剧了相关风险。
他表示，在金融服务方面，人们往往采取更注重掌控的态度，既依赖 PIN 码等安全防护措施，又对盗刷等风险保持警惕；然而，在面对新技术时，人们却往往更乐于迅速采用新设备和应用程序，却缺乏同样的谨慎态度。
“涉及技术，人们的信任度高得惊人，”瓦特内说道，并指出人们往往会毫不犹豫地点击各种提示，授予新技术的访问权限。
他表示，随着人工智能系统越来越能够代表用户采取行动，这种信任程度值得我们进行更深入的审视。

title: 英伟达参投的Firmus计划澳洲IPO 目标估值300亿美元

title: 日本东京9月份核心通胀率升至2.7%，支持加息预期
content:
周五公布的数据显示，日本首都东京9月份核心通胀率有所上升，凸显了日益加剧的价格压力，这为日本央行进一步加息的预期提供了有力支撑。
该数据被视为日本全国通胀趋势的先行指标，将成为影响日本央行最新季度通胀预测的因素之一。该央行将于10月29日至30日召开下一次政策会议，届时将公布这些预测。
政府数据显示，东京9月份核心消费者价格指数（剔除生鲜食品但包含燃料成本）同比上涨2.7%，涨幅较8月份的1.8%有所扩大，并超过了市场预期的2.4%。
剔除生鲜食品和燃料价格后，所谓的“核心的核心”CPI—该指数被日本央行密切关注，被视为衡量趋势性通胀的更佳指标——9月份上涨了3.0%，涨幅超过8月份的2.0%。
尽管政府的燃油补贴此前将核心消费者通胀率控制在日本央行的目标水平之下，但近期批发通胀的飙升凸显了来自中东冲突、日元疲软以及强劲的人工智能（AI）相关需求的日益加剧的价格压力。
日本央行上月将利率上调至31年来的最高水平；行长植田和男释放信号称，日本央行已进入旨在防止通胀超调目标的新阶段，这也为进一步加息敞开了大门。

title: 美债收益率回落削弱加息预期 金价企稳
content:
美债收益率走低，美联储官员释放信号，称需要更多时间评估下一步利率举措，金价小幅收涨；不过中东局势存在升级可能性，能源价格维持高位。
现货黄金交投于每盎司4180美元附近，较上一交易日上涨0.5%，但本周累计跌幅或将达到2%。周四美债整条收益率曲线下行，10年期美债收益率从24年高点回落，市场担忧法国财政前景，推升避险资产需求。黄金不产生利息，高收益率通常对金价形成压制，这也是9月金价下跌6%的主要原因。
美联储副主席菲利普·杰斐逊表示，可能需要更多时间评估是否需要进一步加息，市场对立即加息的押注随之降温。目前交易员认为10月加息概率约27%，本周早些时候该概率为70%。
中东冲突存在恶化迹象，油价上涨，该地区能源流通恢复进程或将受阻。一名美国官员称，五角大楼或将向波斯湾增派一艘航母以及一万名水兵与海军陆战队。本次部署完成后，航母战斗群数量将回到2月底对伊朗开战初期的水平。
万嘉环球市场高级市场分析师陈赫柏表示：“金价开盘表现平静，看似风平浪静，实则暗流涌动。美国通胀回落、市场对美联储10月加息预期降温、油价回调，给黄金带来喘息空间。但持续高企的美债收益率与强势美元构成强大阻力，将金价限制在4100美元附近。”
现货黄金上涨0.1%，报每盎司4182.20美元。白银上涨0.3%，报每盎司61.14美元，前一日涨幅0.9%。铂金与钯金小幅走高。衡量美元强弱的彭博美元现货指数在上一交易日上涨0.4%后，保持平稳。

title: 油价维持涨势 此前美国考虑向中东派遣第三艘航母
content:
油价连续两日上涨后企稳。美国正考虑向中东增派一支航母战斗群，此举或将升级对伊战争，有可能阻碍能源流通的恢复。
12月交割的布伦特原油交易价格高于每桶102美元，此前两个交易日累计涨幅超6%；西德克萨斯中质原油（WTI）价格接近每桶93美元。一名美国官员称，五角大楼或将向波斯湾增派一艘航母以及一万名水兵与海军陆战队，一旦唐纳德·特朗普总统决定加大对伊朗打击力度，此举将提供更多军事选项。
本周原油期货大幅震荡，交易员权衡中东能源流通改善与局势升级风险。美伊战争已进入第八个月，外交谈判暂无明显进展，布伦特原油年内涨幅接近70%。
澳新集团分析师布莱恩·马丁与丹尼尔·海因斯在研报中表示：“经过六个月持续去库，库存处于低位，原油市场极易再度出现价格飙升。投资者越来越担心，伊朗会针对美方在该地区的军事部署，袭击美国资产与能源基础设施。”
局势再添隐忧：英国海上贸易组织表示，收到报告称一艘油轮在霍尔木兹海峡航行时遭到不明飞行物击中。该机构称，船只受损程度与环境影响尚不清楚。
就在市场对中东供应的担忧刚刚有所缓解之际，紧张局势再度升温。华尔街分析师本周早些时候表示，该地区原油流量已接近战前水平，但燃料供应尚未同等程度恢复。
与此同时，伊朗9月似乎没有向油轮装载任何原油，这是美国海上封锁切断伊朗进入全球能源市场渠道的最新信号。
据知情人士透露，为缓解燃料供应紧张，特朗普政府正施压欧盟释放柴油储备，以此规避美国实施出口限制。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特敦促欧洲伙伴助力缓解全球燃料短缺。

title: 美债反弹放大就业数据重要性 加息预期迫近
content:
专题：非农前瞻：经济学家预计9月私营部门新增9万人
债券交易商大举押注美联储即将进一步加息，即便市场预期就业增长放缓，也难以显著改变政策前景。
彭博调查的经济学家预计，美国劳工部周五发布的就业报告将显示，9月新增非农就业约9万人，低于上月的16.2万人。
但该新增水平基本持平于今年月度均值，表明劳动力市场依旧韧性十足，给美联储继续收紧货币政策留出空间。美联储当前核心目标是压低通胀，过去五年通胀持续高于目标水平。
普信集团投资级主管、投资组合经理史蒂夫·布思称：“美债要上涨，新增就业需接近零甚至负增长，而且薪资数据必须大幅不及预期。”“当前环境下，就业市场要触发债市上涨，门槛其实相当高。”
周四美国债市抛售有所缓解。欧洲债务负担加剧引发担忧，投资者涌入美债寻求避险；同时两名美联储官员——米歇尔·鲍曼与菲利普·杰斐逊表示，政策制定者应多观察一段时间，再决定是否需要继续加息。受此影响，两年期美债收益率下行约10个基点，跌破4.8%，10年期美债收益率也从24年高点回落。
但分析师表示，本次反弹并非源于美国经济前景改变，或是推高收益率的压力有所缓解。油价维持在每桶100美元附近，结束对伊战争暂无明显进展。联邦政府高额赤字支出叠加人工智能热潮，持续为经济扩张提供动力。今年通胀已经跃升至3%以上。
期货交易商小幅下调加息押注规模，预计下次加息要等到12月会议，但仍预期到明年7月前至少会有三次25个基点的加息。
不过，此前债市的大幅抛售，令市场走势变得难以预判。
周三美国通胀数据略低于预期时，美债曾短暂走高，但涨幅很快回吐，收益率再度向数十年新高攀升。分析师称，当前市场头寸高度押注利率上行，若就业数据大幅不及预期，投资者平仓部分押注，有可能延续周四的涨势。
蒙特利尔银行资本市场美国利率策略主管伊恩·林根表示：“如果数据被市场解读为劳动力市场提前承压的信号，债市的上涨幅度，会远大于数据符合预期或略强时的下跌幅度。”
但市场对抛售潮已经见顶的信心不足。联博基金固定收益策略师兼投资组合经理卡伦·曼纳称，自美联储9月16日加息会议后，她的看空情绪有所减弱，但仍不确信收益率已经见顶。
曼纳表示：“利率大幅上行的核心逻辑已经在很大程度上兑现，但收益率仍有继续走高的可能。”

title: Bangkok cements its place as gem-trading hub
content:
Francesca Fearon

Published October 2 2026

Thailand’s ruby and sapphire mines may have been largely exhausted more than three decades ago, but the country remains one of the world’s most important centres for the coloured gemstone trade. Its dealers, cutters and treatment specialists handle stones sourced from across Africa and Asia, supplying jewellery manufacturers and international luxury houses.

Gem and jewellery exports excluding unwrought gold reached $13.6bn in 2025, up 41 per cent from the previous year, according to the Gem and Jewelry Institute of Thailand. The wider sector made up almost 8 per cent of the country’s exports and employs more than 800,000 people across the supply chain.

That position comes into focus each September, when gem and jewellery fairs in Bangkok and Hong Kong concentrate buyers, dealers and inventory in two of the industry’s most important Asian trading centres. Last month’s Bangkok Gems & Jewelry Fair generated more than $174mn in trade and attracted more than 50,000 buyers and visitors from 123 countries. Gem trading continues year round, but larger transactions often cluster around the shows as buyers inspect stones and parcels in person and make sourcing decisions face to face.

“Bangkok remains the place to see the finest ruby and sapphire, and those two stones have long sat at the centre of high-jewellery programmes, which is why many European houses return two or three times a year,” says Simon Dussart, founder of Asia Lounges, which trades rubies and sapphires alongside emeralds, garnets, spinels and tourmalines.

For GemMatrix, a trader in rubies, sapphires and emeralds, Bangkok and Hong Kong consistently produce the strongest commercial results, after the company also tested fairs in Las Vegas, Tucson and Vicenza. “Thailand is at the heart of our production and gemstone expertise, while Hong Kong strengthens our access to China and other international markets,” says chief executive Andrei Kornilov.

Thailand is ranked as the world’s third-largest exporter of coloured gemstones, according to the GIT. Its gemstone trade dates back to the 14th century and was once supported by ruby and sapphire mines around Chanthaburi and Trat in the south-east. Although those deposits were largely exhausted by the 1990s, Thailand had by then developed into an international centre for cutting, polishing, heat treatment and trading.

That shift was helped by expertise brought by Burmese émigrés following the 1962 military coup in what is now Myanmar, as well as access to stones from neighbouring countries, Sri Lanka and, increasingly, Africa. When Paraíba tourmaline deposits were discovered in Mozambique, for example, stones were sent to Thailand for heat treatment to enhance their distinctive blue-green colour.

“Thailand-based gem dealers have sharp business intuition,” says Sasha Golokoz, who is the owner of Bangkok-based dealer Vitalit Fine Gems. “They are always on the front line of new discoveries worldwide. They were the first to open buying offices in Madagascar and Mozambique, then Tanzania.”

That combination of trading and processing expertise allows Bangkok-based companies to serve different parts of the jewellery market. GemMatrix supplies calibrated gemstones to manufacturers in Russia, China, India and the US. “We purchase rough emerald, sapphire and ruby at auctions, and the material is then cut in Thailand into calibrated sizes according to exact millimetre dimensions,” says Kornilov.

Such orders require consistency in size, colour, cut and quality, as well as clear disclosure of treatments. A second part of GemMatrix’s business involves sourcing selected rough material or individual stones, which may be cut or recut and assembled into matched pairs, suites and layouts for major jewellery houses.

Those clients may be looking for individual rubies of three carats or more, which Kornilov says are becoming increasingly difficult to source, or suites of smaller stones where colour consistency is more important. For sapphires, he says demand remains concentrated on traditional shapes including ovals, cushions, emerald cuts and pears.

Thailand’s gemstone network also supplies smaller jewellery brands. Kavant & Sharart, a Bangkok-based jeweller for which the US is the largest market, sources most of its coloured stones through established local dealers.

“Having substantial gems physically in front of us is very important, particularly when we are developing collections,” says Shar-Linn Liew, who co-founded the company with Nuttapon “Kenny” Yongkiettakul in 2011. “Side by side we can see how they work with designs.”

Relationships with dealers remain particularly important in a market where stones vary considerably and purchasing cannot always be standardised. “We’ve worked with many of our dealers for years,” says Sophia Hirsh of London-based family jewellery house Hirsh. “For me, the best relationships in this industry are built over time — you develop trust, you learn each other’s tastes.”

The breadth of stones traded in Bangkok is also expanding beyond the rubies and sapphires on which the market was built. “Demand is not limited to ruby and sapphire; spinel, garnet and tourmaline are also on the rise,” says Dussart. “Ruby and sapphire set the tempo for the season; the rest of the palette is what we spend most of the year looking at.”

Dussart uses the fairs primarily to buy for clients rather than to sell. He says demand for colour has benefited garnets, while teal sapphires are again being requested by clients in Europe and Asia. His inventory includes Mandarin, Malay, tsavorite, grape and demantoid garnets.

For Golokoz, smaller independent jewellers can be particularly attractive customers because purchases can be agreed quickly. “They are their own decision makers and can make purchasing decisions on the spot,” she says. Major jewellery houses, by contrast, often work on consignment, with approval and purchasing processes that can take months.

Supply is another concern. Golokoz, who built her business around spinels, tourmalines and garnets, says high-quality spessartite and tsavorite garnets have become increasingly difficult to obtain. Mandarin garnet featured prominently in high jewellery this year, she says, just as supplies of suitable material were becoming scarce.

She has seen similar cycles with Mahenge spinels and lagoon tourmalines from Namibia, where jewellery demand followed earlier activity among gemstone traders. Golokoz is now increasing her focus on neon-pink rubellites, which she says are attracting greater interest and formed part of her offering at Jewellery & Gem World Hong Kong in September.

title: Japanese watchmakers push for overseas growth
content:
Rachael Taylor

Published October 2 2026

Japan’s watchmakers are expanding overseas at a time when growth in the global watch market has become harder to find. The value of Japanese watch exports rose 10 per cent to ¥207.9bn ($1.32bn) in 2025, according to the Japan Clock & Watch Association (JCWA), while Swiss watch exports fell 1.7 per cent to SFr25.6bn ($31.2bn).

The two industries remain vastly different in scale, but the figures point to a broader shift. Japanese manufacturers, long associated internationally with reliable and affordable timepieces, are pushing further into higher-priced mechanical watches and expanding distribution beyond their domestic market. At the same time, smaller Japanese brands are finding overseas buyers attracted by their craftsmanship, design and relatively accessible prices.

The shift is also evident at Japan’s three largest watch groups. Seiko, Citizen and Casio have all reported strong growth in their latest quarterly results. In the three months to June 30, Seiko Group’s watch business sales rose 34 per cent to ¥63bn, with operating profit up 77 per cent to ¥13.3bn. Citizen Group’s watch sales increased 32 per cent to ¥54.8bn, with operating profit up 62 per cent to ¥7.1bn, while Casio’s watch sales rose 29 per cent to ¥51bn.

The momentum extends beyond exports. Japan became the world’s second-largest market for Swiss watch exports in 2025, while domestic shipments by Japanese manufacturers also increased. Mechanical watch volumes rose 29 per cent and digital quartz volumes fell 31 per cent, according to the JCWA.

At Seiko, much of that growth is being driven by a strategy of building its brands internationally and moving further into higher-priced watches. Akio Naito, president of Seiko Watch Corporation, says the group’s recent performance “reflects the steady progress of the global brands strategy we have been pursuing over the past decade, rather than simply favourable market conditions”.

The clearest example is Grand Seiko, the group’s upmarket brand. Its watches had been sold in Japan since 1960, but were not exported until 2010. In 2017, Grand Seiko became a standalone brand, a move that accelerated its international expansion.

Grand Seiko Evolution 9 Spring Drive

Hypebeast x Citizen Zenshin

“One clear example is the US, where Grand Seiko sales increased approximately 10 times within five years of becoming an independent brand,” says Naito.

“The contribution of international markets has grown significantly compared with the period before the brand’s separation. Today, the sales to the non-Japanese consumers are as big as those to the Japanese consumers, if not bigger.” Seiko Group now plans to repeat this with its other fine watchmaking brand, Credor, which began exporting last year after just over 50 years of selling solely within Japan.

Naito says the US is “one of the most important growth markets” for Seiko Group, led by sales of Grand Seiko, Prospex, Presage and Seiko 5 Sports. This year, Seiko extended its relationship with Japanese baseball superstar Shohei Ohtani, who plays for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He is now an ambassador for Seiko and Grand Seiko, and Naito expects the partnership to raise the brands’ profiles not only among US consumers, but also in Taiwan, South Korea and Japan, where the sport is also popular. Other global markets delivering “strong momentum” for Seiko include India and Australia.

Naito says Seiko’s international growth has also been accompanied by a shift in consumer perception. “I cannot speak for the entire industry but, in my view, historically Japanese watchmaking was generally valued in the context of functional and practical excellence,” he says. “However, in recent years at Grand Seiko we have seen a growing appreciation not only for functionality, but also for the craftsmanship and aesthetic sensibility behind our watchmaking.”

This is a trend that Sven Erik Henriksen has also been monitoring closely. A decade ago, the longtime Swiss watch executive discovered small-batch Japanese brand Minase, which specialises in the zaratsu mirror-polishing technique. It was launched in 2005 by Japanese toolmaker Kyowa and uses Swiss-made movements.

Henriksen began representing the brand as a sales agent in Europe and the Middle East in 2016, and his first move was to create branding that focused on its Japanese DNA. “We spent about a year preparing the material,” he recalls. “You can imagine that Japanese people selling Japanese watches to Japanese people do not need to show temples or Mount Fuji.

Minase Seven Windows

Orient Bambino

“They were following a different line of industrial manufacturing and precision, which are the strengths of the brand, but you couldn’t tell that it was Japanese. I sent photographers to Japan to get the feeling of the countryside, and impressions of the traditional dancing, cooking, sake brewing.”

Henriksen says overseas collectors have also become more receptive to Japanese brands. “Customers are more excited about Japanese brands than Swiss brands because they all own two or three Swiss watches and they are looking for something different,” he says. Henriksen exhibits the brand at collector shows in Europe, including Geneva Watch Days and a specialist show called Matsuri that took place in Lyon, France, at the end of September, organised by Japanese watch magazine Wadokei.

With annual production of 600 watches, Minase is one of several boutique Japanese watchmakers gaining international attention. Kurono Tokyo, led by watchmaker Hajime Asaoka , is another. It produces sought-after timepieces at accessible prices, and limits new releases to one per customer. Its latest watch, which opened for pre-order at the end of September, is the $2,380 Calendrier Small Batch Release with a blue dial bearing vertical guilloche stripes and “Japan Made”.

Independent watchmaker Masahiro Kikuno, who in 2013 became the first Japanese full member of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants — the world’s most prestigious assembly of skilled independent watchmakers — has temporarily suspended new orders until at least 2032.

Price is another factor in Japanese brands’ international positioning. Many remain relatively inexpensive compared with Swiss mechanical watches, an advantage that extends beyond small independent makers.

Wiebke Bird, head of Orient Europe at Epson Europe, has been charged with growing the Japanese-made Orient watch brand’s sales in her territory, and its pricing has helped win retail distribution. Seiko Epson — a separate, independently managed company from Seiko Watch Corporation — acquired a majority stake in Orient Watch in 2009, making it a wholly owned subsidiary before fully merging operations in 2017.

“Our offering for in-house mechanical movements is so unique at our price point that really that’s the thing that makes us the most interesting,” says Bird, who says the brand has “largely moved away” from quartz movements. Its entry-level AC0F mechanical model sells for less than £260, and Bird says the brand attracts particularly strong interest from consumers in their twenties and thirties.

The UK, which Orient entered in 2023, has become one of its faster-growing European markets, where it sells directly to consumers online while also partnering with retail chains including Ernest Jones and F Hinds. Last year, it achieved sales growth of 100 per cent in the UK, and expects it to be between 50 per cent and 75 per cent up in 2026. Much of the sales growth in Europe is being driven by watches priced at £500 or less, which Bird says is very different to Orient’s domestic market, where its premium line Orient Star is more dominant.

Despite its European strategy being led by affordability, Bird believes that outdated perceptions of Japanese watches as being “less than” Swiss watches is linked to its history with quartz movements. Seiko was the first brand to launch a commercial quartz wristwatch with the Seiko Astron in 1969, which led Swiss manufacturers to follow suit. This ushered in the so-called quartz crisis of the 1970s as inexpensive quartz watches flooded the market, decimating sales and production of mechanical timepieces.

“[In the decades since the quartz crisis] people have found that [the Japanese watch industry] wasn’t just about the performance of timekeeping at the expense of the craftsmanship or the desirability of a mechanical watch,” Bird says.

“Japanese brands like us are seen more and more to be continuing that mechanical watch tradition and craftsmanship. It’s recognised that we’re using efficiency, design and engineering to deliver an affordable mechanical watch, not just affordable quartz.”

title: OpenAI已向100多个机通报AI智能体未经授权活动事件
content:
OpenAI周四在一篇博客文章中表示，该公司已向100多个机构通报了涉及其AI智能体未经授权活动的事件。此举正值AI 实验室因“失控”AI 智能体的活动而面临日益严格的审查之际。
在 Hugging Face 遭遇意外入侵事件后，这家由萨姆·奥特曼领导的公司正对其 AI 模型的活动进行全面审查。
OpenAI 正在筛查约 50 PB 的数据，以全面掌握“失控智能体”（rogue agent）活动的具体范围。
近几个月来，全球范围内发生了一系列由失控 AI 智能体引发的备受关注的安全入侵事件，这引发了 AI 业界对于能否管控当前正在开发中的更强大 AI 模型的广泛担忧。
OpenAI 表示：“在某些情况下，模型以非预期的方式使用了互联网访问权限，或者事后看来，当时实施的限制措施并不 理想 。过去几个月里，我们一直在采取新的技术和运营措施，以避免此类问题或在问题出现的极早期阶段将其发现，并将继续推进这项工作。”
OpenAI 此前曾表示，鉴于工作规模巨大，这项审查需要数月时间才能完成。
Hugging Face 事件是 OpenAI 迄今为止在其 AI 模型中发现的最严重的“失控智能体”活动。

title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed
content:
A mental health trust in east London, where a man was killed by a fellow patient, has been warned further deaths may occur unless staff issues are addressed.

Hugo Flint Cahan, 34, was strangled by 22-year-old Rolando Torres-Pena at Newham Mental Health Centre, which provides care for acutely mentally ill men, in January 2023.

The coroner has sent a report to the Trust and NHS England raising serious concerns about the care the two men received.

It follows a six-day inquest in September during which the senior coroner for east London, Graeme Irvine, concluded that neglect had more than trivially contributed to Flint Cahan's death.

Asleep on the job

On the night of Flint Cahan's death, staff on the ward were found to have been asleep on the job and on their phones for long periods.

East London NHS Foundation Trust (ELFT) says the failings identified were "wholly unacceptable" and that it has undertaken a "significant programme of work" to improve inpatient services.

The coroner's Prevention of Future Deaths report highlights 14 concerns. These include failing to carry out "timely and thorough observations" of patients, then falsifying records "in the safe knowledge that staff on duty would not report or escalate the deception".

The document also says there were delays in starting CPR on Flint Cahan when he was discovered, that staff misled the police as to what the patients had been doing on the night of the incident, and that staff colluded with each other to take two-hour unauthorised breaks.

Torres-Pena was given a hospital order with no time limit after pleading guilty to manslaughter by diminished responsibility in 2023.

The coroner also raised concerns that many of the failings had been brought up at a previous inquest he'd conducted.

"The findings in this inquest are strikingly similar to the findings of an inquest before this court in 2021, remedial measures reported in that case do not appear to have been implemented effectively by the trust", the report says.

"Findings of dishonesty on this scale are extraordinarily rare in a coronial investigation. The public are entitled to expect a clear explanation of how this was allowed to happen and what is being done to ensure it never happens again," says James Cahan, the family solicitor and Hugo's cousin.

Serious failings

The coroner also criticised NHS England for not making independently produced reports into patient safety at Trusts publically available.

The inquest heard that a report commissioned after Flint Cahan's death identified some of the serious failings investigated by the coroner.

An NHS spokesperson said "patient safety incident investigations should always be published, with any necessary redactions to protect patients' identities, while making sure the lessons and learning are clear".

In a statement, Dr David Bridle, Chief Medical Officer for ELFT, apologised to Flint Cahan's family for the failings in his care.

He says one member of staff on duty on the night of the incident has been sacked while four others are now under investigation by the Trust.

"We will ensure the learning from the coroner's findings informs our continuing work to strengthen patient safety and care," says Dr Bridle.

ELFT and NHS England have until 19 November to respond.

title: 达拉斯联储行长呼吁再加息至少50个基点
content:
达拉斯联储行长洛丽·洛根（Lorie Logan）周四表示，美联储需要将短期借贷成本再上调至少50个基点，以使货币政策转为“适度紧缩”，并推动通胀重回美联储2%的目标轨道。
洛根在向德克萨斯州企业高管和社区领袖发表讲话时表示，美联储上个月将政策利率上调25个基点，使其目前处于3.75%至4.00%的区间，这是收紧政策“重要的一步”；此次讲话是在该地区联储银行总部进行的。
“尽管如此，我目前的评估是，目标利率区间还需要再上调50个基点或更多，以恰当平衡我们双重使命目标相关的前景与风险，”她说，“我们必须恢复物价稳定。”
她表示，经济正在走强，劳动力市场也处于良好的平衡状态。虽然随着暂时性因素的消退，通胀率正在下降，但若不进一步加息，通胀率似乎不太可能降至远低于2.5%的水平。
洛根表示：“再进行几次目标区间上调，就会抵消联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）去年秋季出于风险管理考量而实施的降息举措。”她所指的是美联储负责制定政策的联邦公开市场委员会，该委员会在去年的最后三次会议上累计下调了75个基点的政策利率。
洛根发表上述言论之际，基准10年期美债收益率一度触及24年高点，随后回落至5.24%左右。
洛根表示，长期债券收益率走高表明市场参与者预期经济将强劲增长，且美联储政策利率将处于较高水平；不过，这也可能反映了期限溢价的上升，而期限溢价“可能会拖累经济，从而降低收紧货币政策的必要性”。
她指出，究竟需要何种水平的政策利率才能产生一定的限制性效应尚不确定，且这一水平会随更广泛的金融环境变化而调整。
“我将继续密切关注劳动力市场、物价、经济增长、消费及金融状况，以评估政策是否正变得具有限制性。”

title: The rise of lymphatic drainage beauty videos and whether the massages work
content:
If she's ever feeling bloated, Abbey Alexandra has a go-to routine, using body oil and a wooden roller to perform stomach massages.

She shares before-and-after videos on TikTok, saying she feels the process leaves her depuffed and defined: "You definitely feel a lot better after, they are relaxing."

The technique is a form of lymphatic drainage massage, adapted from a medical treatment and shared as a beauty trend. Celebrity fans include Maya Jama, who shares her clinic sessions, and actress Hailey Bieber, who told Time magazine: "I swear by them."

Whether there is a physical change - or any need for one - is debatable, but fans of the massages claim they help "flatten" and "debloat" and give a "snatched waist" and "sculpted abs". But what's actually happening to their bodies?

What do the videos show?

Many videos on social media promoting lymphatic massage show a woman either standing sideways, facing the front or perhaps lying down with her stomach showing a slight - and very normal - curve outwards.

Then begins the methodical massage in circular motions seemingly draining fluid away. By the end, her stomach appears flatter - if a little red.

But social media body trends should always be viewed with scepticism, says Dr Ella Guest, senior research fellow and health psychologist at the Centre for Appearance Research based at the University of the West of England.

"These images might be altered using photo-editing tools or filters, people standing in particular poses, use of lighting, lots could even be AI-generated," she says.

"I think stopping to reflect on what you see and questioning whether it looks realistic, or if it's very aligned with beauty standards, can be useful. Remember, if something looks too good to be true, it probably is."

What is the lymphatic system?

The lymphatic system is a network of channels and glands throughout the body that helps fight infection and remove excess fluid, according to the NHS.

Dr Xand van Tulleken tells Morning Live that the lymphatic system helps remove excess fluid from tissues and supports the immune system.

"When it is not working properly, it can contribute to swelling, which can be a condition called lymphoedema."

This commonly affects people who have cancers that involve the lymph system or who've had treatment involving the lymph nodes.

It causes swelling in any part of the body, but usually develops in the arms or legs.

"In simple terms, the lymphatic system helps keep your body's fluid levels balanced, cleans up waste, and supports your defences against illness," says van Tulleken.

What's the massage doing?

Dr Xand says manual lymphatic drainage is one of a range of treatments used by medical professionals "if your lymphatic system isn't working as it should".

He describes it as using "light pressure" and "strategic massage techniques" to "clear" your lymphatic system.

"They'll coax excess lymph fluid from your swollen tissues toward your lymph nodes, where the lymph can reabsorb," he says - adding lymph nodes are found in the armpits, neck and groin.

He adds that these massages can be a "safe way" to relieve symptoms for conditions like lymphoedema but are not suitable for some people with pre-existing medical conditions.

He stresses: "No one should get their health advice from Instagram - far safer to use the NHS website, or consult your GP."

Abbey, who has endometriosis which she says causes her to feel bloated, began doing her own massage routines twice a week aer seeing social media posts about lymphatic drainage.

"I started using my hands and then I bought some wooden tools as well.

"After doing my routine, I personally feel less puffy and bloated, particularly around my stomach.

"Visually, I notice that my stomach looks a little more defined and I also feel lighter and more comfortable."

Does it work?

Dr Xand says there is "no need" for most people to perform lymphatic drainage treatments at home.

"There is very little high-quality evidence showing they provide meaningful or lasting benefits for healthy individuals, and it does not promote fat loss," he says.

But he does note that lymphatic drainage massages can feel "relaxing" and some people "can notice a temporary reduction in swelling".

"For most healthy people, regular movement, exercise and staying hydrated are all that's needed to support normal lymphatic function," he says.

"Unless someone has a diagnosed lymphatic condition, I don't think anyone needs routine lymphatic drainage treatments, despite the growing popularity of these practices on social media."

For Abbey, it's something she enjoys. "I know the visual difference is temporary... But I do like how I look and feel afterwards so it'll always be a part of my routine."

However, Guest warns striving for a sculpted stomach could "feed into people's insecurities".

"We know that when we compare ourselves online and try to live up to these trends, we tend to scrutinise our appearance more and feel less satisfied with how we look," she says.

"The reality is that healthy bodies come in a wide range of shapes and sizes."

title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election
content:
Ademba Allans is making it "cool" to vote in Kenya.

The student journalist turned civic mobiliser launched a voter registration drive on social media earlier this year, using snappy selfies infused with music and humour to target young people.

The result astonished him and many observers of Kenyan politics – by the time the registration period ended, 2.6 million new voters across the country had signed up. He is aiming to get another 2.3 million on board in the next round.

"It was the Gen Z way of doing politics," he tells me. "Fun, trendy, sexy, fashionable. Because of how we created the hype around it, people had the fear of missing out. Everybody wanted to be involved."

Gen Z, the term used to describe people born in the late 1990s and early 2000s, burst onto the scene two years ago with mass protests that forced the government to retreat on a widely unpopular tax bill. But their victory was followed by a police crackdown that killed and injured dozens of demonstrators.

Now many young Kenyans are planning to move from the street to the ballot box, angry with a political establishment they accuse of corruption and police brutality.

And they have the numbers to make a difference - more than 30% of voting-age Kenyans are younger than 35.

Polls suggest President William Ruto is looking vulnerable.

But can Gen Z convert a decentralized digital-led rebellion into organised political power?

"These youth-led movements are a wild card, in that they are unpredictable," says political analyst Tom Mboya.

"They don't require much in the way of resources and can pop up at any time. The finance bill protests were political in nature, but the movement has not been tested at an overtly political level. So if they decide to support a candidate, then he's likely to do fairly well."

One of the strengths of the digitally savvy Gen Z activists is that they have been able to mobilise outside the party structures and ethnic allegiances that anchor Kenyan politics.

Allans has been careful not to advocate a particular candidate or party – emphasising leadership rather than politicians, marshalling a new force, he says, outside traditional tribal voting blocs.

"There has never been a case where there is a bloc that is not affiliated to any person or any party. They just want to vote in the right leaders, and this is what we created," he says.

"It's more of a swing vote because you cannot tell who we are going to vote for."

Ruto and his United Democratic Alliance (UDA) are facing strong head winds with less than a year to go before the August 2027 vote.

More than three-quarters of respondents to a survey conducted in June felt the country was moving in the wrong direction, with two-thirds saying their personal economic situation had worsened since Ruto was elected in 2022.

But analysts argue that the president does not necessarily have to be popular to win. He is a master political organiser with the resources of the state, they say.

Ruto's political rivals are also fragmented, and it is not yet clear whether they can form a united opposition to take him on.

One man who has captured the attention of many Gen Zs is Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna. He has emerged as the leader of a movement called Linda Mwananchi (Protect the Citizen), which is getting strong support from disaffected young people.

Sifuna first caught their attention when he tried to stop police from shooting at protesters who were storming parliament during the 2024 demonstrations.

Now he is championing a "people-led" movement that promotes the protection of human rights and rule of law as enshrined in the constitution.

He has yet to officially declare a run for the presidency, but is already on the road rallying support. The BBC caught up with him on a recent trip to Meru county in central Kenya, a region that voted strongly for Ruto in the last election.

"Young people want us to create an environment where everybody feels that they can compete fairly," he told me before starting out on his raucous road show.

"We need to absolutely dismantle the system so that everybody has a fair chance at life, a fair chance at education, a fair chance at employment, and the opportunities to grow themselves.

"This election in 2027 is when this theory that the young people are advancing will be put to the test," he said. "Our challenge as a leadership is to ensure you have a compelling message that then encourages people to come out, let them see the vision for the new country."

Ruto also had a compelling vision for the country when he came to power in 2022.

He promised to transform the economy from the bottom up, with a focus on lifting the marginalised. His government has since introduced changes including landmark reforms that widen access to public healthcare, but many young people felt betrayed by his austerity measures and tax hikes.

"I'm here to participate in a revolution change that we want a new Kenyan youth leader who knows the common problems that are facing the young people," 23-year-old Brandon Muremi told the BBC.

I found him in a relatively quiet corner of the final stop in a hectic day of a "rolling rally" – Sifuna's convoy visited four locations, sometimes blocking traffic as he and local politicians climbed on top of their vehicles and delivered rousing speeches at ear-splitting volumes.

"We are looking for a leader who sticks to his plans, not just talking the promises that he makes," agreed Conrad Mutangili, a 19-year-old mechanical engineering student who had come out of curiosity.

"We are looking for somebody who can actually accomplish and actually bring to the people what they are talking about," he said. "Because they promise sweets, but we don't feel any sugar in our mouths."

"We want immediate results," said a 22-year-old computer science student, Yvonne Kileme, acknowledging that the results of government projects may be more long-term. "And one thing that we want as youths is employment, employment, employment, employment."

Ruto argues strongly that his government is delivering jobs, and says the high rate of youth unemployment is a problem that predates his presidency.

He has reached out to Gen Z with various programmes that offer grants and loans to small business and youth-led enterprises, technology hubs and digital work opportunities.

The national youth leader of Ruto's UDA, Kariuki Ngunjiri, told the BBC he was confident of winning the election with an overwhelming majority.

"The president is a listening president and he's been able to now come down to the youth, get what their concerns are, give them jobs, and that has absolutely, even for the party, given us a head start," he said.

"We are not worried about the social media buzz because we are people who actually engage the young people on real, actual, tangible development. What you see mostly on sponsored hashtags and sponsored headlines does not really concern us."

He was speaking as a senior sports official promised to expand the stadium-building programme with another venue, at a packed UDA town hall meeting in Kangema, about 100km (60 miles) north of the capital, Nairobi.

Like so many others, 23-year-old Shintah Mutahi was job hunting.

"I came to listen to what they were saying," she said, "maybe find an opportunity for a job. I think they can give me a chance, they should just be given some time to do that."

John Kiragu, a local UDA youth leader, said he understood the grievances that had driven young people to protest.

"There have been challenges," he said, "but now the government is really trying hard to consolidate the youth. The government is implementing programmes that will really uplift their lives."

Kiragu told me he was involved in a programme to deal with youth alcoholism – a real problem in this region. Many of the young men who attended the morning town hall meeting were already drunk on a cheap local liquor.

The captain of the local football team, Calvin Ware, also turned up to hear the stadium announcement. He said he had heard similar promises many times before, especially before elections, and this one was not going to influence his vote.

"We have already made our mind," he said. "The whole government should go home. We want to build a new Kenya, new youth, new people, fresh people from all over the country, and we are not basing on tribal [allegiances] or anything else. We just want a change, a change, and a change. Nothing else."

As we were speaking, we heard a loud cheer – the event had ended and people were lining up to receive cash handouts – 350 Kenyan shillings, about $3 (£2.20).

It is common practice to pay people to attend political meetings in Kenya, and politicians can use much larger sums to try and influence votes.

"More so than many other parts of the world, money talks in an election here," says political analyst Mboya. "The cost of politics is significantly higher than in other parts of the world."

Less than a year to Kenya's election, it does feel like politics might be changing, that the race could be shaped by youth disillusionment with the political establishment. But while the Gen Z movement has rejected the "old politics" based on ethnic group and money, those have been the building blocks that win elections in Kenya.

Nobody yet knows what the energy of Gen Z voters will mean at the ballot box.

title: Crypto thieves attack man in home and threaten to kill pregnant wife's baby in 'horrific' robbery
content:
Warning: This story contains distressing details

A businessman was beaten with hammers by masked men who broke into his home and threatened to kill his heavily pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency.

Speaking to the BBC, the couple, who want to remain anonymous, described the attack as "horrific" and said they feared for their unborn baby's life.

The attackers left in a car driven by a getaway driver after the man transferred his crypto savings.

Crimestoppers are offering a £10,000 reward for information in the attack, which was captured on home security footage and is being investigated by the police.

Experts say it is one of a growing type of violent theft known as a "wrench attack" targeting cryptocurrency investors.

As crypto coins have risen in value, reports of these violent robberies linked to digital assets have emerged in the UK, France and the US.

Once funds are transferred, recovering them can be extremely difficult.

The man, who the BBC is calling James, said three intruders forced their way into their Solihull home before launching an assault which lasted 45 minutes.

"The door gets pushed open, I can see gloves coming in, balaclavas," he said.

James tried to fight the men off but they hit him in the face, head and ribs with hammers.

His wife, who was seven months pregnant, was held down on the sofa by one of the criminals.

"He's got a pillow over her face," James said. "He's literally suffocating her on the sofa. I can hear her screaming, 'I can't breathe'."

The couple still had no idea what the criminals wanted until one of the men demanded James unlock his phone and hand it over.

James said the attackers appeared to know he owned cryptocurrency, but had little understanding of how to access it.

Instead, they were taking instructions from someone else connected via a live video call.

"I can hear the guy on FaceTime saying: 'Show me everything on his phone. Show me what apps he's got'," he said.

When the caller identified a crypto wallet containing substantial funds, the threats escalated dramatically.

"He was basically saying: 'Look, if you don't send us this money now, we're going to stab your wife in the stomach and kill your baby. We're going to kill your wife'," James said.

His wife, who also did not want to be named, described the attack that happened in December last year as "horrific" and said she feared James had been killed when he was unresponsive on the floor.

"It was terrifying," she said.

The woman, in her early thirties, was expecting her third child at the time and said she feared she might lose the baby due to the stress of the attack. The baby survived and was born at full term.

The men left after James transferred his savings - hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency - to the digital wallet of the man on the video call.

They also stole several luxury Rolex watches.

James said before they left, he heard the man on the video call tell his accomplices: "You can have 10 grand each but I am taking the rest."

Rise of the 'wrench attack'

Unlike money held in a conventional bank account, cryptocurrency is often controlled directly by the owner through digital wallets or physical storage devices.

For criminals, that combination of speed, anonymity and irreversibility can make crypto holders attractive targets.

Whilst the vast majority of cryptocurrency theft happens online through hacks and scams, crypto investigators at Chainalysis say "wrench attacks" have surged in recent years.

According to their research, $30m (£22.6m) had been stolen so far this year up to June in violent robberies, making 2026 likely to become the single-worst year for violent crypto attacks on record. Home invasions are also on the rise this year, it found.

The US, Brazil, and Thailand are hotspots but France has seen the largest number of attacks by far, as a result of a data breach at a tax office that has apparently allowed wealthy crypto holders to be located.

"The physical security assumptions that protect traditional wealth, such as bank vaults and armored cars, do not automatically apply in crypto. Often, holders keep their assets in comparatively low security setups, like self-custody wallets, that can be compromised without any institutional gatekeeper standing in the way," said researchers in their report.

James said he became an amateur investor in crypto coins in 2020 and made enough money to quit his job in 2023 to trade full time.

Now he has lost everything and is looking to get back to his traditional job.

Police have yet to identify the attackers.

Crimestoppers is offering a £10,000 reward for information leading to progress in the investigation.

Alan Edwards from the charity hopes people might have information about the three attackers, the driver who was parked outside without a face covering, or the man on the phone.

"These criminals are obviously serious and part of some kind of organised crime gang," he said.

"People might be scared to give us information but we are independent of the police and keep people completely anonymous."

The three attackers are all thought to be in their late teens or early 20s and one of them was a black male with a scar under his left eyebrow.

James said he has little hope of recovering the stolen funds, but instead wanted to see those responsible brought to justice.

He also wants his experience to serve as a warning.

"They threatened my wife and my baby," he said. "People need to understand these risks are real."
