title: 摩根士丹利下调苹果目标价至355美元：新iPhone定价压低利润假设，股价上涨后空间有限
content:
摩根士丹利 将 苹果 目标价从360美元小幅下调至355美元，同时维持“增持”评级。此次下调的核心原因并不是公司长期产品前景恶化，而是新一代iPhone定价低于此前预期，对平均售价和毛利率形成压力，而过去半年苹果股价已经上涨超过30%，在盈利预测变化有限的情况下，进一步估值上行空间有所收窄。
摩根士丹利表示，在重新评估iPhone新品定价、产品规格、交付周期、Siri AI、服务业务提价以及供应链情况后，对苹果整体盈利模型的调整幅度很小。
新iPhone定价低于预期，压低ASP和毛利率
这也是摩根士丹利此次下调目标价最直接的原因。
新款iPhone的实际定价低于该机构此前假设，使其下调了iPhone平均售价和毛利率预期。
对于苹果而言，单机售价变化会直接影响硬件业务收入，同时更低的售价也会压缩产品毛利空间。因此，即使新机销量表现不错，只要产品组合和定价低于此前模型假设，对盈利的贡献就会受到一定限制。
不过，这部分负面影响大部分被其他业务改善抵消。
摩根士丹利同时上调了iPhone销量预期，并看到Mac收入继续好于预期，服务业务也存在小幅上行空间。
因此，最终结果并不是苹果盈利预期明显下调，而是此前市场期待的进一步上修没有出现。
股价半年涨超30%，估值空间被提前消耗
另一个重要因素是苹果股价本身已经大幅上涨。
过去六个月，苹果股价累计上涨超过30%，目前股价约333美元，市值约4.86万亿美元。
在股价快速上涨的同时，摩根士丹利对2027和2028财年的盈利预测却基本没有明显变化，因此目标价与现价之间的潜在上涨空间被压缩。
换句话说，摩根士丹利此次下调目标价更像是一次“估值校准”——基本面仍然强，但此前股价上涨已经提前反映了相当一部分未来增长预期。
长期产品周期判断并未改变
尽管下调目标价，摩根士丹利对苹果未来两年以上的产品周期仍然保持积极判断。
该机构认为，在新任CEO John Ternus领导下，苹果未来两年多的产品创新周期可能是过去十多年最重要的一轮之一。
摩根士丹利预计，苹果可能迎来自2015财年以来首次连续四年iPhone销量增长，并预计2026财年至2028财年每股收益复合增速约为13%。
该机构目前仍预计，苹果2027财年每股收益约为10美元，2028财年接近11美元，分别较市场一致预期高出约0%至3%。
这说明，摩根士丹利对苹果长期盈利增长并没有转向悲观。
9月季度偏积极，但12月季度存在预期下修风险
在短期业绩节奏上，摩根士丹利对9月季度相对乐观。
支撑因素包括iPhone生产计划保持韧性、Mac收入表现更强、服务业务提价，以及关税退款带来的帮助。
但12月季度的情况更加复杂。
摩根士丹利认为，目前华尔街部分预测仍没有充分计入新一代iPhone分批上市带来的影响，因此市场对12月季度iPhone出货量的预期可能仍然偏高。
如果实际出货因为错峰上市低于目前市场预测，12月季度可能面临一定的盈利预期下修。
因此，摩根士丹利此次下调目标价的逻辑可以概括为： 苹果长期产品周期依然强劲，但新iPhone售价低于预期削弱了单机盈利能力，而销量、Mac和服务业务的改善只能基本抵消这一影响；与此同时，股价过去半年已经大幅上涨，使现有盈利预测能够支撑的估值上行空间变得有限。
这也是为什么摩根士丹利选择小幅下调目标价，却继续维持“增持”评级。

title: 花旗：美光科技财报可作为闪迪公司业绩的先行参考信号
content:
专题：聚焦美股2026年第二季度财报
美光 科技周三交出超预期财报，花旗分析师预计， 闪迪 （SNDK）将受益于非易失性存储 ——NAND 闪存产品的旺盛需求。
花旗将闪迪目标价定为 2100 美元，较周三收盘价有近 20.7% 的上行空间；分析师维持这家存储设备厂商的 买入 评级。
花旗指出，美光科技（MU）NAND 闪存业务营收增长 42%，受 NAND 闪存供给紧张 推动，产品价格上涨约 30%。
鉴于闪迪是 NAND 闪存解决方案供应商，花旗预计该公司将充分享受 NAND 闪存的需求红利。
花旗分析师阿西亚・默钱特在研报中写道：“闪迪将持续受益于这一结构性利好行业环境。此外，公司 Bics8 工艺已完成认证，构筑起竞争护城河；长期来看，产品结构向数据中心业务占比提升，将进一步利好公司利润率。”

title: 税收优惠叠加股市收益，赛马市场创下历史纪录
content:
核心要点
今年，即便市场担忧海湾冲突会使财力雄厚的中东赛马买家望而却步，全球最大的纯血马拍卖会依旧刷新纪录。
肯塔基州举办的基恩兰九月周岁马拍卖会，今年总成交额达 5.367 亿美元，较去年的纪录高出约 500 万美元。这场为期两周的拍卖会于 9 月 26 日落幕，共有 70 匹周岁马成交价不低于 100 万美元，高于去年的 56 匹，创下 19 年来新高；周岁马平均成交价上涨近 7%，达到 187933 美元。
本场标王是一匹带有白色脚斑的深枣色公马驹，由包含纸业大亨彼得・布兰特在内的一组投资者以 370 万美元拍下。这匹马的父系是冠军种公马 “恶作剧小子”，该种公马已经繁育出三匹肯塔基德比大赛冠军。
赛马繁育从业者、会计师伦・格林表示，《重大综合法案》带来的税收减免，是近年拍卖会行情火爆的重要推手。该法案正式签署生效两个月后举办的上一届拍卖会，销售额同比大涨 24%。
格林称：“如果你事业有成，想要一项既能抵税，又能博取曝光度、登上报刊头条的资产，赛马行业会是相当不错的投资选择。”
《重大综合法案》永久性恢复 100% 加速折旧 这一税收优惠政策，允许企业核销符合条件的经营性资产成本。虽然这项加速折旧政策多用于商业地产、私人飞机，但企业购入赛马，可在购置当年全额核销采购成本。格林补充，马主还可以对骑乘装备、马厩等相关资产做税务抵扣，或是成立有限责任公司，进一步放大税收优惠的收益。
他还提到，股市行情向好、私募股权退出带来巨额财富，但对很多企业家而言，收购一支职业体育队伍依旧遥不可及；而赛马行业的入场门槛要低得多。
基恩兰总裁兼首席执行官香农・阿文指出，行情火热还有其他驱动因素，多地赛马赛事奖金水平有所提升。
来自中东的买家，包括迪拜、卡塔尔王室成员，已经成为高端纯血马市场举足轻重的群体。
拍卖会举办之前，阿文曾担心海湾冲突会阻碍中东买家前来。但事后看来，到场情况并未受冲击。
“不到他们真正现身，我们心里总是悬着一块石头。” 她说，“据我们了解，没有任何人因为冲突而缺席本次拍卖。”
阿文称，约四分之一的周岁马由海外买家购入，买家来自卡塔尔、沙特、阿联酋、利比亚等国；基恩兰并未公布各个国家的细分采购数据。
本次拍卖会最大买家是四家赛马投资合伙机构及马主新组建的联合财团，合计斥资 1620 万美元，购入 20 匹马。阿文表示，合伙投资模式越来越流行，但并未如之前市场担忧的那样拉低整体交易额。
“实际情况恰恰相反，合伙模式把投资人聚集在一起，整体的消费能力反而更强。” 她表示，“合伙模式能够帮助他们分散投资，提高获利机会。我和很多参与合伙竞拍的买家交流后发现，他们很享受和朋友共同投资带来的同好氛围。”

title: Russian dissident Garry Kasparov says US warned him of danger to his life
content:
An exiled Russian opposition figure living in the US says he was warned by American and Lithuanian security services that his life was in danger.

Former chess world champion Garry Kasparov said he was one of two dissidents told to take precautions, which he had done.

His comments come after the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment earlier this month charging five people who allegedly work for a network linked to the Kremlin with plotting attacks and murders in countries including the US, focusing on Russian dissidents and defectors.

Kasparov wrote in his publication The Next Move that he had not been told explicitly that he and fellow Free Russia Forum co-founder Ivan Tyutrin were considered targets, but said both had been warned about their safety.

Spanish newspaper El Mundo reported that it had obtained information that Kasparov, along with another Russian opposition figure, Ilya Ponomarev, had been warned about the plot over the summer by US authorities.

Citing sources close to Kasparov, the paper said he had been placed under enhanced protection over the summer for the first time since he moved to the US.

Kasparov wrote separately: "I will not stop and I will not hide, even if I thought it was possible to do so.

"My family and I will not truly be safe as long as [Russian President Vladimir] Putin is in power in Russia - a circumstance shared by millions."

Kasparov retired from competitive chess in 2005 to pursue a career in politics, founding movements that openly opposed Putin before fleeing Russia in 2013.

He has not returned since. Russia classed him as a foreign agent following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and subsequently added him to a list of terrorists and extremists in 2024 - both categorisations he rejects.

The other reported target, Ponomarev, was the only Russian MP who voted against the illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014 and later went into exile in Ukraine.

He declined to confirm or deny to the Moscow Times whether he had been tipped off about the alleged plot but said the allegations marked "a new level of escalation" by Russia.

A network of individuals working for the Russian intelligence services has operated since at least 2024, the US Justice Department said.

It said the so-called RIS Network had been conspiring and conducting attacks and murders on Russian dissidents and defectors around the world.

Five alleged members of the network had been accused of operating "as part of a global assassination network that reached into the United States, attempting to recruit US citizens and foreigners to carry out killings at the behest of the Kremlin", Assistant Attorney General for national security John A Eisenberg said.

The five people alleged to be responsible for organising the plots are Yuri Khrameev, Kirill Khrameev, Oemis Romagoza Durruthy, Yaidel Delgado Suarez and Angel Eduardo Castro.

All five remain at large, the Justice Department said.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said when the indictment was unsealed that he would not comment on the charges until he had heard or seen "any credible evidence" or "tangible facts".

title: Do US lawmakers finally have capital in the crosshairs?
content:
Oren Cass

Published October 1 2026

The writer is an FT contributing editor and chief economist at American Compass

Greed is so often the undoing of an otherwise brilliant scheme. Never satisfied, people become overconfident, push the envelope too far. And everything comes tumbling down. The high-flyers of finance seem headed towards a similar fate, as capital’s share of US income continues to rise, its share of tax payments continues to fall, inequality worsens, wealth concentrates and deficits become unsustainable. All the while the financial engineering gets ever more absurd.

For just one example, take AQR, the hedge fund behind a fairly recent innovation in tax avoidance called the “tax-aware long-short” account, which wraps leveraged, straddled portfolios around conventional equity indices or established fund strategies to generate large harvestable losses and indefinitely defer taxation on gains. Close to $200bn has poured into the strategy at AQR and its imitators such as Quantinno , which welcomes investors “to the next evolution of tax-loss harvesting” and has seen its assets swell from $2bn to $70bn in just a few years.

Such elaborate gamesmanship helps some of America’s highest earners to reduce taxes on even their wage income . The Financial Times reported earlier this year that fathers at a local sports game in Greenwich, Connecticut, “were fixated on AQR’s Delphi Plus fund, which specialises in ordinary income losses”.

The extraordinary wealth that these individuals and their money managers had already accumulated wasn’t enough, nor was the favourable tax treatment afforded to their capital gains, which in effect meant they might be able to pay a lower share of their income in taxes than their secretaries did. They had to avoid paying taxes altogether, and then claim this as the righteous course.

AQR chief Cliff Asness has said that the moral issue here is that of working for a client’s interests. But things are surely not that simple. A fiduciary duty to a client requires putting his interest above any other, but it does not require pursuing every potential action or developing every potential product.

The ethical business owner or manager operates within not only the letter but also the spirit of the law. It is the letter that determines whether a punishable violation has occurred. But as Milton Friedman observed in his famous essay arguing that “ the social responsibility of business is to increase its profits ”, the “basic rules of the society” include “both those embodied in law and those embodied in ethical custom”. Ethical custom may be a more subjective matter, but a good place to start is with the easily discernible intent of the laws established through the democratic process.

The defenders of the latest “tax-aware” funds make a comical effort to equate the exotic manoeuvres with garden-variety deductions and retirement saving. But the exercise must be enormously complex to justify the huge fees that the funds charge, allowing the financial wizards to pocket a good chunk of the revenue they divert from the public purse. Clearly, they are embarrassed by all this, or at least nervous about the potential consequences.

They should be. The political winds are shifting and even a business-friendly Republican administration is fed up. On Monday, the US Treasury department issued a notice of plans to scrutinise a range of schemes. “Treasury is serious about cracking down on transactions designed to dodge taxes or exploit our federal tax code,” warned Treasury secretary Scott Bessent in a social media post.

Beginning in the 1980s, the US tax code was rebalanced in favour of capital, in the belief that creating better conditions for its holders to deploy it and reap the rewards would ultimately redound to the benefit of all. The theory required some trust that the capitalists would indeed pursue their profit in ways that would be broadly beneficial. Instead, we got a metastasising financial sector dedicated not to productive investment but to helping the rich get richer by moving money in circles, extracting wealth from the real economy and then paying no taxes at all.

The central argument against wealth taxes, high marginal tax rates and taxes on mobile capital is that they will merely fuel avoidance and push productive activity away. But if we get the same with low tax rates, what then? The US is now in a fiscal crisis and capital should expect to find itself in the crosshairs. If the financial sector is determined to be a socially corrosive drag on the economy, then it is going to have to be taxed that way.

title: 沃尔玛启用发光电子价签，助力顾客与员工查找商品
content:
核心要点
沃尔玛希望让顾客尽可能轻松地找到想要的商品。 这家零售巨头依托电子货架标签推出三项全新工具，方便顾客和门店员工查找商品。这也是沃尔玛推进技术现代化、将 AI 融入业务的最新举措。
沃尔玛数字化转型高级副总裁格雷格・卡西表示：“我们坚持以人为本，技术赋能。我们看待 AI 的方式是，利用 AI 协助员工完成工作，节省时间，让员工可以投入到他们最热爱的工作上 —— 花更多精力服务顾客以及和同事协作。”
面向消费者的新功能名为 Shop to Light（寻物亮标） ：顾客在沃尔玛 App 检索商品，导航到对应货架通道后，商品对应的电子价签就会闪烁，帮助定位商品。该功能在试点结束后，现已大范围推广。
配套还有 Pick to Light（拣货亮标） 和 Stock to Light（上货亮标） ，依托相同技术，帮助员工拣选线上订单货品、完成补货上架。卡西称，三项功能将于假日季前在全美门店落地。
卡西说：“这项功能是顾客和门店员工都一直想要的。它帮大家节省时间。我们做很多项目，核心都是提升便利性，让员工与顾客把时间用在更有价值的地方。”
沃尔玛大力提升销售额的过程中，便捷度与配送时效（尤其自提和送货业务）已经成为关键。虽然沃尔玛业务稳步增长、电商销售额持续飙升，但在上次财报发布后，投资者对同店销售及营收前景的担忧压制了股价。
沃尔玛门店约有 12 万种商品。卡西表示，公司既要保持丰富的商品供给，又要简化顾客查找商品的流程，这是重点工作。
公司没有公开该项目相关财务数据。卡西称，试点门店里，这套新功能为顾客购物、员工补货节省了大量时间。自今年夏天在部分门店试点上线以来，Shop to Light 已经累计被顾客触发 500 万次亮灯。
他表示，临近繁忙的假日购物季，这套新功能尤为重要，沃尔玛认为该技术在节省时间方面 “成效显著”。
沃尔玛早已开始使用电子价签替代纸质标签，实现全系统一键统一调价。沃尔玛称，目前已有超过 4300 家门店配备电子价签，计划年底前完成全连锁门店部署。
他补充，价签调价一般在门店无顾客的夜间完成；系统保留人工复核，保证管控机制完善，避免出错。目前门店内大约 90% 的区域已经用上电子价签。
“我们不是为了技术而做技术。” 卡西说，“整个流程始终保留人工参与，我们高度重视人的判断与决策能力。”
更大范围的技术布局
沃尔玛持续投入技术建设，面向消费者端和内部运营同步推进业务现代化。 沃尔玛已经上线 AI 智能购物助手、供应链自动化系统，投入射频识别标签布局，并拥抱智能自主代理，为智能商务铺路；同时斥资数十亿美元改造实体门店。
在最近一次财报电话会上，沃尔玛 CEO 约翰・弗纳表示，公司在技术战略（含 AI 投资）上已经收获可观回报。
“我们相信 AI 几乎可以优化业务的每个环节，改善购物体验，减轻门店员工的工作负担。” 他说道。
不过电子价签与 AI 布局也引发争议：外界担忧动态定价，害怕电子标签会带来涨价，或是在采集顾客购物数据时产生隐私风险。
但弗纳在上周发布的 CEO 公开信中表示，沃尔玛坚持 按商品定价，而非看人定价 ，不会利用顾客信息设置差异化价格。
他写道：“你的收入、购物历史、紧急程度，或是我们预估的支付能力，都不会改变商品标价。”
卡西就任该岗位已近一年。他称上任后的首要目标：在保留人工监督的前提下，加快沃尔玛技术迭代速度。
包括新泽西州在内的多个州议会已经出台法案，出于定价顾虑限制电子价签使用。沃尔玛表示新泽西所有门店均部署了这套系统。
沃尔玛在声明中将相关监管政策称为 “过度反应”，称电子价签并非监控式定价工具，只是现代化的价格展示方式。
沃尔玛还布局无人机配送，这项业务同样面临隐私方面的审查，最快 30 分钟送货上门，现已在得州、佛罗里达等部分州落地。
卡西总结，电子价签新功能的最终目标，是让门店员工腾出更多时间，满足顾客个性化需求。
投资者一直在争论实体零售和电商哪一项对沃尔玛更重要，但卡西认为，新功能证明二者相辅相成。
“不再是非此即彼，而是两者兼顾。门店运营和电商履约本就是一体。”

title: Accenture shares surge 22% as consultancy confounds AI fears
content:
Stephen Foley in New York

Published October 1 2026

Updated October 1 2026

Accenture shares surged 22 per cent on Thursday after the world’s largest publicly traded consulting group said its revenues could accelerate this year, confounding fears that AI would destroy demand for its services.

The 800,000-person company reported an 8 per cent rise in earnings for the 12 months to August, as it benefited from cost-cutting and said AI was helping it to generate more revenue per employee.

Accenture , whose shares in June plunged to a nine-year low over concerns that AI would crush demand for consultants, reported revenues of $74.2bn for the fiscal year, a 4 per cent increase, after a stronger than expected final quarter.

Julie Sweet, chief executive, said Accenture was taking share from rivals in a difficult market.

“Our clients believe AI will help them achieve more than previously possible across the enterprise but they remain at very different stages of readiness,” she said. “Much of our growth today comes from continuing to build their digital core . . . Many are just starting their AI journey.”

Sweet said the company had allowed staff to carry over unused holiday to encourage them to complete work for clients in the final weeks of the fiscal year.

Accenture said its revenues could increase more quickly in the coming year despite concerns about how AI is disrupting the consulting industry.

The group set a target of 3 to 6 per cent growth for the current fiscal year. Wall Street had been expecting around 4 per cent for the mid-point of the range.

Net income for the fiscal year that ended in August was $8.4bn, up 8 per cent, helped by job cuts and other cost-reduction measures the company took a year ago. In the past three months, however, Accenture added more than 15,000 new jobs, taking its global workforce to more than 814,000.

The share price rise took the consultancy’s market capitalisation to more than $135bn. It had fallen from more than $200bn during a post-Covid consulting boom to less than $80bn earlier this year.

Previous technology revolutions boosted consulting firms, as they won work advising companies on how to adapt. But investors have been fretting that AI may not provide a similar stimulus if clients divert spending to in-house AI projects and expect consultants to complete projects using fewer staff and at lower rates.

Sweet said Accenture would continue to expand entry-level hiring, but the overall growth in employee numbers would slow due to AI.

“We are seeing an increase in revenue per person, which is what you would expect in part due to AI,” she told analysts on a conference call.

Accenture’s shares had fallen to a nine-year low in the wake of the company’s previous quarterly results in June, when it lowered its revenue forecasts, blaming the war in the Middle East and delays to two large contracts. The shares are still trading about 15 per cent lower than at the start of the year, even after Thursday’s rally.

Rival consulting firms have highlighted continuing weak demand in recent months. Deloitte reported last week that tech consulting was its slowest-growing division in the past year.

Accenture’s results were “well above expectations”, said Surinder Thind, analyst at Jefferies. “While overall growth remains tepid compared to historical levels, perhaps most importantly, the guidance suggests it is not deteriorating as AI fears would have you believe.”

title: 法国政府公布预算方案 540亿欧元财政“努力”措施再度考验市场神经
content:
法国政府公布了大幅缩减预算赤字的计划，由此拉开的政治角力可能危及总理职位，并加剧投资者对法国债务的担忧。
在明年大选前的最后一份财政计划中，法国政府部长周四公布了一项规模达540亿欧元（612亿美元）的财政“努力”措施细节，旨在遏制失控的支出，并将财政赤字占国内生产总值的比重从今年的5.4%降至2027年的5%。
总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔尼已经示意，将寻求从养老金、公共部门工资以及政府负担的病假福利等敏感支出项目中节省开支。他还表示，尽管企业团体表示反对，2025年开始对大型企业征收的一次性税项将至少部分延长。
预算案提交内阁后，法国财政部长Roland Lescure对记者表示，此次财政调整约60%将通过支出端措施实现。

title: 巴西大选或引爆股汇波动，但真正的交易主线可能不是选举
content:
巴西总统大选进入最后阶段，金融市场正为可能出现的剧烈波动做准备。不过，相比选举结果本身，利率下行、股票估值以及雷亚尔是否被低估，可能才是决定巴西资产中期表现的更重要变量。
最新民调显示，现任总统卢拉与参议员Flávio Bolsonaro在潜在第二轮投票中仍处于统计意义上的胶着状态。巴西首轮总统选举定于10月4日举行，如果没有候选人获得超过50%的有效票，前两名将在10月25日进入第二轮。近期市场通常把Flávio Bolsonaro视为相对更偏市场友好的候选人，其民调改善此前也曾推动巴西资产上涨。
但从资产定价角度看，选举带来的第一反应未必能够持续。
市场可能高估总统改变财政政策的能力
巴西资产历来容易对政治消息作出剧烈反应。如果市场认为卢拉胜选意味着政府支出维持高位，股票和雷亚尔可能承压；如果Flávio Bolsonaro表现更强，市场则可能提前交易财政紧缩和更低通胀。
但这种简单的二元交易存在一个问题：无论谁执政，巴西财政政策都受到相当多制度性约束。
巴西政府支出中存在大量宪法规定的强制性项目，同时财政决策还需要面对国会、地方政府以及不同利益集团之间的博弈。因此，卢拉最终能够增加的支出规模可能低于市场担忧，而Bolsonaro阵营真正能够实现的财政削减幅度，也可能低于竞选期间的政策主张。
这意味着，无论选举结果最初推动巴西股市和雷亚尔向哪个方向大幅波动，随后都存在部分反转的可能。
对外国投资者而言，选举期间出现的极端价格波动反而可能提供反向交易机会，而不是简单追随第一轮政治定价。
比大选更重要的变量可能是利率
政治并不是过去两年压制巴西股票的唯一因素。更直接的阻力来自极高的实际利率。
巴西经通胀调整后的利率长期处于全球最高水平之一。在这种环境下，一方面国债和其他固定收益资产能够提供很高的实际回报，降低股票的相对吸引力；另一方面，高融资成本又直接挤压企业利润和投资活动。
目前这一环境已经开始发生变化。巴西一年期实际利率已经从6月超过11.5%的峰值下降至9.19%。尽管这一水平仍然非常高，但方向已经转向下行。如果实际利率进一步下降，巴西股票将获得双重支撑：债券收益率下降能够提高股票估值，同时企业自身的融资压力也会逐步缓解。
选举决定的可能是“降息速度”，而不是方向
选举仍然重要，但它更可能影响未来降息的节奏。如果下一届政府采取更严格的财政政策，市场通胀预期可能下降，从而为央行更快降低利率创造空间。相反，如果政治结果引发雷亚尔明显贬值，进口价格和通胀压力重新上升，央行则可能放慢甚至暂时停止宽松。
目前掉期市场反映的预期仍较谨慎，定价显示政策利率可能在较长时间内保持稳定。
但从更长期角度看，只要当前极高的实际利率逐步正常化，利率下降仍有可能成为比短期选举交易更持久的股票市场驱动力。
巴西股市看起来便宜，但没有想象中便宜
从国际横向比较来看，巴西股票的估值确实非常低。Ibovespa指数目前的混合远期市盈率约为8.6倍，明显低于墨西哥基准股指的12.2倍，更远低于标普500指数约19倍的水平。自波斯湾战争爆发以来，巴西股票估值的下降幅度也超过不少地区主要市场。
但问题在于，这种国际比较可能夸大巴西股票的便宜程度。
如果不拿巴西与美国或墨西哥相比，而是与其自身过去五年的估值区间比较，Ibovespa目前并没有明显处于低估状态。整体指数的混合远期市盈率Z分数约为0.1，也就是基本处于过去五年的平均估值附近。部分板块甚至已经明显高于自身历史水平。其中金融、原材料以及部分公用事业公司的估值已经处于过去五年相对偏高的位置。
换句话说， 巴西股票的“便宜”主要来自跨市场比较，而不是相对自身历史的大幅折价。
大选制造波动，利率决定中期方向
由此来看，巴西资产接下来可能存在两套不同时间尺度的交易逻辑。
短期内，总统选举无疑会主导雷亚尔和股市波动。不同候选人的财政政策预期、民调变化以及第二轮选举形势，都可能导致市场快速重新定价。近期多项调查均显示卢拉与Flávio Bolsonaro在潜在第二轮中差距很小，并处于统计误差范围内。
但拉长时间来看，真正重要的问题可能不是“谁赢”，而是巴西极高的实际利率什么时候能够真正下降。
如果利率持续回落，企业融资压力减轻，股票估值获得支撑；如果与此同时雷亚尔从当前模型所显示的低估水平回归，则巴西资产可能得到进一步支撑。

title: 台积电据悉考虑在德州新建芯片园区 投资或达数百亿美元
content:
台积电 据悉正在考虑在德克萨斯州建设新的芯片制造园区，可能新增数百亿美元投资，进一步扩大其在美国持续多年的芯片制造布局。
知情人士称，作为英伟达和 苹果 等公司的主要芯片制造商，台积电正在评估增设海外生产设施，以应对人工智能硬件持续旺盛的需求。该公司已承诺在亚利桑那州一处大型园区投资2650亿美元，建设多座晶圆厂；其中一位知情人士表示，正在考虑的德州项目同样将包括多座晶圆厂。
今年以来，北美业务占台积电晶圆营收的75%以上，英伟达和超微等AI芯片设计公司为其部分最先进制程带来大量订单。AI热潮令台积电现有产能承压，副共同营运长侯永清上个月表示，为满足需求，公司过去一年不得不将计划中的设备采购规模提高约一倍。
其中一位知情人士称，如果台积电最终决定投资德州，项目将包括多座芯片制造厂，每座工厂的投资至少为200亿美元。知情人士表示，目前相关计划仍处于早期阶段。因细节尚未公开，他们要求匿名。
其中一位知情人士表示，台积电是否在德州投资，还取决于美国国会能否延长一项将于今年底到期的先进制造业投资税收抵免。这项税收抵免是美国前总统拜登2022年芯片法案的重要组成部分，去年已将抵免比例提高至35%。虽然今年进一步延期尚未找到可行的立法路径，但爱达荷州共和党参议员Mike Crapo和俄勒冈州民主党参议员Ron Wyden表示，他们致力于推动延期。
德州已经拥有规模可观的半导体产业基础，包括韩国三星电子建立的大型芯片生产基地。马斯克也正在该州开发Terafab项目，为其庞大的商业版图供应芯片。
包括总裁魏哲家在内的台积电高管一直表示，公司海外扩张将以客户需求为导向，同时取决于当地政府的合作与支持。除亚利桑那州园区外，台积电还与 索尼 集团合作在日本熊本建设工厂，并在德国萨克森州推进一个尚处于起步阶段的项目。
台湾《经济日报》本周早些时候率先报道，台积电正考虑在德州扩张。
不过，德州并非台积电近期考察的唯一潜在地点。多位知情人士称，台积电还与新加坡官员进行过沟通。新加坡正积极争取半导体投资。
新加坡目前已有多座芯片制造厂，也是Meta Platforms等全球大型AI开发商亚太业务中心的所在地。AI推动了新加坡经济增长，该国希望在相关技术价值链中扮演更重要的角色。
台积电近期与新加坡方面的沟通此前未被报道。台积电通过短信表示：“我们不评论市场传闻。”新加坡经济发展局不予置评。
台积电长期以来主要在台湾建设芯片工厂，生产高度集中也令管理和用工更加简便、高效。随着美国对国家安全的担忧加剧、新冠疫情以及随后AI热潮兴起，公司逐步扩大了全球生产布局。
不过，台积电扩大海外业务预计不会影响其长期以来将最先进芯片制造技术的研发留在台湾的政策。台湾官员已多次重申，台积电将把尖端研发留在台湾；公司高管也表示，这是推进技术发展的最高效方式。

title: 美国制裁压力外溢至保险服务，国际刑事法院与安盛终止合作
content:
美国针对国际刑事法院的制裁压力正在从受制裁官员个人层面进一步影响法院的日常运营体系。国际刑事法院与法国保险集团安盛已决定终止健康保险合同，10月1日起正式生效，法院将改用另一家未具名的保险供应商。双方作出这一决定的主要原因，是担忧美国一旦把现有制裁扩大至整个国际刑事法院，安盛继续提供服务可能面临制裁风险。
安盛数月寻找规避方案，最终仍选择退出
安盛此前已就潜在制裁风险与法院进行数月讨论，并尝试寻找能够继续提供保险服务的替代安排。
但在欧盟没有出台相应“阻断法令”的情况下，安盛未能找到可以有效隔离美国制裁风险的方案。
所谓阻断法令，是用于保护企业免受第三国具有域外效力的制裁或法律措施影响的一类法律机制。部分欧洲议会议员此前已要求欧盟针对美国对国际刑事法院的制裁采取类似措施，但截至目前尚未出台相关安排。
安盛表示，这一案例的复杂之处就在于美国制裁的域外适用风险。对于具有全球业务和美国市场敞口的大型金融机构而言，即使交易对象并不位于美国，继续向受制裁实体提供服务也可能带来合规和经营风险。
美国制裁已开始影响ICC的日常运行
国际刑事法院近两年来一直在调整自身运营体系，以应对美国制裁。
目前已有13名法院相关官员受到美国限制措施影响，其中包括9名法官。受制裁人员还面临信用卡、手机采购、美国快递和酒店预订等方面的实际限制。
法院也因此开始减少对美国企业和基础设施的依赖，包括将办公软件从 微软 产品迁移至德国的openDesk，并对银行、保险及员工薪酬安排进行调整。法院方面将这些措施描述为提高自身在进一步制裁情况下的运营自主性。
这种影响如今进一步延伸到机构层面的服务供应商。安盛退出表明，美国制裁风险已经不再只是限制个别官员的金融和旅行活动，而开始改变国际刑事法院与外部商业机构之间的合作关系。
制裁压力也开始影响ICC的机构安排
9月29日，国际刑事法院《罗马规约》缔约国大会决定，将原定在纽约联合国总部举行的第二十五届会议迁至海牙，理由之一就是部分法院民选官员受到美国制裁，以及部分代表面临签证限制。
这意味着，美国限制措施已经同时影响法院人员、供应商以及国际会议安排。
美国政府近年来持续批评国际刑事法院的管辖范围。双方矛盾在法院2024年针对以色列总理内塔尼亚胡和时任国防部长加兰特签发逮捕令后进一步升级。美国并非《罗马规约》缔约国，而法院方面则坚持其相关案件的管辖权依据。
欧洲目前仍以外交应对为主
面对企业担忧，美国制裁是否会扩大至整个国际刑事法院已经成为欧洲政策层面的一个现实问题。
欧洲议会部分议员希望通过阻断法令，为与ICC开展业务的欧洲企业提供法律保护，但欧盟委员会目前仍把外交沟通作为主要应对方式，并重申对国际刑事法院及其工作人员的支持。
因此，安盛与ICC解约的意义并不只在于更换一家保险公司。
更重要的是，它显示美国制裁已经产生明显的二级效应： 即使一家企业本身并未受到制裁，只要它担心继续为ICC提供服务可能导致自身面临美国处罚，就可能主动终止合作。
对于国际刑事法院而言，接下来需要解决的也不只是找到替代保险商，而是如何确保银行、软件、支付、物流和其他关键商业服务，在制裁进一步扩大的情况下仍能持续运行。

title: 开盘：三大股指齐涨 AI相关股票上涨 尽管10年期美债收益率再创新高
content:
周四美股主要股指高开，10 月新交易月开启，投资者持续买入 AI 概念股；但美债收益率大幅飙升，压制市场多数板块表现。
道指涨0.27%，标普500指数涨0.27%，纳指涨0.44%。
埃森哲 涨19.41%， 高知特 涨10.58%，新 思科 技涨8.62%，加特纳涨6.81%，Fair Isaac Corp涨5.84%， IBM 涨4.90%。
美光 科技交出超预期亮眼财报。这份财报对其他芯片企业与 AI 相关公司的拉动效果，甚至超过美光自身；该股今年累计涨幅已经达到 270%。盘初，英伟达、 AMD 、博通悉数走高。
Alphabet 发布最新 Gemini 大模型，进一步提振市场多头情绪，盘初股价上涨近 2%。9 月科技股领涨大盘，但基准指数内多数个股下跌。周三盘初延续该格局：科技板块以外的绝大多数个股走弱或持平。
美光目前利润率高达 87%，但公司计划上调员工薪酬，这会造成实际利润率低于华尔街市场预期。
尽管油价、利率两大投资者最担忧的风险因素依旧存在，美股 10 月开盘依旧走高。
美国 10 年期国债收益率今日盘中冲高至 5.342%，突破 2007 年 6 月创下的 5.328%，创下 2002 年 4 月 3 日（当时 10 年期美债收益率达到 5.379%）以来的最高水平。美国东部时间周四上午 9 点 10 分，30 年期美债收益率报 5.663%。
西德克萨斯轻质原油（WTI）上涨 1.6%，突破每桶 91 美元。交易员密切关注特朗普在伊朗冲突中的下一步动向，研判他是否会等到中期选举结束之后再采取更多军事行动。
从历史规律看，9 月通常是股市表现偏弱的月份，标普 500 指数 9 月下跌 0.5%，投资者需要应对油价走高和美债收益率飙升双重压力。 道琼斯 工业指数下跌 4.3%；受科技股带动， 纳斯达克 指数表现占优，当月上涨 1.9%。
周三同时是第三季度收官日。标普 500 指数、纳斯达克指数本季度均上涨约 2%，道琼斯指数下跌 2.7%。
富国银行 投资研究所全球资产配置策略主管特蕾西・麦克米伦表示：“尽管上述因素依旧构成市场逆风，但企业盈利持续展现韧性。关键问题在于，在借贷成本居高不下的环境之下，这种盈利强势能否延续。”
市场等待非农
周三公布的数据显示，美国8月通胀升幅低于预期，同时前一个月的价格压力也被向下修正。这份数据降低了市场对10月加息的预期。市场目前预计10月加息概率为36%，低于数据公布前的45%。不过，交易员仍认为12月加息的概率高达89%。
Tastylive全球宏观主管Ilya Spivak表示：“接下来公布的数据会非常重要，市场将观察这些数据，并据此调整对加息的预期。”
他说：“我们现在所处的环境里，市场正同时面对许多相互冲突的力量。”
美国9月非农就业报告定于周五公布。

title: Bluetongue restriction zone to be expanded across all of Scotland
content:
Bluetongue restrictions are to be expanded across the whole of Scotland from Saturday.

Parts of south-west Scotland were already in a restricted zone, after cases in the region began appearing in August. The Scottish government said the decision will make trading more straightforward for farmers, hauliers, and auction markets.

Bluetongue is an insect-borne viral disease that affects sheep and cattle among other animals. It does not affect people or food safety but causes a high rate of death in infected sheep and fertility problems in infected cattle.

The first case in Scotland was reported in early August, in a single sheep on a farm in Dumfries and Galloway.

The decision to expand the zone follows talks with industry representatives, including the National Farmers' Union (NFU) Scotland, the National Sheep Association, and the Scottish Beef Association.

The movement licences currently required to move susceptible livestock into, within, and out of the south-west zone, will no longer be needed after Saturday, due to the whole of Scotland sharing the same disease status.

England and Wales are also in restricted zones, after cases escalated there over the summer.

Jim Fairlie, the Scottish government's minister for agriculture, marine and the islands, said bluetongue is "not going away any time soon" and called the restricted zone covering the whole of Scotland a "practical, sensible step."

The disease has been detected on 40 premises since the south-west Scotland restricted zone was established in early September. The Scottish government said four of those cases were detected outside of the zone by tracing animal movements from the affected farms.

Dumfries and Newton Stewart have the most affected premises, with six in each area.

Call for livestock vaccination

Referring to the autumn trading period, Fairlie said the decision removes "an administrative burden on farmers at what is a critical time in the trading calendar".

"While extending the zone removes the need for movement licences, it does not change our long-term approach to tackling this disease," he said.

"Vaccination remains the single most effective way for farmers to protect their animals from the worst effects of bluetongue, and I would strongly encourage anyone with susceptible livestock to speak to their vet now to discuss the right vaccination approach and to secure supplies ahead of next year's higher-risk season," he added.

A joint Scottish government and industry communications group is being established to promote vaccination and to share advice on the impact of the disease with farmers and veterinary practitioners.

Neil Shand, the chief executive of the Scottish Beef Association, said the decision is "the most logical way forward to prevent trade complications."

Michael Priestley, policy manager with the National Sheep Association, said there was now a "trade-off" between the benefit of eased restrictions and the increased risk of the virus spreading.

He said: "This trade-off is being made because of the faith in the vaccine technology, which to date has offered excellent coverage to livestock in affected areas of the UK."

Symptoms of the disease include nasal discharge, redness and swelling of the lips, nose and muzzle, lameness or reluctance to stand, a decrease in milk production, and diarrhoea in cattle.

Cases must be reported to the UK government's Animal and Plant Health agency, which publishes daily updates.

title: 美国首次申领失业救济人数降至19.7万 创7月以来最低
content:
美国失业救济申请人数小幅下降至7月以来最低水平，续领失业救济人数则降至三年低点，显示劳动力市场稳健。
美国劳工部周四公布的数据显示，截至9月26日当周，首次申领失业救济人数减少1，000人，至19.7万人。经济学家预估中值为20万人。
截至9月19日当周，持续申领失业救济人数减少1.1万人，至170万人，为2023年3月以来最低水平。
过去几个月，美国首次申领失业救济人数一直徘徊在历史低位附近，表明在经济活动强劲之际，企业仍不愿裁员。与此同时，招聘则更为谨慎。
预计政府周五公布的月度就业报告显示，9月失业率维持在4.1%，非农就业人数预计增加约8.5万人。

title: International Criminal Court cuts ties with Axa over US sanctions
content:
Suzi Ring in London

Published October 1 2026

The International Criminal Court has cut ties with its health insurance provider Axa, as the war crimes tribunal attempts to shield itself from the impact of US sanctions.

The ICC and Axa have terminated their contract effective from October 1, according to The Hague court. President Donald Trump has stepped up attacks on the ICC as reports suggested the US would impose sanctions on the whole institution, adding to existing measures against several people working there.

The ICC opted to end its deal with Axa as both parties feared that new, broad-based US sanctions would force the insurer to stop doing business with the court or face punishment.

Axa has held months of discussions internally and with the court about potential workarounds, but the Paris-based insurer was unable to find a solution without a so-called blocking statute, said a person with knowledge of the situation.

Blocking statutes are legal mechanisms used to shield companies engaged in international trade from being forced to comply with sanctions issued by other countries.

A group of MEPs has been calling for the EU to enact a blocking statute in relation to US sanctions against the ICC, but while there is support among dozens of MEPs for such a measure, no such statute has been enacted.

The ICC — which prosecutes individuals for offences including genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity — has been contending with the latest round of US sanctions for nearly two years. Some 13 court officials, including half of the tribunal’s 18 judges, are currently subject to the restrictions.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio launched a campaign in July to dismantle the ICC “brick by brick”, calling on member states to withdraw from the court, while Trump told the UN General Assembly last week that the ICC was “out of control” and an “evil group of people”.

In an interview last month, deputy prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan — who is co-running the prosecutor’s office after former chief prosecutor Karim Khan was ousted — told the FT that the ICC had taken steps to insulate itself against further US sanctions, “ensuring that we are autonomous for the future”.

The court has spent the past year overhauling its systems , shifting its office software from Microsoft to Germany’s openDesk. Individuals at the court who are subject to US sanctions have faced restrictions on holding US credit cards, purchasing mobile phones and receiving packages via US couriers. They have also had hotel reservations cancelled.

While the US, which is not a member of the court, has long criticised the war crimes tribunal for over-reach, the tension has increased during Trump’s second term. The ICC issued an arrest warrant in 2024 against Israeli leader and US ally Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant for alleged war crimes in Gaza.

In response to questions about the use of blocking statutes, the European Commission said earlier this week that it was “in constant touch with our member states but diplomatic outreach remains our preferred option”, whilst reiterating its “full support for the ICC’s work and its staff”.

A spokesperson for the ICC said Axa and the court had “decided by mutual agreement to terminate the contractual relationship” and that it would use a new, unnamed health insurance provider.

Axa said: “It is a complex and sensitive case given the risks arising from the extraterritorial application of US sanctions. Situations of this kind, which are extremely difficult for the individuals affected, are relatively new and reflect an international environment that has become increasingly tense and complex for businesses.”

The Republic of Naoero, north-east of Australia — formerly known as Nauru — told the UN last week that it was withdrawing from the ICC. Niger, Burkina Faso, Venezuela, Mali and Chad have also notified the court of their withdrawal this year.

Additional reporting by Paola Tamma

title: UAE investigates if Flydubai attack was ‘terrorist activity’
content:
Chloe Cornish in Abu Dhabi and James Shotter in Jerusalem

Published October 1 2026

Updated October 1 2026

Investigators are rushing to determine why a pilot attempted to crash a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv on Wednesday, with the United Arab Emirates launching an investigation into possible links to terrorism.

The country’s attorney-general Hamad Saif al Shamsi had ordered a probe to collect evidence on the altercation between the flight’s two pilots, state news agency WAM reported on Thursday.

The investigators will look into “the extent to which [the incident] is related to any terrorist activity” and whether the attack was premeditated, according to WAM.

A person familiar with the situation said Israel was also “involved” in investigating the incident but declined to provide further details.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday that the co-pilot who stabbed the aircraft’s captain and attempted to crash the plane had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination”, without presenting evidence for his claim.

“The attacker, the co-pilot who attacked the captain, is now being interrogated, but here’s what we do know. First, we know that he underwent Islamist radical indoctrination. That appears to be something we’re gathering from the information, his personal information,” Netanyahu told Fox News.

He added that it was too early to tell whether the incident was linked to Iran , but that Israel would know “definitively within a matter of days”.

The flight took off from Dubai before being diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, after the plane’s co-pilot stabbed the pilot and the aircraft plunged 18,000ft within the space of 90 seconds. Passengers and crew struggled with the attacker and managed to land the plane safely.

Netanyahu earlier told CNN that he had spoken to UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed al-Nahyan, and that the Emirati leader had “agreed that Israel would join the interrogation”.

Israel’s far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said on Thursday that the government should demand the extradition of the pilot who carried out the attack.

“Anyone who planned to crash a plane and murder 180 Israelis must be extradited to Israel and pay the ultimate price here,” he said in a statement.

Dubai government-owned Flydubai on Wednesday evening said its flights between the emirate and Israel were suspended “while the investigation continues”, without mentioning which authority was leading the probe.

Flights into Tel Aviv — from Israeli airlines and international carriers such as Delta, KLM, Etihad and Wizz Air — continued to run on Thursday, with only a small number of cancellations or delays. So far, carriers have not been asked to make changes to flights or security by Israeli aviation authorities, according to one airline still flying into the country.

The attacking co-pilot’s identity has not been revealed, although Israel has said he is an Omani national. His motivation remains unknown.

The incident has raised questions about the usually rigorous security checks passengers undergo before flying to Israel, which has a history of aviation-related attacks.

Additional reporting by Peter Campbell in London

title: Israel flight near-miss triggers election furore
content:
James Shotter in Jerusalem and Neri Zilber in Tel Aviv

Published October 1 2026

The near-downing of the Flydubai plane carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv has triggered a political storm in Israel, with Benjamin Netanyahu’s opponents accusing the Israeli prime minister of exploiting the incident for political gain ahead of this month’s election.

The attack came less than a day after Netanyahu — whose campaign has been dogged by recriminations over the security failings around Hamas’s October 7 2023 attack — issued a vague warning that there were “indications that . . . our enemies will try to attack us” ahead of the October 27 vote.

In the wake of the attack, during which the jet nosedived nearly 20,000 feet after one pilot stabbed the other in an apparent attempt to crash the plane, Netanyahu’s allies sought to portray his warning on Tuesday as a sign of the prime minister’s strong security instincts.

Even before the passengers had returned to Israel, defence minister Israel Katz issued a statement saying: “When the Prime Minister and I issue security warnings and alerts based on intelligence, everyone — including our external enemies and uninformed former officials at home — would do well to listen and take them seriously.”

Yair Lapid, who in his position as leader of the opposition demanded — and was granted — a briefing from Netanyahu on the security threats the prime minister had alluded to, later said Netanyahu did not mention any threat to hijack a plane.

“It is forbidden to say what is said in a security update and I am strict about it, but it is allowed to say what wasn’t said: there was no mention of a plane hijacking scenario. Nothing like it. Nothing. Nada,” he wrote on Thursday.

“The Prime Minister’s Office has become so unhinged and out of touch that they are trying to score political points off the plane incident.”

As the Israeli passengers returned home on Wednesday night, the national mood was one of rejoicing, with news cycles dominated by stories of the heroism of the passengers who overpowered the attacking pilot.

But the near-downing of the plane, which came less than four weeks before Israel goes to the polls, has also become part of a campaign in which security already features prominently.

Most opinion surveys suggest the election is too close to call. Netanyahu’s far-right coalition is trailing a broad coalition of opposition groups. But the gap has narrowed in recent weeks and both blocs remain short of a clear majority.

Netanyahu conceded in an interview with CNN on Thursday that there had been no specific intelligence relating to the attack on the plane.

But analysts said that, in the short term, the incident might be a boon for the prime minister as it diverted the news cycle away from longstanding questions over the lapses that preceded the October 7 attack, which happened on his watch and is widely seen as the worst security failure in Israeli history.

Those questions have dominated the public discourse in recent days following reports that Netanyahu — who has sought to cultivate a reputation as Israel’s “Mr Security” over two decades as premier — received advance warnings from Emirati and Egyptian officials that Hamas was preparing for an attack. The prime minister has vociferously denied this.

“There are less than 30 days until the election. Every day that passes and people aren’t talking about October 7 is good for Netanyahu . . . The less he has to talk about October 7, the better it is for him,” said Aviv Bushinsky, a political analyst who previously served as Netanyahu’s chief of staff.

“It’s much better for him to be talking about brave Israelis.”

Indeed, on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu rushed to greet the returning Israelis as they landed at Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion International Airport. Videos on social media subsequently showed him singing a well-known Israeli pop song about life always getting better during a meeting with one passenger and his family.

Jonatan Urich, an adviser to Netanyahu, accused Lapid and other opposition leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett of failing to grasp the urgency of the prime minister’s security warning earlier this week.

“Prime Minister Netanyahu said this yesterday,” Urich wrote on Wednesday of the warning. “Eisenkot, Bennett, and Lapid snickered. Today we all saw what happened. It is forbidden to let them lead Israel.”

The longer-term impact of the incident on Israeli politics is expected to depend on further revelations about the motivations of the attacker, whether he acted alone and how he was in a position to carry out his assault. The United Arab Emirates said it was investigating whether the attack was premeditated or connected to “terrorist activity”.

Analysts said that, unless the investigation revealed serious failures by Israeli authorities, they did not expect it to persuade voters in the country’s deeply polarised society to cross the political divide, not least because most had already decided what they thought of Netanyahu.

“We don’t have any way to predict how voters are going to react to the kind of incident they’ve never seen before,” said Dahlia Scheindlin, a pollster and political analyst.

“What we do know from polls is that voters have not changed their minds about Netanyahu. Not for. Not against,” she added. “I don’t think this is going to be the thing that causes voters to cross blocs.”

But Bennett, a former prime minister, argued the reaction from Netanyahu and his “delusional” aides was another reason why he was unfit to lead the country.

“If you suspected there was a danger that planes will explode on us, what did you do? Who did you convene? What did you check?” Bennett said.

“A prime minister is not a siren,” he said. “I don’t need a prime minister to give warnings, I need a government that will protect.”

title: 味好美营收增长但利润下滑
content:
专题：聚焦美股2026年第二季度财报
这家调味品制造商第三财季销售额上涨 17%，达 20.2 亿美元；公司即将完成与 联合利华 食品业务的合并
内容摘要
味好美公布第三财季销售额大涨 17%，达到 20.2 亿美元，超出华尔街市场预期。
味好美（MKC）在即将完成收购联合利华食品业务之际，公布第三财季销售额同比走高。
这家调味品企业周四公布，截至 8 月 31 日的财季，净利润为 9760 万美元，折合每股收益 36 美分；去年同期净利润 2.255 亿美元，每股收益 84 美分。
剔除部分一次性损益项目后，调整后每股收益为 86 美分。FactSet 调研的分析师此前预期调整后每股收益 76 美分。
本季度总销售额增长 17%，录得 20.2 亿美元，高于华尔街预期的 19.8 亿美元； 内生销售额仅小幅上涨 1.9% 。
味好美消费品板块销售额大增 25%，主要来自收购墨西哥 味好美公司 带来的增量。该板块内生销售额增长 1%，涨价对冲了销量下滑带来的影响。
公司风味解决方案部门销售额上涨 8%，内生增速为 3%。
首席执行官布伦丹・福利表示，严谨落地降本增效举措，抵消了原材料与运费上涨压力，助力利润率提升，同时企业得以持续投入品牌建设。
他补充，味好美仍在推进与联合利华食品业务的合并工作，并购整合规划已经取得重大进展：“我们已经搭建完成未来的管理团队与运营模式，调动跨部门资源，并制定详尽方案，保障交易完成后业务平稳运行、实现预期协同效应。”
展望后市，对于将于 11 月 30 日结束的完整财年，味好美维持指引不变：调整后每股收益 3.05‑3.13 美元；净销售额预计同比上涨 13%‑17%，其中墨西哥味好美最多可贡献 13 个百分点的增速。
分析师一致预期，公司全年调整后每股收益 3.09 美元，总销售额 79.1 亿美元，较去年大约增长 16%。
盘前交易阶段，该股上涨 3.5%，报 48 美元。

title: 埃森哲各地区与各行业业务均实现增长，营收走高
content:
专题：聚焦美股2026年第二季度财报
埃森哲 （ACN）第四财季利润与营收双双上涨，旗下各个地域市场、服务的各客户行业需求均有所提升。
这家咨询企业财报表现超出华尔街预期，同时对新财年的利润、营收继续增长作出业绩指引。
周四盘前交易中，该股上涨 10%，报 202.45 美元；截至周三收盘，该股年内累计下跌 32%。
埃森哲公布第四财季净利润 19.9 亿美元，每股收益 3.29 美元；去年同期为 14.1 亿美元，每股收益 2.25 美元。FactSet 调研分析师此前预期每股收益 3.18 美元。
本季度营收增长约 6%，达 186.8 亿美元，高于分析师 180.3 亿美元的预期。
埃森哲所有地域市场以及全部服务行业板块营收均实现增长，通信、媒体与科技领域增长尤为亮眼。
新签约订单额增长 4%，达到 221.7 亿美元。
对于接下来完整财年，埃森哲给出业绩指引：以本币计营收增速 3%‑6%，每股收益区间 14.39‑14.81 美元。分析师普遍预期全年营收 764 亿美元，每股收益 14.64 美元。
公司预计当前第一财季营收介于 189.5 亿‑196 亿美元，分析师预测值为 193.5 亿美元。

title: 零部件供应问题致使福特F‑150停产，批量交付受到冲击
content:
福特汽车 表示，受供应商相关问题影响，F‑150 生产线停产约一周，对第三季度整车批量交付造成影响。
本次产量受挫，是福特 F‑150 销量复苏道路上遭遇的又一重挑战。此前铝材供应商工厂失火事件，已经困扰该公司皮卡生产长达一年以上。福特整体美国市场销量下滑 10%；包含 F‑150 及重型皮卡在内的福特 F 系列皮卡销量下降 11%。
福特发言人表示，本次车企遭遇的供应链问题源于零部件短缺。首席执行官吉姆・法利称，福特已派遣供应链专项小组快速解决该问题，第四季度的生产预计不会受到波及。
福特表示，计划今年相比 2025 年偏低的产量再多生产 15 万辆皮卡，以此弥补铝材厂火灾造成的销量损失。考克斯汽车咨询公司数据显示，受 2026 年福特销量大幅下滑影响， 现代汽车 有望在美国市场销量排行榜上超越福特，成为美国市场第三大汽车厂商。

title: Keurig Dr Pepper聘任金佰利高管托雷斯执掌咖啡业务分拆公司
content:
托雷斯将主导咖啡业务整合；在皮爷咖啡与克里格业务完成分拆后，出任新分拆企业首席执行官
Keurig Dr Pepper集团（KDP）宣布，已聘请金佰利公司（KMB）的拉斯・托雷斯担任咖啡分拆业务首席执行官。
这家总部位于得克萨斯州弗里斯科的企业周四表示，托雷斯现任金佰利总裁兼首席运营官，将于 11 月 3 日入职，在业务正式分拆前担任咖啡业务部门首席执行官。
托雷斯自 2025 年 5 月起出任金佰利总裁，目前正负责这家消费品巨头的并购整合规划，对应其 400 亿美元收购泰诺制药所属公司康维（KVUE）的项目。
金佰利表示，由公司首席战略、业务拓展及行政官杰夫・梅卢奇接管并购整合规划与相关项目；达拉斯总部的首席财务官纳尔逊・乌尔达内塔负责协同效应落地工作。
金佰利称，原本托雷斯将出任并购后合并企业的总裁兼首席运营官，他会留任至 11 月，协助完成工作交接；收购康维的项目按计划将于今年年底完成。
Keurig Dr Pepper集团去年公布计划，斥资 180 亿美元收购皮爷咖啡母公司 JDE 皮爷集团，并将皮爷咖啡、克里格两大咖啡业务分拆，组建一家专注咖啡赛道的独立公司。公司表示，目标在 2027 年初完成分拆；托雷斯将负责咖啡板块业务整合，分拆落地后就任新公司首席执行官。
Keurig Dr Pepper集团最初选定前首席财务官苏德汉舒・普里亚达尔希出任该咖啡分拆公司 CEO，但去年年底宣布普里亚达尔希不会就任该职位，并将离开公司。
之后集团曾计划由 JDE 皮爷集团负责人拉斐尔・奥利韦拉执掌分拆新公司，但奥利韦拉离职，转而接手荷兰啤酒企业喜力的管理工作。

title: What’s next for the global economy? You asked, we answered
content:
By Martin Sandbu and Tej Parikh

Published September 25 2026

Updated October 1 2026

The global economy is facing another period of uncertainty as conflict in the Middle East and a surge in AI investment add to the pressures created by years of economic shocks and geopolitical upheaval.

What will drive the next stage of global growth? Where are the biggest risks? And how will shifts in bond yields, trade, technology and geopolitics affect businesses and households?

Tej Parikh and Martin Sandbu, answered your questions on the global economy.

This is part of our live Ask an Expert series, giving readers the chance to put their questions directly to FT journalists. For more topics, visit our Ask an Expert page .

For more on the global economy listen to the Economics Show with Soumaya Keynes podfollow.com/economics-show

Question asked by: JM Question: Is there a negative doom loop we need to be worried about re French yields and the political unwillingness to tame the budget? Thank you

Answered by: Martin Sandbu Answer: There is a negative feedback loop to worry about - where rising yields make French public finances look less sustainable and so drive yields even higher etc - but that is also something policymakers have worried about since the eurozone debt crisis and have put in place emergency tools as a result. In particular, the European Central Bank has an instrument ready (the Transmission Protection Instrument) to intervene in case of "unwarranted" spikes in sovereign bond yields. That would be a political shock, though - similar to the UK's trauma of going to the IMF in the 1970s. Governments should know that there is a limit to kicking the can, and that high borrowing costs do have knock on consequences in the here and now (e.g for mortgage holders, and the opportunity cost of spending on debt interest). The language of trade-offs is crucial, but I worry many leaders aren't up to it. That's why I feel bond markets may need to do the job for them.

Question asked by: Sister Sister Question: Will there ever be a debt reckoning or are we heading into a new era of government debts?

Answered by: Tej Parikh Answer: I think the combination of high debt and fiscal ill-discipline (and populist politicians) are not sustainable. As with recent sovereign debt crises, instability in one can create a domino effect. And, doom-loops, where sell-offs become self-reinforcing, are possible (US and France are particular concerns). Efforts to use financial repression also wouldn't go down too well with markets (as seen with Bessent's recent attempts to tame treasuries). I think markets will force discipline, but that may be wishful thinking.

Answered by: Martin Sandbu Answer: There are a lot of questions on government debt in this Q&A, so it's clearly a source of worry. And the basic numbers don't look good - debt-to-GDP ratios are at or near long-term highs, and many big countries' deficit numbers are not closing.But I'm quite heterodox on this and think we may be worrying a tad too much. Debt-to-GDP ratios are mostly stable at the moment - in part thanks to inflation of course. If deficits are no larger than nominal GDP growth (when debt is around or below 100% of GDP), then the ratio can remain stable for some time. Also note that while western governments are seeing rising debt service costs, the share of GDP they spend on interest payments remains below where it was a decade or more ago. It's not quite don't worry, be happy. But I don't think we should happy.

Second, assuming (quantum based) AGI, can governing become out of human hands?

Answered by: Tej Parikh Answer: I think there is huge promise for AI in public services, particularly in tracking and tackling uncollected taxation, boosting efficiency in healthcare and generally in easing administrative inefficiencies. But, getting these fiscal benefits soon depends on how well and fast the technology can be embedded into the bureaucratic machinery (I’m skeptical). Next, at least initially, in some cases, we might see higher demands on the governments due to higher volumes of AI-generated grant, benefit or complaint form applications etc due to high utilisation outside the public sector. As for AGI governance, as much as some may like the idea of a benevolent, efficient, technocrat, policymaking always involves trade-offs and hence debate over values, virtues and prioritisation. Humans might still be best for that. Besides, I don’t think humans would trust AI politicians any more than real ones.

Answered by: Tej Parikh Answer: I don’t think there will be an event as systemic and damaging as the 2008 financial crisis in the near-term. Since that crash the banking system and regulatory oversight has become more robust. But that does not mean there aren’t vulnerabilities. title: Pete Hegseth announces creation of Autonomous Warfare Command
content:
Abigail Hauslohner in Washington

Published October 1 2026

This is an on-site version of the White House Watch newsletter. You can read the previous edition here . Sign up for free here to get it on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Email us at [email protected]

Hello from Washington and welcome to White House Watch. Here’s what we’re looking at today:

Hegseth announces series of new initiatives in “State of the Force” speech

Trump says Powell should be “forced to resign” from Fed board

White House holds crunch talks on diesel export ban

US defence secretary Pete Hegseth announced the creation of an “Autonomous Warfare Command (Autowarcom)” to spearhead the military’s use of unmanned weapons.

Hegseth is creating the new command at a moment of intense public debate over necessary safeguards for AI, after several recent incidents in which advanced AI models under development went rogue and hacked into outside systems without being instructed to do so.

Hegseth said he expected there to be internal resistance to the creation of Autowarcom, which will operate on the same level as other combatant commands such as US Central Command and US Special Operations Command. The new command will be able to deploy weapons and buy drones and other autonomous systems, something the individual services currently do.

It was one of a series of new initiatives announced by Hegseth during his “State of the Force” speech on Wednesday.

Addressing hundreds of junior officers and enlisted troops at Marine Base Quantico, Hegseth touted his overhaul of the military and its culture, which has included the firing of many of the military’s top ranks, and an expanded emphasis on physical appearance and masculinity.

“The ideological clowns are out. The patriotic cowboys are in, with testosterone testing on top,” he said.

Trump said former Federal Reserve chair Jay Powell should be forced off the central bank’s board even after an investigation into a $2.5bn renovation project found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing.

OpenAI’s software has obscured efforts to scrape data from crucial government agencies , according to new findings that show the scale and severity of AI hacks are far larger than previously known. Meanwhile, a US competition watchdog is expanding its investigation of the AI company.

The US has withdrawn its remaining troops from Iraq, marking an end to more than two decades of US involvement in the country.

Trump has unveiled plans for South Korea to invest $200bn in US energy projects , including eight nuclear power plants, a six-gigawatt power facility and a long-delayed liquefied natural gas project.

US government bonds have posted their worst month in four years as investors warn the world’s most important debt market has been gripped by a “vicious loop” of selling.

What’s inside Silicon Valley’s AI “self-regulation” agreement with Trump? Here’s what to know.

Trump has held crisis talks with advisers over whether to impose a diesel export ban or take other steps to contain a fuel crisis that has threatened his party’s midterm election campaign.

Myles McCormick, Jamie Smyth and David Sheppard exclusively report that Trump’s aides have presented the president with options including curbs on international diesel sales, people familiar with the discussions told them.

Administration officials have also briefed foreign allies including the UK about possible disruption to their supplies.

A White House official said Trump was “evaluating all the options on the table” to lower domestic fuel prices and that no decision had been taken on whether to suspend exports.

The crunch talks come as US oil and gas executives surveyed by the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas found that diesel prices would not return to normal for more than a year . Almost half of those polled expect diesel prices will take more than four quarters to return to 2025 levels, according to the anonymous survey of 100 oil and gas companies.

The president is at the centre of a lobbying fight between Republican allies worried about the political impact of the diesel price surge — which has hammered farmers and other parts of US industry — and oil bosses desperate to preserve lucrative exports.

title: 法国监督机构称预算草案的经济假设“乐观” 政府降赤字计划面临风险
content:
法国财政监督机构警告称，政府2027年预算草案所依据的经济假设“乐观”，这给削减高企财政赤字的计划带来风险。
法国政府周四早些时候向内阁提交了一项财政法案，预计经济增速将从2026年的0.5%加快至1%，并计划将财政赤字占国内生产总值（GDP）的比例从5.4%降至5%。
负责监督公共财政的独立机构法国公共财政高级委员会（HCFP）表示，这些预测假设私人投资将显著回升，但法国主权借贷成本飙升可能会传导至企业和家庭的融资环境。
该机构还表示，由于政府提供的时间和信息有限，无法对拟议的所有税收和支出调整进行深入分析。
HCFP主席Amélie de Montchalin表示：“总体而言，我们认为，2027年预算余额预测一方面面临经济情景带来的风险，另一方面也面临各项措施效果存在不确定性的风险。”
尽管法国政府对2027年经济增长1%的预测与彭博最近月度调查中经济学家的预估中值大体一致，但经合组织（OECD）上周更为谨慎，将其预测下调至仅0.7%。
法国正试图重启修复公共财政的努力，此前今年缩减赤字的计划已经偏离轨道。由于政府在议会没有多数席位，而债市抛售又推高了融资成本，财政整顿难度进一步加大。
HCFP表示，明年的预算草案意味着“显著的财政调整”，如果所有拟议措施都得到落实，支出预测“可以实现”。
不过，该机构警告称，为法国不断上升的债务负担支付利息，将吞噬相当大一部分财政改善成果。Montchalin表示，若剔除债务偿付成本，2027年的赤字将降至2019年以来最低；她同时称，在没有严重经济压力的时期，5%的赤字率是前所未有的。
她说：“我们有着危机时期才会出现的赤字，尽管现在并没有危机。”
对于2026年，HCFP表示，5.4%的赤字目标具有可实现性，但相关预测仍面临“重大风险”。
HCFP表示：“鉴于公共财政状况令人担忧，政府提出在2027年削减赤字的目标，是最低限度的必要举措。”

title: 盘前：纳指期货涨0.6% AI相关个股上涨
content:
周四美股期货走高，10 月交易月开启，投资者持续买入 AI 相关股票；不过美债收益率飙升，压制市场多数板块表现。
标普 500 指数期货上涨 0.3%， 纳斯达克 100 指数期货上涨 0.6%； 道琼斯 指数期货上涨 86 点，涨幅 0.2%。
美光 科技交出亮眼财报。这份财报对其他芯片厂商与 AI 企业的提振效果，甚至超过美光自身；该股今年累计涨幅已达 270%。盘初，英伟达、 AMD 、博通悉数走高。
Alphabet 发布最新 Gemini 大模型，进一步提振市场乐观情绪，盘初股价上涨近 2%。9 月，科技股领涨大盘，但基准指数中多数个股下跌。本周三盘初延续该格局：科技板块以外多数个股走弱或持平。
美光目前利润率高达 87%，但公司计划上调员工薪酬，此举会导致实际利润率低于华尔街预期。
尽管油价与利率这两大投资者主要担忧因素依旧存在，美股 10 月开盘仍然走高。周三，美国 10 年期与 30 年期国债收益率均逼近 2002 年以来高位；10 年期美债收益率上行 1 个基点，报 5.298%，30 年期美债收益率升至 5.64%。
西德克萨斯轻质原油（WTI）上涨 1.6%，突破每桶 91 美元。交易员密切关注特朗普在伊朗冲突中的下一步动向，研判他是否会等到中期选举结束之后再采取更多军事行动。
黄金价格上涨。此前公布的美国通胀报告弱于预期，削弱了市场对美联储本月加息的预期。
现货黄金上涨0.8%，至4187.43美元。在9月累计下跌超过6%后，金价以积极表现开启新一个月。
从历史规律看，9 月往往是股市表现偏弱的月份，标普 500 指数本月下跌 0.5%，投资者要同时应对油价走高和美债收益率大幅上行两大压力。道琼斯工业指数下跌 4.3%；得益于科技股带动，纳斯达克指数表现占优，9 月上涨 1.9%。
周三同时是第三季度收官日。标普 500 指数、纳斯达克指数本季度均上涨约 2%，道琼斯指数下跌 2.7%。
富国银行 投资研究所全球资产配置策略主管特蕾西・麦克米伦表示：“尽管上述因素依旧构成逆风，但企业盈利持续展现韧性。关键问题在于，在借贷成本居高不下的环境下，这种盈利强势能否延续。”
市场等待非农
周三公布的数据显示，美国8月通胀升幅低于预期，同时前一个月的价格压力也被向下修正。这份数据降低了市场对10月加息的预期。市场目前预计10月加息概率为36%，低于数据公布前的45%。不过，交易员仍认为12月加息的概率高达89%。
Tastylive全球宏观主管Ilya Spivak表示：“接下来公布的数据会非常重要，市场将观察这些数据，并据此调整对加息的预期。”
他说：“我们现在所处的环境里，市场正同时面对许多相互冲突的力量。”
美国9月非农就业报告定于周五公布。限制黄金涨幅的是美元小幅走强。美元上涨会提高使用其他货币的投资者购买以美元计价金属的成本。
地缘政治方面，伊朗周三表示，已收到美国方面对其最新提案的回应。该提案旨在恢复此前破裂的海湾地区停火安排。几天前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普曾表示，他已经拒绝了这一提案。
焦点个股
科技巨头Alphabet发布迄今为止最强的人工智能模型 Gemini 4 Argon 之后，股价上涨 2%。Alphabet 表示，这款新模型在网络安全、代码编写以及复杂专业工作方面均实现性能提升。
全球专业服务 埃森哲 公司公布第四财季财报后，股价大涨 17%。埃森哲营收达 186.8 亿美元，超出公司给出的 177.5‑184 亿美元业绩指引，同时高于 FactSet 一致预期的 183 亿美元；每股收益 3.29 美元，同样好于市场预期。
这家航天企业火箭实验室与总部位于东京的 Synspective 签署多年发射协议，将执行 20 次 “电子号” 火箭发射任务，股价上涨 4.5%。火箭实验室称，这是 “电子号” 火箭迄今为止规模最大的商业发射合同。
调味品企业味好美第三季度财报超出市场预期，股价走高近 5%。味好美调整后每股收益 86 美分，高于 FactSet 调研分析师预期的 76 美分；营收 20.2 亿美元，市场一致预期为 19.8 亿美元。
Loop Capital 将达乐公司评级从 “持有” 上调至 “买入”，股价上涨 1.3%。分析师表示：“随着假日销售季临近，我们认为当前美国宏观环境对达乐公司十分有利。”

title: Water system a 'disaster', Green deputy leader says
content:
Green Party co-deputy leader Rachel Millward has said her party would nationalise water companies in England and Wales, criticising Prime Minister Andy Burnham's plans to bring them under public control as "vague".

Millward told the BBC the country's water system was an "absolutely unmitigated disaster", arguing there had been "radical underinvestment" over decades.

She said Burnham's plan, which involves removing limits on government ownership of shares in water companies and giving mayors more powers to scrutinise them, did not go far enough.

The Green Party of England and Wales has long called for public ownership of water companies, describing privatisation as a failed experiment.

In its 2024 manifesto, the party estimated that nationalising water companies and the five biggest retail energy firms would cost £30bn over the five years of a parliament.

Last year, the government estimated, external that nationalising the water industry would cost approximately £100bn.

Millward is expected to make a speech about the party's latest policy on nationalising water companies - and how to pay for it - at the Green Party conference in Brighton this weekend.

It comes as the government considers the option of nationalising Thames Water, which is facing a severe financial crisis.

Ahead of the conference, Millward did a round of interviews with local BBC radio stations across England.

Under the leadership of Zack Polanski, the party's brand of "eco-populism" has posed a challenge to Labour on the left of British politics.

Labour's polling numbers have improved markedly in recent months, suggesting Burnham may be winning back some supporters that had drifted towards Polanski's party.

In her interviews, Millward said the party had had a "historic successful year" by winning a by-election in Gorton and Denton, and making significant gains in May's local elections.

She told BBC Radio Newcastle if it had not been for the rise of the Greens, then Sir Keir Starmer - who was ousted as prime minister by his own MPs - would still be in office.

"We can take the credit for that really," she said.

Millward said Labour's rhetoric had "shifted in our direction" under Burnham.

Going forward she said the Greens would push the Labour government to go further and continue calling for rent controls, nationalisation of water companies and wealth taxes.

But Millward faced some tough questions on local issues, some of which she wasn't able to answer.

She was asked by BBC Radio WM about the bin strikes in Birmingham, where a minority coalition of Liberal Democrats, Greens and independents run the council.

She said she hadn't "been given enough information to answer that question" and apologised several times.

"I'm sorry it's not in my briefing, it should have been," she said. "I'm happy to come on another time and chat about it."

These BBC local radio rounds can be tricky, with presenters often asking about issues in their patches.

Millward seemed most comfortable on national topics, arguing the Greens "have the power to set the agenda for this government" and hold Burnham to account.

The Greens have five MPs and hundreds of councillors across the country.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski is currently contesting the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, which will take place next week. A full list of candidates is available on the BBC website.

title: Kanye West's Russia shows officially cancelled after weeks of uncertainty
content:
Two stadium gigs in Russia by Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, have officially been cancelled.

West had been due to perform at the Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg on 10 and 11 October.

But there was confusion in the lead-up to the shows, as the venue had said it wouldn't host him for what would have been the biggest show by a western artist since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

In a post on messaging app Telegram, gig organisers Say Agency confirmed the concerts had been cancelled with "sincere regret".

"The Ye concerts in St Petersburg will not be able to take place on the scheduled dates," the Moscow-based agency wrote.

"We will issue an official statement regarding the status of the project and our plans in the near future."

Gazprom Arena said in August that it had not signed a rental agreement with the concert promoters and so the gig could not take place on its site.

Say Agency had said it was working to resolve the issue with the stadium before confirming they could not go ahead.

The stadium also acknowledged it had received complaints about West's performance.

He has recently apologised for multiple antisemitic and pro-Nazi comments in the past, saying he had "lost touch with reality" as a result of his bipolar disorder.

Russia was invaded by the Nazis in World War Two, and the country's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman was among those who criticised the planned shows.

Maria Zakharova said they were unacceptable and pointed out West's "glorification" of Hitler.

In 2025 West started selling swastika T-shirts and released a song called Heil Hitler.

Pro-war bloggers in Russia also questioned whether the country should be hosting an American artist while the US provided financial and military support for Ukraine.

West is yet to comment publicly on the cancellation.

His first major concert in the US for more than five years was held in Los Angeles in April, and he has since played in countries including Spain, Portugal and the Netherlands.

However, his Russian shows aren't the only gigs to have been cancelled.

Last summer West was set to headline London's Wireless Festival but was barred from entering the UK, forcing organisers to cancel the whole event.

West shows were also cancelled in Poland, Italy and France.

title: Tourette's campaigner Davidson asks to watch Scottish Baftas via video link after racial slur row
content:
Tourette's campaigner John Davidson has asked to watch the Scottish Baftas ceremony via a video link at the venue after he shouted a racial slur during the Bafta Film Awards in February.

The movie I Swear, which tells the story of Davidson growing up with Tourette syndrome in Scotland in the 1980s, has been nominated for seven Scottish Baftas.

It scooped three prizes at the Bafta Film Awards in London in February.

But the event was overshadowed by Davidson, whose condition involves involuntary tics, shouting the N-word at presenters Michael B Jordan and Delroy Lindo.

The BBC later apologised for not editing out the slur from its BBC One broadcast, which was shown on a two-hour delay, and remained on BBC iPlayer until the following day.

Bafta Scotland said it had worked with safeguarding and inclusion experts to allow Davidson to take part in its forthcoming ceremony in Glasgow "in the safest way possible for all".

It said Davidson, who was awarded an MBE in 2019 for his work in raising awareness of Tourette's, had suggested watching from a separate room in the venue with his family and friends.

Davidson, from Galashiels, shouted loudly several times before and during the Bafta ceremony in February.

He later said he was "deeply mortified if anyone considers my involuntary tics to be intentional or to carry any meaning".

"I have spent my life trying to support and empower the Tourette's community and to teach empathy, kindness and understanding from others and I will continue to do so," he said in a statement.

"I chose to leave the auditorium early into the ceremony as I was aware of the distress my tics were causing."

At the time, Bafta thanked Davidson for his "dignity and consideration of others, on what should have been a night of celebration for him".

"We take full responsibility for putting our guests in a very difficult situation and we apologise to all," it added.

"We will learn from this and keep inclusion at the core of all we do, maintaining our belief in film and storytelling as a critical conduit for compassion and empathy."

Capaldi, Carlyle and Mullan among Scottish Bafta nominees

This year's Scottish Bafta nominees include I Swear stars Peter Mullan, Robert Aramayo, Scott Ellis Watson and Shirley Henderson.

In the Actor Television category, Dougray Scott is nominated for Summerwater, Jack Lowden for Slow Horses, Peter Capaldi for Criminal Record and Robert Carlyle for The Hack.

There are also three nominations each for the Netflix crime drama Dept Q and BBC comedy Dinosaur while Dept Q's Leah Byrne also received an Audience Award nomination.

The winners will be announced on 15 November at a ceremony in Glasgow hosted by broadcaster Edith Bowman.

title: SpaceX即将把谷歌AI芯片送入轨道，推进太空数据中心构想
content:
核心要点
谷歌母公司 Alphabet 计划周四将自研 AI 芯片搭乘 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号火箭送入太空，向着实现太空数据中心迈出关键一步。
发射计划于太平洋时间上午 11 点 15 分，在加利福尼亚州圣巴巴拉县的范登堡空军基地实施。
SpaceX 把太空超级计算机称作人工智能基础设施的下一个前沿领域，宣扬轨道拥有 “无限空间”，借此摆脱地面建设数据中心所遭遇的各类社会阻力。在本次不载人的 “运输者‑18” 拼车发射任务中，SpaceX 将运载多颗 Planet Labs 卫星，其中包含一颗太阳能驱动原型卫星，搭载谷歌张量处理单元（TPU）。
这是 Alphabet “捕日者计划” 的首次在轨实测。该高风险研发项目由谷歌于 2025 年 11 月对外公布，目标打造可在太空持续运行、依靠太阳能供电的可靠 AI 计算基础设施。
Alphabet 在介绍本次发射计划的官方博客中表示，捕日者计划旨在 “探索未来太空能否承载可扩展的机器学习基础设施”。
Alphabet 是 SpaceX 的重要投资方。SpaceX 今年 6 月完成史上规模空前的 IPO，尽管两家企业的 AI 部门互为竞争对手，但双方保持深度合作关系。目前 Alphabet 持有的 SpaceX 股权估值超过 820 亿美元。
Alphabet 在博文中提到，处于近地轨道的卫星 “几乎可以持续接收太阳光，太阳能发电量最高可达地面的 8 倍”。公司长远设想是 “把多组卫星星座相互联网，在轨道上处理规模更大的 AI 计算任务”。
这家谷歌母公司此前已经在加州大学戴维斯分校的实验室完成 TPU 运行 AI 任务的地面测试，但芯片在近地轨道严酷环境中的实际表现仍是未知。
马斯克执掌的 SpaceX 同样公布规划：自主研发轨道数据中心。整套系统由华盛顿州雷德蒙德工厂制造的大批卫星集群组成，卫星搭载图形处理器，太阳能电池板将由马斯克旗下车企 特斯拉 协助生产。
今年早些时候，马斯克称太空数据中心会成为成本最低的 AI 训练方案，“最晚两到三年内就可以落地实现”。SpaceX 首席运营官格温妮・肖特韦尔在 9 月一场活动中表示，企业将于 2027 年部署 “太空超级计算”。
行业专家指出，即便太空数据中心未来具备可行性，现阶段依旧属于遥不可及的构想。一方面火箭发射运力紧张、成本高昂；另一方面轨道数据中心还需要能耐受极端温度的散热系统与芯片，同时做好抗辐射防护。太空碎片与轨道拥挤问题同样会制约该方案落地。
本次 “运输者‑18” 是 SpaceX 单日第二场具备里程碑意义的发射。周四，该公司还将从佛罗里达航天海岸执行 NASA 载人 13 号任务，运送航天员前往国际空间站，开启为期六个月的在轨驻留。

title: Australia’s banks show how to prepare for cable blackouts
content:
Elisabeth Braw

Published October 1 2026

The writer is the author of ‘The Undersea War: The International Battle for Supremacy at the Bottom of the World’. She is a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council and advises M&C Saatchi World Services

Australia is connected to the rest of the world by a rather small number of subsea data cables. Those cables efficiently transmit all the connectivity the country needs; they even offer spare capacity. But if the cables were damaged, Australia would struggle. Now the country is creating a backup that would thwart the worst harm — and other countries should learn from the Australians’ pragmatic take.

Earlier this year, executives from National Australia Bank sat down with managers from other leading financial institutions and government officials. The purpose of the gathering was to simulate what would happen if the country’s subsea cables suddenly became unavailable. “In the first stage, we hypothesised that the cables on the east coast, where most of our cables run, were cut,” Brad Carr, NAB’s executive in charge of geopolitical risk, who conceived the simulation exercise, told me. “And then we assumed the cables on the west coast were cut too.” The teams switched to satellite communications, only to discover that this transmitted a minuscule portion of the data — that is, money — they needed to send.

On their own, satellites won’t save banks or anyone else if cables suffer a massive outage. The Australians realised that they needed to plan for a situation in which their country found itself cut off from the rest of the modern world. Repair ships and their crews excel at their task, but they need time to get to the fault site, and malicious actors could obstruct them. Then there are administrative delays. Repairs to cables that travel through Indonesian waters — including the crucial links that connect Australia and Singapore — require Indonesian permits, which can take over a month to obtain.

For all these reasons, Australia needed a backup plan, the exercise demonstrated. Its major banks had already, together with the government, begun developing a plan that would allow the financial system to work in a mostly offline situation. “If we have a major incident, how can we make sure that our customers can pay for groceries?” Carr explained.

In parallel, the government has launched CI Fortify , guidance for infrastructure operators “in preparation for instances of crisis or service disruption”; it also expects operators to be able to isolate their infrastructure from other networks and systems for up to three months to be able to provide critical services to Australians.

If the cables were cut, the country would have to become digitally self-sufficient, relying on its domestic connectivity. In a crisis Australian consumers would be able to use their debit cards and withdraw cash from ATMs, and banks would be able to make necessary transactions, though without access to international bank-clearing systems. “It’s like field surgery, not a complete hospital,” a person familiar with the efforts told me. “There will be blood, but it will save the patient.”

Finland is making similar advances. And this summer, Sweden’s central bank teamed up with retail banks and payment cards “to enable card payments to be made even in the event of disruptions in data communication lasting up to seven days”.

Australian leaders are acutely aware of China’s fast-growing submarine fleet and the mysterious visits paid by Chinese research vessels to nearby waters. It could be nothing — but if it’s not, Australia will weather the storm a whole lot better than the countries that treat the risk of a major cable incident as unlikely. In August, Vietnam — which was less prepared — faced a major subsea-cable crisis when four of its eight major cables were damaged and connectivity dropped by 30 per cent.

Much of modern life would come to a halt without undersea cables. Planning for the turmoil that would hit the financial system if they were cut creates resilience at little expense.

title: 美国汇市干预收效有限，日本首相称政策将提振日元市场信心
content:
核心要点
在美国参与的汇率干预等托举日元的举措效果不及预期之后，日本首相于周四表示，本届政府的政策将重建市场对日元的信心。
高市早苗对日本电视台表示，上月与美国总统特朗普会谈时，她向对方提出日元估值被低估是一大问题。
“我国经济政策的目标并非操控汇率。” 高市早苗称。
“本届政府将针对危机应对与增长领域实施大规模投资，提升经济供给能力，以此挖掘日本的增长潜力。”
“上述举措将增强日本的全球竞争力，进而帮助市场建立对日元的信心。”
美元兑日元 实时报价|交易所 157.91，上涨 0.52（+0.33%） 最新|美国东部时间 7：58 加入观察列表
日元持续走弱，令日本政策制定者颇为棘手。
德意志银行数据显示，美日联合入市托举日元，叠加日本央行 9 月加息 25 个基点，推动日元成为第三季度 G10 货币中表现最优币种，日元兑美元本季度升值 3.3%。
美国东部时间周四凌晨 5 点 57 分，美元兑日元报 158.37；该汇率虽已从 7 月末 163 以上的高点回落，但较去年同期仍走高约 7.65%（日元同比贬值）。
法国兴业 银行首席外汇策略师基特・朱克斯在周三研报中写道：“市场普遍预期短期内日本很可能再度出手干预美元兑日元汇率，当前市场定价体现出投资者不想因突如其来的干预蒙受损失。”
“但油价若再度飙升，很容易逆转近期风险情绪的好转，因此市场仍需保持谨慎。” 他补充道。
华侨银行研究部外汇策略师沈孟松、黄卓勤在周一报告中指出：“日元估值虽已处于低位，但这并未有效缓解贬值压力。”
“尽管再度干预的威慑能够避免日元无序贬值，但如果没有国内政策调整作为配套，仅靠汇市干预难以实现日元持续回升。”
日元疲软困扰日本决策层
日元贬值抬高了日本进口成本，推高整体通胀。批评观点认为，高市早苗的财政支出计划是打压日元、推升国债收益率的诱因。
外界认为，美国政策制定者同样对日元弱势心存顾虑，因为日元持续走弱有可能倒逼日本抛售所持美国国债。
美国财政部数据显示，日本是美债最大海外持有方，持有超过 1.1 万亿美元美国债务。
高市早苗表示，日本政府财政支出规模将与降低政府债务占 GDP 比重的目标保持一致，同时会 “适度管控” 国债发行规模。
“我们会保障财政支出所需资金，满足各类财政需求。” 她补充道。

title: Is circular financing in AI a problem?
content:
Toby Nangle

Published October 1 2026

There are lots of ways in which circular financing among AI companies can be organised. A new report from a team of Bank for International Settlements researchers lists three.

First, there are those tech firms who receive both financing and business from another tech firm; so, maybe including Amazon pouring billions into Anthropic while also supplying the Trainium chips used to train Claude.

Second, suppliers could be financing customers to stimulate demand for their products, a bit like old-fashioned vendor financing. Nvidia’s pivot to providing ‘ balance sheet as a service ’ comes to mind — along with numerous reports of the giant chipmaker pumping cash in the direction of its financially more precarious customers so that they can buy more chips.

Or the flow could run the other way: customers financing suppliers in order to secure critical inputs. And finance can take many forms, from straight-up loans and equity injections through to forward compute contracts. So maybe the $300bn of business with which OpenAI is backstopping Oracle’s data centre build-out counts, even if OpenAI doesn’t actually have the $300bn and is relying on current or future investors to supply it.

Third comes everything else: reciprocal commercial relationships where goods or services flow both ways.

Looking at a universe of 1,246 AI firms split across compute, infrastructure, data tools, models and applications, the report’s authors — Jon Frost, Rudraksh Kansal, Kumar Rishabh, Vatsala Shreeti and Leanne Si Ying Zhang — found, perhaps unsurprisingly, a lot of circular relationships.

Totting up all the incoming investment flowing to AI firms between 2021 and 2025, they reckon more than half came from other AI firms. And looking just at this lump of AI-to-AI deals, almost half of these were between firms that shared some commercial relationship, suggesting “that a significant portion of financing and commercial relationships in AI are self-referencing.”

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

But is it a problem?

... circular relationships make reported demand partly endogenous to firms’ own financing decisions. For example, when a supplier finances a customer, part of the supplier’s revenue growth reflects its own capital investment, rather than organic final demand. This makes it harder for investors, lenders and supervisors to gauge what part of the current AI boom is based on organic demand.

Beyond making analysts’ lives a bit tricky, are there real-life problems for the rest of us?

The parallel with the telecommunications boom of the late 1990s is instructive : upstream equipment vendors such as Lucent and Nortel financed network operators so that the operators could buy the vendors’ equipment. This meant that part of the equipment vendors’ reported sales was being funded by the vendors themselves. For a time, as operators expanded their networks, equipment orders also expanded and vendors booked both the sales and loans as assets. However, when operators’ own revenues failed to materialise or slowed, they could neither repay the loans nor sustain the equipment purchases. Equipment vendors then sustained both financial losses and a loss of sales. Such dynamics may also play out in AI if revenue growth and end user demand fall short of firms’ expectations.

Some content could not load. Check your internet connection or browser settings.

We couldn’t find a market cap series for Lucent, but the Nortel market cap chart suggests circular financing can be a problem. But is it a problem this time ?

...these circular arrangements tend to be opaque, making monitoring and supervision difficult. Many of the firms involved in AI are private and may disclose limited information. Even where firms are publicly listed, deal terms can often be complex, mixing cash investments with long-term purchase commitments and guarantees on the value of the underlying assets. Residual value guarantees (RVGs) are one example, where the guarantor pledges to cover any shortfall in an asset’s worth (such as chips or data centre equipment) after a fixed period. These contingent commitments sit off balance sheet and only materialise during a downturn – when a guarantor is least able to absorb them. As such, reported deal values may not capture the whole picture, and headline figures can differ substantially from disbursed amounts. Moreover, many of these firms reside in different sectors and jurisdictions, making it difficult for a single supervisor or regulator to monitor these risks.

Hmm. Without the necessary disclosures to pore through, even the hardest-working supervisor or investor is going to struggle to know whether it’s a problem until after the fact.

But there is a silver lining. If it does turn out to be a problem, the BIS reckon that at least we’ll all know about it. Not only through a public equity market swoon, and upending of macroeconomically significant investment. But also because they reckon risks will be magnified by hidden leverage and interconnected exposures across private credit and special purpose vehicles used to finance AI infrastructure. 😬

title: 图表揭示：上个季度股债市场剧烈震荡
content:
核心要点
截至 9 月的这三个月，是美伊冲突爆发后第二个完整交易季度，股市震荡加剧。 交易员密切关注中东局势消息；冲突陷入僵持。美国总统特朗普扬言要对德黑兰发动 “经济登陆日” 打击，据报道，他回绝了伊朗提出的有条件停火提议。
股市上涨动能减弱
霍尔木兹海峡持续封锁，引发能源市场与通胀恐慌，但股票整体在第三季度仍取得正收益。 不过上涨力度明显放缓。
华尔街主要股指季度收盘涨跌不一：标普 500 指数上涨 2.03%， 道琼斯 工业指数下跌 1.9%，科技股集中的 纳斯达克 综合指数季度涨幅 2.2%。 三大指数平均涨幅仅 0.6%，相比上个季度两位数的涨幅，本轮上涨明显降温。
涨势放缓背后，资金从 AI 板块撤离，该行业持续震荡。7 月，某半导体公司财报利润暴涨超 19 倍、超出市场预期，叠加中国竞争相关利空消息，资金获利了结引发芯片股大跌；次月，市场担忧融资与资本开支问题，AI 板块再度剧烈波动。
9 月，多位 AI 领域核心人物 ——Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥・阿莫代、OpenAI 首席执行官山姆・奥尔特曼，出于安全考量呼吁放缓 AI 技术研发速度，AI 与科技股承压。
韩国科技权重高的综合股指（Kospi）本季度暴跌近 20%，费城半导体指数下跌超 11%。
AI 巨头个股表现分化：英伟达本季度涨幅超 14%， 微软 大涨 37.5%，两家企业财报数据强劲、需求旺盛； 甲骨文 、博通均跌超 6%。Meta 股价飙升近 30%，其 Muse AI 个人智能代理上线数周内，在美国下载量达到数十万次。
美国以外市场表现参差不齐：欧洲主要股指小幅收涨；亚洲市场，韩国 Kospi 指数下跌 19.3%，中国沪深 300 指数下跌 12.5%，澳大利亚基准股指持平。
新兴市场同样分化。截至 9 月三个月，MSCI 新兴市场指数下跌 1%；尼日利亚、保加利亚、哥伦比亚、波兰、乌克兰、希腊对应的 MSCI 指数均录得两位数涨幅。 但对许多投资者而言，AI 前景和企业盈利乐观预期压倒各类利空因素。
瑞银 全球财富管理首席投资官马克・海费莱周一在研报中表示，团队维持股票乐观判断，仓位布局继续博弈市场进一步上行。 他建议：“投资者可在股票底仓做广泛分散配置，同时定向布局变革创新板块与周期机会，降低对单一股票或一小撮科技公司的过度依赖。我们持续看好 AI、电力资源与长寿赛道，推荐跨行业、跨区域均衡持仓。”
债券遭遇抛售
第三季度全球主权债券陷入抛售潮。市场博弈伊朗战争的后续走向，押注通胀上行、央行继续加息。
债市压力持续加大，美国 10 年期国债、30 年期国债收益率分别触及多年新高。美国政府融资成本在 G7 发达经济体中处于高位，基准 10 年期美债收益率站稳 5% 上方，30 年期美债收益率高于 5.5%。

债券收益率与价格呈反向变动。

贝莱德 策略师在每周市场点评中称，市场对美联储进一步收紧政策的预期或许高估。 “上周全球债券抛售加速，长端美债收益率升至 20 多年新高，源于市场对继续加息的预期。我们认为市场预期可能超前。在经济走强背景下，一次加息若巩固美联储政策可信度，整体而言利好风险资产。”
油价突破 100 美元
中东僵局再度推升油价。 截至 9 月 30 日三个月，国际基准布伦特原油即月期货大涨 42%，收于 103.53 美元 / 桶，为本十年季度涨幅第三高，仅次于今年一季度伊朗开战时期、2020 年新冠疫情高峰期。美国 WTI 原油即月期货上涨 30.1%，报 90.42 美元 / 桶。
